PART I: Definitions

I.10  Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
I.11  Network provider means a practitioner or clinic that has an agreement with the Plan to provide treatment.
I.12  Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.

I.19  Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Member's details, the covers the Member bought and any extensions.

PART II: Limits and deductible
II.1  Dental Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
II.2  Vision Care: limit $400 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
II.3  Therapy Services: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
II.4  Hearing Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
II.5  Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

PART III: Customer support
III.1  The Plan's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
III.2  Outside these hours the Member can leave a message and the Plan will call back on the next working day.

PART IV: Coordination of benefits
IV.1  If a treatment is also covered by another plan, the Plan will pay only the part of the cost that the other plan does not pay.
IV.2  The Member must tell the Plan about any other plan that covers the Member or the Member's dependants.

PART V: Leaving the plan
V.1  Cover ends on the day the Member's employment ends or the day the Member stops being eligible, whichever is earlier.
V.2  Claims for treatment received before cover ended may be submitted up to 90 days afterwards.

PART VI: Automatic renewal
VI.1  Unless the Member tells the Plan otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Plan holds.
VI.2  The Member can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Plan's helpline.

PART VII: Reasonable precautions
VII.1  The Member must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
VII.2  The Member must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

PART VIII: Exchange of information
VIII.1  To prevent fraud, the Plan may check the details the Member gives against public records and industry databases.
VIII.2  The Plan may contact previous insurers to confirm the Member's claims history.

PART IX: Cancellation
IX.1  The Member can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
IX.2  After the first 14 days the Member can cancel at any time; the Plan will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
IX.3  The Plan can cancel this policy by giving the Member 30 days' written notice to the last address the Plan holds.

PART X: Therapy Services
X.1  The Plan will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
X.2  The most the Plan will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $300 per treatment.
X.3  The Plan will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
X.4  The Plan will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

PART XI: Records and evidence
XI.1  The Member should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
XI.2  Where proof of value is missing, the Plan may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
XI.3  The Plan may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

PART XII: Cooperation
XII.1  The Member must give the Plan all the help and information the Plan reasonably need to settle a claim.
XII.2  The Member must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Plan's written permission.

PART XIII: Taxes
XIII.1  The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
XIII.2  If the tax rate changes, the Plan may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

PART XIV: Accessibility
XIV.1  This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

PART XV: Interest
XV.1  The Plan will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

PART XVI: Sanctions
XVI.1  The Plan will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Plan to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

XX.1  The Plan will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.

XX.4  The most the Plan will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $600 per treatment.
XX.5  The Plan will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.

XXI.1  Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.

XXII.1  The Plan may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Plan's behalf.

XXIII.1  The Plan will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.

XXIII.4  The Plan will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

XXV.1  If the Plan does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Plan has given up the right to enforce it later.

PART XXVI: Optional cover: Hearing Care
XXVI.1  The Plan will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
XXVI.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Member's schedule.
XXVI.3  The most the Plan will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $150 per treatment.
XXVI.4  The Plan will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

PART XXVII: Wellness allowance
XXVII.1  Each plan year the Member may claim up to $250 towards a gym membership or fitness class.
XXVII.2  The wellness allowance is not subject to any deductible and does not count towards other limits.

PART XXVIII: Claims documents
XXVIII.1  The Member must provide, at the Member's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Plan reasonably ask for.
XXVIII.2  The Plan may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

PART XXIX: Data protection
XXIX.1  The Plan will use the personal information the Member provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
XXIX.2  The Plan will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
XXIX.3  The Member can ask for a copy of the personal information the Plan holds by writing to the Plan's data protection officer.

PART XXX: Electronic documents

XXX.2  The Member must tell the Plan if the Member's email address changes.
XXX.3  Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

PART IX: Taxes
IX.1  The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
IX.2  If the tax rate changes, the Insurer may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

PART X: Arbitration
X.1  If the Insurer accepts a claim but disagree with the Policyholder about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
X.2  Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against the Insurer.

PART XI: Records and evidence
XI.1  The Policyholder should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
XI.2  Where proof of value is missing, the Insurer may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
XI.3  The Insurer may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

PART XII: Market conditions
XII.1  If the replacement item is no longer available, the Insurer will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

PART XIII: Interest
XIII.1  The Insurer will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

PART XIV: Third-party administrators
XIV.1  The Insurer may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Insurer's behalf.
XIV.2  Any company the Insurer appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

PART XV: Discounts
XV.1  Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
XV.2  If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Insurer may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

PART XVI: Claims documents
XVI.1  The Policyholder must provide, at the Policyholder's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Insurer reasonably ask for.
XVI.2  The Insurer may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

PART XVII: Contents temporarily removed
XVII.1  The Policyholder's contents are covered while temporarily removed from the home to another building in the same country, for up to 60 days.
XVII.2  Contents in a student hall of residence are covered only if the student is a member of the Policyholder's family.

PART XVIII: Freezer contents
XVIII.1  The Insurer will pay for food in a domestic freezer that spoils because of a rise or fall in temperature.
XVIII.2  The Insurer will not pay if the freezer is more than fifteen years old, or if the electricity supplier cut the supply deliberately.

PART XIX: Instalment agreements
XIX.1  If the Policyholder pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
XIX.2  Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

PART XX: Communication
XX.1  The Insurer will communicate with the Policyholder in English.
XX.2  The Insurer may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

PART XXI: Electronic documents
XXI.1  The Insurer will send documents by email unless the Policyholder asks for paper copies.
XXI.2  The Policyholder must tell the Insurer if the Policyholder's email address changes.
XXI.3  Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

PART XXII: Change of address
XXII.1  The Policyholder must tell the Insurer within 30 days if the Policyholder changes the Policyholder's address.
XXII.2  The Insurer may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

PART XXIII: Payment of claims
XXIII.1  The Insurer will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Policyholder's name.
XXIII.2  The Insurer aims to pay accepted claims within 10 working days of receiving all the documents the Insurer needs.

PART XXIV: Interpretation
XXIV.1  Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
XXIV.2  Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
XXIV.3  Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

PART XXV: Renewal
XXV.1  The Insurer will write to the Policyholder at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
XXV.2  The Insurer is not obliged to offer renewal.

PART XXVI: Environmental commitment
XXVI.1  Where practical, the Insurer will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
XXVI.2  The Policyholder may ask for a new part instead, and the Insurer will tell the Policyholder whether any additional cost would apply.

XXVII.1  This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
XXVII.2  Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

XXVIII.1  If the Policyholder rents the home, the Insurer will pay for damage to fixtures and fittings that the Policyholder installed and are responsible for.
XXVIII.2  This cover applies only to improvements the Policyholder paid for, not to items provided by the landlord.

PART XXIX: Premium payment
XXIX.1  The Policyholder must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
XXIX.2  If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, the Insurer may cancel the policy after giving notice.

XXXI.2  After the first 14 days the Policyholder can cancel at any time; the Insurer will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $30.
XXXI.3  The Insurer can cancel this policy by giving the Policyholder 30 days' written notice to the last address the Insurer holds.

XXXII.1  Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
XXXII.2  A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

XXXIII.1  The Policyholder must tell the Insurer as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
XXXIII.2  The Insurer may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

XXXIV.1  The Insurer will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Insurer to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

# Device Protection Plan Terms
Issued by Voltguard Protection Ltd

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Accessories means cases, chargers and earbuds.
- **1.2** Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
- **1.3** Breakdown means the failure of a part to work as the manufacturer intended, from an internal electrical or mechanical fault.
- **1.4** Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 24 months after the device was bought.

## 2. Limits and service fee
- **2.1** Accidental Damage: limit $1,500 per incident; service fee $79 per claim.
- **2.2** Breakdown: limit $1,000 per incident; service fee $25 per claim.
- **2.3** Theft and Loss: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $149 per claim.
- **2.4** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the service fee is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Instalment agreements
- **3.1** If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
- **3.2** Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

## 4. Renewal
- **4.1** We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
- **4.2** We are not obliged to offer renewal.

## 5. Reasonable precautions
- **5.1** You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
- **5.2** You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

## 6. Communication
- **6.1** We will communicate with you in English.
- **6.2** We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

## 7. Currency
- **7.1** All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
- **7.2** Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

## 8. Environmental commitment
- **8.1** Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
- **8.2** You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

## 9. Interpretation
- **9.1** Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
- **9.2** Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
- **9.3** Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

## 10. Assignment
- **10.1** You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

## 11. Breakdown
- **11.1** We will repair or replace your device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
- **11.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 45 days after the policy start date.
- **11.3** The most we will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $80 per incident.
- **11.4** We will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
- **11.5** We will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

## 12. Interest
- **12.1** We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

## 13. Market conditions
- **13.1** If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

## 14. Governing law
- **14.1** This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
- **14.2** Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

## 15. Fraud
- **15.1** If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
- **15.2** We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

## 16. Optional cover: Theft and Loss
- **16.1** We will replace your device if it is stolen or lost.
- **16.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **16.3** The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.
- **16.4** We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Insurer, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
I.2  Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
I.3  Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
I.4  Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
I.5  Family means the Insured Person's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Insured Person.
I.6  Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,000 metres.
I.7  Limit means the most the Insurer will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
I.8  Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
I.9  Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
I.10  Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which the Insured Person received treatment or advice in the 12 months before the policy start date.
I.11  Premium means the amount the Insured Person must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
I.12  Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
I.13  Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 6 hours.
I.14  Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
I.15  Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
I.16  Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
I.17  Territory means the countries in which cover applies, as shown in the schedule.
I.18  Travelling companion means a person who has booked to travel with the Insured Person on the same trip.
I.19  Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

II.1  Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.

II.3  Trip Cancellation: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.4  Travel Delay: limit $500 per incident; excess $25 per claim.

19.1 You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.

SECTION 21 - RECOVERY OF COSTS
21.1 If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

SECTION 22 - CURRENCY
22.1 All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
22.2 Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

23.1 You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.

26.1 If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

27.1 We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.

33.1 If our medical adviser agrees it is necessary, we will arrange and pay for you to be brought home.

SECTION 34 - SEVERABILITY
34.1 If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

SECTION 35 - RENEWAL

37.1 You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.

SECTION 38 - COMMUNICATION
38.1 We will communicate with you in English.

SECTION 39 - INTEREST

40.1 We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.

43.1 When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.

44.1 We will pay reasonable additional travel and accommodation costs to reach your destination if you arrive too late to board your booked transport because public transport fails.

SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS
1.1 Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
1.2 Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 3,000 metres.
1.3 Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.

1.5 Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
1.6 Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 12 hours.
1.7 Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
1.8 Travelling companion means a person who has booked to travel with you on the same trip.

SECTION 2 - LIMITS AND EXCESS
2.1 Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $75 per claim.
2.2 Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $50,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
2.3 Trip Cancellation: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.4 Travel Delay: limit $750 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
2.5 Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

SECTION 3 - EMERGENCY MEDICAL EXPENSES
3.1 We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
3.2 The most we will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $250 per incident.
3.3 The most we will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $300 per incident.
3.4 We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
3.5 We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
3.6 We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

SECTION 4 - OPTIONAL COVER: TRAVEL DELAY
4.1 We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
4.2 This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
4.3 We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

SECTION 5 - GENERAL EXCLUSIONS
5.1 We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
5.2 We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
5.3 We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

SECTION 6 - MAKING A CLAIM
6.1 You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
6.2 You must notify us of a claim within 60 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
6.3 We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

SECTION 7 - WAIVER
7.1 If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

SECTION 8 - GOVERNING LAW
8.1 This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
8.2 Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

SECTION 9 - AUTOMATIC RENEWAL
9.1 Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
9.2 You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

SECTION 10 - REASONABLE PRECAUTIONS
10.1 You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
10.2 You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

SECTION 11 - ELECTRONIC DOCUMENTS
11.1 We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
11.2 You must tell us if your email address changes.
11.3 Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

SECTION 12 - PAYMENT OF CLAIMS
12.1 We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
12.2 We aim to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

SECTION 13 - CANCELLATION
13.1 You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
13.2 After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
13.3 We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

SECTION 14 - RENTAL CAR EXCESS
14.1 If you hire a car during the trip, we will reimburse any excess you must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.
14.2 This section applies only to cars hired from a licensed rental company under a written agreement.

SECTION 15 - ASSIGNMENT
15.1 You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

SECTION 16 - EXCHANGE OF INFORMATION
16.1 To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
16.2 We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

SECTION 17 - THIRD-PARTY ADMINISTRATORS
17.1 We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
17.2 Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

SECTION 18 - CUSTOMER SUPPORT
18.1 Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
18.2 Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

SECTION 19 - MARKET CONDITIONS
19.1 If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

SECTION 20 - SALVAGE
20.1 When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
20.2 If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

SECTION 21 - ARBITRATION
21.1 If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
21.2 Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

SECTION 22 - FRAUD
22.1 If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.

EMPLOYEE HEALTH BENEFITS PLAN: SUMMARY PLAN DESCRIPTION
Issued by the Staff Welfare Fund

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Plan, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
I.2  Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
I.3  Dependant means the Member's spouse or partner, or a child under 21 who is enrolled in the plan.
I.4  Family means the Member's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Member.
I.5  Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
I.6  Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
I.7  Hearing aid replacement period means 36 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
I.8  Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
I.9  Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
I.10  Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
I.11  Network provider means a practitioner or clinic that has an agreement with the Plan to provide treatment.
I.12  Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
I.13  Plan year means the twelve months starting on the Member's coverage start date.
I.14  Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Member's schedule.
I.15  Premium means the amount the Member must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
I.16  Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
I.17  Registered practitioner means a practitioner registered with the professional body for their discipline.
I.18  Replacement period means 12 months from the date of the Member's last eyewear claim.
I.19  Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

PART II: Limits and deductible
II.1  Dental Care: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
II.2  Vision Care: limit $500 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
II.3  Therapy Services: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
II.4  Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
II.5  The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Optional cover: Hearing Care
III.1  The Plan will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
III.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Member's schedule.
III.3  The most the Plan will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $150 per treatment.
III.4  The Plan will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

PART IV: Therapy Services
IV.1  The Plan will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
IV.2  The most the Plan will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $200 per treatment.
IV.3  The Plan will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
IV.4  The Plan will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

PART V: Vision Care
V.1  The Plan will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
V.2  The most the Plan will pay for Frames under this section is $150 per treatment.
V.3  The Plan will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
V.4  The Plan will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

PART VI: Dental Care
VI.1  The Plan will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
VI.2  No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 90 days after the policy start date.
VI.3  The most the Plan will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $750 per treatment.
VI.4  The most the Plan will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $800 per treatment.
VI.5  The Plan will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
VI.6  The Plan will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

PART VII: General exclusions
VII.1  The Plan will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Member.
VII.2  The Plan will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
VII.3  The Plan will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Plan from paying.

PART VIII: Making a claim
VIII.1  The Plan may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
VIII.2  The Member must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
VIII.3  The Member must notify the Plan of a claim within 60 days of the treatment. The Plan will not pay any claim notified after that time.

PART IX: Geographical limits
IX.1  Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
IX.2  Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

PART X: Reasonable precautions
X.1  The Member must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
X.2  The Member must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

PART XI: Environmental commitment
XI.1  Where practical, the Plan will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
XI.2  The Member may ask for a new part instead, and the Plan will tell the Member whether any additional cost would apply.

PART XII: Severability
XII.1  If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

PART XIII: Customer support
XIII.1  The Plan's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
XIII.2  Outside these hours the Member can leave a message and the Plan will call back on the next working day.

PART XIV: Payment of claims
XIV.1  The Plan will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Member's name.
XIV.2  The Plan aims to pay accepted claims within 15 working days of receiving all the documents the Plan needs.

PART XV: Interpretation
XV.1  Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
XV.2  Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
XV.3  Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

PART XVI: Automatic renewal
XVI.1  Unless the Member tells the Plan otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Plan holds.
XVI.2  The Member can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Plan's helpline.

PART XVII: Waiver
XVII.1  If the Plan does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Plan has given up the right to enforce it later.

PART XVIII: Notices
XVIII.1  Any notice the Plan gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Plan holds.
XVIII.2  Notices from the Member should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

PART XIX: Premium payment
XIX.1  The Member must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
XIX.2  If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, the Plan may cancel the policy after giving notice.

PART XX: Accessibility
XX.1  This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

PART XXI: Joint policyholders
XXI.1  Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
XXI.2  A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

PART XXII: Cooperation
XXII.1  The Member must give the Plan all the help and information the Plan reasonably need to settle a claim.
XXII.2  The Member must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Plan's written permission.

PART XXIII: Recovery of costs
XXIII.1  If the Plan pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Plan may ask the Member to repay the amount.

PART XXIV: Records and evidence
XXIV.1  The Member should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
XXIV.2  Where proof of value is missing, the Plan may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
XXIV.3  The Plan may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

PART XXV: Data protection
XXV.1  The Plan will use the personal information the Member provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
XXV.2  The Plan will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
XXV.3  The Member can ask for a copy of the personal information the Plan holds by writing to the Plan's data protection officer.

PART XXVI: Appeals
XXVI.1  If the Plan declines all or part of a claim, the Member may appeal in writing within 60 days of the decision.
XXVI.2  An appeal will be reviewed by someone who was not involved in the original decision.
XXVI.3  The Plan will give the Member a written decision on the appeal within 30 days.

PART XXVII: Other insurance
XXVII.1  If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Plan will pay only the Plan's proportionate share.
XXVII.2  The Member must tell the Plan about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Member makes a claim.

PART XXVIII: Currency
XXVIII.1  All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
XXVIII.2  Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

PART XXIX: Sanctions
XXIX.1  The Plan will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Plan to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

PART XXX: Change of address
XXX.1  The Member must tell the Plan within 30 days if the Member changes the Member's address.
XXX.2  The Plan may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

PART XXXI: Taxes
XXXI.1  The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
XXXI.2  If the tax rate changes, the Plan may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

PART XXXII: Fraud
XXXII.1  If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Plan will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
XXXII.2  The Plan may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

PART XXXIII: Claims documents
XXXIII.1  The Member must provide, at the Member's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Plan reasonably ask for.
XXXIII.2  The Plan may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

PART XXXIV: Exchange of information
XXXIV.1  To prevent fraud, the Plan may check the details the Member gives against public records and industry databases.
XXXIV.2  The Plan may contact previous insurers to confirm the Member's claims history.

PART XXXV: Salvage
XXXV.1  When the Plan replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Plan's property.
XXXV.2  If stolen property is recovered after the Plan has paid a claim, the Member must tell the Plan and either return the payment or give the Plan the property.

PART XXXVI: Duty of fair presentation
XXXVI.1  The Member must answer all questions the Plan asks honestly and to the best of the Member's knowledge.
XXXVI.2  If the Member gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Plan may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
XXXVI.3  If the Member gives incorrect information carelessly, the Plan may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

PART XXXVII: Communication
XXXVII.1  The Plan will communicate with the Member in English.
XXXVII.2  The Plan may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

PART XXXVIII: Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
XXXVIII.1  A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

PART XXXIX: Inflation
XXXIX.1  The Plan may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
XXXIX.2  Any adjustment will be shown in the Member's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

PART XXXX: How to read this document
XXXX.1  This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
XXXX.2  Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
XXXX.3  Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

PART XXXXI: Instalment agreements
XXXXI.1  If the Member pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
XXXXI.2  Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

PART XXXXII: Coordination of benefits
XXXXII.1  If a treatment is also covered by another plan, the Plan will pay only the part of the cost that the other plan does not pay.
XXXXII.2  The Member must tell the Plan about any other plan that covers the Member or the Member's dependants.

PART XXXXIII: Wellness allowance
XXXXIII.1  Each plan year the Member may claim up to $250 towards a gym membership or fitness class.
XXXXIII.2  The wellness allowance is not subject to any deductible and does not count towards other limits.

state.claim: File note. Leila Eriksen (policy B135123, start date 20 November 2025) claims under Travel Delay for meals and a hotel night during a departure delay. The schedule shows these covers: Baggage and Personal Belongings, Emergency Medical Expenses, Trip Cancellation, Travel Delay; extensions: none. The incident happened on 23 November 2025 and was notified on 30 November 2025. The delay was caused by a technical fault with the aircraft. The trip was booked through an online travel agent. The destination was a coastal town Leila had visited before. Leila paid for the trip with a credit card. The assessed loss is $809.40.
state.policy:
ANNUAL MULTI-TRIP TRAVEL COVER
Issued by Meridian Travel Insurance Ltd
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Meridian Travel Insurance Ltd and "the Insured Person" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Insurer, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
(b) Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
(c) Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
(d) Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
(e) Family means the Insured Person's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Insured Person.
(f) Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,000 metres.
(g) Limit means the most the Insurer will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
(h) Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
(i) Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which the Insured Person received treatment or advice in the 6 months before the policy start date.
(j) Premium means the amount the Insured Person must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
(k) Public transport means any scheduled train, bus, coach, ferry or aircraft.
(l) Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 12 hours.
(m) Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
(n) Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
(o) Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
(p) Territory means the countries in which cover applies, as shown in the schedule.
(q) Travelling companion means a person who has booked to travel with the Insured Person on the same trip.
(r) Trip means a journey that starts and ends in the Insured Person's home country during the policy period.
(s) Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $75 per claim.
(b) Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $25,000 per incident; excess $150 per claim.
(c) Trip Cancellation: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(d) Travel Delay: limit $500 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(e) The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

Article 3. Emergency Medical Expenses
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $400 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $500 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for any claim arising from the Insured Person's being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

Article 4. Baggage and Personal Belongings
(a) The Insurer will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to the Insured Person's baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Valuables under this section is $250 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $300 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

Article 5. Optional cover: Travel Delay
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if the Insured Person's outbound departure is delayed.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Insured Person's schedule.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

Article 6. Trip Cancellation
(a) The Insurer will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if the Insured Person must cancel the trip for a reason beyond the Insured Person's control.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 7 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $300 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before the Insured Person bought the policy.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation because the Insured Person no longer wish to travel.

Article 7. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Insured Person.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.

Article 8. Making a claim
(a) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(b) The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(c) The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 14 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

Article 9. Other insurance
(a) If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Insurer will pay only the Insurer's proportionate share.
(b) The Insured Person must tell the Insurer about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Insured Person makes a claim.

Article 10. Payment of claims
(a) The Insurer will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Insured Person's name.
(b) The Insurer aims to pay accepted claims within 15 working days of receiving all the documents the Insurer needs.

Article 11. Taxes
(a) The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
(b) If the tax rate changes, the Insurer may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

Article 12. Change of address
(a) The Insured Person must tell the Insurer within 30 days if the Insured Person changes the Insured Person's address.
(b) The Insurer may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

Article 13. Interest
(a) The Insurer will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

Article 14. Customer support
(a) The Insurer's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
(b) Outside these hours the Insured Person can leave a message and the Insurer will call back on the next working day.

Article 15. Cancellation
(a) The Insured Person can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
(b) After the first 14 days the Insured Person can cancel at any time; the Insurer will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
(c) The Insurer can cancel this policy by giving the Insured Person 30 days' written notice to the last address the Insurer holds.

Article 16. Waiver
(a) If the Insurer does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Insurer has given up the right to enforce it later.

Article 17. Duty of fair presentation
(a) The Insured Person must answer all questions the Insurer asks honestly and to the best of the Insured Person's knowledge.
(b) If the Insured Person gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Insurer may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
(c) If the Insured Person gives incorrect information carelessly, the Insurer may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

Article 18. Missed departure
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable additional travel and accommodation costs to reach the Insured Person's destination if the Insured Person arrives too late to board the Insured Person's booked transport because public transport fails.
(b) The Insured Person must allow enough time to reach the departure point, and must obtain written confirmation of the delay from the transport operator.

Article 19. Rental car excess
(a) If the Insured Person hires a car during the trip, the Insurer will reimburse any excess the Insured Person must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.
(b) This section applies only to cars hired from a licensed rental company under a written agreement.

Article 20. Geographical limits
(a) Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
(b) Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

Article 21. How to read this document
(a) This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
(b) Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
(c) Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

Article 22. Interpretation
(a) Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
(b) Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
(c) Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

Article 23. Renewal
(a) The Insurer will write to the Insured Person at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
(b) The Insurer is not obliged to offer renewal.

Article 24. Changes in circumstances
(a) The Insured Person must tell the Insurer as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
(b) The Insurer may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

Article 25. Joint policyholders
(a) Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
(b) A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

Article 26. Environmental commitment
(a) Where practical, the Insurer will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
(b) The Insured Person may ask for a new part instead, and the Insurer will tell the Insured Person whether any additional cost would apply.

Article 27. Inflation
(a) The Insurer may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
(b) Any adjustment will be shown in the Insured Person's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

Article 28. Discounts
(a) Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
(b) If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Insurer may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

Article 29. Compensation scheme
(a) The Insurer is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
(b) If the Insurer cannot meet the Insurer's obligations, the Insured Person may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

Article 30. Subrogation
(a) The Insurer will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Insured Person's name the defence or settlement of any claim.
(b) The Insurer can take action in the Insured Person's name to recover any payment the Insurer makes from anyone responsible for the loss.

Article 31. Market conditions
(a) If the replacement item is no longer available, the Insurer will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

Article 32. Exchange of information
(a) To prevent fraud, the Insurer may check the details the Insured Person gives against public records and industry databases.
(b) The Insurer may contact previous insurers to confirm the Insured Person's claims history.

Article 33. Third-party administrators
(a) The Insurer may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Insurer's behalf.
(b) Any company the Insurer appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

Article 34. Repatriation
(a) If the Insurer's medical adviser agrees it is necessary, the Insurer will arrange and pay for the Insured Person to be brought home.
(b) The Insurer will decide the method of transport and the time of repatriation after speaking to the treating doctor.

Article 35. Cooperation
(a) The Insured Person must give the Insurer all the help and information the Insurer reasonably need to settle a claim.
(b) The Insured Person must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Insurer's written permission.

Article 36. Communication
(a) The Insurer will communicate with the Insured Person in English.
(b) The Insurer may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

Article 37. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
(a) A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

Article 38. Accessibility
(a) This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

Article 39. Data protection
(a) The Insurer will use the personal information the Insured Person provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
(b) The Insurer will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
(c) The Insured Person can ask for a copy of the personal information the Insurer holds by writing to the Insurer's data protection officer.

Article 40. Electronic documents
(a) The Insurer will send documents by email unless the Insured Person asks for paper copies.
(b) The Insured Person must tell the Insurer if the Insured Person's email address changes.
(c) Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

Article 41. Fraud
(a) If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Insurer will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
(b) The Insurer may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

Article 42. Notices
(a) Any notice the Insurer gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Insurer holds.
(b) Notices from the Insured Person should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

Article 43. Salvage
(a) When the Insurer replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Insurer's property.
(b) If stolen property is recovered after the Insurer has paid a claim, the Insured Person must tell the Insurer and either return the payment or give the Insurer the property.

Article 44. Severability
(a) If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

Article 45. Premium payment
(a) The Insured Person must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
(b) If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, the Insurer may cancel the policy after giving notice.

Article 46. Complaints
(a) If the Insured Person has a complaint, the Insured Person should first contact the Insurer's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
(b) The Insurer will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
(c) If the Insured Person remains dissatisfied, the Insured Person may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

Article 47. Legal expenses abroad
(a) The Insurer will pay legal costs to pursue compensation for the Insured Person's injury or death caused by a third party during the trip.
(b) The Insurer will not pay legal costs unless the Insurer's legal adviser agrees that the claim has a reasonable prospect of success.

Article 48. Assignment
(a) The Insured Person cannot transfer the Insured Person's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Insurer's written consent.

Article 49. Recovery of costs
(a) If the Insurer pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Insurer may ask the Insured Person to repay the amount.

Article 50. Reasonable precautions
(a) The Insured Person must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
(b) The Insured Person must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

Article 51. Personal liability
(a) The Insurer will pay damages the Insured Person becomes legally liable to pay for accidental injury to another person or accidental damage to their property during the trip.
(b) This section does not cover liability arising from the use of motor vehicles, boats or aircraft.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay under this section is $2,000,000 for all claims arising from one event.

Article 52. Automatic renewal
(a) Unless the Insured Person tells the Insurer otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Insurer holds.
(b) The Insured Person can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Insurer's helpline.

Article 53. Records and evidence
(a) The Insured Person should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
(b) Where proof of value is missing, the Insurer may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
(c) The Insurer may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

Article 54. Arbitration
(a) If the Insurer accepts a claim but disagree with the Insured Person about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
(b) Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against the Insurer.

Article 55. Claims documents
(a) The Insured Person must provide, at the Insured Person's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Insurer reasonably ask for.
(b) The Insurer may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

Article 56. Governing law
(a) This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
(b) Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

Article 57. Currency
(a) All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
(b) Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

Article 58. Emergency assistance
(a) The Insurer's emergency assistance service is available 24 hours a day on the number shown in the schedule.
(b) The Insured Person must contact the assistance service before being admitted to hospital as an in-patient, unless it is an emergency.
(c) The assistance service can arrange payment guarantees, interpreters and transport home.

Article 59. Sanctions
(a) The Insurer will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Insurer to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

Article 60. Instalment agreements
(a) If the Insured Person pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
(b) Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

# Household Contents Cover: Policy Booklet
Issued by Lantern General Insurance

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
- **1.2** Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
- **1.3** Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
- **1.4** Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
- **1.5** Contents means household goods and personal possessions that belong to you or your family.
- **1.6** Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
- **1.7** Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
- **1.8** Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
- **1.9** High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
- **1.10** Home means the private residence at the address shown in the schedule.
- **1.11** Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
- **1.12** Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
- **1.13** Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.
- **1.14** Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
- **1.15** Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
- **1.16** Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
- **1.17** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.18** Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
- **1.19** Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
- **1.20** Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
- **1.21** Unoccupied means not lived in by you or a member of your family for more than 60 consecutive days.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Theft: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
- **2.2** Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
- **2.3** Accidental Damage: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.4** Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
- **2.5** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Flood
- **3.1** We will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering your home.
- **3.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for your area had been issued before the policy started.

## 4. Theft
- **4.1** We will pay for contents stolen from your home.
- **4.2** The most we will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,500 per incident.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Bicycles under this section is $800 per incident.
- **4.4** We will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
- **4.5** We will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
- **4.6** We will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

## 5. Escape of Water
- **5.1** We will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
- **5.2** The most we will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.
- **5.3** We will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
- **5.4** We will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

- **6.1** We will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to your contents inside the home.
- **6.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **6.3** The most we will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $750 per incident.
- **6.4** We will not pay for damage caused by pets.
- **6.5** We will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

- **7.1** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
- **7.2** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

- **7.4** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

- **9.1** We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
- **9.2** We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

- **10.1** If the keys to your home are lost or stolen, we will pay the cost of replacing the locks to the outside doors.
- **10.2** The most we will pay under this clause is $300 for any one claim.

- **11.1** We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

## 12. Automatic renewal
- **12.1** Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
- **12.2** You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

## 13. How to read this document
- **13.1** This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
- **13.2** Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
- **13.3** Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

- **15.1** To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.

- **16.1** We will pay for plants, trees and shrubs in the garden of the home that are damaged by fire, lightning or theft.

- **17.1** The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
- **17.2** If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

- **18.1** Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.

6.1 We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
