CASE PRESENTATION A
# Group Health Cash Plan
Issued by the Staff Welfare Fund

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
- **1.2** Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
- **1.3** Dependant means your spouse or partner, or a child under 21 who is enrolled in the plan.
- **1.4** Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
- **1.5** Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
- **1.6** Hearing aid replacement period means 24 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
- **1.7** Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
- **1.8** Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one treatment.
- **1.9** Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
- **1.10** Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
- **1.11** Network provider means a practitioner or clinic that has an agreement with us to provide treatment.
- **1.12** Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
- **1.13** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.14** Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
- **1.15** Registered practitioner means a practitioner registered with the professional body for their discipline.
- **1.16** Replacement period means 24 months from the date of your last eyewear claim.

## 2. Limits and deductible
- **2.1** Dental Care: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
- **2.2** Vision Care: limit $500 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
- **2.3** Therapy Services: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
- **2.4** Hearing Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
- **2.5** The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Customer support
- **3.1** Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
- **3.2** Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

## 4. Cancellation
- **4.1** You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
- **4.2** After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
- **4.3** We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

## 5. Salvage
- **5.1** When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
- **5.2** If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

## 6. Market conditions
- **6.1** If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

## 7. Discounts
- **7.1** Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
- **7.2** If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

## 8. Premium payment
- **8.1** You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
- **8.2** If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

## 9. Appeals
- **9.1** If we decline all or part of a claim, you may appeal in writing within 60 days of the decision.
- **9.2** An appeal will be reviewed by someone who was not involved in the original decision.
- **9.3** We will give you a written decision on the appeal within 30 days.

## 10. Arbitration
- **10.1** If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
- **10.2** Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

## 11. Subrogation
- **11.1** We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
- **11.2** We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

## 12. Joint policyholders
- **12.1** Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
- **12.2** A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

## 13. Third-party administrators
- **13.1** We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
- **13.2** Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

## 14. Interpretation
- **14.1** Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
- **14.2** Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
- **14.3** Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

## 15. Inflation
- **15.1** We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
- **15.2** Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

## 16. Dental Care
- **16.1** We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
- **16.2** No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
- **16.3** The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.
- **16.4** The most we will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $600 per treatment.
- **16.5** We will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
- **16.6** We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

## 17. Data protection
- **17.1** We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
- **17.2** We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
- **17.3** You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

## 18. Wellness allowance
- **18.1** Each plan year you may claim up to $100 towards a gym membership or fitness class.
- **18.2** The wellness allowance is not subject to any deductible and does not count towards other limits.

## 19. Taxes
- **19.1** The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
- **19.2** If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

## 20. Sanctions
- **20.1** We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

## 21. Complaints
- **21.1** If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
- **21.2** We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
- **21.3** If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

## 22. Eligibility
- **22.1** Employees who work at least 20 hours a week are eligible to join the plan from their first day of employment.
- **22.2** Contractors, agency workers and employees on unpaid leave of more than three months are not eligible.

## 23. Instalment agreements
- **23.1** If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
- **23.2** Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

## 24. Environmental commitment
- **24.1** Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
- **24.2** You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

## 25. Assignment
- **25.1** You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

## 26. Leaving the plan
- **26.1** Cover ends on the day your employment ends or the day you stop being eligible, whichever is earlier.
- **26.2** Claims for treatment received before cover ended may be submitted up to 90 days afterwards.

## 27. Exchange of information
- **27.1** To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
- **27.2** We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

## 28. Notices
- **28.1** Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
- **28.2** Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

## 29. Cooperation
- **29.1** You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
- **29.2** You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

## 30. Electronic documents
- **30.1** We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
- **30.2** You must tell us if your email address changes.
- **30.3** Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

## 31. Duty of fair presentation
- **31.1** You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
- **31.2** If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
- **31.3** If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

## 32. Other insurance
- **32.1** If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
- **32.2** You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

## 33. Geographical limits
- **33.1** Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
- **33.2** Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

## 34. Communication
- **34.1** We will communicate with you in English.
- **34.2** We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

## 35. Currency
- **35.1** All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
- **35.2** Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

## 36. Coordination of benefits
- **36.1** If a treatment is also covered by another plan, we will pay only the part of the cost that the other plan does not pay.
- **36.2** You must tell us about any other plan that covers you or your dependants.

## 37. Dependants
- **37.1** You may enrol dependants at the start of each plan year or within 30 days of a qualifying life event.
- **37.2** Benefits paid for dependants count towards the same annual limits as your own claims.

## 38. Claims documents
- **38.1** You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
- **38.2** We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

## 39. Records and evidence
- **39.1** You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
- **39.2** Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
- **39.3** We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

## 40. Optional cover: Hearing Care
- **40.1** We will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
- **40.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **40.3** The most we will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $150 per treatment.
- **40.4** We will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

## 41. Governing law
- **41.1** This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
- **41.2** Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

## 42. Interest
- **42.1** We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

## 43. Compensation scheme
- **43.1** We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
- **43.2** If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

## 44. Renewal
- **44.1** We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
- **44.2** We are not obliged to offer renewal.

## 45. Vision Care
- **45.1** We will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
- **45.2** The most we will pay for Frames under this section is $120 per treatment.
- **45.3** We will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
- **45.4** We will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

## 46. Recovery of costs
- **46.1** If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

## 47. Therapy Services
- **47.1** We will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
- **47.2** The most we will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $200 per treatment.
- **47.3** We will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
- **47.4** We will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

## 48. How to read this document
- **48.1** This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
- **48.2** Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
- **48.3** Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

## 49. General exclusions
- **49.1** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
- **49.2** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
- **49.3** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
- **49.4** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
- **49.5** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

## 50. Payment of claims
- **50.1** We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
- **50.2** We aim to pay accepted claims within 10 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

## 51. Changes in circumstances
- **51.1** You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
- **51.2** We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

## 52. Reasonable precautions
- **52.1** You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
- **52.2** You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

## 53. Severability
- **53.1** If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

## 54. Making a claim
- **54.1** You must notify us of a claim within 14 days of the treatment. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **54.2** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **54.3** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

CASE PRESENTATION A
# Household Contents Cover: Policy Booklet
Issued by Lantern General Insurance

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
- **1.2** Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
- **1.3** Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
- **1.4** Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
- **1.5** Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
- **1.6** Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
- **1.7** Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
- **1.8** High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
- **1.9** Home means the private residence at the address shown in the schedule.
- **1.10** Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
- **1.11** Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.
- **1.12** Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
- **1.13** Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
- **1.14** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.15** Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
- **1.16** Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
- **1.17** Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
- **1.18** Unoccupied means not lived in by you or a member of your family for more than 30 consecutive days.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.2** Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
- **2.3** Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.4** Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
- **2.5** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Theft
- **3.1** We will pay for contents stolen from your home.
- **3.2** The most we will pay for High-risk items under this section is $2,500 per incident.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Bicycles under this section is $800 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
- **3.5** We will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
- **3.6** We will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

## 4. Flood
- **4.1** We will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering your home.
- **4.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
- **4.4** We will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for your area had been issued before the policy started.

## 5. Optional cover: Accidental Damage
- **5.1** We will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to your contents inside the home.
- **5.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **5.3** The most we will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $500 per incident.
- **5.4** We will not pay for damage caused by pets.
- **5.5** We will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

## 6. Escape of Water
- **6.1** We will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
- **6.2** The most we will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.
- **6.3** We will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
- **6.4** We will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

## 7. General exclusions
- **7.1** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
- **7.2** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **7.3** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
- **7.4** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
- **7.5** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
- **7.6** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.

## 8. Making a claim
- **8.1** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **8.2** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **8.3** You must notify us of a claim within 90 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

## 9. Records and evidence
- **9.1** You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
- **9.2** Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
- **9.3** We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

## 10. Notices
- **10.1** Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
- **10.2** Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

## 11. Geographical limits
- **11.1** Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
- **11.2** Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

## 12. Freezer contents
- **12.1** We will pay for food in a domestic freezer that spoils because of a rise or fall in temperature.
- **12.2** We will not pay if the freezer is more than fifteen years old, or if the electricity supplier cut the supply deliberately.

## 13. Premium payment
- **13.1** You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
- **13.2** If an instalment is not paid within 21 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

## 14. Tenant's improvements
- **14.1** If you rent the home, we will pay for damage to fixtures and fittings that you installed and are responsible for.
- **14.2** This cover applies only to improvements you paid for, not to items provided by the landlord.

## 15. Environmental commitment
- **15.1** Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
- **15.2** You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

## 16. Complaints
- **16.1** If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
- **16.2** We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
- **16.3** If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

## 17. Waiver
- **17.1** If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

## 18. Governing law
- **18.1** This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
- **18.2** Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

## 19. Subrogation
- **19.1** We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
- **19.2** We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

## 20. Garden and outdoor cover
- **20.1** We will pay for plants, trees and shrubs in the garden of the home that are damaged by fire, lightning or theft.
- **20.2** We will not pay for damage caused by frost, storms, drought or animals.

## 21. Inflation
- **21.1** We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
- **21.2** Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

## 22. Currency
- **22.1** All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
- **22.2** Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

## 23. Joint policyholders
- **23.1** Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
- **23.2** A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

## 24. Interest
- **24.1** We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

## 25. Reasonable precautions
- **25.1** You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
- **25.2** You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

## 26. Other insurance
- **26.1** If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
- **26.2** You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

## 27. Communication
- **27.1** We will communicate with you in English.
- **27.2** We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

## 28. Payment of claims
- **28.1** We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
- **28.2** We aim to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

## 29. Discounts
- **29.1** Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
- **29.2** If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

## 30. Fraud
- **30.1** If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
- **30.2** We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

## 31. Compensation scheme
- **31.1** We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
- **31.2** If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

## 32. Renewal
- **32.1** We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
- **32.2** We are not obliged to offer renewal.

## 33. Taxes
- **33.1** The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
- **33.2** If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

## 34. Assignment
- **34.1** You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

## 35. Cancellation
- **35.1** You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
- **35.2** After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
- **35.3** We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

## 36. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
- **36.1** A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

## 37. Market conditions
- **37.1** If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

## 38. Exchange of information
- **38.1** To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
- **38.2** We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

## 39. Automatic renewal
- **39.1** Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
- **39.2** You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

## 40. Data protection
- **40.1** We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
- **40.2** We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
- **40.3** You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

## 41. Customer support
- **41.1** Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
- **41.2** Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

## 42. Sanctions
- **42.1** We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

## 43. Third-party administrators
- **43.1** We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
- **43.2** Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

## 44. Contents temporarily removed
- **44.1** Your contents are covered while temporarily removed from the home to another building in the same country, for up to 60 days.
- **44.2** Contents in a student hall of residence are covered only if the student is a member of your family.

## 45. Salvage
- **45.1** When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
- **45.2** If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

## 46. Electronic documents
- **46.1** We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
- **46.2** You must tell us if your email address changes.
- **46.3** Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

## 47. Changes in circumstances
- **47.1** You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
- **47.2** We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

## 48. Instalment agreements
- **48.1** If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
- **48.2** Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

## 49. Alternative accommodation
- **49.1** If your home cannot be lived in after damage covered by this policy, we will pay the reasonable cost of comparable temporary accommodation.
- **49.2** We will also pay for the temporary housing of pets that live with you.
- **49.3** Cover ends when the home is fit to live in again or after twelve months, whichever is sooner.

## 50. Locks and keys
- **50.1** If the keys to your home are lost or stolen, we will pay the cost of replacing the locks to the outside doors.
- **50.2** The most we will pay under this clause is $500 for any one claim.

## 51. Accessibility
- **51.1** This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

## 52. Change of address
- **52.1** You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
- **52.2** We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

## 53. Cooperation
- **53.1** You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
- **53.2** You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

## 54. Severability
- **54.1** If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

## 55. Recovery of costs
- **55.1** If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

## 56. Duty of fair presentation
- **56.1** You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
- **56.2** If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
- **56.3** If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

## 57. Interpretation
- **57.1** Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
- **57.2** Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
- **57.3** Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

## 58. Arbitration
- **58.1** If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
- **58.2** Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

# Single-Trip Travel Protection Plan
Issued by Meridian Travel Insurance Ltd

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
- **1.2** Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
- **1.3** Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
- **1.4** Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
- **1.5** Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
- **1.6** Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,500 metres.
- **1.7** Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
- **1.8** Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
- **1.9** Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
- **1.10** Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
- **1.11** Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which you received treatment or advice in the 3 months before the policy start date.
- **1.12** Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
- **1.13** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.14** Public transport means any scheduled train, bus, coach, ferry or aircraft.
- **1.15** Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 8 hours.
- **1.16** Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
- **1.17** Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
- **1.18** Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
- **1.19** Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
- **1.20** Territory means the countries in which cover applies, as shown in the schedule.
- **1.21** Travelling companion means a person who has booked to travel with you on the same trip.
- **1.22** Trip means a journey that starts and ends in your home country during the policy period.
- **1.23** Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $75 per claim.
- **2.2** Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $50,000 per incident; excess $150 per claim.
- **2.3** Trip Cancellation: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Travel Delay: limit $300 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
- **2.5** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Trip Cancellation
- **3.1** We will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if you must cancel the trip for a reason beyond your control.
- **3.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 10 days after the policy start date.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $200 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before you bought the policy.
- **3.5** We will not pay for cancellation because you no longer wish to travel.

## 4. Customer support
- **4.1** Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
- **4.2** Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

## 5. Emergency Medical Expenses
- **5.1** We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
- **5.2** The most we will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $400 per incident.
- **5.3** The most we will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $300 per incident.
- **5.4** We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
- **5.5** We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
- **5.6** We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

## 6. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
- **6.1** A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

## 7. Repatriation
- **7.1** If our medical adviser agrees it is necessary, we will arrange and pay for you to be brought home.
- **7.2** We will decide the method of transport and the time of repatriation after speaking to the treating doctor.

## 8. Optional cover: Travel Delay
- **8.1** We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
- **8.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **8.3** We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

## 9. Discounts
- **9.1** Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
- **9.2** If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

## 10. Environmental commitment

- **11.3** If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

- **12.2** The most we will pay for Valuables under this section is $500 per incident.
- **12.3** The most we will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $300 per incident.
- **12.4** We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
- **12.5** We will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
- **12.6** We will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

## 13. General exclusions
- **13.1** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

## 15. Instalment agreements
- **15.1** If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
- **15.2** Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

## 16. Claims documents
- **16.1** You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
- **16.2** We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

## 17. Third-party administrators

- **17.2** Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

PART I: Definitions

GROUP HEALTH CASH PLAN
Issued by the Benefits Trust
In this policy, "the Plan" means the Benefits Trust and "the Member" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Plan, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
(b) Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
(c) Dependant means the Member's spouse or partner, or a child under 21 who is enrolled in the plan.
(d) Family means the Member's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Member.
(e) Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
(f) Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
(g) Hearing aid replacement period means 36 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
(h) Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
(i) Limit means the most the Plan will pay for all claims under a section arising from one treatment.
(j) Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
(k) Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
(l) Network provider means a practitioner or clinic that has an agreement with the Plan to provide treatment.
(m) Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
(n) Premium means the amount the Member must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
(o) Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
(p) Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
(q) Replacement period means 12 months from the date of the Member's last eyewear claim.
(r) Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

Article 2. Limits and deductible
(a) Dental Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
(b) Vision Care: limit $300 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
(c) Therapy Services: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
(d) Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
(e) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Vision Care
(a) The Plan will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
(b) The most the Plan will pay for Frames under this section is $120 per treatment.
(c) The Plan will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
(d) The Plan will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

Article 4. Optional cover: Hearing Care
(a) The Plan will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Member's schedule.
(c) The most the Plan will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $100 per treatment.
(d) The Plan will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

Article 5. Dental Care
(a) The Plan will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Plan will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $750 per treatment.
(d) The most the Plan will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $600 per treatment.
(e) The Plan will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
(f) The Plan will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

Article 6. Therapy Services
(a) The Plan will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
(b) The most the Plan will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $300 per treatment.
(c) The Plan will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
(d) The Plan will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

Article 7. General exclusions
(a) The Plan will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
(b) The Plan will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
(c) The Plan will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
(d) The Plan will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Member.
(e) The Plan will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Plan from paying.

Article 8. Making a claim
(a) The Plan may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(b) The Member must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(c) The Member must notify the Plan of a claim within 90 days of the treatment. The Plan will not pay any claim notified after that time.

Article 9. Customer support
(a) The Plan's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
(b) Outside these hours the Member can leave a message and the Plan will call back on the next working day.

Article 10. Third-party administrators
(a) The Plan may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Plan's behalf.
(b) Any company the Plan appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

Article 11. Governing law
(a) This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
(b) Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

Article 12. Geographical limits
(a) Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
(b) Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

Article 13. Taxes
(a) The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
(b) If the tax rate changes, the Plan may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

Article 14. Discounts
(a) Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
(b) If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Plan may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

Article 15. Dependants
(a) The Member may enrol dependants at the start of each plan year or within 30 days of a qualifying life event.
(b) Benefits paid for dependants count towards the same annual limits as the Member's own claims.

Article 16. Interpretation
(a) Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
(b) Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
(c) Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

Article 17. Instalment agreements
(a) If the Member pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
(b) Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

Article 18. Premium payment
(a) The Member must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
(b) If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, the Plan may cancel the policy after giving notice.

Article 19. Cooperation
(a) The Member must give the Plan all the help and information the Plan reasonably need to settle a claim.
(b) The Member must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Plan's written permission.

Article 20. Fraud
(a) If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Plan will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
(b) The Plan may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

Article 21. Renewal
(a) The Plan will write to the Member at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
(b) The Plan is not obliged to offer renewal.

Article 22. Changes in circumstances
(a) The Member must tell the Plan as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
(b) The Plan may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

Article 23. Cancellation
(a) The Member can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
(b) After the first 14 days the Member can cancel at any time; the Plan will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $30.
(c) The Plan can cancel this policy by giving the Member 30 days' written notice to the last address the Plan holds.

Article 24. How to read this document
(a) This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
(b) Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
(c) Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

Article 25. Automatic renewal
(a) Unless the Member tells the Plan otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Plan holds.
(b) The Member can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Plan's helpline.

Article 26. Wellness allowance
(a) Each plan year the Member may claim up to $250 towards a gym membership or fitness class.
(b) The wellness allowance is not subject to any deductible and does not count towards other limits.

Article 27. Subrogation
(a) The Plan will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Member's name the defence or settlement of any claim.
(b) The Plan can take action in the Member's name to recover any payment the Plan makes from anyone responsible for the loss.

Article 28. Coordination of benefits
(a) If a treatment is also covered by another plan, the Plan will pay only the part of the cost that the other plan does not pay.
(b) The Member must tell the Plan about any other plan that covers the Member or the Member's dependants.

Article 29. Accessibility
(a) This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

Article 30. Market conditions
(a) If the replacement item is no longer available, the Plan will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

Article 31. Sanctions
(a) The Plan will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Plan to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

Article 32. Claims documents
(a) The Member must provide, at the Member's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Plan reasonably ask for.
(b) The Plan may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

Article 33. Data protection
(a) The Plan will use the personal information the Member provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
(b) The Plan will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
(c) The Member can ask for a copy of the personal information the Plan holds by writing to the Plan's data protection officer.

Article 34. Reasonable precautions
(a) The Member must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
(b) The Member must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

RENTERS CONTENTS PROTECTION
Issued by Lantern General Insurance
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Lantern General Insurance and "the Policyholder" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
(b) Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Insurer, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
(c) Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
(d) Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
(e) Contents means household goods and personal possessions that belong to the Policyholder or the Policyholder's family.
(f) Family means the Policyholder's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Policyholder.
(g) Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
(h) Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
(i) High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
(j) Home means the private residence at the address shown in the schedule.
(k) Limit means the most the Insurer will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
(l) Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.
(m) Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
(n) Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Policyholder's details, the covers the Policyholder bought and any extensions.
(o) Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
(p) Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 60 consecutive days.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Theft: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
(b) Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(c) Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(d) Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
(e) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Theft
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $800 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

Article 4. Flood
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

Article 5. Optional cover: Accidental Damage
(a) The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $750 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

Article 6. Escape of Water
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $2,000 per incident.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

Article 7. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

Article 8. Making a claim
(a) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(b) The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(c) The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 21 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

Article 9. Automatic renewal
(a) Unless the Policyholder tells the Insurer otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Insurer holds.
(b) The Policyholder can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Insurer's helpline.

Article 10. Subrogation
(a) The Insurer will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Policyholder's name the defence or settlement of any claim.
(b) The Insurer can take action in the Policyholder's name to recover any payment the Insurer makes from anyone responsible for the loss.

Article 11. Customer support
(a) The Insurer's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
(b) Outside these hours the Policyholder can leave a message and the Insurer will call back on the next working day.

Article 12. Interpretation
(a) Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
(b) Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
(c) Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

Article 13. Severability
(a) If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

Article 14. Data protection
(a) The Insurer will use the personal information the Policyholder provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
(b) The Insurer will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
(c) The Policyholder can ask for a copy of the personal information the Insurer holds by writing to the Insurer's data protection officer.

Article 15. How to read this document
(a) This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
(b) Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
(c) Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

Article 16. Other insurance
(a) If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Insurer will pay only the Insurer's proportionate share.
(b) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Policyholder makes a claim.

Article 17. Interest
(a) The Insurer will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

Article 18. Payment of claims
(a) The Insurer will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Policyholder's name.
(b) The Insurer aims to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents the Insurer needs.

Article 19. Compensation scheme
(a) The Insurer is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
(b) If the Insurer cannot meet the Insurer's obligations, the Policyholder may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

Article 20. Cooperation
(a) The Policyholder must give the Insurer all the help and information the Insurer reasonably need to settle a claim.
(b) The Policyholder must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Insurer's written permission.

Article 21. Claims documents
(a) The Policyholder must provide, at the Policyholder's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Insurer reasonably ask for.
(b) The Insurer may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

Article 22. Electronic documents
(a) The Insurer will send documents by email unless the Policyholder asks for paper copies.
(b) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer if the Policyholder's email address changes.
(c) Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

Article 23. Freezer contents
(a) The Insurer will pay for food in a domestic freezer that spoils because of a rise or fall in temperature.
(b) The Insurer will not pay if the freezer is more than fifteen years old, or if the electricity supplier cut the supply deliberately.

Article 24. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
(a) A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

Article 25. Premium payment
(a) The Policyholder must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
(b) If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, the Insurer may cancel the policy after giving notice.

Article 26. Change of address
(a) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer within 30 days if the Policyholder changes the Policyholder's address.
(b) The Insurer may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

Article 27. Complaints
(a) If the Policyholder has a complaint, the Policyholder should first contact the Insurer's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
(b) The Insurer will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
(c) If the Policyholder remains dissatisfied, the Policyholder may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

Article 28. Inflation
(a) The Insurer may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
(b) Any adjustment will be shown in the Policyholder's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

Article 29. Alternative accommodation
(a) If the Policyholder's home cannot be lived in after damage covered by this policy, the Insurer will pay the reasonable cost of comparable temporary accommodation.
(b) The Insurer will also pay for the temporary housing of pets that live with the Policyholder.
(c) Cover ends when the home is fit to live in again or after twelve months, whichever is sooner.

Article 30. Sanctions
(a) The Insurer will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Insurer to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

Article 31. Currency
(a) All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
(b) Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

Article 32. Reasonable precautions
(a) The Policyholder must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
(b) The Policyholder must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

Article 33. Governing law
(a) This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
(b) Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

Article 34. Environmental commitment
(a) Where practical, the Insurer will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
(b) The Policyholder may ask for a new part instead, and the Insurer will tell the Policyholder whether any additional cost would apply.

Article 35. Cancellation
(a) The Policyholder can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
(b) After the first 14 days the Policyholder can cancel at any time; the Insurer will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
(c) The Insurer can cancel this policy by giving the Policyholder 30 days' written notice to the last address the Insurer holds.

Article 36. Arbitration
(a) If the Insurer accepts a claim but disagree with the Policyholder about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
(b) Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against the Insurer.

Article 37. Exchange of information
(a) To prevent fraud, the Insurer may check the details the Policyholder gives against public records and industry databases.
(b) The Insurer may contact previous insurers to confirm the Policyholder's claims history.

Article 38. Taxes
(a) The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
(b) If the tax rate changes, the Insurer may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

Article 39. Assignment
(a) The Policyholder cannot transfer the Policyholder's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Insurer's written consent.

Article 40. Market conditions
(a) If the replacement item is no longer available, the Insurer will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

Article 41. Salvage
(a) When the Insurer replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Insurer's property.
(b) If stolen property is recovered after the Insurer has paid a claim, the Policyholder must tell the Insurer and either return the payment or give the Insurer the property.

Article 42. Garden and outdoor cover
(a) The Insurer will pay for plants, trees and shrubs in the garden of the home that are damaged by fire, lightning or theft.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by frost, storms, drought or animals.

Article 43. Recovery of costs
(a) If the Insurer pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Insurer may ask the Policyholder to repay the amount.

Article 44. Changes in circumstances
(a) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
(b) The Insurer may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

Article 45. Instalment agreements
(a) If the Policyholder pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
(b) Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

Article 46. Tenant's improvements
(a) If the Policyholder rents the home, the Insurer will pay for damage to fixtures and fittings that the Policyholder installed and are responsible for.
(b) This cover applies only to improvements the Policyholder paid for, not to items provided by the landlord.

Article 47. Discounts
(a) Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
(b) If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Insurer may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

# Group Health Cash Plan
Issued by the Benefits Trust

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
- **1.2** Hearing aid replacement period means 24 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
- **1.3** Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
- **1.4** Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
- **1.5** Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
- **1.6** Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.

## 2. Limits and deductible
- **2.1** Dental Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
- **2.2** Vision Care: limit $300 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
- **2.3** Therapy Services: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Hearing Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
- **2.5** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Inflation
- **3.1** We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
- **3.2** Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

## 4. Dental Care
- **4.1** We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
- **4.2** No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 90 days after the policy start date.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.
- **4.4** The most we will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $800 per treatment.
- **4.5** We will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
- **4.6** We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

## 5. Geographical limits
- **5.1** Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
- **5.2** Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

## 6. Leaving the plan
- **6.1** Cover ends on the day your employment ends or the day you stop being eligible, whichever is earlier.
- **6.2** Claims for treatment received before cover ended may be submitted up to 90 days afterwards.

## 7. Customer support
- **7.1** Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
- **7.2** Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

## 8. Renewal
- **8.1** We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
- **8.2** We are not obliged to offer renewal.

## 9. Appeals
- **9.1** If we decline all or part of a claim, you may appeal in writing within 60 days of the decision.
- **9.2** An appeal will be reviewed by someone who was not involved in the original decision.
- **9.3** We will give you a written decision on the appeal within 30 days.

## 10. Payment of claims
- **10.1** We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
- **10.2** We aim to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

## 11. Complaints
- **11.1** If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
- **11.2** We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
- **11.3** If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

## 12. Environmental commitment
- **12.1** Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
- **12.2** You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

## 13. Eligibility
- **13.1** Employees who work at least 20 hours a week are eligible to join the plan from their first day of employment.
- **13.2** Contractors, agency workers and employees on unpaid leave of more than three months are not eligible.

## 14. Interpretation
- **14.1** Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
- **14.2** Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
- **14.3** Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

## 15. Wellness allowance
- **15.1** Each plan year you may claim up to $100 towards a gym membership or fitness class.
- **15.2** The wellness allowance is not subject to any deductible and does not count towards other limits.

## 16. Compensation scheme
- **16.1** We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
- **16.2** If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

## 17. Dependants
- **17.1** You may enrol dependants at the start of each plan year or within 30 days of a qualifying life event.
- **17.2** Benefits paid for dependants count towards the same annual limits as your own claims.

## 18. Optional cover: Hearing Care
- **18.1** We will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
- **18.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **18.3** The most we will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $100 per treatment.
- **18.4** We will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

## 19. General exclusions
- **19.1** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
- **19.2** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
- **19.3** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

## 20. Electronic documents
- **20.1** We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
- **20.2** You must tell us if your email address changes.
- **20.3** Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

## 21. Coordination of benefits
- **21.1** If a treatment is also covered by another plan, we will pay only the part of the cost that the other plan does not pay.
- **21.2** You must tell us about any other plan that covers you or your dependants.

## 22. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
- **22.1** A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

## 23. Recovery of costs
- **23.1** If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

## 24. Cancellation
- **24.1** You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
- **24.2** After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
- **24.3** We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

## 25. Making a claim
- **25.1** You must notify us of a claim within 30 days of the treatment. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **25.2** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **25.3** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

## 26. Subrogation
- **26.1** We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
- **26.2** We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

## 27. Exchange of information
- **27.1** To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
- **27.2** We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

## 28. Market conditions
- **28.1** If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

## 29. Change of address
- **29.1** You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
- **29.2** We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

## 30. Communication
- **30.1** We will communicate with you in English.
- **30.2** We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

## 31. Fraud
- **31.1** If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
- **31.2** We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

## 32. Taxes
- **32.1** The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
- **32.2** If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.
