CASE PRESENTATION A
# Employee Health Benefits Plan: Summary Plan Description
Issued by Wellspring Benefits Administration

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
- **1.2** Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
- **1.3** Dependant means your spouse or partner, or a child under 21 who is enrolled in the plan.
- **1.4** Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
- **1.5** Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
- **1.6** Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
- **1.7** Hearing aid replacement period means 24 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
- **1.8** Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
- **1.9** Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one treatment.
- **1.10** Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
- **1.11** Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
- **1.12** Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
- **1.13** Plan year means the twelve months starting on your coverage start date.
- **1.14** Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
- **1.15** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.16** Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
- **1.17** Registered practitioner means a practitioner registered with the professional body for their discipline.
- **1.18** Replacement period means 12 months from the date of your last eyewear claim.
- **1.19** Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
- **1.20** Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

## 2. Limits and deductible
- **2.1** Dental Care: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
- **2.2** Vision Care: limit $300 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
- **2.3** Therapy Services: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Hearing Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
- **2.5** The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Vision Care
- **3.1** We will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
- **3.2** The most we will pay for Frames under this section is $150 per treatment.
- **3.3** We will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
- **3.4** We will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

## 4. Dental Care
- **4.1** We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
- **4.2** No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 90 days after the policy start date.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.
- **4.4** The most we will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $600 per treatment.
- **4.5** We will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
- **4.6** We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

## 5. Optional cover: Hearing Care
- **5.1** We will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
- **5.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **5.3** The most we will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $100 per treatment.
- **5.4** We will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

## 6. Therapy Services
- **6.1** We will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
- **6.2** The most we will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $300 per treatment.
- **6.3** We will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
- **6.4** We will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

## 7. General exclusions
- **7.1** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
- **7.2** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
- **7.3** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
- **7.4** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
- **7.5** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
- **7.6** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

## 8. Making a claim
- **8.1** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **8.2** You must notify us of a claim within 21 days of the treatment. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **8.3** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

## 9. Severability
- **9.1** If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

## 10. Other insurance
- **10.1** If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
- **10.2** You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

## 11. Joint policyholders
- **11.1** Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
- **11.2** A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

## 12. Third-party administrators
- **12.1** We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
- **12.2** Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

## 13. Renewal
- **13.1** We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
- **13.2** We are not obliged to offer renewal.

## 14. Interest
- **14.1** We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

## 15. Compensation scheme
- **15.1** We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
- **15.2** If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

## 16. Inflation
- **16.1** We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
- **16.2** Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

## 17. Geographical limits
- **17.1** Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
- **17.2** Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

## 18. Complaints
- **18.1** If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
- **18.2** We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
- **18.3** If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

## 19. Wellness allowance
- **19.1** Each plan year you may claim up to $100 towards a gym membership or fitness class.
- **19.2** The wellness allowance is not subject to any deductible and does not count towards other limits.

## 20. Accessibility
- **20.1** This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

## 21. Records and evidence
- **21.1** You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
- **21.2** Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
- **21.3** We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

## 22. Currency
- **22.1** All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
- **22.2** Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

## 23. Change of address
- **23.1** You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
- **23.2** We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

## 24. Sanctions
- **24.1** We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

## 25. Discounts
- **25.1** Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
- **25.2** If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

## 26. Instalment agreements
- **26.1** If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
- **26.2** Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

## 27. Electronic documents
- **27.1** We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
- **27.2** You must tell us if your email address changes.
- **27.3** Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

## 28. Automatic renewal
- **28.1** Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
- **28.2** You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

## 29. Communication
- **29.1** We will communicate with you in English.
- **29.2** We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

## 30. Changes in circumstances
- **30.1** You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
- **30.2** We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

## 31. Notices
- **31.1** Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
- **31.2** Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

## 32. Reasonable precautions
- **32.1** You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
- **32.2** You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

## 33. Payment of claims
- **33.1** We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
- **33.2** We aim to pay accepted claims within 10 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

## 34. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
- **34.1** A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

## 35. Assignment
- **35.1** You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

## 36. Exchange of information
- **36.1** To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
- **36.2** We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

## 37. Arbitration
- **37.1** If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
- **37.2** Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

## 38. Salvage
- **38.1** When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
- **38.2** If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

## 39. Data protection
- **39.1** We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
- **39.2** We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
- **39.3** You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

## 40. Cooperation
- **40.1** You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
- **40.2** You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

## 41. How to read this document
- **41.1** This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
- **41.2** Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
- **41.3** Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

## 42. Appeals
- **42.1** If we decline all or part of a claim, you may appeal in writing within 60 days of the decision.
- **42.2** An appeal will be reviewed by someone who was not involved in the original decision.
- **42.3** We will give you a written decision on the appeal within 30 days.

## 43. Recovery of costs
- **43.1** If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

## 44. Market conditions
- **44.1** If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

## 45. Leaving the plan
- **45.1** Cover ends on the day your employment ends or the day you stop being eligible, whichever is earlier.
- **45.2** Claims for treatment received before cover ended may be submitted up to 90 days afterwards.

## 46. Claims documents
- **46.1** You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
- **46.2** We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

## 47. Coordination of benefits
- **47.1** If a treatment is also covered by another plan, we will pay only the part of the cost that the other plan does not pay.
- **47.2** You must tell us about any other plan that covers you or your dependants.

## 48. Eligibility
- **48.1** Employees who work at least 20 hours a week are eligible to join the plan from their first day of employment.
- **48.2** Contractors, agency workers and employees on unpaid leave of more than three months are not eligible.

## 49. Governing law
- **49.1** This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
- **49.2** Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

## 50. Fraud
- **50.1** If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
- **50.2** We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

## 51. Duty of fair presentation
- **51.1** You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
- **51.2** If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
- **51.3** If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

## 52. Taxes
- **52.1** The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
- **52.2** If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

TRAVEL INSURANCE POLICY WORDING
Issued by Bluewater Assurance
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Bluewater Assurance and "the Insured Person" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Insurer, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
(b) Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
(c) Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
(d) Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
(e) Family means the Insured Person's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Insured Person.
(f) Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,500 metres.
(g) Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
(h) Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which the Insured Person received treatment or advice in the 3 months before the policy start date.
(i) Premium means the amount the Insured Person must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
(j) Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
(k) Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 6 hours.
(l) Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
(m) Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Insured Person's details, the covers the Insured Person bought and any extensions.
(n) Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
(o) Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
(p) Travelling companion means a person who has booked to travel with the Insured Person on the same trip.
(q) Trip means a journey that starts and ends in the Insured Person's home country during the policy period.
(r) Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(b) Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
(c) Trip Cancellation: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(d) Travel Delay: limit $500 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
(e) The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

Article 3. Baggage and Personal Belongings
(a) The Insurer will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to the Insured Person's baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Valuables under this section is $400 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $300 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

Article 4. Trip Cancellation
(a) The Insurer will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if the Insured Person must cancel the trip for a reason beyond the Insured Person's control.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 14 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $300 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before the Insured Person bought the policy.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation because the Insured Person no longer wish to travel.

Article 5. Severability
(a) If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

Article 6. Recovery of costs
(a) If the Insurer pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Insurer may ask the Insured Person to repay the amount.

Article 7. Other insurance
(a) If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Insurer will pay only the Insurer's proportionate share.
(b) The Insured Person must tell the Insurer about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Insured Person makes a claim.

Article 8. Taxes
(a) The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
(b) If the tax rate changes, the Insurer may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

Article 9. Notices
(a) Any notice the Insurer gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Insurer holds.
(b) Notices from the Insured Person should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

Article 10. Waiver
(a) If the Insurer does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Insurer has given up the right to enforce it later.

Article 11. Joint policyholders
(a) Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
(b) A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

Article 12. Cancellation
(a) The Insured Person can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
(b) After the first 14 days the Insured Person can cancel at any time; the Insurer will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $30.
(c) The Insurer can cancel this policy by giving the Insured Person 30 days' written notice to the last address the Insurer holds.

Article 13. Compensation scheme
(a) The Insurer is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
(b) If the Insurer cannot meet the Insurer's obligations, the Insured Person may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

Article 14. Governing law
(a) This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
(b) Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

Article 15. Complaints
(a) If the Insured Person has a complaint, the Insured Person should first contact the Insurer's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
(b) The Insurer will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
(c) If the Insured Person remains dissatisfied, the Insured Person may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

Article 16. Optional cover: Travel Delay
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if the Insured Person's outbound departure is delayed.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Insured Person's schedule.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

Article 17. Environmental commitment
(a) Where practical, the Insurer will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
(b) The Insured Person may ask for a new part instead, and the Insurer will tell the Insured Person whether any additional cost would apply.

Article 18. Interest
(a) The Insurer will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

Article 19. Emergency Medical Expenses
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $250 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $300 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for any claim arising from the Insured Person's being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

Article 20. Discounts
(a) Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
(b) If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Insurer may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

Article 21. Third-party administrators
(a) The Insurer may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Insurer's behalf.
(b) Any company the Insurer appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

Article 22. How to read this document
(a) This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
(b) Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
(c) Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

Article 23. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Insured Person.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

Article 24. Claims documents
(a) The Insured Person must provide, at the Insured Person's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Insurer reasonably ask for.
(b) The Insurer may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

Article 25. Accessibility
(a) This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

Article 26. Instalment agreements
(a) If the Insured Person pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
(b) Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

Article 27. Reasonable precautions
(a) The Insured Person must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
(b) The Insured Person must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

Article 28. Automatic renewal
(a) Unless the Insured Person tells the Insurer otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Insurer holds.
(b) The Insured Person can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Insurer's helpline.

Article 29. Emergency assistance
(a) The Insurer's emergency assistance service is available 24 hours a day on the number shown in the schedule.
(b) The Insured Person must contact the assistance service before being admitted to hospital as an in-patient, unless it is an emergency.
(c) The assistance service can arrange payment guarantees, interpreters and transport home.

Article 30. Rental car excess
(a) If the Insured Person hires a car during the trip, the Insurer will reimburse any excess the Insured Person must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.
(b) This section applies only to cars hired from a licensed rental company under a written agreement.

Article 31. Making a claim
(a) The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 90 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(b) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(c) The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

Article 32. Legal expenses abroad
(a) The Insurer will pay legal costs to pursue compensation for the Insured Person's injury or death caused by a third party during the trip.
(b) The Insurer will not pay legal costs unless the Insurer's legal adviser agrees that the claim has a reasonable prospect of success.

Article 33. Data protection
(a) The Insurer will use the personal information the Insured Person provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
(b) The Insurer will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
(c) The Insured Person can ask for a copy of the personal information the Insurer holds by writing to the Insurer's data protection officer.

GROUP HEALTH CASH PLAN
Issued by the Benefits Trust
In this policy, "the Plan" means the Benefits Trust and "the Member" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Plan, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
(b) Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
(c) Dependant means the Member's spouse or partner, or a child under 21 who is enrolled in the plan.
(d) Family means the Member's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Member.
(e) Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
(f) Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
(g) Hearing aid replacement period means 36 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
(h) Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
(i) Limit means the most the Plan will pay for all claims under a section arising from one treatment.
(j) Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
(k) Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
(l) Network provider means a practitioner or clinic that has an agreement with the Plan to provide treatment.
(m) Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
(n) Premium means the amount the Member must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
(o) Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
(p) Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
(q) Replacement period means 12 months from the date of the Member's last eyewear claim.
(r) Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

Article 2. Limits and deductible
(a) Dental Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
(b) Vision Care: limit $300 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
(c) Therapy Services: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
(d) Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
(e) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Vision Care
(a) The Plan will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
(b) The most the Plan will pay for Frames under this section is $120 per treatment.
(c) The Plan will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
(d) The Plan will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

Article 4. Optional cover: Hearing Care
(a) The Plan will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Member's schedule.
(c) The most the Plan will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $100 per treatment.
(d) The Plan will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

Article 5. Dental Care
(a) The Plan will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Plan will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $750 per treatment.
(d) The most the Plan will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $600 per treatment.
(e) The Plan will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
(f) The Plan will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

Article 6. Therapy Services
(a) The Plan will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
(b) The most the Plan will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $300 per treatment.
(c) The Plan will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
(d) The Plan will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

Article 7. General exclusions
(a) The Plan will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
(b) The Plan will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
(c) The Plan will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
(d) The Plan will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Member.
(e) The Plan will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Plan from paying.

Article 8. Making a claim
(a) The Plan may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(b) The Member must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(c) The Member must notify the Plan of a claim within 90 days of the treatment. The Plan will not pay any claim notified after that time.

Article 9. Customer support
(a) The Plan's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
(b) Outside these hours the Member can leave a message and the Plan will call back on the next working day.

Article 10. Third-party administrators
(a) The Plan may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Plan's behalf.
(b) Any company the Plan appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

Article 11. Governing law
(a) This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
(b) Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

Article 12. Geographical limits
(a) Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
(b) Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

Article 13. Taxes
(a) The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
(b) If the tax rate changes, the Plan may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

Article 14. Discounts
(a) Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
(b) If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Plan may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

Article 15. Dependants
(a) The Member may enrol dependants at the start of each plan year or within 30 days of a qualifying life event.
(b) Benefits paid for dependants count towards the same annual limits as the Member's own claims.

Article 16. Interpretation
(a) Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
(b) Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
(c) Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

Article 17. Instalment agreements
(a) If the Member pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
(b) Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

Article 18. Premium payment
(a) The Member must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
(b) If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, the Plan may cancel the policy after giving notice.

Article 19. Cooperation
(a) The Member must give the Plan all the help and information the Plan reasonably need to settle a claim.
(b) The Member must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Plan's written permission.

Article 20. Fraud
(a) If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Plan will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
(b) The Plan may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

Article 21. Renewal
(a) The Plan will write to the Member at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
(b) The Plan is not obliged to offer renewal.

Article 22. Changes in circumstances
(a) The Member must tell the Plan as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
(b) The Plan may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

Article 23. Cancellation
(a) The Member can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
(b) After the first 14 days the Member can cancel at any time; the Plan will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $30.
(c) The Plan can cancel this policy by giving the Member 30 days' written notice to the last address the Plan holds.

Article 24. How to read this document
(a) This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
(b) Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
(c) Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

Article 25. Automatic renewal
(a) Unless the Member tells the Plan otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Plan holds.
(b) The Member can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Plan's helpline.

Article 26. Wellness allowance
(a) Each plan year the Member may claim up to $250 towards a gym membership or fitness class.
(b) The wellness allowance is not subject to any deductible and does not count towards other limits.

Article 27. Subrogation
(a) The Plan will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Member's name the defence or settlement of any claim.
(b) The Plan can take action in the Member's name to recover any payment the Plan makes from anyone responsible for the loss.

Article 28. Coordination of benefits
(a) If a treatment is also covered by another plan, the Plan will pay only the part of the cost that the other plan does not pay.
(b) The Member must tell the Plan about any other plan that covers the Member or the Member's dependants.

Article 29. Accessibility
(a) This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

Article 30. Market conditions
(a) If the replacement item is no longer available, the Plan will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

Article 31. Sanctions
(a) The Plan will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Plan to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

Article 32. Claims documents
(a) The Member must provide, at the Member's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Plan reasonably ask for.
(b) The Plan may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

Article 33. Data protection
(a) The Plan will use the personal information the Member provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
(b) The Plan will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
(c) The Member can ask for a copy of the personal information the Plan holds by writing to the Plan's data protection officer.

Article 34. Reasonable precautions
(a) The Member must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
(b) The Member must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

EMPLOYEE HEALTH BENEFITS PLAN: SUMMARY PLAN DESCRIPTION
Issued by Wellspring Benefits Administration

SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS
1.1 Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
1.2 Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
1.3 Dependant means your spouse or partner, or a child under 21 who is enrolled in the plan.
1.4 Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
1.5 Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
1.6 Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
1.7 Hearing aid replacement period means 36 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
1.8 Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
1.9 Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one treatment.
1.10 Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
1.11 Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
1.12 Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
1.13 Plan year means the twelve months starting on your coverage start date.
1.14 Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
1.15 Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
1.16 Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
1.17 Registered practitioner means a practitioner registered with the professional body for their discipline.
1.18 Replacement period means 24 months from the date of your last eyewear claim.
1.19 Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
1.20 Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

SECTION 2 - LIMITS AND DEDUCTIBLE
2.1 Dental Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
2.2 Vision Care: limit $300 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
2.3 Therapy Services: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
2.4 Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
2.5 The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

SECTION 3 - DENTAL CARE
3.1 We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
3.2 No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
3.3 The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.
3.4 The most we will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $800 per treatment.
3.5 We will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
3.6 We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

SECTION 4 - THERAPY SERVICES
4.1 We will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
4.2 The most we will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $300 per treatment.
4.3 We will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
4.4 We will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

SECTION 5 - VISION CARE
5.1 We will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
5.2 The most we will pay for Frames under this section is $150 per treatment.
5.3 We will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
5.4 We will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

SECTION 6 - OPTIONAL COVER: HEARING CARE
6.1 We will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
6.2 This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
6.3 The most we will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $150 per treatment.
6.4 We will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

SECTION 7 - GENERAL EXCLUSIONS
7.1 We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
7.2 We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
7.3 We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
7.4 We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

SECTION 8 - MAKING A CLAIM
8.1 You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
8.2 We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
8.3 You must notify us of a claim within 14 days of the treatment. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

SECTION 9 - TAXES
9.1 The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
9.2 If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

SECTION 10 - THIRD-PARTY ADMINISTRATORS
10.1 We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
10.2 Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

SECTION 11 - JOINT POLICYHOLDERS
11.1 Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
11.2 A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

SECTION 12 - RENEWAL
12.1 We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
12.2 We are not obliged to offer renewal.

SECTION 13 - INSTALMENT AGREEMENTS
13.1 If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
13.2 Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

SECTION 14 - ACCESSIBILITY
14.1 This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

SECTION 15 - OTHER INSURANCE
15.1 If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
15.2 You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

SECTION 16 - COMPLAINTS
16.1 If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
16.2 We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
16.3 If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

SECTION 17 - COORDINATION OF BENEFITS
17.1 If a treatment is also covered by another plan, we will pay only the part of the cost that the other plan does not pay.
17.2 You must tell us about any other plan that covers you or your dependants.

SECTION 18 - SEVERABILITY
18.1 If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

SECTION 19 - RECORDS AND EVIDENCE
19.1 You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
19.2 Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
19.3 We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

SECTION 20 - DISCOUNTS
20.1 Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
20.2 If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

SECTION 21 - CHANGE OF ADDRESS
21.1 You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
21.2 We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

SECTION 22 - WAIVER
22.1 If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

SECTION 23 - INFLATION
23.1 We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
23.2 Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

SECTION 24 - ELECTRONIC DOCUMENTS
24.1 We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
24.2 You must tell us if your email address changes.
24.3 Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

SECTION 25 - CLAIMS DOCUMENTS
25.1 You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
25.2 We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

SECTION 26 - DUTY OF FAIR PRESENTATION
26.1 You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
26.2 If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
26.3 If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

SECTION 27 - HOW TO READ THIS DOCUMENT
27.1 This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
27.2 Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
27.3 Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

SECTION 28 - PAYMENT OF CLAIMS
28.1 We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
28.2 We aim to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

SECTION 29 - RECOVERY OF COSTS
29.1 If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

SECTION 30 - SUBROGATION
30.1 We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
30.2 We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

SECTION 31 - MARKET CONDITIONS
31.1 If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

SECTION 32 - APPEALS
32.1 If we decline all or part of a claim, you may appeal in writing within 60 days of the decision.
32.2 An appeal will be reviewed by someone who was not involved in the original decision.
32.3 We will give you a written decision on the appeal within 30 days.

SECTION 33 - DATA PROTECTION
33.1 We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
33.2 We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
33.3 You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

SECTION 34 - NOTICES
34.1 Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
34.2 Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

SECTION 35 - SANCTIONS
35.1 We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

SECTION 36 - COMPENSATION SCHEME
36.1 We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
36.2 If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

SECTION 37 - ARBITRATION
37.1 If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
37.2 Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

SECTION 38 - SALVAGE
38.1 When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
38.2 If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

SECTION 39 - ENVIRONMENTAL COMMITMENT
39.1 Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
39.2 You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

SECTION 40 - CUSTOMER SUPPORT
40.1 Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
40.2 Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

SECTION 41 - WELLNESS ALLOWANCE
41.1 Each plan year you may claim up to $100 towards a gym membership or fitness class.
41.2 The wellness allowance is not subject to any deductible and does not count towards other limits.

SECTION 42 - GEOGRAPHICAL LIMITS
42.1 Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
42.2 Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

SECTION 43 - CURRENCY
43.1 All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
43.2 Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

SECTION 44 - CANCELLATION
44.1 You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
44.2 After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
44.3 We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

SECTION 45 - REASONABLE PRECAUTIONS
45.1 You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
45.2 You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

SECTION 46 - AUTOMATIC RENEWAL
46.1 Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
46.2 You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

SECTION 47 - INTEREST
47.1 We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

SECTION 48 - GOVERNING LAW
48.1 This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
48.2 Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

SECTION 49 - ELIGIBILITY
49.1 Employees who work at least 20 hours a week are eligible to join the plan from their first day of employment.
49.2 Contractors, agency workers and employees on unpaid leave of more than three months are not eligible.

SECTION 50 - EXCHANGE OF INFORMATION
50.1 To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
50.2 We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

SECTION 51 - ASSIGNMENT
51.1 You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

SECTION 52 - COOPERATION
52.1 You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
52.2 You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

SECTION 53 - LEAVING THE PLAN
53.1 Cover ends on the day your employment ends or the day you stop being eligible, whichever is earlier.
53.2 Claims for treatment received before cover ended may be submitted up to 90 days afterwards.

SECTION 54 - CHANGES IN CIRCUMSTANCES
54.1 You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
54.2 We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

SECTION 55 - FRAUD
55.1 If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
55.2 We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

SECTION 56 - COMMUNICATION
56.1 We will communicate with you in English.
56.2 We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

SECTION 57 - CONTRACTS (RIGHTS OF THIRD PARTIES)
57.1 A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

SECTION 58 - PREMIUM PAYMENT
58.1 You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
58.2 If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

SECTION 59 - DEPENDANTS
59.1 You may enrol dependants at the start of each plan year or within 30 days of a qualifying life event.
59.2 Benefits paid for dependants count towards the same annual limits as your own claims.

SECTION 60 - INTERPRETATION
60.1 Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
60.2 Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.

state.policy:
ANNUAL MULTI-TRIP TRAVEL COVER
Issued by Northstar Underwriting
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Northstar Underwriting and "the Insured Person" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
(b) Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
(c) Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
(d) Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,500 metres.
(e) Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
(f) Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
(g) Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which the Insured Person received treatment or advice in the 6 months before the policy start date.
(h) Premium means the amount the Insured Person must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
(i) Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 6 hours.
(j) Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
(k) Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
(l) Travelling companion means a person who has booked to travel with the Insured Person on the same trip.
(m) Trip means a journey that starts and ends in the Insured Person's home country during the policy period.
(n) Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(b) Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $25,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
(c) Trip Cancellation: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(d) Travel Delay: limit $500 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
(e) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Emergency Medical Expenses
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $250 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $500 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for any claim arising from the Insured Person's being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

Article 4. Trip Cancellation
(a) The Insurer will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if the Insured Person must cancel the trip for a reason beyond the Insured Person's control.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 10 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $200 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before the Insured Person bought the policy.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation because the Insured Person no longer wish to travel.

Article 5. Optional cover: Travel Delay
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if the Insured Person's outbound departure is delayed.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Insured Person's schedule.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

Article 6. Baggage and Personal Belongings
(a) The Insurer will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to the Insured Person's baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Valuables under this section is $500 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $300 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

Article 7. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Insured Person.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

Article 8. Making a claim
(a) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(b) The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 90 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(c) The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

Article 9. Accessibility
(a) This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

Article 10. Recovery of costs
(a) If the Insurer pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Insurer may ask the Insured Person to repay the amount.

Article 11. Market conditions
(a) If the replacement item is no longer available, the Insurer will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

Article 12. Cooperation
(a) The Insured Person must give the Insurer all the help and information the Insurer reasonably need to settle a claim.
(b) The Insured Person must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Insurer's written permission.

Article 13. Interpretation
(a) Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
(b) Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
(c) Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

Article 14. Duty of fair presentation
(a) The Insured Person must answer all questions the Insurer asks honestly and to the best of the Insured Person's knowledge.
(b) If the Insured Person gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Insurer may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
(c) If the Insured Person gives incorrect information carelessly, the Insurer may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

Article 15. Joint policyholders
(a) Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
(b) A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

Article 16. Premium payment
(a) The Insured Person must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
(b) If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, the Insurer may cancel the policy after giving notice.

Article 17. Records and evidence
(a) The Insured Person should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
(b) Where proof of value is missing, the Insurer may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
(c) The Insurer may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

Article 18. Reasonable precautions
(a) The Insured Person must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
(b) The Insured Person must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

Article 19. Cancellation
(a) The Insured Person can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
(b) After the first 14 days the Insured Person can cancel at any time; the Insurer will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
(c) The Insurer can cancel this policy by giving the Insured Person 30 days' written notice to the last address the Insurer holds.

Article 20. Changes in circumstances
(a) The Insured Person must tell the Insurer as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
(b) The Insurer may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

Article 21. Automatic renewal
(a) Unless the Insured Person tells the Insurer otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Insurer holds.
(b) The Insured Person can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Insurer's helpline.

Article 22. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
(a) A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

Article 23. Taxes
(a) The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
(b) If the tax rate changes, the Insurer may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

Article 24. Electronic documents
(a) The Insurer will send documents by email unless the Insured Person asks for paper copies.
(b) The Insured Person must tell the Insurer if the Insured Person's email address changes.
(c) Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

Article 25. Currency
(a) All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
(b) Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

Article 26. Exchange of information
(a) To prevent fraud, the Insurer may check the details the Insured Person gives against public records and industry databases.
(b) The Insurer may contact previous insurers to confirm the Insured Person's claims history.

Article 27. Sanctions
(a) The Insurer will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Insurer to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

Article 28. Subrogation
(a) The Insurer will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Insured Person's name the defence or settlement of any claim.
(b) The Insurer can take action in the Insured Person's name to recover any payment the Insurer makes from anyone responsible for the loss.

Article 29. Customer support
(a) The Insurer's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
(b) Outside these hours the Insured Person can leave a message and the Insurer will call back on the next working day.

Article 30. Instalment agreements
(a) If the Insured Person pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
(b) Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

Article 31. How to read this document
(a) This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
(b) Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
(c) Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

Article 32. Missed departure
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable additional travel and accommodation costs to reach the Insured Person's destination if the Insured Person arrives too late to board the Insured Person's booked transport because public transport fails.
(b) The Insured Person must allow enough time to reach the departure point, and must obtain written confirmation of the delay from the transport operator.

Article 33. Claims documents
(a) The Insured Person must provide, at the Insured Person's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Insurer reasonably ask for.
(b) The Insurer may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

Article 34. Payment of claims
(a) The Insurer will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Insured Person's name.
(b) The Insurer aims to pay accepted claims within 15 working days of receiving all the documents the Insurer needs.

Article 35. Third-party administrators
(a) The Insurer may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Insurer's behalf.
(b) Any company the Insurer appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

Article 36. Change of address
(a) The Insured Person must tell the Insurer within 30 days if the Insured Person changes the Insured Person's address.
(b) The Insurer may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

Article 37. Compensation scheme
(a) The Insurer is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
(b) If the Insurer cannot meet the Insurer's obligations, the Insured Person may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

Article 38. Communication
(a) The Insurer will communicate with the Insured Person in English.
(b) The Insurer may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

Article 39. Repatriation
(a) If the Insurer's medical adviser agrees it is necessary, the Insurer will arrange and pay for the Insured Person to be brought home.
(b) The Insurer will decide the method of transport and the time of repatriation after speaking to the treating doctor.

Article 40. Fraud
(a) If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Insurer will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
(b) The Insurer may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

Article 41. Data protection
(a) The Insurer will use the personal information the Insured Person provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
(b) The Insurer will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
(c) The Insured Person can ask for a copy of the personal information the Insurer holds by writing to the Insurer's data protection officer.

Article 42. Legal expenses abroad
(a) The Insurer will pay legal costs to pursue compensation for the Insured Person's injury or death caused by a third party during the trip.
(b) The Insurer will not pay legal costs unless the Insurer's legal adviser agrees that the claim has a reasonable prospect of success.

Article 43. Personal liability
(a) The Insurer will pay damages the Insured Person becomes legally liable to pay for accidental injury to another person or accidental damage to their property during the trip.
(b) This section does not cover liability arising from the use of motor vehicles, boats or aircraft.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay under this section is $2,000,000 for all claims arising from one event.

Article 44. Governing law
(a) This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
(b) Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

Article 45. Other insurance
(a) If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Insurer will pay only the Insurer's proportionate share.
(b) The Insured Person must tell the Insurer about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Insured Person makes a claim.

Article 46. Notices
(a) Any notice the Insurer gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Insurer holds.
(b) Notices from the Insured Person should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

Article 47. Interest
(a) The Insurer will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

Article 48. Severability
(a) If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

Article 49. Waiver
(a) If the Insurer does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Insurer has given up the right to enforce it later.

Article 50. Rental car excess
(a) If the Insured Person hires a car during the trip, the Insurer will reimburse any excess the Insured Person must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.
(b) This section applies only to cars hired from a licensed rental company under a written agreement.

Article 51. Complaints
(a) If the Insured Person has a complaint, the Insured Person should first contact the Insurer's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
(b) The Insurer will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
(c) If the Insured Person remains dissatisfied, the Insured Person may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

Article 52. Emergency assistance
(a) The Insurer's emergency assistance service is available 24 hours a day on the number shown in the schedule.
(b) The Insured Person must contact the assistance service before being admitted to hospital as an in-patient, unless it is an emergency.
(c) The assistance service can arrange payment guarantees, interpreters and transport home.

Article 53. Salvage
(a) When the Insurer replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Insurer's property.
(b) If stolen property is recovered after the Insurer has paid a claim, the Insured Person must tell the Insurer and either return the payment or give the Insurer the property.

Article 54. Discounts
(a) Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
(b) If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Insurer may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

Article 55. Renewal
(a) The Insurer will write to the Insured Person at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
(b) The Insurer is not obliged to offer renewal.

Article 56. Environmental commitment
(a) Where practical, the Insurer will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
(b) The Insured Person may ask for a new part instead, and the Insurer will tell the Insured Person whether any additional cost would apply.

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.

- **1.5** Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.

- **1.7** Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.

- **1.9** Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.

- **1.12** Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
- **1.13** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.

- **1.15** Replacement device means a device of the same or similar specification, which may be refurbished.
- **1.16** Wearables means smartwatches and fitness trackers.

## 2. Limits and service fee
- **2.1** Accidental Damage: limit $1,500 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
- **2.2** Breakdown: limit $1,000 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
- **2.3** Theft and Loss: limit $800 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
- **2.4** The service fee is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Interest
- **3.1** We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

- **4.1** If a device is found after we have replaced it, the found device becomes our property and must be sent to us.

## 5. Duty of fair presentation
- **5.1** You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
- **5.2** If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
- **5.3** If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

## 6. Third-party administrators
- **6.1** We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.

- **18.1** We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.

- **52.1** You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
- **52.2** Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
