TRAVEL INSURANCE POLICY WORDING
Issued by Northstar Underwriting

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
I.2  Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
I.3  Family means the Insured Person's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Insured Person.
I.4  Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,000 metres.
I.5  Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
I.6  Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
I.7  Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
I.8  Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which the Insured Person received treatment or advice in the 12 months before the policy start date.
I.9  Premium means the amount the Insured Person must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
I.10  Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 8 hours.
I.11  Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Insured Person's details, the covers the Insured Person bought and any extensions.
I.12  Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
I.13  Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
I.14  Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $1,500 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.2  Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $25,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
II.3  Trip Cancellation: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.4  Travel Delay: limit $500 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
II.5  Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

PART III: Baggage and Personal Belongings
III.1  The Insurer will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to the Insured Person's baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
III.2  The most the Insurer will pay for Valuables under this section is $250 per incident.
III.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $300 per incident.
III.4  The Insurer will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
III.5  The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
III.6  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

PART IV: Optional cover: Travel Delay
IV.1  The Insurer will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if the Insured Person's outbound departure is delayed.
IV.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Insured Person's schedule.
IV.3  The Insurer will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

PART V: Trip Cancellation
V.1  The Insurer will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if the Insured Person must cancel the trip for a reason beyond the Insured Person's control.
V.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 7 days after the policy start date.
V.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $300 per incident.
V.4  The Insurer will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before the Insured Person bought the policy.
V.5  The Insurer will not pay for cancellation because the Insured Person no longer wish to travel.

PART VI: Emergency Medical Expenses
VI.1  The Insurer will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
VI.2  The most the Insurer will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $250 per incident.
VI.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $300 per incident.
VI.4  The Insurer will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
VI.5  The Insurer will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
VI.6  The Insurer will not pay for any claim arising from the Insured Person's being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

PART VII: General exclusions
VII.1  The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
VII.2  The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
VII.3  The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Insured Person.

PART VIII: Making a claim
VIII.1  The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 60 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
VIII.2  The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
VIII.3  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

PART IX: Currency
IX.1  All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
IX.2  Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

PART X: Automatic renewal
X.1  Unless the Insured Person tells the Insurer otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Insurer holds.
X.2  The Insured Person can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Insurer's helpline.

PART XI: Joint policyholders
XI.1  Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
XI.2  A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

PART XII: Personal liability
XII.1  The Insurer will pay damages the Insured Person becomes legally liable to pay for accidental injury to another person or accidental damage to their property during the trip.
XII.2  This section does not cover liability arising from the use of motor vehicles, boats or aircraft.
XII.3  The most the Insurer will pay under this section is $1,000,000 for all claims arising from one event.

PART XIII: Market conditions
XIII.1  If the replacement item is no longer available, the Insurer will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

PART XIV: Electronic documents
XIV.1  The Insurer will send documents by email unless the Insured Person asks for paper copies.
XIV.2  The Insured Person must tell the Insurer if the Insured Person's email address changes.
XIV.3  Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

PART XV: Waiver
XV.1  If the Insurer does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Insurer has given up the right to enforce it later.

PART XVI: Rental car excess
XVI.1  If the Insured Person hires a car during the trip, the Insurer will reimburse any excess the Insured Person must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.
XVI.2  This section applies only to cars hired from a licensed rental company under a written agreement.

PART XVII: Cancellation
XVII.1  The Insured Person can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
XVII.2  After the first 14 days the Insured Person can cancel at any time; the Insurer will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
XVII.3  The Insurer can cancel this policy by giving the Insured Person 30 days' written notice to the last address the Insurer holds.

PART XVIII: Premium payment
XVIII.1  The Insured Person must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
XVIII.2  If an instalment is not paid within 21 days of its due date, the Insurer may cancel the policy after giving notice.

PART XIX: Taxes
XIX.1  The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
XIX.2  If the tax rate changes, the Insurer may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

PART XX: Legal expenses abroad
XX.1  The Insurer will pay legal costs to pursue compensation for the Insured Person's injury or death caused by a third party during the trip.
XX.2  The Insurer will not pay legal costs unless the Insurer's legal adviser agrees that the claim has a reasonable prospect of success.

PART XXI: Inflation
XXI.1  The Insurer may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
XXI.2  Any adjustment will be shown in the Insured Person's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

PART XXII: Changes in circumstances
XXII.1  The Insured Person must tell the Insurer as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
XXII.2  The Insurer may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

PART XXIII: Claims documents
XXIII.1  The Insured Person must provide, at the Insured Person's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Insurer reasonably ask for.
XXIII.2  The Insurer may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

PART XXIV: Discounts
XXIV.1  Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
XXIV.2  If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Insurer may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

CASE PRESENTATION B
# Employee Health Benefits Plan: Summary Plan Description
Issued by the Staff Welfare Fund

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
- **1.2** Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
- **1.3** Dependant means your spouse or partner, or a child under 21 who is enrolled in the plan.
- **1.4** Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
- **1.5** Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
- **1.6** Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
- **1.7** Hearing aid replacement period means 36 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
- **1.8** Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
- **1.9** Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one treatment.
- **1.10** Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
- **1.11** Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
- **1.12** Network provider means a practitioner or clinic that has an agreement with us to provide treatment.
- **1.13** Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
- **1.14** Plan year means the twelve months starting on your coverage start date.
- **1.15** Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
- **1.16** Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
- **1.17** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.18** Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
- **1.19** Registered practitioner means a practitioner registered with the professional body for their discipline.
- **1.20** Replacement period means 24 months from the date of your last eyewear claim.
- **1.21** Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
- **1.22** Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

## 2. Limits and deductible
- **2.1** Dental Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
- **2.2** Vision Care: limit $400 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
- **2.3** Therapy Services: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
- **2.5** The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Accessibility
- **3.1** This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

## 4. Vision Care
- **4.1** We will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
- **4.2** The most we will pay for Frames under this section is $120 per treatment.
- **4.3** We will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
- **4.4** We will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

## 5. Currency
- **5.1** All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
- **5.2** Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

## 6. Reasonable precautions
- **6.1** You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
- **6.2** You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

## 7. Interpretation
- **7.1** Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
- **7.2** Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
- **7.3** Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

## 8. How to read this document
- **8.1** This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
- **8.2** Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
- **8.3** Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

## 9. Discounts
- **9.1** Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
- **9.2** If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

## 10. Renewal
- **10.1** We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
- **10.2** We are not obliged to offer renewal.

## 11. Geographical limits
- **11.1** Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
- **11.2** Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

## 12. Leaving the plan
- **12.1** Cover ends on the day your employment ends or the day you stop being eligible, whichever is earlier.
- **12.2** Claims for treatment received before cover ended may be submitted up to 90 days afterwards.

## 13. Sanctions
- **13.1** We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

## 14. Dependants
- **14.1** You may enrol dependants at the start of each plan year or within 30 days of a qualifying life event.
- **14.2** Benefits paid for dependants count towards the same annual limits as your own claims.

## 15. Salvage
- **15.1** When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
- **15.2** If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

## 16. Claims documents
- **16.1** You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
- **16.2** We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

## 17. Customer support
- **17.1** Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
- **17.2** Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

## 18. Therapy Services
- **18.1** We will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
- **18.2** The most we will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $300 per treatment.
- **18.3** We will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
- **18.4** We will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

## 19. Dental Care
- **19.1** We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
- **19.2** No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 90 days after the policy start date.
- **19.3** The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.
- **19.4** The most we will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $600 per treatment.
- **19.5** We will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
- **19.6** We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

## 20. Recovery of costs
- **20.1** If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

## 21. Records and evidence
- **21.1** You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
- **21.2** Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
- **21.3** We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

## 22. Electronic documents
- **22.1** We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
- **22.2** You must tell us if your email address changes.
- **22.3** Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

## 23. Coordination of benefits
- **23.1** If a treatment is also covered by another plan, we will pay only the part of the cost that the other plan does not pay.
- **23.2** You must tell us about any other plan that covers you or your dependants.

## 24. Automatic renewal
- **24.1** Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
- **24.2** You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

## 25. Notices
- **25.1** Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
- **25.2** Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

## 26. Inflation
- **26.1** We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
- **26.2** Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

## 27. Market conditions
- **27.1** If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

## 28. Subrogation
- **28.1** We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
- **28.2** We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

## 29. Waiver
- **29.1** If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

## 30. Communication
- **30.1** We will communicate with you in English.
- **30.2** We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

## 31. Interest
- **31.1** We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

## 32. Optional cover: Hearing Care
- **32.1** We will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
- **32.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **32.3** The most we will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $150 per treatment.
- **32.4** We will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

## 33. General exclusions
- **33.1** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
- **33.2** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
- **33.3** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
- **33.4** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
- **33.5** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
- **33.6** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

## 34. Wellness allowance
- **34.1** Each plan year you may claim up to $250 towards a gym membership or fitness class.
- **34.2** The wellness allowance is not subject to any deductible and does not count towards other limits.

## 35. Joint policyholders
- **35.1** Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
- **35.2** A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

## 36. Cancellation
- **36.1** You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
- **36.2** After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
- **36.3** We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

## 37. Third-party administrators
- **37.1** We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
- **37.2** Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

## 38. Duty of fair presentation
- **38.1** You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
- **38.2** If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
- **38.3** If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

## 39. Arbitration
- **39.1** If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
- **39.2** Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

## 40. Compensation scheme
- **40.1** We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
- **40.2** If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

## 41. Premium payment
- **41.1** You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
- **41.2** If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

## 42. Environmental commitment
- **42.1** Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
- **42.2** You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

## 43. Assignment
- **43.1** You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

## 44. Payment of claims
- **44.1** We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
- **44.2** We aim to pay accepted claims within 10 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

## 45. Other insurance
- **45.1** If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
- **45.2** You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

## 46. Governing law
- **46.1** This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
- **46.2** Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

## 47. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
- **47.1** A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

## 48. Exchange of information
- **48.1** To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
- **48.2** We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

## 49. Eligibility
- **49.1** Employees who work at least 20 hours a week are eligible to join the plan from their first day of employment.
- **49.2** Contractors, agency workers and employees on unpaid leave of more than three months are not eligible.

## 50. Changes in circumstances
- **50.1** You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
- **50.2** We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

## 51. Instalment agreements
- **51.1** If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
- **51.2** Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

## 52. Severability
- **52.1** If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

## 53. Fraud
- **53.1** If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
- **53.2** We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

## 54. Appeals
- **54.1** If we decline all or part of a claim, you may appeal in writing within 60 days of the decision.
- **54.2** An appeal will be reviewed by someone who was not involved in the original decision.
- **54.3** We will give you a written decision on the appeal within 30 days.

## 55. Making a claim
- **55.1** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **55.2** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **55.3** You must notify us of a claim within 30 days of the treatment. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

## 56. Cooperation
- **56.1** You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
- **56.2** You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

## 57. Complaints
- **57.1** If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
- **57.2** We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
- **57.3** If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

## 58. Change of address
- **58.1** You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
- **58.2** We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

## 59. Taxes
- **59.1** The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
- **59.2** If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

## 60. Data protection
- **60.1** We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
- **60.2** We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
- **60.3** You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

# Renters Contents Protection
Issued by Keystone Home Mutual

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
- **1.2** Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
- **1.3** Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
- **1.4** Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
- **1.5** Contents means household goods and personal possessions that belong to you or your family.
- **1.6** Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
- **1.7** Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
- **1.8** Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
- **1.9** High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
- **1.10** Home means the private residence at the address shown in the schedule.
- **1.11** Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
- **1.12** Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
- **1.13** Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.
- **1.14** Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
- **1.15** Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
- **1.16** Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.

- **2.1** Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
- **2.2** Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.

## 3. Theft
- **3.1** We will pay for contents stolen from your home.

- **3.3** The most we will pay for Bicycles under this section is $800 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
- **3.5** We will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.

- **4.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
- **4.4** We will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for your area had been issued before the policy started.

## 5. Optional cover: Accidental Damage
- **5.1** We will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to your contents inside the home.
- **5.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **5.3** The most we will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $750 per incident.
- **5.4** We will not pay for damage caused by pets.
- **5.5** We will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

## 6. Escape of Water
- **6.1** We will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
- **6.2** The most we will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.
- **6.3** We will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
- **6.4** We will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

## 7. General exclusions
- **7.1** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
- **7.2** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
- **7.3** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **7.4** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
- **7.5** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.

## 8. Making a claim
- **8.1** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **8.2** You must notify us of a claim within 90 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **8.3** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

## 9. Instalment agreements
- **9.1** If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.

HOME CONTENTS INSURANCE POLICY
Issued by Keystone Home Mutual
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Keystone Home Mutual and "the Policyholder" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
(b) Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Insurer, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
(c) Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
(d) Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
(e) Contents means household goods and personal possessions that belong to the Policyholder or the Policyholder's family.
(f) Family means the Policyholder's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Policyholder.
(g) Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
(h) Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
(i) High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
(j) Home means the private residence at the address shown in the schedule.
(k) Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
(l) Limit means the most the Insurer will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
(m) Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.
(n) Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Policyholder's schedule.
(o) Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
(p) Premium means the amount the Policyholder must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
(q) Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
(r) Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
(s) Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Policyholder's details, the covers the Policyholder bought and any extensions.
(t) Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
(u) Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 60 consecutive days.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Theft: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(b) Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
(c) Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(d) Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(e) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Sanctions
(a) The Insurer will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Insurer to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

Article 4. How to read this document
(a) This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
(b) Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
(c) Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

Article 5. Subrogation
(a) The Insurer will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Policyholder's name the defence or settlement of any claim.
(b) The Insurer can take action in the Policyholder's name to recover any payment the Insurer makes from anyone responsible for the loss.

Article 6. Taxes
(a) The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
(b) If the tax rate changes, the Insurer may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

Article 7. Fraud
(a) If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Insurer will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
(b) The Insurer may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

Article 8. Optional cover: Accidental Damage
(a) The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $500 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

Article 9. Recovery of costs
(a) If the Insurer pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Insurer may ask the Policyholder to repay the amount.

Article 10. Flood
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

Article 11. Cancellation
(a) The Policyholder can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
(b) After the first 14 days the Policyholder can cancel at any time; the Insurer will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
(c) The Insurer can cancel this policy by giving the Policyholder 30 days' written notice to the last address the Insurer holds.

Article 12. Cooperation
(a) The Policyholder must give the Insurer all the help and information the Insurer reasonably need to settle a claim.
(b) The Policyholder must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Insurer's written permission.

Article 13. Automatic renewal
(a) Unless the Policyholder tells the Insurer otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Insurer holds.
(b) The Policyholder can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Insurer's helpline.

Article 14. Environmental commitment
(a) Where practical, the Insurer will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
(b) The Policyholder may ask for a new part instead, and the Insurer will tell the Policyholder whether any additional cost would apply.

Article 15. Accessibility
(a) This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

Article 16. Change of address
(a) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer within 30 days if the Policyholder changes the Policyholder's address.
(b) The Insurer may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

Article 17. Alternative accommodation
(a) If the Policyholder's home cannot be lived in after damage covered by this policy, the Insurer will pay the reasonable cost of comparable temporary accommodation.
(b) The Insurer will also pay for the temporary housing of pets that live with the Policyholder.
(c) Cover ends when the home is fit to live in again or after twelve months, whichever is sooner.

Article 18. Instalment agreements
(a) If the Policyholder pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
(b) Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

Article 19. Electronic documents
(a) The Insurer will send documents by email unless the Policyholder asks for paper copies.
(b) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer if the Policyholder's email address changes.
(c) Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

Article 20. Records and evidence
(a) The Policyholder should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
(b) Where proof of value is missing, the Insurer may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
(c) The Insurer may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

Article 21. Claims documents
(a) The Policyholder must provide, at the Policyholder's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Insurer reasonably ask for.
(b) The Insurer may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

Article 22. Discounts
(a) Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
(b) If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Insurer may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

Article 23. Locks and keys
(a) If the keys to the Policyholder's home are lost or stolen, the Insurer will pay the cost of replacing the locks to the outside doors.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay under this clause is $300 for any one claim.

Article 24. Geographical limits
(a) Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
(b) Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

Article 25. Salvage
(a) When the Insurer replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Insurer's property.
(b) If stolen property is recovered after the Insurer has paid a claim, the Policyholder must tell the Insurer and either return the payment or give the Insurer the property.

Article 26. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
(a) A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

Article 27. Notices
(a) Any notice the Insurer gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Insurer holds.
(b) Notices from the Policyholder should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

Article 28. Other insurance
(a) If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Insurer will pay only the Insurer's proportionate share.
(b) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Policyholder makes a claim.

Article 29. Freezer contents
(a) The Insurer will pay for food in a domestic freezer that spoils because of a rise or fall in temperature.
(b) The Insurer will not pay if the freezer is more than fifteen years old, or if the electricity supplier cut the supply deliberately.

Article 30. Escape of Water
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

Article 31. Communication
(a) The Insurer will communicate with the Policyholder in English.
(b) The Insurer may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

Article 32. Tenant's improvements
(a) If the Policyholder rents the home, the Insurer will pay for damage to fixtures and fittings that the Policyholder installed and are responsible for.
(b) This cover applies only to improvements the Policyholder paid for, not to items provided by the landlord.

Article 33. Theft
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $500 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

Article 34. Compensation scheme
(a) The Insurer is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
(b) If the Insurer cannot meet the Insurer's obligations, the Policyholder may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

Article 35. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

Article 36. Contents temporarily removed
(a) The Policyholder's contents are covered while temporarily removed from the home to another building in the same country, for up to 60 days.
(b) Contents in a student hall of residence are covered only if the student is a member of the Policyholder's family.

Article 37. Data protection
(a) The Insurer will use the personal information the Policyholder provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
(b) The Insurer will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
(c) The Policyholder can ask for a copy of the personal information the Insurer holds by writing to the Insurer's data protection officer.

Article 38. Renewal
(a) The Insurer will write to the Policyholder at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
(b) The Insurer is not obliged to offer renewal.

Article 39. Severability
(a) If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

Article 40. Premium payment
(a) The Policyholder must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
(b) If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, the Insurer may cancel the policy after giving notice.

Article 41. Arbitration
(a) If the Insurer accepts a claim but disagree with the Policyholder about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
(b) Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against the Insurer.

Article 42. Joint policyholders
(a) Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
(b) A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

Article 43. Interest
(a) The Insurer will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

Article 44. Customer support
(a) The Insurer's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
(b) Outside these hours the Policyholder can leave a message and the Insurer will call back on the next working day.

Article 45. Waiver
(a) If the Insurer does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Insurer has given up the right to enforce it later.

Article 46. Governing law
(a) This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
(b) Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

Article 47. Inflation
(a) The Insurer may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
(b) Any adjustment will be shown in the Policyholder's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

Article 48. Changes in circumstances
(a) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
(b) The Insurer may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

Article 49. Making a claim
(a) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(b) The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 60 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(c) The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

Article 50. Duty of fair presentation
(a) The Policyholder must answer all questions the Insurer asks honestly and to the best of the Policyholder's knowledge.
(b) If the Policyholder gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Insurer may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
(c) If the Policyholder gives incorrect information carelessly, the Insurer may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

Article 51. Interpretation
(a) Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
(b) Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
(c) Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

Article 52. Exchange of information
(a) To prevent fraud, the Insurer may check the details the Policyholder gives against public records and industry databases.
(b) The Insurer may contact previous insurers to confirm the Policyholder's claims history.

Article 53. Third-party administrators
(a) The Insurer may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Insurer's behalf.
(b) Any company the Insurer appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

Article 54. Reasonable precautions
(a) The Policyholder must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
(b) The Policyholder must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

Article 55. Garden and outdoor cover
(a) The Insurer will pay for plants, trees and shrubs in the garden of the home that are damaged by fire, lightning or theft.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by frost, storms, drought or animals.

Article 56. Complaints
(a) If the Policyholder has a complaint, the Policyholder should first contact the Insurer's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
(b) The Insurer will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
(c) If the Policyholder remains dissatisfied, the Policyholder may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

Article 57. Currency
(a) All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
(b) Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

Article 58. Payment of claims
(a) The Insurer will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Policyholder's name.
(b) The Insurer aims to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents the Insurer needs.

Article 59. Market conditions
(a) If the replacement item is no longer available, the Insurer will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

Article 60. Assignment
(a) The Policyholder cannot transfer the Policyholder's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Insurer's written consent.

DEVICE PROTECTION PLAN TERMS
Issued by Tessera Warranty Company

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.
I.2  Accessories means cases, chargers and earbuds.
I.3  Authorised repairer means a repairer approved in writing by the Provider.
I.4  Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
I.5  Device means the item shown in the schedule, bought new from an authorised retailer.
I.6  Family means the Customer's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Customer.
I.7  Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
I.8  Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 24 months after the device was bought.
I.9  Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Customer's schedule.
I.10  Premium means the amount the Customer must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
I.11  Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
I.12  Replacement device means a device of the same or similar specification, which may be refurbished.
I.13  Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Customer's details, the covers the Customer bought and any extensions.
I.14  Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
I.15  Wearables means smartwatches and fitness trackers.

PART II: Limits and service fee
II.1  Accidental Damage: limit $1,500 per incident; service fee $79 per claim.
II.2  Breakdown: limit $1,500 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
II.3  Theft and Loss: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
II.4  The service fee is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Optional cover: Theft and Loss
III.1  The Provider will replace the Customer's device if it is stolen or lost.
III.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Customer's schedule.
III.3  The most the Provider will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
III.4  The Provider will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
III.5  The Provider will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

PART IV: Accidental Damage
IV.1  The Provider will repair or replace the Customer's device if it is accidentally damaged.
IV.2  The most the Provider will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.
IV.3  The most the Provider will pay for Wearables under this section is $300 per incident.
IV.4  The Provider will not pay for cosmetic damage, such as scratches or dents, that does not affect how the device works.
IV.5  The Provider will not pay for damage following a repair by anyone other than the Provider or an authorised repairer. This exclusion does not apply if the Provider approved the repair in writing beforehand.

PART V: Breakdown
V.1  The Provider will repair or replace the Customer's device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
V.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 45 days after the policy start date.
V.3  The most the Provider will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $80 per incident.
V.4  The Provider will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
V.5  The Provider will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

PART VI: General exclusions
VI.1  The Provider will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Provider from paying.
VI.2  The Provider will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Customer.
VI.3  The Provider will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
VI.4  The Provider will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
VI.5  The Provider will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
VI.6  The Provider will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

PART VII: Making a claim
VII.1  The Provider may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
VII.2  The Customer must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
VII.3  The Customer must notify the Provider of a claim within 90 days of the incident. The Provider will not pay any claim notified after that time.

PART VIII: Transferring the plan
VIII.1  The Customer may transfer the plan to a new owner of the device by telling the Provider in writing.
VIII.2  The remaining term of the plan transfers with the device; the term does not restart.

PART IX: Market conditions
IX.1  If the replacement item is no longer available, the Provider will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

PART X: Severability
X.1  If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

PART XI: Environmental commitment
XI.1  Where practical, the Provider will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
XI.2  The Customer may ask for a new part instead, and the Provider will tell the Customer whether any additional cost would apply.

PART XII: Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
XII.1  A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

PART XIII: Software support
XIII.1  The Provider's helpline can give advice on setting up and using the Customer's device.
XIII.2  Software support does not include fixing problems caused by third-party apps or unofficial operating systems.

PART XIV: Joint policyholders
XIV.1  Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
XIV.2  A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

PART XV: Duty of fair presentation
XV.1  The Customer must answer all questions the Provider asks honestly and to the best of the Customer's knowledge.
XV.2  If the Customer gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Provider may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
XV.3  If the Customer gives incorrect information carelessly, the Provider may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

PART XVI: Recovery of costs
XVI.1  If the Provider pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Provider may ask the Customer to repay the amount.

PART XVII: Salvage
XVII.1  When the Provider replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Provider's property.
XVII.2  If stolen property is recovered after the Provider has paid a claim, the Customer must tell the Provider and either return the payment or give the Provider the property.

PART XVIII: Inflation
XVIII.1  The Provider may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
XVIII.2  Any adjustment will be shown in the Customer's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

PART XIX: Exchange of information
XIX.1  To prevent fraud, the Provider may check the details the Customer gives against public records and industry databases.
XIX.2  The Provider may contact previous insurers to confirm the Customer's claims history.

PART XX: Taxes
XX.1  The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
XX.2  If the tax rate changes, the Provider may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

PART XXI: Sanctions
XXI.1  The Provider will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Provider to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

PART XXII: Currency
XXII.1  All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
XXII.2  Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

PART XXIII: Change of address
XXIII.1  The Customer must tell the Provider within 30 days if the Customer changes the Customer's address.
XXIII.2  The Provider may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

PART XXIV: Accessibility
XXIV.1  This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

PART XXV: Customer support
XXV.1  The Provider's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
XXV.2  Outside these hours the Customer can leave a message and the Provider will call back on the next working day.

PART XXVI: Records and evidence
XXVI.1  The Customer should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
XXVI.2  Where proof of value is missing, the Provider may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
XXVI.3  The Provider may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

PART XXVII: Electronic documents
XXVII.1  The Provider will send documents by email unless the Customer asks for paper copies.
XXVII.2  The Customer must tell the Provider if the Customer's email address changes.
XXVII.3  Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

PART XXVIII: Repair process
XXVIII.1  After a claim is accepted, the Provider will send a prepaid mailer or book a courier collection.
XXVIII.2  The Provider aims to return repaired devices within 10 business days of receiving them.

PART XXIX: Other insurance
XXIX.1  If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Provider will pay only the Provider's proportionate share.
XXIX.2  The Customer must tell the Provider about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Customer makes a claim.

PART XXX: Unrecoverable devices
XXX.1  If a device is found after the Provider has replaced it, the found device becomes the Provider's property and must be sent to the Provider.
XXX.2  The Provider may block devices reported as lost or stolen so that they cannot be used on mobile networks.

PART XXXI: Discounts
XXXI.1  Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
XXXI.2  If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Provider may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

PART XXXII: Fraud
XXXII.1  If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Provider will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
XXXII.2  The Provider may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

PART XXXIII: Claims documents
XXXIII.1  The Customer must provide, at the Customer's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Provider reasonably ask for.
XXXIII.2  The Provider may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

PART XXXIV: Reasonable precautions
XXXIV.1  The Customer must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
XXXIV.2  The Customer must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

PART XXXV: Interpretation
XXXV.1  Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
XXXV.2  Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
XXXV.3  Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

PART XXXVI: Data protection
XXXVI.1  The Provider will use the personal information the Customer provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
XXXVI.2  The Provider will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
XXXVI.3  The Customer can ask for a copy of the personal information the Provider holds by writing to the Provider's data protection officer.

PART XXXVII: Assignment
XXXVII.1  The Customer cannot transfer the Customer's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Provider's written consent.

PART XXXVIII: Cooperation
XXXVIII.1  The Customer must give the Provider all the help and information the Provider reasonably need to settle a claim.
XXXVIII.2  The Customer must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Provider's written permission.

PART XXXIX: Notices
XXXIX.1  Any notice the Provider gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Provider holds.
XXXIX.2  Notices from the Customer should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

PART XXXX: Data and backups
XXXX.1  The Provider is not responsible for recovering or restoring any data, software or settings stored on the Customer's device.
XXXX.2  The Customer should back up the Customer's data regularly and before sending the device for repair.

PART XXXXI: Third-party administrators
XXXXI.1  The Provider may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Provider's behalf.
XXXXI.2  Any company the Provider appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

PART XXXXII: Premium payment
XXXXII.1  The Customer must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
XXXXII.2  If an instalment is not paid within 21 days of its due date, the Provider may cancel the policy after giving notice.

PART XXXXIII: Geographical limits
XXXXIII.1  Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
XXXXIII.2  Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

PART XXXXIV: Complaints
XXXXIV.1  If the Customer has a complaint, the Customer should first contact the Provider's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
XXXXIV.2  The Provider will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.

EMPLOYEE HEALTH BENEFITS PLAN: SUMMARY PLAN DESCRIPTION
Issued by the Staff Welfare Fund

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Plan, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
I.2  Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
I.3  Dependant means the Member's spouse or partner, or a child under 21 who is enrolled in the plan.
I.4  Family means the Member's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Member.
I.5  Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
I.6  Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
I.7  Hearing aid replacement period means 36 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
I.8  Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
I.9  Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
I.10  Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
I.11  Network provider means a practitioner or clinic that has an agreement with the Plan to provide treatment.
I.12  Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
I.13  Plan year means the twelve months starting on the Member's coverage start date.
I.14  Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Member's schedule.
I.15  Premium means the amount the Member must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
I.16  Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
I.17  Registered practitioner means a practitioner registered with the professional body for their discipline.
I.18  Replacement period means 12 months from the date of the Member's last eyewear claim.
I.19  Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

PART II: Limits and deductible
II.1  Dental Care: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
II.2  Vision Care: limit $500 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
II.3  Therapy Services: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
II.4  Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
II.5  The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Optional cover: Hearing Care
III.1  The Plan will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
III.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Member's schedule.
III.3  The most the Plan will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $150 per treatment.
III.4  The Plan will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

PART IV: Therapy Services
IV.1  The Plan will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
IV.2  The most the Plan will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $200 per treatment.
IV.3  The Plan will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
IV.4  The Plan will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

PART V: Vision Care
V.1  The Plan will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
V.2  The most the Plan will pay for Frames under this section is $150 per treatment.
V.3  The Plan will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
V.4  The Plan will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

PART VI: Dental Care
VI.1  The Plan will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
VI.2  No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 90 days after the policy start date.
VI.3  The most the Plan will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $750 per treatment.
VI.4  The most the Plan will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $800 per treatment.
VI.5  The Plan will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
VI.6  The Plan will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

PART VII: General exclusions
VII.1  The Plan will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Member.
VII.2  The Plan will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
VII.3  The Plan will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Plan from paying.

PART VIII: Making a claim
VIII.1  The Plan may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
VIII.2  The Member must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
VIII.3  The Member must notify the Plan of a claim within 60 days of the treatment. The Plan will not pay any claim notified after that time.

PART IX: Geographical limits
IX.1  Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
IX.2  Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

PART X: Reasonable precautions
X.1  The Member must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
X.2  The Member must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

PART XI: Environmental commitment
XI.1  Where practical, the Plan will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
XI.2  The Member may ask for a new part instead, and the Plan will tell the Member whether any additional cost would apply.

PART XII: Severability
XII.1  If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

PART XIII: Customer support
XIII.1  The Plan's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
XIII.2  Outside these hours the Member can leave a message and the Plan will call back on the next working day.

PART XIV: Payment of claims
XIV.1  The Plan will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Member's name.
XIV.2  The Plan aims to pay accepted claims within 15 working days of receiving all the documents the Plan needs.

PART XV: Interpretation
XV.1  Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
XV.2  Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
XV.3  Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

PART XVI: Automatic renewal
XVI.1  Unless the Member tells the Plan otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Plan holds.
XVI.2  The Member can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Plan's helpline.

PART XVII: Waiver
XVII.1  If the Plan does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Plan has given up the right to enforce it later.

PART XVIII: Notices
XVIII.1  Any notice the Plan gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Plan holds.
XVIII.2  Notices from the Member should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

PART XIX: Premium payment
XIX.1  The Member must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
XIX.2  If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, the Plan may cancel the policy after giving notice.

PART XX: Accessibility
XX.1  This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

PART XXI: Joint policyholders
XXI.1  Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
XXI.2  A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

PART XXII: Cooperation
XXII.1  The Member must give the Plan all the help and information the Plan reasonably need to settle a claim.
XXII.2  The Member must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Plan's written permission.

PART XXIII: Recovery of costs
XXIII.1  If the Plan pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Plan may ask the Member to repay the amount.

PART XXIV: Records and evidence
XXIV.1  The Member should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
XXIV.2  Where proof of value is missing, the Plan may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
XXIV.3  The Plan may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

PART XXV: Data protection
XXV.1  The Plan will use the personal information the Member provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
XXV.2  The Plan will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
XXV.3  The Member can ask for a copy of the personal information the Plan holds by writing to the Plan's data protection officer.

PART XXVI: Appeals
XXVI.1  If the Plan declines all or part of a claim, the Member may appeal in writing within 60 days of the decision.
XXVI.2  An appeal will be reviewed by someone who was not involved in the original decision.
XXVI.3  The Plan will give the Member a written decision on the appeal within 30 days.

PART XXVII: Other insurance
XXVII.1  If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Plan will pay only the Plan's proportionate share.
XXVII.2  The Member must tell the Plan about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Member makes a claim.

PART XXVIII: Currency
XXVIII.1  All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
XXVIII.2  Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

PART XXIX: Sanctions
XXIX.1  The Plan will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Plan to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

PART XXX: Change of address
XXX.1  The Member must tell the Plan within 30 days if the Member changes the Member's address.
XXX.2  The Plan may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

PART XXXI: Taxes
XXXI.1  The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
XXXI.2  If the tax rate changes, the Plan may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

PART XXXII: Fraud
XXXII.1  If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Plan will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
XXXII.2  The Plan may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

PART XXXIII: Claims documents
XXXIII.1  The Member must provide, at the Member's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Plan reasonably ask for.
XXXIII.2  The Plan may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

PART XXXIV: Exchange of information
XXXIV.1  To prevent fraud, the Plan may check the details the Member gives against public records and industry databases.
XXXIV.2  The Plan may contact previous insurers to confirm the Member's claims history.

PART XXXV: Salvage
XXXV.1  When the Plan replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Plan's property.
XXXV.2  If stolen property is recovered after the Plan has paid a claim, the Member must tell the Plan and either return the payment or give the Plan the property.

PART XXXVI: Duty of fair presentation
XXXVI.1  The Member must answer all questions the Plan asks honestly and to the best of the Member's knowledge.
XXXVI.2  If the Member gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Plan may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
XXXVI.3  If the Member gives incorrect information carelessly, the Plan may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

PART XXXVII: Communication
XXXVII.1  The Plan will communicate with the Member in English.
XXXVII.2  The Plan may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

PART XXXVIII: Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
XXXVIII.1  A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

PART XXXIX: Inflation
XXXIX.1  The Plan may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
XXXIX.2  Any adjustment will be shown in the Member's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

PART XXXX: How to read this document
XXXX.1  This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
XXXX.2  Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
XXXX.3  Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

PART XXXXI: Instalment agreements
XXXXI.1  If the Member pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
XXXXI.2  Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

PART XXXXII: Coordination of benefits
XXXXII.1  If a treatment is also covered by another plan, the Plan will pay only the part of the cost that the other plan does not pay.
XXXXII.2  The Member must tell the Plan about any other plan that covers the Member or the Member's dependants.

PART XXXXIII: Wellness allowance
XXXXIII.1  Each plan year the Member may claim up to $250 towards a gym membership or fitness class.
XXXXIII.2  The wellness allowance is not subject to any deductible and does not count towards other limits.

## 25. Discounts
- **25.1** Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
- **25.2** If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

## 26. Renewal
- **26.1** We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
- **26.2** We are not obliged to offer renewal.

- **27.1** Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
- **27.2** You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

## 28. Cooperation
- **28.1** You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
- **28.2** You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

## 29. Environmental commitment
- **29.1** Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
- **29.2** You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

## 30. Change of address
- **30.1** You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
- **30.2** We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

- **31.1** We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
- **31.2** If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

## 32. Records and evidence
- **32.1** You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
- **32.2** Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
- **32.3** We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

- **33.1** You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
