- **33.3** We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

- **34.1** We will pay damages you become legally liable to pay for accidental injury to another person or accidental damage to their property during the trip.

- **34.3** The most we will pay under this section is $5,000,000 for all claims arising from one event.

- **35.1** If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

- **36.2** You must contact the assistance service before being admitted to hospital as an in-patient, unless it is an emergency.
- **36.3** The assistance service can arrange payment guarantees, interpreters and transport home.

- **37.1** We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

## 38. Subrogation
- **38.1** We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
- **38.2** We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

- **39.1** Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
- **39.2** Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

- **52.1** This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.

## 54. Salvage
- **54.1** When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.

## 55. Communication
- **55.1** We will communicate with you in English.
- **55.2** We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

- **57.2** Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

## 58. Exchange of information
- **58.1** To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
- **58.2** We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

## 59. Legal expenses abroad
- **59.1** We will pay legal costs to pursue compensation for your injury or death caused by a third party during the trip.
- **59.2** We will not pay legal costs unless our legal adviser agrees that the claim has a reasonable prospect of success.

Issued by Compass Mutual
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Compass Mutual and "the Insured Person" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
(b) Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
(c) Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
(d) Family means the Insured Person's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Insured Person.
(e) Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,500 metres.
(f) Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
(g) Limit means the most the Insurer will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
(h) Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
(i) Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
(j) Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which the Insured Person received treatment or advice in the 3 months before the policy start date.
(k) Premium means the amount the Insured Person must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
(l) Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
(m) Public transport means any scheduled train, bus, coach, ferry or aircraft.
(n) Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 12 hours.
(o) Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
(p) Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Insured Person's details, the covers the Insured Person bought and any extensions.
(q) Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
(r) Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
(s) Trip means a journey that starts and ends in the Insured Person's home country during the policy period.
(t) Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $1,500 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(b) Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $150 per claim.
(c) Trip Cancellation: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(d) Travel Delay: limit $500 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(e) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Trip Cancellation
(a) The Insurer will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if the Insured Person must cancel the trip for a reason beyond the Insured Person's control.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 7 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $200 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before the Insured Person bought the policy.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation because the Insured Person no longer wish to travel.

Article 4. Optional cover: Travel Delay
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if the Insured Person's outbound departure is delayed.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Insured Person's schedule.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

Article 5. Emergency Medical Expenses
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $400 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $300 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for any claim arising from the Insured Person's being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

Article 6. Baggage and Personal Belongings
(a) The Insurer will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to the Insured Person's baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Valuables under this section is $250 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $450 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

Article 7. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Insured Person.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

Article 8. Making a claim

(b) The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 14 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(c) The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

Article 9. Instalment agreements
(a) If the Insured Person pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
(b) Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

Article 10. Customer support
(a) The Insurer's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
(b) Outside these hours the Insured Person can leave a message and the Insurer will call back on the next working day.

Article 11. Missed departure
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable additional travel and accommodation costs to reach the Insured Person's destination if the Insured Person arrives too late to board the Insured Person's booked transport because public transport fails.
(b) The Insured Person must allow enough time to reach the departure point, and must obtain written confirmation of the delay from the transport operator.

Article 12. Changes in circumstances
(a) The Insured Person must tell the Insurer as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
(b) The Insurer may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

Article 13. Cooperation
(a) The Insured Person must give the Insurer all the help and information the Insurer reasonably need to settle a claim.
(b) The Insured Person must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Insurer's written permission.

Article 14. Change of address
(a) The Insured Person must tell the Insurer within 30 days if the Insured Person changes the Insured Person's address.
(b) The Insurer may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

Article 15. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
(a) A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

Article 16. Severability
(a) If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

Article 17. Arbitration
(a) If the Insurer accepts a claim but disagree with the Insured Person about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
(b) Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against the Insurer.

Article 18. Fraud
(a) If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Insurer will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
(b) The Insurer may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

Article 19. Inflation
(a) The Insurer may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
(b) Any adjustment will be shown in the Insured Person's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

Article 20. Repatriation
(a) If the Insurer's medical adviser agrees it is necessary, the Insurer will arrange and pay for the Insured Person to be brought home.
(b) The Insurer will decide the method of transport and the time of repatriation after speaking to the treating doctor.

Article 21. Emergency assistance
(a) The Insurer's emergency assistance service is available 24 hours a day on the number shown in the schedule.
(b) The Insured Person must contact the assistance service before being admitted to hospital as an in-patient, unless it is an emergency.
(c) The assistance service can arrange payment guarantees, interpreters and transport home.

Article 22. Records and evidence
(a) The Insured Person should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
(b) Where proof of value is missing, the Insurer may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
(c) The Insurer may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

Article 23. Rental car excess
(a) If the Insured Person hires a car during the trip, the Insurer will reimburse any excess the Insured Person must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.
(b) This section applies only to cars hired from a licensed rental company under a written agreement.

Article 24. Notices
(a) Any notice the Insurer gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Insurer holds.
(b) Notices from the Insured Person should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

Article 25. Discounts
(a) Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
(b) If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Insurer may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

CASE PRESENTATION B
# Household Contents Cover: Policy Booklet
Issued by Lantern General Insurance

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
- **1.2** Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
- **1.3** Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
- **1.4** Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
- **1.5** Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
- **1.6** Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
- **1.7** Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
- **1.8** High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
- **1.9** Home means the private residence at the address shown in the schedule.
- **1.10** Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
- **1.11** Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.
- **1.12** Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
- **1.13** Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
- **1.14** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.15** Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
- **1.16** Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
- **1.17** Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
- **1.18** Unoccupied means not lived in by you or a member of your family for more than 30 consecutive days.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.2** Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
- **2.3** Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.4** Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
- **2.5** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Theft
- **3.1** We will pay for contents stolen from your home.
- **3.2** The most we will pay for High-risk items under this section is $2,500 per incident.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Bicycles under this section is $800 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
- **3.5** We will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
- **3.6** We will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

## 4. Flood
- **4.1** We will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering your home.
- **4.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
- **4.4** We will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for your area had been issued before the policy started.

## 5. Optional cover: Accidental Damage
- **5.1** We will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to your contents inside the home.
- **5.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **5.3** The most we will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $500 per incident.
- **5.4** We will not pay for damage caused by pets.
- **5.5** We will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

## 6. Escape of Water
- **6.1** We will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
- **6.2** The most we will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.
- **6.3** We will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
- **6.4** We will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

## 7. General exclusions
- **7.1** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
- **7.2** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **7.3** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
- **7.4** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
- **7.5** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
- **7.6** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.

## 8. Making a claim
- **8.1** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **8.2** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **8.3** You must notify us of a claim within 90 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

## 9. Records and evidence
- **9.1** You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
- **9.2** Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
- **9.3** We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

## 10. Notices
- **10.1** Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
- **10.2** Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

## 11. Geographical limits
- **11.1** Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
- **11.2** Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

## 12. Freezer contents
- **12.1** We will pay for food in a domestic freezer that spoils because of a rise or fall in temperature.
- **12.2** We will not pay if the freezer is more than fifteen years old, or if the electricity supplier cut the supply deliberately.

## 13. Premium payment
- **13.1** You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
- **13.2** If an instalment is not paid within 21 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

## 14. Tenant's improvements
- **14.1** If you rent the home, we will pay for damage to fixtures and fittings that you installed and are responsible for.
- **14.2** This cover applies only to improvements you paid for, not to items provided by the landlord.

## 15. Environmental commitment
- **15.1** Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
- **15.2** You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

## 16. Complaints
- **16.1** If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
- **16.2** We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
- **16.3** If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

## 17. Waiver
- **17.1** If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

## 18. Governing law
- **18.1** This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
- **18.2** Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

## 19. Subrogation
- **19.1** We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
- **19.2** We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

## 20. Garden and outdoor cover
- **20.1** We will pay for plants, trees and shrubs in the garden of the home that are damaged by fire, lightning or theft.
- **20.2** We will not pay for damage caused by frost, storms, drought or animals.

## 21. Inflation
- **21.1** We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
- **21.2** Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

## 22. Currency
- **22.1** All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
- **22.2** Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

## 23. Joint policyholders
- **23.1** Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
- **23.2** A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

## 24. Interest
- **24.1** We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

## 25. Reasonable precautions
- **25.1** You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
- **25.2** You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

## 26. Other insurance
- **26.1** If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
- **26.2** You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

## 27. Communication
- **27.1** We will communicate with you in English.
- **27.2** We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

## 28. Payment of claims
- **28.1** We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
- **28.2** We aim to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

## 29. Discounts
- **29.1** Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
- **29.2** If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

## 30. Fraud
- **30.1** If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
- **30.2** We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

## 31. Compensation scheme
- **31.1** We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
- **31.2** If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

## 32. Renewal
- **32.1** We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
- **32.2** We are not obliged to offer renewal.

## 33. Taxes
- **33.1** The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
- **33.2** If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

## 34. Assignment
- **34.1** You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

## 35. Cancellation
- **35.1** You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
- **35.2** After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
- **35.3** We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

## 36. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
- **36.1** A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

## 37. Market conditions
- **37.1** If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

## 38. Exchange of information
- **38.1** To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
- **38.2** We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

## 39. Automatic renewal
- **39.1** Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
- **39.2** You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

## 40. Data protection
- **40.1** We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
- **40.2** We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
- **40.3** You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

## 41. Customer support
- **41.1** Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
- **41.2** Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

## 42. Sanctions
- **42.1** We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

## 43. Third-party administrators
- **43.1** We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
- **43.2** Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

## 44. Contents temporarily removed
- **44.1** Your contents are covered while temporarily removed from the home to another building in the same country, for up to 60 days.
- **44.2** Contents in a student hall of residence are covered only if the student is a member of your family.

## 45. Salvage
- **45.1** When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
- **45.2** If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

## 46. Electronic documents
- **46.1** We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
- **46.2** You must tell us if your email address changes.
- **46.3** Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

## 47. Changes in circumstances
- **47.1** You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
- **47.2** We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

## 48. Instalment agreements
- **48.1** If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
- **48.2** Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

## 49. Alternative accommodation
- **49.1** If your home cannot be lived in after damage covered by this policy, we will pay the reasonable cost of comparable temporary accommodation.
- **49.2** We will also pay for the temporary housing of pets that live with you.
- **49.3** Cover ends when the home is fit to live in again or after twelve months, whichever is sooner.

## 50. Locks and keys
- **50.1** If the keys to your home are lost or stolen, we will pay the cost of replacing the locks to the outside doors.
- **50.2** The most we will pay under this clause is $500 for any one claim.

## 51. Accessibility
- **51.1** This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

## 52. Change of address
- **52.1** You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
- **52.2** We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

## 53. Cooperation
- **53.1** You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
- **53.2** You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

## 54. Severability
- **54.1** If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

## 55. Recovery of costs
- **55.1** If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

## 56. Duty of fair presentation
- **56.1** You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
- **56.2** If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
- **56.3** If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

## 57. Interpretation
- **57.1** Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
- **57.2** Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
- **57.3** Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

## 58. Arbitration
- **58.1** If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
- **58.2** Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

(h) Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Policyholder's schedule.
(i) Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
(j) Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
(k) Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
(l) Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 60 consecutive days.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(b) Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
(c) Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(d) Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(e) The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

Article 3. Escape of Water
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $2,000 per incident.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

Article 4. Theft
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $800 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

Article 5. Optional cover: Accidental Damage
(a) The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $750 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

Article 6. Flood
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

Article 7. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.

Article 8. Making a claim
(a) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(b) The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 30 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(c) The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

Article 9. Cooperation
(a) The Policyholder must give the Insurer all the help and information the Insurer reasonably need to settle a claim.
(b) The Policyholder must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Insurer's written permission.

Article 10. Interpretation
(a) Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
(b) Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
(c) Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

Article 11. Alternative accommodation
(a) If the Policyholder's home cannot be lived in after damage covered by this policy, the Insurer will pay the reasonable cost of comparable temporary accommodation.
(b) The Insurer will also pay for the temporary housing of pets that live with the Policyholder.
(c) Cover ends when the home is fit to live in again or after twelve months, whichever is sooner.

Article 12. Duty of fair presentation
(a) The Policyholder must answer all questions the Insurer asks honestly and to the best of the Policyholder's knowledge.
(b) If the Policyholder gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Insurer may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
(c) If the Policyholder gives incorrect information carelessly, the Insurer may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

Article 13. Environmental commitment
(a) Where practical, the Insurer will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
(b) The Policyholder may ask for a new part instead, and the Insurer will tell the Policyholder whether any additional cost would apply.

Article 14. Electronic documents
(a) The Insurer will send documents by email unless the Policyholder asks for paper copies.
(b) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer if the Policyholder's email address changes.
(c) Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

Article 15. Locks and keys
(a) If the keys to the Policyholder's home are lost or stolen, the Insurer will pay the cost of replacing the locks to the outside doors.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay under this clause is $300 for any one claim.

Article 16. Automatic renewal
(a) Unless the Policyholder tells the Insurer otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Insurer holds.
(b) The Policyholder can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Insurer's helpline.

Article 17. Other insurance
(a) If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Insurer will pay only the Insurer's proportionate share.
(b) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Policyholder makes a claim.

Article 18. Waiver
(a) If the Insurer does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Insurer has given up the right to enforce it later.

Article 19. Renewal
(a) The Insurer will write to the Policyholder at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
(b) The Insurer is not obliged to offer renewal.

Article 20. Discounts
(a) Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
(b) If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Insurer may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

Article 21. Premium payment
(a) The Policyholder must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
(b) If an instalment is not paid within 21 days of its due date, the Insurer may cancel the policy after giving notice.

Article 22. Freezer contents
(a) The Insurer will pay for food in a domestic freezer that spoils because of a rise or fall in temperature.
(b) The Insurer will not pay if the freezer is more than fifteen years old, or if the electricity supplier cut the supply deliberately.

Article 23. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
(a) A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

Article 24. Market conditions
(a) If the replacement item is no longer available, the Insurer will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

Article 25. How to read this document
(a) This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
(b) Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
(c) Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

Article 26. Severability
(a) If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

Article 27. Data protection
(a) The Insurer will use the personal information the Policyholder provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
(b) The Insurer will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
(c) The Policyholder can ask for a copy of the personal information the Insurer holds by writing to the Insurer's data protection officer.

Article 28. Compensation scheme
(a) The Insurer is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
(b) If the Insurer cannot meet the Insurer's obligations, the Policyholder may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

Article 29. Interest
(a) The Insurer will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

Article 30. Subrogation
(a) The Insurer will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Policyholder's name the defence or settlement of any claim.
(b) The Insurer can take action in the Policyholder's name to recover any payment the Insurer makes from anyone responsible for the loss.

Article 31. Governing law
(a) This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
(b) Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

Article 32. Communication
(a) The Insurer will communicate with the Policyholder in English.
(b) The Insurer may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

Article 33. Records and evidence
(a) The Policyholder should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
(b) Where proof of value is missing, the Insurer may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
(c) The Insurer may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

Article 34. Assignment
(a) The Policyholder cannot transfer the Policyholder's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Insurer's written consent.

Article 35. Joint policyholders
(a) Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
(b) A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

Article 36. Recovery of costs
(a) If the Insurer pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Insurer may ask the Policyholder to repay the amount.

Article 37. Accessibility
(a) This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

Article 38. Changes in circumstances
(a) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
(b) The Insurer may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

Article 39. Third-party administrators
(a) The Insurer may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Insurer's behalf.
(b) Any company the Insurer appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

Article 40. Geographical limits
(a) Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
(b) Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

Article 41. Change of address
(a) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer within 30 days if the Policyholder changes the Policyholder's address.
(b) The Insurer may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

Article 42. Garden and outdoor cover
(a) The Insurer will pay for plants, trees and shrubs in the garden of the home that are damaged by fire, lightning or theft.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by frost, storms, drought or animals.

Article 43. Payment of claims
(a) The Insurer will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Policyholder's name.
(b) The Insurer aims to pay accepted claims within 10 working days of receiving all the documents the Insurer needs.

Article 44. Currency
(a) All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
(b) Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

Article 45. Reasonable precautions
(a) The Policyholder must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
(b) The Policyholder must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

Article 46. Fraud
(a) If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Insurer will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
(b) The Insurer may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

Article 47. Arbitration
(a) If the Insurer accepts a claim but disagree with the Policyholder about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
(b) Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against the Insurer.

Article 48. Claims documents
(a) The Policyholder must provide, at the Policyholder's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Insurer reasonably ask for.
(b) The Insurer may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

Article 49. Tenant's improvements
(a) If the Policyholder rents the home, the Insurer will pay for damage to fixtures and fittings that the Policyholder installed and are responsible for.
(b) This cover applies only to improvements the Policyholder paid for, not to items provided by the landlord.

Article 50. Exchange of information
(a) To prevent fraud, the Insurer may check the details the Policyholder gives against public records and industry databases.
(b) The Insurer may contact previous insurers to confirm the Policyholder's claims history.

Article 51. Inflation
(a) The Insurer may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
(b) Any adjustment will be shown in the Policyholder's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

Article 52. Complaints
(a) If the Policyholder has a complaint, the Policyholder should first contact the Insurer's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
(b) The Insurer will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
(c) If the Policyholder remains dissatisfied, the Policyholder may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

Article 53. Notices
(a) Any notice the Insurer gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Insurer holds.
(b) Notices from the Policyholder should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

state.policy:
ANNUAL MULTI-TRIP TRAVEL COVER
Issued by Compass Mutual
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Compass Mutual and "the Insured Person" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
(b) Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
(c) Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
(d) Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 3,000 metres.
(e) Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
(f) Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
(g) Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which the Insured Person received treatment or advice in the 3 months before the policy start date.
(h) Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
(i) Public transport means any scheduled train, bus, coach, ferry or aircraft.
(j) Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 12 hours.
(k) Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Insured Person's details, the covers the Insured Person bought and any extensions.
(l) Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
(m) Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
(n) Territory means the countries in which cover applies, as shown in the schedule.
(o) Trip means a journey that starts and ends in the Insured Person's home country during the policy period.
(p) Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(b) Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $150 per claim.
(c) Trip Cancellation: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(d) Travel Delay: limit $750 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(e) The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

Article 3. Optional cover: Travel Delay
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if the Insured Person's outbound departure is delayed.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Insured Person's schedule.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

Article 4. Trip Cancellation
(a) The Insurer will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if the Insured Person must cancel the trip for a reason beyond the Insured Person's control.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 14 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $300 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before the Insured Person bought the policy.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation because the Insured Person no longer wish to travel.

Article 5. Baggage and Personal Belongings
(a) The Insurer will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to the Insured Person's baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Valuables under this section is $500 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $450 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

Article 6. Emergency Medical Expenses
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $250 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $500 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for any claim arising from the Insured Person's being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

Article 7. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

ANNUAL MULTI-TRIP TRAVEL COVER
Issued by Compass Mutual

SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS
1.1 Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
1.2 Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 3,000 metres.
1.3 Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
1.4 Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which you received treatment or advice in the 6 months before the policy start date.
1.5 Public transport means any scheduled train, bus, coach, ferry or aircraft.
1.6 Trip means a journey that starts and ends in your home country during the policy period.

SECTION 2 - LIMITS AND EXCESS
2.1 Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.2 Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $25,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.3 Trip Cancellation: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.4 Travel Delay: limit $750 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
2.5 Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

SECTION 3 - EMERGENCY MEDICAL EXPENSES
3.1 We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
3.2 The most we will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $250 per incident.
3.3 The most we will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $500 per incident.
3.4 We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
3.5 We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
3.6 We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

SECTION 4 - GENERAL EXCLUSIONS
4.1 We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
4.2 We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
4.3 We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

SECTION 5 - MAKING A CLAIM
5.1 You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
5.2 You must notify us of a claim within 21 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
5.3 We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

SECTION 6 - CHANGE OF ADDRESS
6.1 You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
6.2 We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

SECTION 7 - MISSED DEPARTURE
7.1 We will pay reasonable additional travel and accommodation costs to reach your destination if you arrive too late to board your booked transport because public transport fails.
7.2 You must allow enough time to reach the departure point, and must obtain written confirmation of the delay from the transport operator.

SECTION 8 - SANCTIONS
8.1 We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

SECTION 9 - ELECTRONIC DOCUMENTS
9.1 We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
9.2 You must tell us if your email address changes.
9.3 Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

SECTION 10 - COOPERATION
10.1 You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
10.2 You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

SECTION 11 - ARBITRATION
11.1 If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
11.2 Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

SECTION 12 - CUSTOMER SUPPORT
12.1 Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
12.2 Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

SECTION 13 - COMMUNICATION
13.1 We will communicate with you in English.
13.2 We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

SECTION 14 - GEOGRAPHICAL LIMITS
14.1 Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
14.2 Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

SECTION 15 - COMPENSATION SCHEME
15.1 We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
15.2 If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

SECTION 16 - RENTAL CAR EXCESS
16.1 If you hire a car during the trip, we will reimburse any excess you must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.
16.2 This section applies only to cars hired from a licensed rental company under a written agreement.

SECTION 17 - REASONABLE PRECAUTIONS
17.1 You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.

TRAVEL INSURANCE POLICY WORDING
Issued by Bluewater Assurance
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Bluewater Assurance and "the Insured Person" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Insurer, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
(b) Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
(c) Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
(d) Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
(e) Family means the Insured Person's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Insured Person.
(f) Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,500 metres.
(g) Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
(h) Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which the Insured Person received treatment or advice in the 3 months before the policy start date.
(i) Premium means the amount the Insured Person must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
(j) Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
(k) Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 6 hours.
(l) Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
(m) Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Insured Person's details, the covers the Insured Person bought and any extensions.
(n) Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
(o) Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
(p) Travelling companion means a person who has booked to travel with the Insured Person on the same trip.
(q) Trip means a journey that starts and ends in the Insured Person's home country during the policy period.
(r) Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(b) Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
(c) Trip Cancellation: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(d) Travel Delay: limit $500 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
(e) The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

Article 3. Baggage and Personal Belongings
(a) The Insurer will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to the Insured Person's baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Valuables under this section is $400 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $300 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

Article 4. Trip Cancellation
(a) The Insurer will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if the Insured Person must cancel the trip for a reason beyond the Insured Person's control.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 14 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $300 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before the Insured Person bought the policy.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation because the Insured Person no longer wish to travel.

Article 5. Severability
(a) If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

Article 6. Recovery of costs
(a) If the Insurer pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Insurer may ask the Insured Person to repay the amount.

Article 7. Other insurance
(a) If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Insurer will pay only the Insurer's proportionate share.
(b) The Insured Person must tell the Insurer about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Insured Person makes a claim.

Article 8. Taxes
(a) The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
(b) If the tax rate changes, the Insurer may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

Article 9. Notices
(a) Any notice the Insurer gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Insurer holds.
(b) Notices from the Insured Person should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

Article 10. Waiver
(a) If the Insurer does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Insurer has given up the right to enforce it later.

Article 11. Joint policyholders
(a) Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
(b) A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

Article 12. Cancellation
(a) The Insured Person can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
(b) After the first 14 days the Insured Person can cancel at any time; the Insurer will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $30.
(c) The Insurer can cancel this policy by giving the Insured Person 30 days' written notice to the last address the Insurer holds.

Article 13. Compensation scheme
(a) The Insurer is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
(b) If the Insurer cannot meet the Insurer's obligations, the Insured Person may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

Article 14. Governing law
(a) This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
(b) Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

Article 15. Complaints
(a) If the Insured Person has a complaint, the Insured Person should first contact the Insurer's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
(b) The Insurer will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
(c) If the Insured Person remains dissatisfied, the Insured Person may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

Article 16. Optional cover: Travel Delay
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if the Insured Person's outbound departure is delayed.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Insured Person's schedule.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

Article 17. Environmental commitment
(a) Where practical, the Insurer will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
(b) The Insured Person may ask for a new part instead, and the Insurer will tell the Insured Person whether any additional cost would apply.

Article 18. Interest
(a) The Insurer will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

Article 19. Emergency Medical Expenses
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $250 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $300 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for any claim arising from the Insured Person's being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

Article 20. Discounts
(a) Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
(b) If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Insurer may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

Article 21. Third-party administrators
(a) The Insurer may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Insurer's behalf.
(b) Any company the Insurer appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

Article 22. How to read this document
(a) This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
(b) Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
(c) Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

Article 23. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Insured Person.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

Article 24. Claims documents
(a) The Insured Person must provide, at the Insured Person's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Insurer reasonably ask for.
(b) The Insurer may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

Article 25. Accessibility
(a) This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

Article 26. Instalment agreements
(a) If the Insured Person pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
(b) Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

Article 27. Reasonable precautions
(a) The Insured Person must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
(b) The Insured Person must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

Article 28. Automatic renewal
(a) Unless the Insured Person tells the Insurer otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Insurer holds.
(b) The Insured Person can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Insurer's helpline.

Article 29. Emergency assistance
(a) The Insurer's emergency assistance service is available 24 hours a day on the number shown in the schedule.
(b) The Insured Person must contact the assistance service before being admitted to hospital as an in-patient, unless it is an emergency.
(c) The assistance service can arrange payment guarantees, interpreters and transport home.

Article 30. Rental car excess
(a) If the Insured Person hires a car during the trip, the Insurer will reimburse any excess the Insured Person must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.
(b) This section applies only to cars hired from a licensed rental company under a written agreement.

Article 31. Making a claim
(a) The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 90 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(b) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(c) The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

Article 32. Legal expenses abroad
(a) The Insurer will pay legal costs to pursue compensation for the Insured Person's injury or death caused by a third party during the trip.
(b) The Insurer will not pay legal costs unless the Insurer's legal adviser agrees that the claim has a reasonable prospect of success.

Article 33. Data protection
(a) The Insurer will use the personal information the Insured Person provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
(b) The Insurer will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
(c) The Insured Person can ask for a copy of the personal information the Insurer holds by writing to the Insurer's data protection officer.

SINGLE-TRIP TRAVEL PROTECTION PLAN
Issued by Compass Mutual
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Compass Mutual and "the Insured Person" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Insurer, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
(b) Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
(c) Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
(d) Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,500 metres.
(e) Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
(f) Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
(g) Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which the Insured Person received treatment or advice in the 3 months before the policy start date.
(h) Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
(i) Public transport means any scheduled train, bus, coach, ferry or aircraft.
(j) Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 6 hours.
(k) Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
(l) Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
(m) Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
(n) Territory means the countries in which cover applies, as shown in the schedule.
(o) Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(b) Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $50,000 per incident; excess $150 per claim.
(c) Trip Cancellation: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(d) Travel Delay: limit $300 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
(e) The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

Article 3. Optional cover: Travel Delay
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if the Insured Person's outbound departure is delayed.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Insured Person's schedule.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

Article 4. Baggage and Personal Belongings
(a) The Insurer will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to the Insured Person's baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Valuables under this section is $250 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $300 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

Article 5. Trip Cancellation
(a) The Insurer will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if the Insured Person must cancel the trip for a reason beyond the Insured Person's control.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 7 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $300 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before the Insured Person bought the policy.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation because the Insured Person no longer wish to travel.

Article 6. Emergency Medical Expenses
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $250 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $500 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for any claim arising from the Insured Person's being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

Article 7. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Insured Person.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

Article 8. Making a claim
(a) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(b) The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 21 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(c) The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

Article 9. Other insurance
(a) If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Insurer will pay only the Insurer's proportionate share.
(b) The Insured Person must tell the Insurer about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Insured Person makes a claim.

Article 10. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
(a) A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

Article 11. Communication
(a) The Insurer will communicate with the Insured Person in English.
(b) The Insurer may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

Article 12. Market conditions
(a) If the replacement item is no longer available, the Insurer will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

Article 13. Claims documents
(a) The Insured Person must provide, at the Insured Person's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Insurer reasonably ask for.
(b) The Insurer may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

Article 14. Discounts
(a) Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
(b) If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Insurer may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

Article 15. Compensation scheme
(a) The Insurer is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
(b) If the Insurer cannot meet the Insurer's obligations, the Insured Person may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

Article 16. Change of address
(a) The Insured Person must tell the Insurer within 30 days if the Insured Person changes the Insured Person's address.
(b) The Insurer may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

Article 17. Sanctions
(a) The Insurer will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Insurer to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

Article 18. Governing law
(a) This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
(b) Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

Article 19. Fraud
(a) If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Insurer will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
(b) The Insurer may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

Article 20. Environmental commitment
(a) Where practical, the Insurer will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
(b) The Insured Person may ask for a new part instead, and the Insurer will tell the Insured Person whether any additional cost would apply.

Article 21. Interpretation
(a) Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
(b) Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
(c) Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

Article 22. Exchange of information
(a) To prevent fraud, the Insurer may check the details the Insured Person gives against public records and industry databases.
(b) The Insurer may contact previous insurers to confirm the Insured Person's claims history.

# Annual Multi-Trip Travel Cover
Issued by Compass Mutual

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.

- **2.1** Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
