## 3. Baggage and Personal Belongings
- **3.1** We will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to your baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
- **3.2** The most we will pay for Valuables under this section is $250 per incident.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $300 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
- **3.5** We will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
- **3.6** We will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

## 4. Fraud
- **4.1** If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
- **4.2** We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

## 5. Other insurance
- **5.1** If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
- **5.2** You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

## 6. Notices
- **6.1** Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
- **6.2** Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

## 7. Accessibility
- **7.1** This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

## 8. Exchange of information
- **8.1** To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
- **8.2** We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

## 9. Personal liability
- **9.1** We will pay damages you become legally liable to pay for accidental injury to another person or accidental damage to their property during the trip.
- **9.2** This section does not cover liability arising from the use of motor vehicles, boats or aircraft.
- **9.3** The most we will pay under this section is $1,000,000 for all claims arising from one event.

## 10. Subrogation
- **10.1** We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
- **10.2** We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

## 11. Interpretation
- **11.1** Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
- **11.2** Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
- **11.3** Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

## 12. Assignment
- **12.1** You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

## 13. Premium payment
- **13.1** You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
- **13.2** If an instalment is not paid within 21 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

## 14. Emergency Medical Expenses
- **14.1** We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
- **14.2** The most we will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $250 per incident.
- **14.3** The most we will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $300 per incident.
- **14.4** We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
- **14.5** We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
- **14.6** We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

## 15. Recovery of costs
- **15.1** If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

## 16. Compensation scheme
- **16.1** We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
- **16.2** If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

## 17. Change of address
- **17.1** You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
- **17.2** We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

## 18. Payment of claims
- **18.1** We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
- **18.2** We aim to pay accepted claims within 10 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

## 19. Sanctions
- **19.1** We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

## 20. Optional cover: Travel Delay
- **20.1** We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
- **20.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **20.3** We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

## 21. Discounts
- **21.1** Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
- **21.2** If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

## 22. Cancellation
- **22.1** You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
- **22.2** After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
- **22.3** We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

## 23. Trip Cancellation
- **23.1** We will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if you must cancel the trip for a reason beyond your control.
- **23.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 7 days after the policy start date.
- **23.3** The most we will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $300 per incident.
- **23.4** We will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before you bought the policy.
- **23.5** We will not pay for cancellation because you no longer wish to travel.

## 24. Repatriation
- **24.1** If our medical adviser agrees it is necessary, we will arrange and pay for you to be brought home.
- **24.2** We will decide the method of transport and the time of repatriation after speaking to the treating doctor.

## 25. Changes in circumstances
- **25.1** You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
- **25.2** We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

## 26. Geographical limits
- **26.1** Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
- **26.2** Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

## 27. General exclusions
- **27.1** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **27.2** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
- **27.3** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
- **27.4** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

## 28. Electronic documents
- **28.1** We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
- **28.2** You must tell us if your email address changes.
- **28.3** Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

## 29. Records and evidence
- **29.1** You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
- **29.2** Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
- **29.3** We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

## 30. Waiver
- **30.1** If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

## 31. Salvage
- **31.1** When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
- **31.2** If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

## 32. Claims documents
- **32.1** You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
- **32.2** We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

## 33. Currency
- **33.1** All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
- **33.2** Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

## 34. Communication
- **34.1** We will communicate with you in English.
- **34.2** We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

## 35. Joint policyholders
- **35.1** Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
- **35.2** A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

## 36. Taxes
- **36.1** The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
- **36.2** If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

## 37. Reasonable precautions
- **37.1** You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
- **37.2** You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

## 38. Emergency assistance
- **38.1** Our emergency assistance service is available 24 hours a day on the number shown in the schedule.
- **38.2** You must contact the assistance service before being admitted to hospital as an in-patient, unless it is an emergency.
- **38.3** The assistance service can arrange payment guarantees, interpreters and transport home.

## 39. Environmental commitment
- **39.1** Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
- **39.2** You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

## 40. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
- **40.1** A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

## 41. Instalment agreements
- **41.1** If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
- **41.2** Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

## 42. Data protection
- **42.1** We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
- **42.2** We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
- **42.3** You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

## 43. Interest
- **43.1** We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

## 44. Rental car excess
- **44.1** If you hire a car during the trip, we will reimburse any excess you must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.
- **44.2** This section applies only to cars hired from a licensed rental company under a written agreement.

## 45. Arbitration
- **45.1** If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
- **45.2** Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

## 46. Making a claim
- **46.1** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **46.2** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **46.3** You must notify us of a claim within 14 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

## 47. Legal expenses abroad
- **47.1** We will pay legal costs to pursue compensation for your injury or death caused by a third party during the trip.
- **47.2** We will not pay legal costs unless our legal adviser agrees that the claim has a reasonable prospect of success.

## 48. How to read this document
- **48.1** This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
- **48.2** Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
- **48.3** Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

## 49. Severability
- **49.1** If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

EMPLOYEE HEALTH BENEFITS PLAN: SUMMARY PLAN DESCRIPTION
Issued by the Staff Welfare Fund

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Plan, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
I.2  Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
I.3  Family means the Member's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Member.
I.4  Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
I.5  Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
I.6  Hearing aid replacement period means 24 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
I.7  Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
I.8  Limit means the most the Plan will pay for all claims under a section arising from one treatment.
I.9  Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
I.10  Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
I.11  Network provider means a practitioner or clinic that has an agreement with the Plan to provide treatment.
I.12  Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
I.13  Plan year means the twelve months starting on the Member's coverage start date.
I.14  Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Member's schedule.
I.15  Premium means the amount the Member must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
I.16  Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
I.17  Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
I.18  Replacement period means 12 months from the date of the Member's last eyewear claim.
I.19  Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Member's details, the covers the Member bought and any extensions.

PART II: Limits and deductible
II.1  Dental Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
II.2  Vision Care: limit $400 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
II.3  Therapy Services: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
II.4  Hearing Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
II.5  Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

PART III: Customer support
III.1  The Plan's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
III.2  Outside these hours the Member can leave a message and the Plan will call back on the next working day.

PART IV: Coordination of benefits
IV.1  If a treatment is also covered by another plan, the Plan will pay only the part of the cost that the other plan does not pay.
IV.2  The Member must tell the Plan about any other plan that covers the Member or the Member's dependants.

PART V: Leaving the plan
V.1  Cover ends on the day the Member's employment ends or the day the Member stops being eligible, whichever is earlier.
V.2  Claims for treatment received before cover ended may be submitted up to 90 days afterwards.

PART VI: Automatic renewal
VI.1  Unless the Member tells the Plan otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Plan holds.
VI.2  The Member can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Plan's helpline.

PART VII: Reasonable precautions
VII.1  The Member must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
VII.2  The Member must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

PART VIII: Exchange of information
VIII.1  To prevent fraud, the Plan may check the details the Member gives against public records and industry databases.
VIII.2  The Plan may contact previous insurers to confirm the Member's claims history.

PART IX: Cancellation
IX.1  The Member can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
IX.2  After the first 14 days the Member can cancel at any time; the Plan will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
IX.3  The Plan can cancel this policy by giving the Member 30 days' written notice to the last address the Plan holds.

PART X: Therapy Services
X.1  The Plan will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
X.2  The most the Plan will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $300 per treatment.
X.3  The Plan will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
X.4  The Plan will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

PART XI: Records and evidence
XI.1  The Member should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
XI.2  Where proof of value is missing, the Plan may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
XI.3  The Plan may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

PART XII: Cooperation
XII.1  The Member must give the Plan all the help and information the Plan reasonably need to settle a claim.
XII.2  The Member must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Plan's written permission.

PART XIII: Taxes
XIII.1  The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
XIII.2  If the tax rate changes, the Plan may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

PART XIV: Accessibility
XIV.1  This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

PART XV: Interest
XV.1  The Plan will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

PART XVI: Sanctions
XVI.1  The Plan will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Plan to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

PART XVII: Premium payment
XVII.1  The Member must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
XVII.2  If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, the Plan may cancel the policy after giving notice.

PART XVIII: Appeals
XVIII.1  If the Plan declines all or part of a claim, the Member may appeal in writing within 60 days of the decision.
XVIII.2  An appeal will be reviewed by someone who was not involved in the original decision.
XVIII.3  The Plan will give the Member a written decision on the appeal within 30 days.

PART XIX: Assignment
XIX.1  The Member cannot transfer the Member's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Plan's written consent.

PART XX: Dental Care
XX.1  The Plan will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
XX.2  No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 90 days after the policy start date.
XX.3  The most the Plan will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.
XX.4  The most the Plan will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $600 per treatment.
XX.5  The Plan will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
XX.6  The Plan will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

PART XXI: Interpretation
XXI.1  Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
XXI.2  Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
XXI.3  Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

PART XXII: Third-party administrators
XXII.1  The Plan may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Plan's behalf.
XXII.2  Any company the Plan appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

PART XXIII: Vision Care
XXIII.1  The Plan will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
XXIII.2  The most the Plan will pay for Frames under this section is $150 per treatment.
XXIII.3  The Plan will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
XXIII.4  The Plan will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

PART XXIV: Complaints
XXIV.1  If the Member has a complaint, the Member should first contact the Plan's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
XXIV.2  The Plan will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
XXIV.3  If the Member remains dissatisfied, the Member may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

PART XXV: Waiver
XXV.1  If the Plan does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Plan has given up the right to enforce it later.

PART XXVI: Optional cover: Hearing Care
XXVI.1  The Plan will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
XXVI.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Member's schedule.
XXVI.3  The most the Plan will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $150 per treatment.
XXVI.4  The Plan will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

PART XXVII: Wellness allowance
XXVII.1  Each plan year the Member may claim up to $250 towards a gym membership or fitness class.
XXVII.2  The wellness allowance is not subject to any deductible and does not count towards other limits.

PART XXVIII: Claims documents
XXVIII.1  The Member must provide, at the Member's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Plan reasonably ask for.
XXVIII.2  The Plan may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

PART XXIX: Data protection
XXIX.1  The Plan will use the personal information the Member provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
XXIX.2  The Plan will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
XXIX.3  The Member can ask for a copy of the personal information the Plan holds by writing to the Plan's data protection officer.

PART XXX: Electronic documents
XXX.1  The Plan will send documents by email unless the Member asks for paper copies.
XXX.2  The Member must tell the Plan if the Member's email address changes.
XXX.3  Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

PART XXXI: Compensation scheme
XXXI.1  The Plan is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
XXXI.2  If the Plan cannot meet the Plan's obligations, the Member may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

PART XXXII: Fraud
XXXII.1  If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Plan will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
XXXII.2  The Plan may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

PART XXXIII: Recovery of costs
XXXIII.1  If the Plan pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Plan may ask the Member to repay the amount.

PART XXXIV: Market conditions
XXXIV.1  If the replacement item is no longer available, the Plan will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

PART XXXV: Notices
XXXV.1  Any notice the Plan gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Plan holds.
XXXV.2  Notices from the Member should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

PART XXXVI: Joint policyholders
XXXVI.1  Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
XXXVI.2  A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

PART XXXVII: Change of address
XXXVII.1  The Member must tell the Plan within 30 days if the Member changes the Member's address.
XXXVII.2  The Plan may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

PART XXXVIII: Eligibility
XXXVIII.1  Employees who work at least 20 hours a week are eligible to join the plan from their first day of employment.
XXXVIII.2  Contractors, agency workers and employees on unpaid leave of more than three months are not eligible.

PART XXXIX: Geographical limits
XXXIX.1  Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
XXXIX.2  Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

PART XXXX: General exclusions
XXXX.1  The Plan will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Member.
XXXX.2  The Plan will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
XXXX.3  The Plan will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
XXXX.4  The Plan will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
XXXX.5  The Plan will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Plan from paying.

PART XXXXI: Currency
XXXXI.1  All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
XXXXI.2  Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

PART XXXXII: Changes in circumstances
XXXXII.1  The Member must tell the Plan as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
XXXXII.2  The Plan may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

PART XXXXIII: Making a claim
XXXXIII.1  The Member must notify the Plan of a claim within 90 days of the treatment. The Plan will not pay any claim notified after that time.
XXXXIII.2  The Member must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
XXXXIII.3  The Plan may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

PART XXXXIV: Inflation
XXXXIV.1  The Plan may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
XXXXIV.2  Any adjustment will be shown in the Member's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

PART XXXXV: Other insurance
XXXXV.1  If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Plan will pay only the Plan's proportionate share.
XXXXV.2  The Member must tell the Plan about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Member makes a claim.

PART XXXXVI: Subrogation
XXXXVI.1  The Plan will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Member's name the defence or settlement of any claim.
XXXXVI.2  The Plan can take action in the Member's name to recover any payment the Plan makes from anyone responsible for the loss.

PART XXXXVII: Governing law
XXXXVII.1  This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
XXXXVII.2  Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

PART XXXXVIII: Duty of fair presentation
XXXXVIII.1  The Member must answer all questions the Plan asks honestly and to the best of the Member's knowledge.
XXXXVIII.2  If the Member gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Plan may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
XXXXVIII.3  If the Member gives incorrect information carelessly, the Plan may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

PART XXXXIX: Payment of claims
XXXXIX.1  The Plan will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Member's name.
XXXXIX.2  The Plan aims to pay accepted claims within 10 working days of receiving all the documents the Plan needs.

PART XXXXX: Discounts
XXXXX.1  Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
XXXXX.2  If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Plan may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

ANNUAL MULTI-TRIP TRAVEL COVER
Issued by Compass Mutual

SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS
1.1 Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
1.2 Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 3,000 metres.
1.3 Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
1.4 Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which you received treatment or advice in the 6 months before the policy start date.
1.5 Public transport means any scheduled train, bus, coach, ferry or aircraft.
1.6 Trip means a journey that starts and ends in your home country during the policy period.

SECTION 2 - LIMITS AND EXCESS
2.1 Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.2 Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $25,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.3 Trip Cancellation: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.4 Travel Delay: limit $750 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
2.5 Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

SECTION 3 - EMERGENCY MEDICAL EXPENSES
3.1 We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
3.2 The most we will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $250 per incident.
3.3 The most we will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $500 per incident.
3.4 We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
3.5 We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
3.6 We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

SECTION 4 - GENERAL EXCLUSIONS
4.1 We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
4.2 We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
4.3 We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

SECTION 5 - MAKING A CLAIM
5.1 You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
5.2 You must notify us of a claim within 21 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
5.3 We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

SECTION 6 - CHANGE OF ADDRESS
6.1 You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
6.2 We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

SECTION 7 - MISSED DEPARTURE
7.1 We will pay reasonable additional travel and accommodation costs to reach your destination if you arrive too late to board your booked transport because public transport fails.
7.2 You must allow enough time to reach the departure point, and must obtain written confirmation of the delay from the transport operator.

SECTION 8 - SANCTIONS
8.1 We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

SECTION 9 - ELECTRONIC DOCUMENTS
9.1 We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
9.2 You must tell us if your email address changes.
9.3 Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

SECTION 10 - COOPERATION
10.1 You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
10.2 You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

SECTION 11 - ARBITRATION
11.1 If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
11.2 Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

SECTION 12 - CUSTOMER SUPPORT
12.1 Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
12.2 Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

SECTION 13 - COMMUNICATION
13.1 We will communicate with you in English.
13.2 We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

SECTION 14 - GEOGRAPHICAL LIMITS
14.1 Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
14.2 Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

SECTION 15 - COMPENSATION SCHEME
15.1 We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
15.2 If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

SECTION 16 - RENTAL CAR EXCESS
16.1 If you hire a car during the trip, we will reimburse any excess you must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.
16.2 This section applies only to cars hired from a licensed rental company under a written agreement.

SECTION 17 - REASONABLE PRECAUTIONS
17.1 You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
17.2 You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

SECTION 18 - INSTALMENT AGREEMENTS
18.1 If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
18.2 Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

SECTION 19 - RENEWAL
19.1 We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
19.2 We are not obliged to offer renewal.

SECTION 20 - JOINT POLICYHOLDERS
20.1 Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
20.2 A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

SECTION 21 - INTERPRETATION
21.1 Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
21.2 Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
21.3 Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

SECTION 22 - EMERGENCY ASSISTANCE
22.1 Our emergency assistance service is available 24 hours a day on the number shown in the schedule.
22.2 You must contact the assistance service before being admitted to hospital as an in-patient, unless it is an emergency.
22.3 The assistance service can arrange payment guarantees, interpreters and transport home.

SECTION 23 - REPATRIATION
23.1 If our medical adviser agrees it is necessary, we will arrange and pay for you to be brought home.
23.2 We will decide the method of transport and the time of repatriation after speaking to the treating doctor.

SECTION 24 - CLAIMS DOCUMENTS
24.1 You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
24.2 We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

SECTION 25 - RECOVERY OF COSTS
25.1 If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

SECTION 26 - PAYMENT OF CLAIMS
26.1 We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
26.2 We aim to pay accepted claims within 10 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

SECTION 27 - RECORDS AND EVIDENCE
27.1 You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
27.2 Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
27.3 We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS
1.1 Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.

1.13 Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
1.14 Plan year means the twelve months starting on your coverage start date.
1.15 Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
1.16 Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
1.17 Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
1.18 Registered practitioner means a practitioner registered with the professional body for their discipline.
1.19 Replacement period means 12 months from the date of your last eyewear claim.
1.20 Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
1.21 Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

SECTION 2 - LIMITS AND DEDUCTIBLE
2.1 Dental Care: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
2.2 Vision Care: limit $300 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
2.3 Therapy Services: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
2.4 Hearing Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
2.5 The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

SECTION 3 - DENTAL CARE
3.1 We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
3.2 No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 90 days after the policy start date.
3.3 The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.
3.4 The most we will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $600 per treatment.
3.5 We will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
3.6 We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

SECTION 4 - THERAPY SERVICES
4.1 We will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
4.2 The most we will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $300 per treatment.
4.3 We will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
4.4 We will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

SECTION 5 - OPTIONAL COVER: HEARING CARE
5.1 We will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
5.2 This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
5.3 The most we will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $100 per treatment.
5.4 We will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

SECTION 6 - VISION CARE
6.1 We will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
6.2 The most we will pay for Frames under this section is $150 per treatment.
6.3 We will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
6.4 We will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

SECTION 7 - GENERAL EXCLUSIONS
7.1 We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
7.2 We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
7.3 We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
7.4 We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
7.5 We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
7.6 We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

SECTION 8 - MAKING A CLAIM
8.1 You must notify us of a claim within 60 days of the treatment. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
8.2 We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
8.3 You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

SECTION 9 - COMMUNICATION
9.1 We will communicate with you in English.
9.2 We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

SECTION 10 - CLAIMS DOCUMENTS
10.1 You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
10.2 We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

SECTION 11 - MARKET CONDITIONS
11.1 If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

SECTION 12 - RENEWAL
12.1 We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
12.2 We are not obliged to offer renewal.

SECTION 13 - COORDINATION OF BENEFITS
13.1 If a treatment is also covered by another plan, we will pay only the part of the cost that the other plan does not pay.
13.2 You must tell us about any other plan that covers you or your dependants.

SECTION 14 - RECOVERY OF COSTS
14.1 If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

SECTION 15 - WELLNESS ALLOWANCE
15.1 Each plan year you may claim up to $100 towards a gym membership or fitness class.
15.2 The wellness allowance is not subject to any deductible and does not count towards other limits.

SECTION 16 - CONTRACTS (RIGHTS OF THIRD PARTIES)
16.1 A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

SECTION 17 - COMPENSATION SCHEME
17.1 We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
17.2 If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

SECTION 18 - TAXES
18.1 The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
18.2 If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

SECTION 19 - GOVERNING LAW
19.1 This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
19.2 Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

SECTION 20 - AUTOMATIC RENEWAL
20.1 Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
20.2 You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

SECTION 21 - SALVAGE
21.1 When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
21.2 If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

SECTION 22 - JOINT POLICYHOLDERS
22.1 Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
22.2 A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

SECTION 23 - SUBROGATION
23.1 We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
23.2 We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

SECTION 24 - COMPLAINTS
24.1 If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
24.2 We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
24.3 If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

SECTION 25 - WAIVER
25.1 If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

SECTION 26 - DISCOUNTS
26.1 Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
26.2 If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

SECTION 27 - ELIGIBILITY
27.1 Employees who work at least 20 hours a week are eligible to join the plan from their first day of employment.
27.2 Contractors, agency workers and employees on unpaid leave of more than three months are not eligible.

SECTION 28 - INFLATION
28.1 We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
28.2 Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

SECTION 29 - APPEALS
29.1 If we decline all or part of a claim, you may appeal in writing within 60 days of the decision.
29.2 An appeal will be reviewed by someone who was not involved in the original decision.
29.3 We will give you a written decision on the appeal within 30 days.

SECTION 30 - EXCHANGE OF INFORMATION
30.1 To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
30.2 We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

SECTION 31 - GEOGRAPHICAL LIMITS
31.1 Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
31.2 Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

SECTION 32 - DUTY OF FAIR PRESENTATION
32.1 You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
32.2 If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
32.3 If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

SECTION 33 - NOTICES
33.1 Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
33.2 Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

SECTION 34 - PAYMENT OF CLAIMS
34.1 We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
34.2 We aim to pay accepted claims within 10 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

SECTION 35 - ARBITRATION
35.1 If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
35.2 Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

SECTION 36 - SANCTIONS
36.1 We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

SECTION 37 - INTERPRETATION
37.1 Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
37.2 Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
37.3 Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

SECTION 38 - CURRENCY
38.1 All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
38.2 Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

SECTION 39 - REASONABLE PRECAUTIONS
39.1 You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
39.2 You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

SECTION 40 - INTEREST
40.1 We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

SECTION 41 - CHANGE OF ADDRESS
41.1 You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
41.2 We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

SECTION 42 - FRAUD
42.1 If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
42.2 We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

SECTION 43 - CUSTOMER SUPPORT
43.1 Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
43.2 Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

SECTION 44 - CHANGES IN CIRCUMSTANCES
44.1 You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
44.2 We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

SECTION 45 - DEPENDANTS
45.1 You may enrol dependants at the start of each plan year or within 30 days of a qualifying life event.
45.2 Benefits paid for dependants count towards the same annual limits as your own claims.

SECTION 46 - PREMIUM PAYMENT
46.1 You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
46.2 If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

SECTION 47 - ELECTRONIC DOCUMENTS
47.1 We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
47.2 You must tell us if your email address changes.
47.3 Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

SECTION 48 - RECORDS AND EVIDENCE
48.1 You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
48.2 Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
48.3 We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

CASE PRESENTATION B
# Annual Multi-Trip Travel Cover
Issued by Bluewater Assurance

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
- **1.2** Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
- **1.3** Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
- **1.4** Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,500 metres.
- **1.5** Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
- **1.6** Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
- **1.7** Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
- **1.8** Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
- **1.9** Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which you received treatment or advice in the 12 months before the policy start date.
- **1.10** Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
- **1.11** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.12** Public transport means any scheduled train, bus, coach, ferry or aircraft.
- **1.13** Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 6 hours.
- **1.14** Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
- **1.15** Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
- **1.16** Territory means the countries in which cover applies, as shown in the schedule.
- **1.17** Travelling companion means a person who has booked to travel with you on the same trip.
- **1.18** Trip means a journey that starts and ends in your home country during the policy period.
- **1.19** Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $1,500 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.2** Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $25,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.3** Trip Cancellation: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.4** Travel Delay: limit $300 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.5** The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Waiver
- **3.1** If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

## 4. Baggage and Personal Belongings
- **4.1** We will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to your baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
- **4.2** The most we will pay for Valuables under this section is $400 per incident.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $450 per incident.
- **4.4** We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
- **4.5** We will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
- **4.6** We will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

## 5. Automatic renewal
- **5.1** Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
- **5.2** You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

## 6. Duty of fair presentation
- **6.1** You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
- **6.2** If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
- **6.3** If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

## 7. Sanctions
- **7.1** We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

## 8. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
- **8.1** A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

## 9. Discounts
- **9.1** Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
- **9.2** If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

## 10. Changes in circumstances
- **10.1** You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
- **10.2** We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

## 11. Data protection
- **11.1** We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
- **11.2** We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
- **11.3** You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

## 12. Optional cover: Travel Delay
- **12.1** We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
- **12.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **12.3** We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

## 13. Market conditions
- **13.1** If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

## 14. Emergency Medical Expenses
- **14.1** We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
- **14.2** The most we will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $400 per incident.
- **14.3** The most we will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $500 per incident.
- **14.4** We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
- **14.5** We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
- **14.6** We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

## 15. Severability
- **15.1** If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

## 16. Recovery of costs
- **16.1** If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

## 17. Change of address
- **17.1** You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
- **17.2** We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

## 18. Salvage
- **18.1** When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
- **18.2** If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

## 19. Trip Cancellation
- **19.1** We will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if you must cancel the trip for a reason beyond your control.
- **19.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 10 days after the policy start date.
- **19.3** The most we will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $200 per incident.
- **19.4** We will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before you bought the policy.
- **19.5** We will not pay for cancellation because you no longer wish to travel.

## 20. Accessibility
- **20.1** This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

## 21. Rental car excess
- **21.1** If you hire a car during the trip, we will reimburse any excess you must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.
- **21.2** This section applies only to cars hired from a licensed rental company under a written agreement.

## 22. Cooperation
- **22.1** You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
- **22.2** You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

## 23. Notices
- **23.1** Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
- **23.2** Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

## 24. Geographical limits
- **24.1** Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
- **24.2** Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

## 25. General exclusions
- **25.1** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
- **25.2** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
- **25.3** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **25.4** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
- **25.5** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
- **25.6** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

## 26. Emergency assistance
- **26.1** Our emergency assistance service is available 24 hours a day on the number shown in the schedule.
- **26.2** You must contact the assistance service before being admitted to hospital as an in-patient, unless it is an emergency.
- **26.3** The assistance service can arrange payment guarantees, interpreters and transport home.

## 27. Fraud
- **27.1** If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
- **27.2** We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

## 28. Legal expenses abroad
- **28.1** We will pay legal costs to pursue compensation for your injury or death caused by a third party during the trip.
- **28.2** We will not pay legal costs unless our legal adviser agrees that the claim has a reasonable prospect of success.

## 29. Making a claim
- **29.1** You must notify us of a claim within 60 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **29.2** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **29.3** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

## 30. Communication
- **30.1** We will communicate with you in English.
- **30.2** We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

Hello,

My policy started on June 4, 2026 and my schedule lists Baggage and Personal Belongings, Emergency Medical Expenses, Trip Cancellation, Travel Delay (extensions: none). Aiko

HOME CONTENTS INSURANCE POLICY
Issued by Hearthstone Insurance plc
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Hearthstone Insurance plc and "the Policyholder" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
(b) Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Insurer, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
(c) Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
(d) Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
(e) Contents means household goods and personal possessions that belong to the Policyholder or the Policyholder's family.
(f) Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
(g) Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
(h) High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
(i) Home means the private residence at the address shown in the schedule.
(j) Limit means the most the Insurer will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
(k) Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Policyholder's schedule.
(l) Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
(m) Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
(n) Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Policyholder's details, the covers the Policyholder bought and any extensions.
(o) Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
(p) Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 60 consecutive days.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(b) Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
(c) Accidental Damage: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(d) Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
(e) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Contents temporarily removed
(a) The Policyholder's contents are covered while temporarily removed from the home to another building in the same country, for up to 60 days.
(b) Contents in a student hall of residence are covered only if the student is a member of the Policyholder's family.

Article 4. Fraud
(a) If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Insurer will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
(b) The Insurer may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

Article 5. Cooperation
(a) The Policyholder must give the Insurer all the help and information the Insurer reasonably need to settle a claim.
(b) The Policyholder must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Insurer's written permission.

Article 6. Taxes
(a) The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
(b) If the tax rate changes, the Insurer may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

Article 7. Optional cover: Accidental Damage
(a) The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $750 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

Article 8. Escape of Water
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $2,000 per incident.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

Article 9. Claims documents
(a) The Policyholder must provide, at the Policyholder's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Insurer reasonably ask for.
(b) The Insurer may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

Article 10. Theft
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $800 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

Article 11. Severability
(a) If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

Article 12. Flood
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

Article 13. Electronic documents
(a) The Insurer will send documents by email unless the Policyholder asks for paper copies.
(b) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer if the Policyholder's email address changes.
(c) Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

Article 14. Subrogation
(a) The Insurer will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Policyholder's name the defence or settlement of any claim.
(b) The Insurer can take action in the Policyholder's name to recover any payment the Insurer makes from anyone responsible for the loss.

Article 15. Automatic renewal
(a) Unless the Policyholder tells the Insurer otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Insurer holds.
(b) The Policyholder can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Insurer's helpline.

Article 16. Changes in circumstances
(a) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
(b) The Insurer may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

Article 17. Market conditions
(a) If the replacement item is no longer available, the Insurer will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

Article 18. Environmental commitment
(a) Where practical, the Insurer will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
(b) The Policyholder may ask for a new part instead, and the Insurer will tell the Policyholder whether any additional cost would apply.

Article 19. Tenant's improvements
(a) If the Policyholder rents the home, the Insurer will pay for damage to fixtures and fittings that the Policyholder installed and are responsible for.
(b) This cover applies only to improvements the Policyholder paid for, not to items provided by the landlord.

Article 20. Change of address
(a) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer within 30 days if the Policyholder changes the Policyholder's address.
(b) The Insurer may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

Article 21. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.

Article 22. Waiver
(a) If the Insurer does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Insurer has given up the right to enforce it later.

Article 23. Other insurance
(a) If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Insurer will pay only the Insurer's proportionate share.
(b) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Policyholder makes a claim.

Article 24. Third-party administrators
(a) The Insurer may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Insurer's behalf.
(b) Any company the Insurer appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

Article 25. Premium payment
(a) The Policyholder must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
(b) If an instalment is not paid within 21 days of its due date, the Insurer may cancel the policy after giving notice.

Article 26. Locks and keys
(a) If the keys to the Policyholder's home are lost or stolen, the Insurer will pay the cost of replacing the locks to the outside doors.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay under this clause is $500 for any one claim.

Article 27. Data protection
(a) The Insurer will use the personal information the Policyholder provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
(b) The Insurer will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
(c) The Policyholder can ask for a copy of the personal information the Insurer holds by writing to the Insurer's data protection officer.

Article 28. Sanctions
(a) The Insurer will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Insurer to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

Article 29. Freezer contents
(a) The Insurer will pay for food in a domestic freezer that spoils because of a rise or fall in temperature.
(b) The Insurer will not pay if the freezer is more than fifteen years old, or if the electricity supplier cut the supply deliberately.

Article 30. Customer support
(a) The Insurer's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
(b) Outside these hours the Policyholder can leave a message and the Insurer will call back on the next working day.

Article 31. Joint policyholders
(a) Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
(b) A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

Article 32. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
(a) A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

Article 33. Assignment
(a) The Policyholder cannot transfer the Policyholder's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Insurer's written consent.

Article 34. Garden and outdoor cover
(a) The Insurer will pay for plants, trees and shrubs in the garden of the home that are damaged by fire, lightning or theft.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by frost, storms, drought or animals.

Article 35. Cancellation
(a) The Policyholder can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
(b) After the first 14 days the Policyholder can cancel at any time; the Insurer will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
(c) The Insurer can cancel this policy by giving the Policyholder 30 days' written notice to the last address the Insurer holds.

Article 36. Renewal
(a) The Insurer will write to the Policyholder at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
(b) The Insurer is not obliged to offer renewal.

Article 37. Making a claim
(a) The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(b) The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 60 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(c) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

Article 38. Payment of claims
(a) The Insurer will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Policyholder's name.
(b) The Insurer aims to pay accepted claims within 10 working days of receiving all the documents the Insurer needs.

Article 39. Accessibility
(a) This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

Article 40. Duty of fair presentation
(a) The Policyholder must answer all questions the Insurer asks honestly and to the best of the Policyholder's knowledge.
(b) If the Policyholder gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Insurer may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
(c) If the Policyholder gives incorrect information carelessly, the Insurer may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

SECTION 15 - FRAUD

SECTION 16 - CLAIMS DOCUMENTS

16.2 We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

SECTION 18 - DATA AND BACKUPS

SECTION 21 - MARKET CONDITIONS
