EMPLOYEE HEALTH BENEFITS PLAN: SUMMARY PLAN DESCRIPTION
Issued by Cedar Benefits Services

SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS
1.1 Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
1.2 Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
1.3 Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
1.4 Hearing aid replacement period means 24 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
1.5 Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one treatment.
1.6 Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
1.7 Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
1.8 Network provider means a practitioner or clinic that has an agreement with us to provide treatment.
1.9 Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
1.10 Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
1.11 Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
1.12 Replacement period means 12 months from the date of your last eyewear claim.
1.13 Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
1.14 Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

SECTION 2 - LIMITS AND DEDUCTIBLE
2.1 Dental Care: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
2.2 Vision Care: limit $500 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
2.3 Therapy Services: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
2.4 Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
2.5 The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

SECTION 3 - DENTAL CARE
3.1 We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
3.2 No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
3.3 The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $750 per treatment.
3.4 The most we will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $800 per treatment.
3.5 We will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
3.6 We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

SECTION 4 - VISION CARE
4.1 We will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
4.2 The most we will pay for Frames under this section is $120 per treatment.
4.3 We will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
4.4 We will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

SECTION 5 - THERAPY SERVICES
5.1 We will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
5.2 The most we will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $300 per treatment.
5.3 We will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
5.4 We will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

SECTION 6 - OPTIONAL COVER: HEARING CARE
6.1 We will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
6.2 This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
6.3 The most we will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $150 per treatment.
6.4 We will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

SECTION 7 - GENERAL EXCLUSIONS
7.1 We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
7.2 We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
7.3 We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
7.4 We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
7.5 We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

SECTION 8 - MAKING A CLAIM
8.1 We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
8.2 You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
8.3 You must notify us of a claim within 21 days of the treatment. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

SECTION 9 - MARKET CONDITIONS
9.1 If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

SECTION 10 - TAXES
10.1 The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
10.2 If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

SECTION 11 - CONTRACTS (RIGHTS OF THIRD PARTIES)
11.1 A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

SECTION 12 - CLAIMS DOCUMENTS
12.1 You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
12.2 We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

SECTION 13 - SUBROGATION
13.1 We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
13.2 We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

SECTION 14 - ARBITRATION
14.1 If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
14.2 Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

SECTION 15 - CHANGE OF ADDRESS
15.1 You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
15.2 We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

SECTION 16 - ENVIRONMENTAL COMMITMENT
16.1 Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
16.2 You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

SECTION 17 - FRAUD
17.1 If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
17.2 We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

SECTION 18 - OTHER INSURANCE
18.1 If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
18.2 You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

SECTION 19 - ELECTRONIC DOCUMENTS
19.1 We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
19.2 You must tell us if your email address changes.
19.3 Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

SECTION 20 - DEPENDANTS
20.1 You may enrol dependants at the start of each plan year or within 30 days of a qualifying life event.
20.2 Benefits paid for dependants count towards the same annual limits as your own claims.

SECTION 21 - SEVERABILITY
21.1 If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

SECTION 22 - HOW TO READ THIS DOCUMENT
22.1 This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
22.2 Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
22.3 Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

SECTION 23 - CURRENCY
23.1 All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
23.2 Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

SECTION 24 - ASSIGNMENT
24.1 You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

SECTION 25 - CUSTOMER SUPPORT
25.1 Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
25.2 Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

SECTION 26 - JOINT POLICYHOLDERS
26.1 Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
26.2 A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

SECTION 27 - WELLNESS ALLOWANCE
27.1 Each plan year you may claim up to $250 towards a gym membership or fitness class.
27.2 The wellness allowance is not subject to any deductible and does not count towards other limits.

SECTION 28 - DUTY OF FAIR PRESENTATION
28.1 You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
28.2 If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
28.3 If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

SECTION 29 - ACCESSIBILITY
29.1 This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

SECTION 30 - LEAVING THE PLAN
30.1 Cover ends on the day your employment ends or the day you stop being eligible, whichever is earlier.
30.2 Claims for treatment received before cover ended may be submitted up to 90 days afterwards.

SECTION 31 - INSTALMENT AGREEMENTS
31.1 If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
31.2 Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

SECTION 32 - DISCOUNTS
32.1 Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
32.2 If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

SECTION 33 - SALVAGE
33.1 When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
33.2 If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

SECTION 34 - COORDINATION OF BENEFITS
34.1 If a treatment is also covered by another plan, we will pay only the part of the cost that the other plan does not pay.
34.2 You must tell us about any other plan that covers you or your dependants.

SECTION 35 - RECORDS AND EVIDENCE
35.1 You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
35.2 Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
35.3 We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

SECTION 36 - COOPERATION
36.1 You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
36.2 You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

SECTION 37 - ELIGIBILITY
37.1 Employees who work at least 20 hours a week are eligible to join the plan from their first day of employment.
37.2 Contractors, agency workers and employees on unpaid leave of more than three months are not eligible.

SECTION 38 - INFLATION
38.1 We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
38.2 Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

SECTION 39 - COMMUNICATION
39.1 We will communicate with you in English.
39.2 We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

SECTION 40 - REASONABLE PRECAUTIONS
40.1 You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
40.2 You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

SECTION 41 - CHANGES IN CIRCUMSTANCES
41.1 You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
41.2 We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

SECTION 42 - RECOVERY OF COSTS
42.1 If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

SECTION 43 - RENEWAL
43.1 We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
43.2 We are not obliged to offer renewal.

SECTION 44 - GOVERNING LAW
44.1 This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
44.2 Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

SECTION 45 - COMPENSATION SCHEME
45.1 We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
45.2 If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

SECTION 46 - GEOGRAPHICAL LIMITS
46.1 Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
46.2 Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

SECTION 47 - SANCTIONS
47.1 We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

SECTION 48 - NOTICES
48.1 Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
48.2 Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

SECTION 49 - INTEREST
49.1 We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

SECTION 50 - WAIVER
50.1 If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

SECTION 51 - DATA PROTECTION
51.1 We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
51.2 We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
51.3 You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

SECTION 52 - PREMIUM PAYMENT
52.1 You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
52.2 If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

SECTION 53 - THIRD-PARTY ADMINISTRATORS
53.1 We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
53.2 Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

SECTION 54 - CANCELLATION
54.1 You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
54.2 After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
54.3 We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

SECTION 55 - EXCHANGE OF INFORMATION
55.1 To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
55.2 We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

SECTION 56 - COMPLAINTS
56.1 If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
56.2 We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
56.3 If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

57.1 Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
57.2 Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.

state.policy:
GROUP HEALTH CASH PLAN
Issued by Wellspring Benefits Administration

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Plan, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
I.2  Dependant means the Member's spouse or partner, or a child under 21 who is enrolled in the plan.
I.3  Family means the Member's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Member.
I.4  Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
I.5  Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
I.6  Hearing aid replacement period means 36 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
I.7  Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
I.8  Limit means the most the Plan will pay for all claims under a section arising from one treatment.
I.9  Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
I.10  Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
I.11  Network provider means a practitioner or clinic that has an agreement with the Plan to provide treatment.
I.12  Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
I.13  Plan year means the twelve months starting on the Member's coverage start date.
I.14  Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Member's schedule.
I.15  Premium means the amount the Member must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
I.16  Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
I.17  Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
I.18  Replacement period means 12 months from the date of the Member's last eyewear claim.
I.19  Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Member's details, the covers the Member bought and any extensions.
I.20  Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

PART II: Limits and deductible
II.1  Dental Care: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
II.2  Vision Care: limit $300 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
II.3  Therapy Services: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
II.4  Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
II.5  Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

PART III: Payment of claims
III.1  The Plan will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Member's name.
III.2  The Plan aims to pay accepted claims within 10 working days of receiving all the documents the Plan needs.

PART IV: Fraud
IV.1  If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Plan will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
IV.2  The Plan may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

PART V: Compensation scheme
V.1  The Plan is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
V.2  If the Plan cannot meet the Plan's obligations, the Member may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

PART VI: Complaints
VI.1  If the Member has a complaint, the Member should first contact the Plan's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
VI.2  The Plan will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
VI.3  If the Member remains dissatisfied, the Member may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

PART VII: Therapy Services
VII.1  The Plan will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
VII.2  The most the Plan will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $300 per treatment.
VII.3  The Plan will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
VII.4  The Plan will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

PART VIII: Governing law
VIII.1  This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
VIII.2  Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

PART IX: Cooperation
IX.1  The Member must give the Plan all the help and information the Plan reasonably need to settle a claim.
IX.2  The Member must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Plan's written permission.

PART X: Duty of fair presentation
X.1  The Member must answer all questions the Plan asks honestly and to the best of the Member's knowledge.
X.2  If the Member gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Plan may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
X.3  If the Member gives incorrect information carelessly, the Plan may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

PART XI: Taxes
XI.1  The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
XI.2  If the tax rate changes, the Plan may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

PART XII: Optional cover: Hearing Care
XII.1  The Plan will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
XII.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Member's schedule.
XII.3  The most the Plan will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $100 per treatment.
XII.4  The Plan will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

PART XIII: Electronic documents
XIII.1  The Plan will send documents by email unless the Member asks for paper copies.
XIII.2  The Member must tell the Plan if the Member's email address changes.
XIII.3  Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

PART XIV: Arbitration
XIV.1  If the Plan accepts a claim but disagree with the Member about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
XIV.2  Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against the Plan.

PART XV: Vision Care
XV.1  The Plan will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
XV.2  The most the Plan will pay for Frames under this section is $120 per treatment.
XV.3  The Plan will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
XV.4  The Plan will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

PART XVI: Discounts
XVI.1  Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
XVI.2  If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Plan may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

PART XVII: Environmental commitment
XVII.1  Where practical, the Plan will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
XVII.2  The Member may ask for a new part instead, and the Plan will tell the Member whether any additional cost would apply.

PART XVIII: Other insurance
XVIII.1  If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Plan will pay only the Plan's proportionate share.
XVIII.2  The Member must tell the Plan about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Member makes a claim.

PART XIX: Dependants
XIX.1  The Member may enrol dependants at the start of each plan year or within 30 days of a qualifying life event.
XIX.2  Benefits paid for dependants count towards the same annual limits as the Member's own claims.

PART XX: Geographical limits
XX.1  Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
XX.2  Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

PART XXI: Interpretation
XXI.1  Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
XXI.2  Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
XXI.3  Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

PART XXII: Salvage
XXII.1  When the Plan replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Plan's property.
XXII.2  If stolen property is recovered after the Plan has paid a claim, the Member must tell the Plan and either return the payment or give the Plan the property.

PART XXIII: Instalment agreements
XXIII.1  If the Member pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
XXIII.2  Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

PART XXIV: Sanctions
XXIV.1  The Plan will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Plan to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

PART XXV: Claims documents
XXV.1  The Member must provide, at the Member's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Plan reasonably ask for.
XXV.2  The Plan may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

PART XXVI: Records and evidence
XXVI.1  The Member should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
XXVI.2  Where proof of value is missing, the Plan may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
XXVI.3  The Plan may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

PART XXVII: Third-party administrators
XXVII.1  The Plan may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Plan's behalf.
XXVII.2  Any company the Plan appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

PART XXVIII: Dental Care
XXVIII.1  The Plan will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
XXVIII.2  No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 90 days after the policy start date.
XXVIII.3  The most the Plan will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.
XXVIII.4  The most the Plan will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $600 per treatment.
XXVIII.5  The Plan will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
XXVIII.6  The Plan will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

PART XXIX: Premium payment
XXIX.1  The Member must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
XXIX.2  If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, the Plan may cancel the policy after giving notice.

PART XXX: General exclusions
XXX.1  The Plan will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Member.
XXX.2  The Plan will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
XXX.3  The Plan will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
XXX.4  The Plan will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

PART XXXI: Communication
XXXI.1  The Plan will communicate with the Member in English.
XXXI.2  The Plan may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

PART XXXII: Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
XXXII.1  A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

PART XXXIII: Interest
XXXIII.1  The Plan will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

PART XXXIV: Appeals
XXXIV.1  If the Plan declines all or part of a claim, the Member may appeal in writing within 60 days of the decision.
XXXIV.2  An appeal will be reviewed by someone who was not involved in the original decision.
XXXIV.3  The Plan will give the Member a written decision on the appeal within 30 days.

PART XXXV: Customer support
XXXV.1  The Plan's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
XXXV.2  Outside these hours the Member can leave a message and the Plan will call back on the next working day.

PART XXXVI: How to read this document
XXXVI.1  This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
XXXVI.2  Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
XXXVI.3  Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

PART XXXVII: Waiver
XXXVII.1  If the Plan does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Plan has given up the right to enforce it later.

PART XXXVIII: Renewal
XXXVIII.1  The Plan will write to the Member at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
XXXVIII.2  The Plan is not obliged to offer renewal.

PART XXXIX: Leaving the plan
XXXIX.1  Cover ends on the day the Member's employment ends or the day the Member stops being eligible, whichever is earlier.
XXXIX.2  Claims for treatment received before cover ended may be submitted up to 90 days afterwards.

PART XXXX: Recovery of costs
XXXX.1  If the Plan pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Plan may ask the Member to repay the amount.

PART XXXXI: Assignment
XXXXI.1  The Member cannot transfer the Member's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Plan's written consent.

PART XXXXII: Coordination of benefits
XXXXII.1  If a treatment is also covered by another plan, the Plan will pay only the part of the cost that the other plan does not pay.
XXXXII.2  The Member must tell the Plan about any other plan that covers the Member or the Member's dependants.

PART XXXXIII: Change of address
XXXXIII.1  The Member must tell the Plan within 30 days if the Member changes the Member's address.
XXXXIII.2  The Plan may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

PART XXXXIV: Inflation
XXXXIV.1  The Plan may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
XXXXIV.2  Any adjustment will be shown in the Member's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

PART XXXXV: Changes in circumstances
XXXXV.1  The Member must tell the Plan as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
XXXXV.2  The Plan may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

PART XXXXVI: Accessibility
XXXXVI.1  This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

PART XXXXVII: Automatic renewal
XXXXVII.1  Unless the Member tells the Plan otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Plan holds.
XXXXVII.2  The Member can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Plan's helpline.

PART XXXXVIII: Data protection
XXXXVIII.1  The Plan will use the personal information the Member provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
XXXXVIII.2  The Plan will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
XXXXVIII.3  The Member can ask for a copy of the personal information the Plan holds by writing to the Plan's data protection officer.

PART XXXXIX: Cancellation
XXXXIX.1  The Member can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
XXXXIX.2  After the first 14 days the Member can cancel at any time; the Plan will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
XXXXIX.3  The Plan can cancel this policy by giving the Member 30 days' written notice to the last address the Plan holds.

PART XXXXX: Eligibility
XXXXX.1  Employees who work at least 20 hours a week are eligible to join the plan from their first day of employment.
XXXXX.2  Contractors, agency workers and employees on unpaid leave of more than three months are not eligible.

PART XXXXXI: Severability
XXXXXI.1  If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

PART XXXXXII: Making a claim
XXXXXII.1  The Plan may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
XXXXXII.2  The Member must notify the Plan of a claim within 60 days of the treatment. The Plan will not pay any claim notified after that time.
XXXXXII.3  The Member must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

PART XXXXXIII: Joint policyholders
XXXXXIII.1  Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
XXXXXIII.2  A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

PART XXXXXIV: Notices
XXXXXIV.1  Any notice the Plan gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Plan holds.
XXXXXIV.2  Notices from the Member should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

PART XXXXXV: Market conditions
XXXXXV.1  If the replacement item is no longer available, the Plan will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

PART XXXXXVI: Exchange of information
XXXXXVI.1  To prevent fraud, the Plan may check the details the Member gives against public records and industry databases.
XXXXXVI.2  The Plan may contact previous insurers to confirm the Member's claims history.

PART XXXXXVII: Reasonable precautions
XXXXXVII.1  The Member must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
XXXXXVII.2  The Member must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

PART XXXXXVIII: Currency
XXXXXVIII.1  All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
XXXXXVIII.2  Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

PART XXXXXIX: Wellness allowance
XXXXXIX.1  Each plan year the Member may claim up to $250 towards a gym membership or fitness class.
XXXXXIX.2  The wellness allowance is not subject to any deductible and does not count towards other limits.

PART XXXXXX: Subrogation
XXXXXX.1  The Plan will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Member's name the defence or settlement of any claim.
XXXXXX.2  The Plan can take action in the Member's name to recover any payment the Plan makes from anyone responsible for the loss.

RENTERS CONTENTS PROTECTION
Issued by Lantern General Insurance

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
I.2  Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Insurer, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
I.3  Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
I.4  Family means the Policyholder's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Policyholder.
I.5  Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
I.6  High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
I.7  Home means the private residence at the address shown in the schedule.
I.8  Limit means the most the Insurer will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
I.9  Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.
I.10  Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Policyholder's schedule.
I.11  Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
I.12  Premium means the amount the Policyholder must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
I.13  Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
I.14  Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
I.15  Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 45 consecutive days.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.2  Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.3  Accidental Damage: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.4  Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
II.5  The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Theft
III.1  The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
III.2  The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,500 per incident.
III.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $500 per incident.
III.4  The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
III.5  The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
III.6  The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

PART IV: Flood
IV.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
IV.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
IV.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
IV.4  The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

PART V: Optional cover: Accidental Damage
V.1  The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
V.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
V.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $500 per incident.
V.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
V.5  The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

PART VI: Escape of Water
VI.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
VI.2  The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.

VII.4  The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

VIII.1  The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

PART XII: Data protection
XII.1  The Insurer will use the personal information the Policyholder provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
XII.2  The Insurer will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
XII.3  The Policyholder can ask for a copy of the personal information the Insurer holds by writing to the Insurer's data protection officer.

PART XIII: Change of address
XIII.1  The Policyholder must tell the Insurer within 30 days if the Policyholder changes the Policyholder's address.
XIII.2  The Insurer may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

PART XIV: Currency
XIV.1  All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
XIV.2  Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

PART XV: Renewal

PART XVI: Assignment

PART XX: Accessibility

PART XXI: Locks and keys
XXI.1  If the keys to the Policyholder's home are lost or stolen, the Insurer will pay the cost of replacing the locks to the outside doors.
XXI.2  The most the Insurer will pay under this clause is $500 for any one claim.

PART XXII: Notices

XXII.2  Notices from the Policyholder should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

PART XXIII: Sanctions

GROUP HEALTH CASH PLAN
Issued by Wellspring Benefits Administration

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Plan, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
I.2  Dependant means the Member's spouse or partner, or a child under 21 who is enrolled in the plan.
I.3  Family means the Member's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Member.
I.4  Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
I.5  Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
I.6  Hearing aid replacement period means 36 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
I.7  Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
I.8  Limit means the most the Plan will pay for all claims under a section arising from one treatment.
I.9  Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
I.10  Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
I.11  Network provider means a practitioner or clinic that has an agreement with the Plan to provide treatment.
I.12  Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
I.13  Plan year means the twelve months starting on the Member's coverage start date.
I.14  Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Member's schedule.
I.15  Premium means the amount the Member must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
I.16  Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
I.17  Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
I.18  Replacement period means 12 months from the date of the Member's last eyewear claim.
I.19  Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Member's details, the covers the Member bought and any extensions.
I.20  Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

PART II: Limits and deductible
II.1  Dental Care: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
II.2  Vision Care: limit $300 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
II.3  Therapy Services: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
II.4  Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
II.5  Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

PART III: Payment of claims
III.1  The Plan will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Member's name.
III.2  The Plan aims to pay accepted claims within 10 working days of receiving all the documents the Plan needs.

PART IV: Fraud
IV.1  If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Plan will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
IV.2  The Plan may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

PART V: Compensation scheme
V.1  The Plan is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
V.2  If the Plan cannot meet the Plan's obligations, the Member may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

PART VI: Complaints
VI.1  If the Member has a complaint, the Member should first contact the Plan's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
VI.2  The Plan will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
VI.3  If the Member remains dissatisfied, the Member may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

PART VII: Therapy Services
VII.1  The Plan will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
VII.2  The most the Plan will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $300 per treatment.
VII.3  The Plan will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
VII.4  The Plan will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

PART VIII: Governing law
VIII.1  This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
VIII.2  Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

PART IX: Cooperation
IX.1  The Member must give the Plan all the help and information the Plan reasonably need to settle a claim.
IX.2  The Member must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Plan's written permission.

PART X: Duty of fair presentation
X.1  The Member must answer all questions the Plan asks honestly and to the best of the Member's knowledge.
X.2  If the Member gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Plan may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
X.3  If the Member gives incorrect information carelessly, the Plan may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

PART XI: Taxes
XI.1  The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
XI.2  If the tax rate changes, the Plan may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

PART XII: Optional cover: Hearing Care
XII.1  The Plan will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
XII.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Member's schedule.
XII.3  The most the Plan will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $100 per treatment.
XII.4  The Plan will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

XIII.3  Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

Issued by Lantern General Insurance

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.

I.3  Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
I.4  Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Policyholder's details, the covers the Policyholder bought and any extensions.
I.5  Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Theft: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
II.2  Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.3  Accidental Damage: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.4  Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
II.5  The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Freezer contents
III.1  The Insurer will pay for food in a domestic freezer that spoils because of a rise or fall in temperature.
III.2  The Insurer will not pay if the freezer is more than fifteen years old, or if the electricity supplier cut the supply deliberately.

PART IV: Reasonable precautions
IV.1  The Policyholder must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
IV.2  The Policyholder must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

PART V: Changes in circumstances
V.1  The Policyholder must tell the Insurer as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
V.2  The Insurer may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

PART VI: Taxes
VI.1  The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
VI.2  If the tax rate changes, the Insurer may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

PART VII: Payment of claims
VII.1  The Insurer will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Policyholder's name.
VII.2  The Insurer aims to pay accepted claims within 10 working days of receiving all the documents the Insurer needs.

PART VIII: Fraud
VIII.1  If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Insurer will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
VIII.2  The Insurer may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

PART IX: Optional cover: Accidental Damage
IX.1  The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
IX.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
IX.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $750 per incident.
IX.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
IX.5  The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

PART X: Flood
X.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
X.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
X.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
X.4  The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

PART XI: Cooperation
XI.1  The Policyholder must give the Insurer all the help and information the Insurer reasonably need to settle a claim.
XI.2  The Policyholder must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Insurer's written permission.

PART XII: Currency

XII.2  Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

PART XIII: Customer support

XIII.2  Outside these hours the Policyholder can leave a message and the Insurer will call back on the next working day.

PART XIV: General exclusions
XIV.1  The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.
XIV.2  The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

XV.1  The Policyholder must answer all questions the Insurer asks honestly and to the best of the Policyholder's knowledge.
XV.2  If the Policyholder gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Insurer may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.

PART XXVII: Sanctions

6.1 We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

19.1 You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.

CASE PRESENTATION A
EMPLOYEE HEALTH BENEFITS PLAN: SUMMARY PLAN DESCRIPTION
Issued by the Staff Welfare Fund

SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS
1.1 Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
1.2 Dependant means your spouse or partner, or a child under 21 who is enrolled in the plan.
1.3 Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
1.4 Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
1.5 Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
1.6 Hearing aid replacement period means 36 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
1.7 Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
1.8 Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one treatment.
1.9 Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
1.10 Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
1.11 Network provider means a practitioner or clinic that has an agreement with us to provide treatment.
1.12 Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
1.13 Plan year means the twelve months starting on your coverage start date.
1.14 Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
1.15 Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
1.16 Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
1.17 Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
1.18 Registered practitioner means a practitioner registered with the professional body for their discipline.
1.19 Replacement period means 12 months from the date of your last eyewear claim.
1.20 Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
1.21 Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

SECTION 2 - LIMITS AND DEDUCTIBLE
2.1 Dental Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
2.2 Vision Care: limit $500 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
2.3 Therapy Services: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
2.4 Hearing Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
2.5 The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

SECTION 3 - THERAPY SERVICES
3.1 We will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
3.2 The most we will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $300 per treatment.
3.3 We will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
3.4 We will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

SECTION 4 - DENTAL CARE
4.1 We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
4.2 No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
4.3 The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.
4.4 The most we will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $600 per treatment.
4.5 We will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
4.6 We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

SECTION 5 - OPTIONAL COVER: HEARING CARE
5.1 We will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
5.2 This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
5.3 The most we will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $150 per treatment.
5.4 We will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

SECTION 6 - VISION CARE
6.1 We will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
6.2 The most we will pay for Frames under this section is $120 per treatment.
6.3 We will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
6.4 We will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

SECTION 7 - GENERAL EXCLUSIONS
7.1 We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
7.2 We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
7.3 We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

SECTION 8 - MAKING A CLAIM
8.1 We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
8.2 You must notify us of a claim within 60 days of the treatment. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
8.3 You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

SECTION 9 - FRAUD
9.1 If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
9.2 We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

SECTION 10 - OTHER INSURANCE
10.1 If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
10.2 You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

SECTION 11 - SUBROGATION
11.1 We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
11.2 We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

SECTION 12 - INTERPRETATION
12.1 Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
12.2 Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
12.3 Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

SECTION 13 - ELECTRONIC DOCUMENTS
13.1 We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
13.2 You must tell us if your email address changes.
13.3 Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

SECTION 14 - CHANGE OF ADDRESS
14.1 You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
14.2 We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

SECTION 15 - ACCESSIBILITY
15.1 This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

SECTION 16 - CUSTOMER SUPPORT
16.1 Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
16.2 Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

SECTION 17 - DUTY OF FAIR PRESENTATION
17.1 You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
17.2 If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
17.3 If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

SECTION 18 - NOTICES
18.1 Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
18.2 Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

SECTION 19 - RECOVERY OF COSTS
19.1 If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

SECTION 20 - PREMIUM PAYMENT
20.1 You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
20.2 If an instalment is not paid within 21 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

SECTION 21 - SANCTIONS
21.1 We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

SECTION 22 - COORDINATION OF BENEFITS
22.1 If a treatment is also covered by another plan, we will pay only the part of the cost that the other plan does not pay.
22.2 You must tell us about any other plan that covers you or your dependants.

SECTION 23 - CLAIMS DOCUMENTS
23.1 You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
23.2 We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

SECTION 24 - INFLATION
24.1 We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
24.2 Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

SECTION 25 - DEPENDANTS
25.1 You may enrol dependants at the start of each plan year or within 30 days of a qualifying life event.
25.2 Benefits paid for dependants count towards the same annual limits as your own claims.

SECTION 26 - GOVERNING LAW
26.1 This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
26.2 Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

SECTION 27 - INSTALMENT AGREEMENTS
27.1 If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
27.2 Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

SECTION 28 - WELLNESS ALLOWANCE
28.1 Each plan year you may claim up to $100 towards a gym membership or fitness class.
28.2 The wellness allowance is not subject to any deductible and does not count towards other limits.

SECTION 29 - MARKET CONDITIONS
29.1 If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

SECTION 30 - SALVAGE
30.1 When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
30.2 If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

SECTION 31 - COMMUNICATION
31.1 We will communicate with you in English.
31.2 We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

SECTION 32 - WAIVER
32.1 If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

SECTION 33 - ELIGIBILITY
33.1 Employees who work at least 20 hours a week are eligible to join the plan from their first day of employment.
33.2 Contractors, agency workers and employees on unpaid leave of more than three months are not eligible.

SECTION 34 - GEOGRAPHICAL LIMITS
34.1 Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
34.2 Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

SECTION 35 - THIRD-PARTY ADMINISTRATORS
35.1 We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
35.2 Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

SECTION 36 - COMPLAINTS
36.1 If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
36.2 We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
36.3 If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

SECTION 37 - CONTRACTS (RIGHTS OF THIRD PARTIES)
37.1 A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

SECTION 38 - EXCHANGE OF INFORMATION
38.1 To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
38.2 We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

SECTION 39 - AUTOMATIC RENEWAL
39.1 Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
39.2 You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

SECTION 40 - DATA PROTECTION
40.1 We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
40.2 We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
40.3 You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

SECTION 41 - HOW TO READ THIS DOCUMENT
41.1 This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
41.2 Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
41.3 Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

SECTION 42 - ASSIGNMENT
42.1 You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

SECTION 43 - JOINT POLICYHOLDERS
43.1 Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
43.2 A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

SECTION 44 - ARBITRATION
44.1 If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
44.2 Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

SECTION 45 - CANCELLATION
45.1 You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
45.2 After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $30.
45.3 We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

SECTION 46 - LEAVING THE PLAN
46.1 Cover ends on the day your employment ends or the day you stop being eligible, whichever is earlier.
46.2 Claims for treatment received before cover ended may be submitted up to 90 days afterwards.

SECTION 47 - RENEWAL
47.1 We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
47.2 We are not obliged to offer renewal.

SECTION 48 - CURRENCY
48.1 All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
48.2 Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

SECTION 49 - DISCOUNTS
49.1 Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
49.2 If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

SECTION 50 - REASONABLE PRECAUTIONS
50.1 You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
50.2 You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

SECTION 51 - APPEALS
51.1 If we decline all or part of a claim, you may appeal in writing within 60 days of the decision.
51.2 An appeal will be reviewed by someone who was not involved in the original decision.
51.3 We will give you a written decision on the appeal within 30 days.

SECTION 52 - PAYMENT OF CLAIMS
52.1 We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
52.2 We aim to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

SECTION 53 - COOPERATION
53.1 You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
53.2 You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

SECTION 54 - INTEREST
54.1 We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

SECTION 55 - COMPENSATION SCHEME
55.1 We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
55.2 If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

SECTION 56 - TAXES
56.1 The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
56.2 If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

SECTION 57 - RECORDS AND EVIDENCE
57.1 You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
57.2 Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
57.3 We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

SECTION 58 - CHANGES IN CIRCUMSTANCES
58.1 You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
58.2 We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

SECTION 59 - ENVIRONMENTAL COMMITMENT
59.1 Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
59.2 You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

SECTION 60 - SEVERABILITY
60.1 If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

+
+    date = "Oct 24, 2016"
+    tgt_dir = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='sdl_test_')

+
+    # setting up list of all HTML report files that should be downloaded for
+    # specified date
+    files = ["".join(c) + ".HTM" for c in list(
+        itertools.product(prefixes, game_ids))]
+    # adding JSON game report files
+    files.extend(["".join((gid, ".json")) for gid in game_ids])
+    # adding shootout report for one of the games
+    files.append("SO020082.HTM")
+
+    sdl = SummaryDownloader(tgt_dir, date, zip_summaries=False)
+    sdl.run()
+    tgt_dir = sdl.get_tgt_dir()

+    assert sorted(os.listdir(tgt_dir)) == sorted(files)

+    sdl = SummaryDownloader(tgt_dir, date)
+    sdl.run()
+    zip_path = sdl.get_zip_path()
+
+    zip = ZipFile(zip_path)
+
+    assert sorted(zip.namelist()) == sorted(files)
