ANNUAL MULTI-TRIP TRAVEL COVER
Issued by Compass Mutual
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Compass Mutual and "the Insured Person" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
(b) Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
(c) Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
(d) Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,000 metres.
(e) Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
(f) Limit means the most the Insurer will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
(g) Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
(h) Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
(i) Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which the Insured Person received treatment or advice in the 12 months before the policy start date.
(j) Premium means the amount the Insured Person must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
(k) Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
(l) Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 12 hours.
(m) Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
(n) Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Insured Person's details, the covers the Insured Person bought and any extensions.
(o) Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
(p) Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
(q) Territory means the countries in which cover applies, as shown in the schedule.
(r) Travelling companion means a person who has booked to travel with the Insured Person on the same trip.
(s) Trip means a journey that starts and ends in the Insured Person's home country during the policy period.
(t) Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $75 per claim.
(b) Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(c) Trip Cancellation: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(d) Travel Delay: limit $500 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
(e) The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

Article 3. Customer support
(a) The Insurer's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
(b) Outside these hours the Insured Person can leave a message and the Insurer will call back on the next working day.

Article 4. Repatriation
(a) If the Insurer's medical adviser agrees it is necessary, the Insurer will arrange and pay for the Insured Person to be brought home.
(b) The Insurer will decide the method of transport and the time of repatriation after speaking to the treating doctor.

Article 5. Currency
(a) All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
(b) Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

Article 6. Communication
(a) The Insurer will communicate with the Insured Person in English.
(b) The Insurer may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

Article 7. Notices
(a) Any notice the Insurer gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Insurer holds.
(b) Notices from the Insured Person should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

Article 8. Emergency Medical Expenses
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $250 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $500 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for any claim arising from the Insured Person's being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

Article 9. Changes in circumstances
(a) The Insured Person must tell the Insurer as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
(b) The Insurer may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

Article 10. Exchange of information
(a) To prevent fraud, the Insurer may check the details the Insured Person gives against public records and industry databases.
(b) The Insurer may contact previous insurers to confirm the Insured Person's claims history.

Article 11. Electronic documents
(a) The Insurer will send documents by email unless the Insured Person asks for paper copies.
(b) The Insured Person must tell the Insurer if the Insured Person's email address changes.
(c) Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

Article 12. Trip Cancellation
(a) The Insurer will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if the Insured Person must cancel the trip for a reason beyond the Insured Person's control.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 10 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $200 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before the Insured Person bought the policy.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation because the Insured Person no longer wish to travel.

Article 13. Environmental commitment
(a) Where practical, the Insurer will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
(b) The Insured Person may ask for a new part instead, and the Insurer will tell the Insured Person whether any additional cost would apply.

Article 14. Renewal
(a) The Insurer will write to the Insured Person at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
(b) The Insurer is not obliged to offer renewal.

Article 15. Baggage and Personal Belongings
(a) The Insurer will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to the Insured Person's baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Valuables under this section is $500 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $450 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

Article 16. Cancellation
(a) The Insured Person can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
(b) After the first 14 days the Insured Person can cancel at any time; the Insurer will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $30.
(c) The Insurer can cancel this policy by giving the Insured Person 30 days' written notice to the last address the Insurer holds.

Article 17. Geographical limits
(a) Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
(b) Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

Article 18. Personal liability
(a) The Insurer will pay damages the Insured Person becomes legally liable to pay for accidental injury to another person or accidental damage to their property during the trip.
(b) This section does not cover liability arising from the use of motor vehicles, boats or aircraft.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay under this section is $2,000,000 for all claims arising from one event.

Article 19. Claims documents
(a) The Insured Person must provide, at the Insured Person's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Insurer reasonably ask for.
(b) The Insurer may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

Article 20. Governing law
(a) This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
(b) Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

Article 21. Third-party administrators
(a) The Insurer may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Insurer's behalf.
(b) Any company the Insurer appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

Article 22. Compensation scheme
(a) The Insurer is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
(b) If the Insurer cannot meet the Insurer's obligations, the Insured Person may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

Article 23. Optional cover: Travel Delay
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if the Insured Person's outbound departure is delayed.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Insured Person's schedule.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

Article 24. Assignment
(a) The Insured Person cannot transfer the Insured Person's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Insurer's written consent.

Article 25. Discounts
(a) Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
(b) If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Insurer may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

Article 26. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Insured Person.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.

Article 27. Inflation
(a) The Insurer may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
(b) Any adjustment will be shown in the Insured Person's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

Article 28. Taxes
(a) The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
(b) If the tax rate changes, the Insurer may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

Article 29. Waiver
(a) If the Insurer does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Insurer has given up the right to enforce it later.

Article 30. Data protection
(a) The Insurer will use the personal information the Insured Person provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
(b) The Insurer will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
(c) The Insured Person can ask for a copy of the personal information the Insurer holds by writing to the Insurer's data protection officer.

Article 31. Interpretation
(a) Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
(b) Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
(c) Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

Article 32. Fraud
(a) If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Insurer will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
(b) The Insurer may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

Article 33. Premium payment
(a) The Insured Person must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
(b) If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, the Insurer may cancel the policy after giving notice.

Article 34. Making a claim
(a) The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 21 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(b) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(c) The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

Article 35. Salvage
(a) When the Insurer replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Insurer's property.
(b) If stolen property is recovered after the Insurer has paid a claim, the Insured Person must tell the Insurer and either return the payment or give the Insurer the property.

Article 36. How to read this document
(a) This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
(b) Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
(c) Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

Article 37. Automatic renewal
(a) Unless the Insured Person tells the Insurer otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Insurer holds.
(b) The Insured Person can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Insurer's helpline.

Issued by Bluewater Assurance
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Bluewater Assurance and "the Insured Person" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Insurer, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
(b) Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
(c) Limit means the most the Insurer will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.

(e) Territory means the countries in which cover applies, as shown in the schedule.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(b) Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $25,000 per incident; excess $150 per claim.
(c) Trip Cancellation: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(d) Travel Delay: limit $750 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(e) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Optional cover: Travel Delay
(a) The Insurer will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if the Insured Person's outbound departure is delayed.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Insured Person's schedule.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

Article 4. Trip Cancellation
(a) The Insurer will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if the Insured Person must cancel the trip for a reason beyond the Insured Person's control.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 7 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $300 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before the Insured Person bought the policy.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation because the Insured Person no longer wish to travel.

Article 5. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Insured Person.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

Article 6. Making a claim

(b) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(c) The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

Article 7. Reasonable precautions
(a) The Insured Person must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
(b) The Insured Person must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

Article 8. Geographical limits
(a) Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
(b) Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

Article 9. Cooperation
(a) The Insured Person must give the Insurer all the help and information the Insurer reasonably need to settle a claim.
(b) The Insured Person must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Insurer's written permission.

Article 10. Salvage
(a) When the Insurer replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Insurer's property.
(b) If stolen property is recovered after the Insurer has paid a claim, the Insured Person must tell the Insurer and either return the payment or give the Insurer the property.

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Insurer, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.

I.6  Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
I.7  Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which the Insured Person received treatment or advice in the 6 months before the policy start date.
I.8  Premium means the amount the Insured Person must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
I.9  Public transport means any scheduled train, bus, coach, ferry or aircraft.
I.10  Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 8 hours.
I.11  Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
I.12  Territory means the countries in which cover applies, as shown in the schedule.
I.13  Travelling companion means a person who has booked to travel with the Insured Person on the same trip.
I.14  Trip means a journey that starts and ends in the Insured Person's home country during the policy period.
I.15  Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.2  Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
II.3  Trip Cancellation: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.4  Travel Delay: limit $750 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.5  The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Optional cover: Travel Delay
III.1  The Insurer will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if the Insured Person's outbound departure is delayed.
III.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Insured Person's schedule.
III.3  The Insurer will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

PART IV: Trip Cancellation
IV.1  The Insurer will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if the Insured Person must cancel the trip for a reason beyond the Insured Person's control.
IV.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 10 days after the policy start date.
IV.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $200 per incident.
IV.4  The Insurer will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before the Insured Person bought the policy.
IV.5  The Insurer will not pay for cancellation because the Insured Person no longer wish to travel.

PART V: Baggage and Personal Belongings
V.1  The Insurer will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to the Insured Person's baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
V.2  The most the Insurer will pay for Valuables under this section is $500 per incident.
V.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $450 per incident.
V.4  The Insurer will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
V.5  The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
V.6  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

PART VI: Emergency Medical Expenses
VI.1  The Insurer will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
VI.2  The most the Insurer will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $250 per incident.
VI.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $500 per incident.
VI.4  The Insurer will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
VI.5  The Insurer will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
VI.6  The Insurer will not pay for any claim arising from the Insured Person's being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

PART VII: General exclusions
VII.1  The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
VII.2  The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
VII.3  The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.
VII.4  The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
VII.5  The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
VII.6  The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Insured Person.

PART VIII: Making a claim
VIII.1  The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
VIII.2  The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 90 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
VIII.3  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

PART IX: Governing law
IX.1  This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
IX.2  Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

PART X: Repatriation
X.1  If the Insurer's medical adviser agrees it is necessary, the Insurer will arrange and pay for the Insured Person to be brought home.
X.2  The Insurer will decide the method of transport and the time of repatriation after speaking to the treating doctor.

PART XI: Communication
XI.1  The Insurer will communicate with the Insured Person in English.
XI.2  The Insurer may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

PART XII: Arbitration
XII.1  If the Insurer accepts a claim but disagree with the Insured Person about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
XII.2  Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against the Insurer.

XIII.1  If the Insured Person pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.

XIV.1  The Insurer will send documents by email unless the Insured Person asks for paper copies.
XIV.2  The Insured Person must tell the Insurer if the Insured Person's email address changes.

PART XV: Notices
XV.1  Any notice the Insurer gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Insurer holds.
XV.2  Notices from the Insured Person should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

PART XVI: Interest
XVI.1  The Insurer will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

PART XVII: Cancellation
XVII.1  The Insured Person can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
XVII.2  After the first 14 days the Insured Person can cancel at any time; the Insurer will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $30.
XVII.3  The Insurer can cancel this policy by giving the Insured Person 30 days' written notice to the last address the Insurer holds.

XVIII.1  Where practical, the Insurer will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
XVIII.2  The Insured Person may ask for a new part instead, and the Insurer will tell the Insured Person whether any additional cost would apply.

PART XIX: Compensation scheme
XIX.1  The Insurer is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
XIX.2  If the Insurer cannot meet the Insurer's obligations, the Insured Person may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

PART XX: Other insurance
XX.1  If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Insurer will pay only the Insurer's proportionate share.
XX.2  The Insured Person must tell the Insurer about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Insured Person makes a claim.

XXI.1  The Insurer will pay damages the Insured Person becomes legally liable to pay for accidental injury to another person or accidental damage to their property during the trip.
XXI.2  This section does not cover liability arising from the use of motor vehicles, boats or aircraft.
XXI.3  The most the Insurer will pay under this section is $5,000,000 for all claims arising from one event.

PART XXII: Recovery of costs
XXII.1  If the Insurer pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Insurer may ask the Insured Person to repay the amount.

PART XXIII: Salvage
XXIII.1  When the Insurer replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Insurer's property.
XXIII.2  If stolen property is recovered after the Insurer has paid a claim, the Insured Person must tell the Insurer and either return the payment or give the Insurer the property.

PART XXIV: Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
XXIV.1  A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

PART XXV: Records and evidence
XXV.1  The Insured Person should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
XXV.2  Where proof of value is missing, the Insurer may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
XXV.3  The Insurer may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

PART XXVI: Reasonable precautions
XXVI.1  The Insured Person must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
XXVI.2  The Insured Person must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

PART XXVII: Duty of fair presentation
XXVII.1  The Insured Person must answer all questions the Insurer asks honestly and to the best of the Insured Person's knowledge.
XXVII.2  If the Insured Person gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Insurer may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
XXVII.3  If the Insured Person gives incorrect information carelessly, the Insurer may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

PART XXVIII: Currency
XXVIII.1  All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
XXVIII.2  Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

PART XXIX: Change of address
XXIX.1  The Insured Person must tell the Insurer within 30 days if the Insured Person changes the Insured Person's address.
XXIX.2  The Insurer may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

PART XXX: Sanctions

# Staff Health Reimbursement Plan Rules
Issued by the Benefits Trust

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
- **1.2** Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
- **1.3** Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
- **1.4** Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
- **1.5** Plan year means the twelve months starting on your coverage start date.

## 2. Limits and deductible
- **2.1** Dental Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
- **2.2** Vision Care: limit $400 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
- **2.3** Therapy Services: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
- **2.5** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Currency
- **3.1** All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
- **3.2** Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

## 4. Dental Care
- **4.1** We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
- **4.2** No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $750 per treatment.
- **4.4** The most we will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $800 per treatment.
- **4.5** We will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
- **4.6** We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

## 5. Changes in circumstances
- **5.1** You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
- **5.2** We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

## 6. Salvage
- **6.1** When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
- **6.2** If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

## 7. Exchange of information
- **7.1** To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
- **7.2** We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

## 8. Data protection
- **8.1** We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
- **8.2** We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
- **8.3** You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

## 9. Wellness allowance
- **9.1** Each plan year you may claim up to $100 towards a gym membership or fitness class.
- **9.2** The wellness allowance is not subject to any deductible and does not count towards other limits.

## 10. Joint policyholders
- **10.1** Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
- **10.2** A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

## 11. Payment of claims
- **11.1** We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
- **11.2** We aim to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

## 12. Communication
- **12.1** We will communicate with you in English.
- **12.2** We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

## 13. Eligibility
- **13.1** Employees who work at least 20 hours a week are eligible to join the plan from their first day of employment.
- **13.2** Contractors, agency workers and employees on unpaid leave of more than three months are not eligible.

## 14. Appeals
- **14.1** If we decline all or part of a claim, you may appeal in writing within 60 days of the decision.
- **14.2** An appeal will be reviewed by someone who was not involved in the original decision.
- **14.3** We will give you a written decision on the appeal within 30 days.

## 15. Duty of fair presentation
- **15.1** You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
- **15.2** If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
- **15.3** If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

## 16. Therapy Services
- **16.1** We will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
- **16.2** The most we will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $300 per treatment.
- **16.3** We will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
- **16.4** We will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

## 17. Leaving the plan
- **17.1** Cover ends on the day your employment ends or the day you stop being eligible, whichever is earlier.
- **17.2** Claims for treatment received before cover ended may be submitted up to 90 days afterwards.

## 18. Compensation scheme
- **18.1** We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
- **18.2** If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

## 19. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
- **19.1** A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

## 20. Geographical limits
- **20.1** Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
- **20.2** Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

## 21. General exclusions
- **21.1** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
- **21.2** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **21.3** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

## 22. Environmental commitment
- **22.1** Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
- **22.2** You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

## 23. Reasonable precautions
- **23.1** You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
- **23.2** You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

## 24. Waiver
- **24.1** If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

## 25. Making a claim
- **25.1** You must notify us of a claim within 90 days of the treatment. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **25.2** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **25.3** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

II.3  Theft and Loss: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.

CASE PRESENTATION B
# Single-Trip Travel Protection Plan
Issued by Compass Mutual

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
- **1.2** Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
- **1.3** Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
- **1.4** Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
- **1.5** Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
- **1.6** Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 3,000 metres.
- **1.7** Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
- **1.8** Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
- **1.9** Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
- **1.10** Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which you received treatment or advice in the 12 months before the policy start date.
- **1.11** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.12** Public transport means any scheduled train, bus, coach, ferry or aircraft.
- **1.13** Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 8 hours.
- **1.14** Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
- **1.15** Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
- **1.16** Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
- **1.17** Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
- **1.18** Territory means the countries in which cover applies, as shown in the schedule.
- **1.19** Travelling companion means a person who has booked to travel with you on the same trip.
- **1.20** Trip means a journey that starts and ends in your home country during the policy period.
- **1.21** Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $1,500 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.2** Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $25,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.3** Trip Cancellation: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Travel Delay: limit $750 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.5** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Baggage and Personal Belongings
- **3.1** We will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to your baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
- **3.2** The most we will pay for Valuables under this section is $400 per incident.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $300 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
- **3.5** We will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
- **3.6** We will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

## 4. Trip Cancellation
- **4.1** We will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if you must cancel the trip for a reason beyond your control.
- **4.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 10 days after the policy start date.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $300 per incident.
- **4.4** We will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before you bought the policy.
- **4.5** We will not pay for cancellation because you no longer wish to travel.

## 5. Emergency Medical Expenses
- **5.1** We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
- **5.2** The most we will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $400 per incident.
- **5.3** The most we will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $500 per incident.
- **5.4** We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
- **5.5** We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
- **5.6** We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

## 6. Optional cover: Travel Delay
- **6.1** We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
- **6.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **6.3** We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

## 7. General exclusions
- **7.1** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
- **7.2** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
- **7.3** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
- **7.4** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.

## 8. Making a claim
- **8.1** You must notify us of a claim within 90 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **8.2** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **8.3** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

## 9. Joint policyholders
- **9.1** Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
- **9.2** A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

## 10. Assignment
- **10.1** You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

## 11. Changes in circumstances
- **11.1** You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
- **11.2** We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

## 12. Recovery of costs
- **12.1** If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

## 13. Communication
- **13.1** We will communicate with you in English.
- **13.2** We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

## 14. Market conditions
- **14.1** If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

## 15. Inflation
- **15.1** We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
- **15.2** Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

## 16. Taxes
- **16.1** The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
- **16.2** If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

## 17. Notices
- **17.1** Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
- **17.2** Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

## 18. Rental car excess
- **18.1** If you hire a car during the trip, we will reimburse any excess you must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.
- **18.2** This section applies only to cars hired from a licensed rental company under a written agreement.

## 19. Electronic documents
- **19.1** We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
- **19.2** You must tell us if your email address changes.
- **19.3** Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

## 20. Accessibility
- **20.1** This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

## 21. Customer support
- **21.1** Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
- **21.2** Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

## 22. Salvage
- **22.1** When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
- **22.2** If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

## 23. How to read this document
- **23.1** This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
- **23.2** Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
- **23.3** Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

## 24. Interpretation
- **24.1** Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
- **24.2** Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
- **24.3** Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

## 25. Cancellation
- **25.1** You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
- **25.2** After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
- **25.3** We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

## 26. Payment of claims
- **26.1** We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
- **26.2** We aim to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

## 27. Governing law
- **27.1** This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
- **27.2** Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

## 28. Complaints
- **28.1** If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
- **28.2** We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
- **28.3** If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

## 29. Compensation scheme
- **29.1** We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
- **29.2** If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

## 30. Fraud
- **30.1** If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
- **30.2** We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

## 31. Instalment agreements
- **31.1** If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
- **31.2** Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

## 32. Currency
- **32.1** All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
- **32.2** Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

## 33. Missed departure
- **33.1** We will pay reasonable additional travel and accommodation costs to reach your destination if you arrive too late to board your booked transport because public transport fails.
- **33.2** You must allow enough time to reach the departure point, and must obtain written confirmation of the delay from the transport operator.

## 34. Renewal
- **34.1** We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
- **34.2** We are not obliged to offer renewal.

## 35. Geographical limits
- **35.1** Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
- **35.2** Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

## 36. Duty of fair presentation
- **36.1** You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
- **36.2** If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
- **36.3** If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

## 37. Data protection
- **37.1** We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
- **37.2** We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
- **37.3** You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

## 38. Exchange of information
- **38.1** To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
- **38.2** We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

## 39. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
- **39.1** A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

## 40. Automatic renewal
- **40.1** Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
- **40.2** You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

## 41. Cooperation
- **41.1** You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
- **41.2** You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

## 42. Severability
- **42.1** If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

## 43. Change of address
- **43.1** You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
- **43.2** We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

## 44. Sanctions
- **44.1** We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

## 45. Premium payment
- **45.1** You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
- **45.2** If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

## 46. Third-party administrators
- **46.1** We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
- **46.2** Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

## 47. Repatriation
- **47.1** If our medical adviser agrees it is necessary, we will arrange and pay for you to be brought home.
- **47.2** We will decide the method of transport and the time of repatriation after speaking to the treating doctor.

## 48. Emergency assistance
- **48.1** Our emergency assistance service is available 24 hours a day on the number shown in the schedule.
- **48.2** You must contact the assistance service before being admitted to hospital as an in-patient, unless it is an emergency.
- **48.3** The assistance service can arrange payment guarantees, interpreters and transport home.

## 49. Personal liability
- **49.1** We will pay damages you become legally liable to pay for accidental injury to another person or accidental damage to their property during the trip.
- **49.2** This section does not cover liability arising from the use of motor vehicles, boats or aircraft.
- **49.3** The most we will pay under this section is $1,000,000 for all claims arising from one event.

## 50. Subrogation
- **50.1** We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
- **50.2** We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

## 51. Records and evidence
- **51.1** You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
- **51.2** Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
- **51.3** We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

## 52. Legal expenses abroad
- **52.1** We will pay legal costs to pursue compensation for your injury or death caused by a third party during the trip.
- **52.2** We will not pay legal costs unless our legal adviser agrees that the claim has a reasonable prospect of success.

## 53. Claims documents
- **53.1** You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
- **53.2** We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

## 54. Reasonable precautions
- **54.1** You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
- **54.2** You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

## 55. Arbitration
- **55.1** If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
- **55.2** Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

## 56. Discounts
- **56.1** Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
- **56.2** If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

## 57. Interest
- **57.1** We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

## 58. Waiver
- **58.1** If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

## 59. Other insurance
- **59.1** If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
- **59.2** You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

## 60. Environmental commitment
- **60.1** Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
- **60.2** You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

PART I: Definitions

XX.1  The Policyholder's contents are covered while temporarily removed from the home to another building in the same country, for up to 60 days.
XX.2  Contents in a student hall of residence are covered only if the student is a member of the Policyholder's family.

PART XXI: Other insurance
XXI.1  If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Insurer will pay only the Insurer's proportionate share.
XXI.2  The Policyholder must tell the Insurer about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Policyholder makes a claim.

PART XXII: Subrogation
XXII.1  The Insurer will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Policyholder's name the defence or settlement of any claim.
XXII.2  The Insurer can take action in the Policyholder's name to recover any payment the Insurer makes from anyone responsible for the loss.

PART XXIII: Third-party administrators
XXIII.1  The Insurer may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Insurer's behalf.
XXIII.2  Any company the Insurer appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

PART XXIV: Notices
XXIV.1  Any notice the Insurer gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Insurer holds.
XXIV.2  Notices from the Policyholder should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

PART XXV: Taxes
XXV.1  The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
XXV.2  If the tax rate changes, the Insurer may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

PART XXVI: Change of address
XXVI.1  The Policyholder must tell the Insurer within 30 days if the Policyholder changes the Policyholder's address.
XXVI.2  The Insurer may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

PART XXVII: Salvage
XXVII.1  When the Insurer replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Insurer's property.
XXVII.2  If stolen property is recovered after the Insurer has paid a claim, the Policyholder must tell the Insurer and either return the payment or give the Insurer the property.

PART XXVIII: Claims documents
XXVIII.1  The Policyholder must provide, at the Policyholder's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Insurer reasonably ask for.
XXVIII.2  The Insurer may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

PART XXIX: Interest
XXIX.1  The Insurer will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

PART XXX: Payment of claims
XXX.1  The Insurer will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Policyholder's name.
XXX.2  The Insurer aims to pay accepted claims within 15 working days of receiving all the documents the Insurer needs.

PART XXXI: Alternative accommodation
XXXI.1  If the Policyholder's home cannot be lived in after damage covered by this policy, the Insurer will pay the reasonable cost of comparable temporary accommodation.
XXXI.2  The Insurer will also pay for the temporary housing of pets that live with the Policyholder.
XXXI.3  Cover ends when the home is fit to live in again or after twelve months, whichever is sooner.

PART XXXII: Automatic renewal
XXXII.1  Unless the Policyholder tells the Insurer otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Insurer holds.
XXXII.2  The Policyholder can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Insurer's helpline.

PART XXXIII: Freezer contents
XXXIII.1  The Insurer will pay for food in a domestic freezer that spoils because of a rise or fall in temperature.
XXXIII.2  The Insurer will not pay if the freezer is more than fifteen years old, or if the electricity supplier cut the supply deliberately.

PART XXXIV: Complaints
XXXIV.1  If the Policyholder has a complaint, the Policyholder should first contact the Insurer's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
XXXIV.2  The Insurer will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
XXXIV.3  If the Policyholder remains dissatisfied, the Policyholder may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

PART XXXV: Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
XXXV.1  A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

PART XXXVI: Interpretation
XXXVI.1  Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
XXXVI.2  Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
XXXVI.3  Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

PART XXXVII: Recovery of costs
XXXVII.1  If the Insurer pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Insurer may ask the Policyholder to repay the amount.

PART XXXVIII: Environmental commitment
XXXVIII.1  Where practical, the Insurer will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
XXXVIII.2  The Policyholder may ask for a new part instead, and the Insurer will tell the Policyholder whether any additional cost would apply.

PART XXXIX: Garden and outdoor cover
XXXIX.1  The Insurer will pay for plants, trees and shrubs in the garden of the home that are damaged by fire, lightning or theft.
XXXIX.2  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by frost, storms, drought or animals.

PART XXXX: Data protection
XXXX.1  The Insurer will use the personal information the Policyholder provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
XXXX.2  The Insurer will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
XXXX.3  The Policyholder can ask for a copy of the personal information the Insurer holds by writing to the Insurer's data protection officer.

PART XXXXI: Fraud
XXXXI.1  If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Insurer will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
XXXXI.2  The Insurer may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

CASE PRESENTATION A
# Device Protection Plan Terms
Issued by Brightline Device Cover

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.
- **1.2** Accessories means cases, chargers and earbuds.
- **1.3** Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any service fee, limit or sublimit is applied.
- **1.4** Authorised repairer means a repairer approved in writing by us.
- **1.5** Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
- **1.6** Breakdown means the failure of a part to work as the manufacturer intended, from an internal electrical or mechanical fault.
- **1.7** Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
- **1.8** Device means the item shown in the schedule, bought new from an authorised retailer.
- **1.9** Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
- **1.10** Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
- **1.11** Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
- **1.12** Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 24 months after the device was bought.
- **1.13** Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
- **1.14** Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
- **1.15** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.16** Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
- **1.17** Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
- **1.18** Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
- **1.19** Wearables means smartwatches and fitness trackers.

## 2. Limits and service fee
- **2.1** Accidental Damage: limit $1,500 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
- **2.2** Breakdown: limit $1,500 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
- **2.3** Theft and Loss: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $149 per claim.
- **2.4** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the service fee is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Changes in circumstances
- **3.1** You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
- **3.2** We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

## 4. Recovery of costs
- **4.1** If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

## 5. Renewal
- **5.1** We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
- **5.2** We are not obliged to offer renewal.

## 6. Breakdown
- **6.1** We will repair or replace your device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.

- **8.2** Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

- **9.1** Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.

- **10.1** Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
- **10.2** If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

- **11.1** If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
- **11.2** We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

## 12. How to read this document
- **12.1** This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
- **12.2** Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
- **12.3** Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

## 13. Data protection
- **13.1** We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
- **13.2** We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
- **13.3** You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

## 14. Severability
- **14.1** If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

## 15. Accessibility
- **15.1** This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

## 16. Accidental Damage
- **16.1** We will repair or replace your device if it is accidentally damaged.
- **16.2** The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
- **16.3** The most we will pay for Wearables under this section is $300 per incident.
- **16.4** We will not pay for cosmetic damage, such as scratches or dents, that does not affect how the device works.
- **16.5** We will not pay for damage following a repair by anyone other than us or an authorised repairer. This exclusion does not apply if we approved the repair in writing beforehand.

## 17. Transferring the plan
- **17.1** You may transfer the plan to a new owner of the device by telling us in writing.
- **17.2** The remaining term of the plan transfers with the device; the term does not restart.

## 18. Sanctions
- **18.1** We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

## 19. Optional cover: Theft and Loss
- **19.1** We will replace your device if it is stolen or lost.
- **19.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **19.3** The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
- **19.4** We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
- **19.5** We will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

## 20. Electronic documents
- **20.1** We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
- **20.2** You must tell us if your email address changes.
- **20.3** Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

## 21. Notices
- **21.1** Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
- **21.2** Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

## 22. Communication
- **22.1** We will communicate with you in English.
- **22.2** We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

## 23. General exclusions
- **23.1** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
- **23.2** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **23.3** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

- **24.1** If we cannot repair your device economically, we will replace it with a replacement device.
