EMPLOYEE HEALTH BENEFITS PLAN: SUMMARY PLAN DESCRIPTION
Issued by the Benefits Trust
In this policy, "the Plan" means the Benefits Trust and "the Member" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Family means the Member's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Member.
(b) Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
(c) Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
(d) Hearing aid replacement period means 36 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
(e) Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
(f) Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
(g) Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
(h) Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
(i) Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Member's schedule.
(j) Premium means the amount the Member must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
(k) Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
(l) Replacement period means 24 months from the date of the Member's last eyewear claim.
(m) Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Member's details, the covers the Member bought and any extensions.
(n) Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

Article 2. Limits and deductible
(a) Dental Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
(b) Vision Care: limit $300 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
(c) Therapy Services: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
(d) Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
(e) The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

Article 3. Payment of claims
(a) The Plan will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Member's name.
(b) The Plan aims to pay accepted claims within 10 working days of receiving all the documents the Plan needs.

Article 4. Geographical limits
(a) Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
(b) Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

Article 5. Reasonable precautions
(a) The Member must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
(b) The Member must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

Article 6. How to read this document
(a) This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
(b) Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
(c) Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

Article 7. Waiver
(a) If the Plan does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Plan has given up the right to enforce it later.

Article 8. Dental Care
(a) The Plan will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Plan will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $750 per treatment.
(d) The most the Plan will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $600 per treatment.
(e) The Plan will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
(f) The Plan will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

Article 9. Salvage
(a) When the Plan replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Plan's property.
(b) If stolen property is recovered after the Plan has paid a claim, the Member must tell the Plan and either return the payment or give the Plan the property.

Article 10. Records and evidence
(a) The Member should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
(b) Where proof of value is missing, the Plan may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
(c) The Plan may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

Article 11. Fraud
(a) If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Plan will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
(b) The Plan may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

Article 12. Sanctions
(a) The Plan will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Plan to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

Article 13. Dependants
(a) The Member may enrol dependants at the start of each plan year or within 30 days of a qualifying life event.
(b) Benefits paid for dependants count towards the same annual limits as the Member's own claims.

Article 14. Market conditions
(a) If the replacement item is no longer available, the Plan will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

Article 15. Coordination of benefits
(a) If a treatment is also covered by another plan, the Plan will pay only the part of the cost that the other plan does not pay.
(b) The Member must tell the Plan about any other plan that covers the Member or the Member's dependants.

Article 16. Cancellation
(a) The Member can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
(b) After the first 14 days the Member can cancel at any time; the Plan will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
(c) The Plan can cancel this policy by giving the Member 30 days' written notice to the last address the Plan holds.

Article 17. Notices
(a) Any notice the Plan gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Plan holds.
(b) Notices from the Member should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

Article 18. Automatic renewal
(a) Unless the Member tells the Plan otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Plan holds.
(b) The Member can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Plan's helpline.

Article 19. Joint policyholders
(a) Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
(b) A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

Article 20. Optional cover: Hearing Care
(a) The Plan will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Member's schedule.
(c) The most the Plan will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $150 per treatment.
(d) The Plan will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

Article 21. Taxes
(a) The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
(b) If the tax rate changes, the Plan may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

Article 22. Cooperation
(a) The Member must give the Plan all the help and information the Plan reasonably need to settle a claim.
(b) The Member must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Plan's written permission.

Article 23. Compensation scheme
(a) The Plan is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
(b) If the Plan cannot meet the Plan's obligations, the Member may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

Article 24. Premium payment
(a) The Member must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
(b) If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, the Plan may cancel the policy after giving notice.

Article 25. Inflation
(a) The Plan may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
(b) Any adjustment will be shown in the Member's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

Article 26. Change of address
(a) The Member must tell the Plan within 30 days if the Member changes the Member's address.
(b) The Plan may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

Article 27. Therapy Services
(a) The Plan will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
(b) The most the Plan will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $200 per treatment.
(c) The Plan will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
(d) The Plan will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

Article 28. Changes in circumstances
(a) The Member must tell the Plan as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
(b) The Plan may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

Article 29. Interest
(a) The Plan will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

Article 30. Interpretation
(a) Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
(b) Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
(c) Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

Article 31. Data protection
(a) The Plan will use the personal information the Member provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
(b) The Plan will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
(c) The Member can ask for a copy of the personal information the Plan holds by writing to the Plan's data protection officer.

Article 32. Customer support
(a) The Plan's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
(b) Outside these hours the Member can leave a message and the Plan will call back on the next working day.

Article 33. Vision Care
(a) The Plan will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
(b) The most the Plan will pay for Frames under this section is $150 per treatment.
(c) The Plan will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
(d) The Plan will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

Article 34. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
(a) A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

Article 35. General exclusions
(a) The Plan will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
(b) The Plan will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
(c) The Plan will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Member.
(d) The Plan will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
(e) The Plan will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Plan from paying.

Article 36. Instalment agreements
(a) If the Member pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
(b) Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

Article 37. Duty of fair presentation
(a) The Member must answer all questions the Plan asks honestly and to the best of the Member's knowledge.
(b) If the Member gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Plan may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
(c) If the Member gives incorrect information carelessly, the Plan may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

Article 38. Assignment
(a) The Member cannot transfer the Member's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Plan's written consent.

Article 39. Third-party administrators
(a) The Plan may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Plan's behalf.
(b) Any company the Plan appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

Article 40. Recovery of costs
(a) If the Plan pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Plan may ask the Member to repay the amount.

Article 41. Governing law
(a) This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
(b) Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

Article 42. Eligibility
(a) Employees who work at least 20 hours a week are eligible to join the plan from their first day of employment.
(b) Contractors, agency workers and employees on unpaid leave of more than three months are not eligible.

Article 43. Making a claim
(a) The Member must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(b) The Member must notify the Plan of a claim within 60 days of the treatment. The Plan will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(c) The Plan may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

Article 44. Complaints
(a) If the Member has a complaint, the Member should first contact the Plan's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
(b) The Plan will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
(c) If the Member remains dissatisfied, the Member may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

Article 45. Severability
(a) If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

Article 46. Environmental commitment
(a) Where practical, the Plan will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
(b) The Member may ask for a new part instead, and the Plan will tell the Member whether any additional cost would apply.

ANNUAL MULTI-TRIP TRAVEL COVER
Issued by Meridian Travel Insurance Ltd

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
I.2  Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 6 hours.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $1,500 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.2  Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $150 per claim.
II.3  Trip Cancellation: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.4  Travel Delay: limit $750 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.5  The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Change of address
III.1  The Insured Person must tell the Insurer within 30 days if the Insured Person changes the Insured Person's address.
III.2  The Insurer may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

PART IV: Other insurance
IV.1  If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Insurer will pay only the Insurer's proportionate share.
IV.2  The Insured Person must tell the Insurer about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Insured Person makes a claim.

PART V: Duty of fair presentation
V.1  The Insured Person must answer all questions the Insurer asks honestly and to the best of the Insured Person's knowledge.
V.2  If the Insured Person gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Insurer may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
V.3  If the Insured Person gives incorrect information carelessly, the Insurer may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

PART VI: Joint policyholders
VI.1  Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
VI.2  A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

PART VII: Market conditions
VII.1  If the replacement item is no longer available, the Insurer will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

PART VIII: Optional cover: Travel Delay
VIII.1  The Insurer will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if the Insured Person's outbound departure is delayed.
VIII.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Insured Person's schedule.
VIII.3  The Insurer will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

PART IX: General exclusions
IX.1  The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Insured Person.
IX.2  The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
IX.3  The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

PART X: Interpretation
X.1  Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
X.2  Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
X.3  Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

PART XI: Legal expenses abroad
XI.1  The Insurer will pay legal costs to pursue compensation for the Insured Person's injury or death caused by a third party during the trip.
XI.2  The Insurer will not pay legal costs unless the Insurer's legal adviser agrees that the claim has a reasonable prospect of success.

PART XII: Records and evidence
XII.1  The Insured Person should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
XII.2  Where proof of value is missing, the Insurer may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
XII.3  The Insurer may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

PART XIII: Exchange of information
XIII.1  To prevent fraud, the Insurer may check the details the Insured Person gives against public records and industry databases.
XIII.2  The Insurer may contact previous insurers to confirm the Insured Person's claims history.

PART XIV: Making a claim
XIV.1  The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 14 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
XIV.2  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
XIV.3  The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

PART XV: Cancellation
XV.1  The Insured Person can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
XV.2  After the first 14 days the Insured Person can cancel at any time; the Insurer will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
XV.3  The Insurer can cancel this policy by giving the Insured Person 30 days' written notice to the last address the Insurer holds.

PART XVI: Accessibility
XVI.1  This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

PART XVII: Complaints
XVII.1  If the Insured Person has a complaint, the Insured Person should first contact the Insurer's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
XVII.2  The Insurer will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
XVII.3  If the Insured Person remains dissatisfied, the Insured Person may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

PART XVIII: Notices
XVIII.1  Any notice the Insurer gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Insurer holds.
XVIII.2  Notices from the Insured Person should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

HOME CONTENTS INSURANCE POLICY
Issued by Hearthstone Insurance plc

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
I.2  Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Insurer, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
I.3  Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
I.4  Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
I.5  Contents means household goods and personal possessions that belong to the Policyholder or the Policyholder's family.
I.6  Family means the Policyholder's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Policyholder.
I.7  Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
I.8  Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
I.9  High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
I.10  Home means the private residence at the address shown in the schedule.
I.11  Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
I.12  Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.
I.13  Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Policyholder's schedule.
I.14  Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
I.15  Premium means the amount the Policyholder must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
I.16  Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
I.17  Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
I.18  Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Policyholder's details, the covers the Policyholder bought and any extensions.
I.19  Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
I.20  Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 60 consecutive days.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Theft: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.2  Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
II.3  Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.4  Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
II.5  The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Claims documents
III.1  The Policyholder must provide, at the Policyholder's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Insurer reasonably ask for.
III.2  The Insurer may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

PART IV: Salvage
IV.1  When the Insurer replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Insurer's property.
IV.2  If stolen property is recovered after the Insurer has paid a claim, the Policyholder must tell the Insurer and either return the payment or give the Insurer the property.

PART V: Complaints
V.1  If the Policyholder has a complaint, the Policyholder should first contact the Insurer's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
V.2  The Insurer will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
V.3  If the Policyholder remains dissatisfied, the Policyholder may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

PART VI: Governing law
VI.1  This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
VI.2  Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

PART VII: Sanctions
VII.1  The Insurer will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Insurer to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

PART VIII: Theft
VIII.1  The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
VIII.2  The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
VIII.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $800 per incident.
VIII.4  The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
VIII.5  The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
VIII.6  The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

PART IX: Freezer contents
IX.1  The Insurer will pay for food in a domestic freezer that spoils because of a rise or fall in temperature.
IX.2  The Insurer will not pay if the freezer is more than fifteen years old, or if the electricity supplier cut the supply deliberately.

PART X: Records and evidence
X.1  The Policyholder should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
X.2  Where proof of value is missing, the Insurer may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
X.3  The Insurer may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

PART XI: Alternative accommodation
XI.1  If the Policyholder's home cannot be lived in after damage covered by this policy, the Insurer will pay the reasonable cost of comparable temporary accommodation.
XI.2  The Insurer will also pay for the temporary housing of pets that live with the Policyholder.
XI.3  Cover ends when the home is fit to live in again or after twelve months, whichever is sooner.

PART XII: Cooperation
XII.1  The Policyholder must give the Insurer all the help and information the Insurer reasonably need to settle a claim.
XII.2  The Policyholder must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Insurer's written permission.

PART XIII: Interest
XIII.1  The Insurer will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

PART XIV: Escape of Water
XIV.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
XIV.2  The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.
XIV.3  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
XIV.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

XV.1  The Insurer will use the personal information the Policyholder provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.

XV.3  The Policyholder can ask for a copy of the personal information the Insurer holds by writing to the Insurer's data protection officer.

XVI.1  The Insurer will pay for plants, trees and shrubs in the garden of the home that are damaged by fire, lightning or theft.

XVII.1  This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

XVIII.1  Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.

XIX.1  This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.

XXII.1  Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.

XXIII.4  The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

PART XXIV: General exclusions
XXIV.1  The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
XXIV.2  The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
XXIV.3  The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.

PART XXV: Subrogation
XXV.1  The Insurer will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Policyholder's name the defence or settlement of any claim.
XXV.2  The Insurer can take action in the Policyholder's name to recover any payment the Insurer makes from anyone responsible for the loss.

PART XXVI: Communication
XXVI.1  The Insurer will communicate with the Policyholder in English.
XXVI.2  The Insurer may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

XXVII.1  If the keys to the Policyholder's home are lost or stolen, the Insurer will pay the cost of replacing the locks to the outside doors.

XXVIII.1  The Policyholder must tell the Insurer within 30 days if the Policyholder changes the Policyholder's address.
XXVIII.2  The Insurer may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

PART XXIX: Currency
XXIX.1  All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.

XXXI.1  If the Policyholder rents the home, the Insurer will pay for damage to fixtures and fittings that the Policyholder installed and are responsible for.
XXXI.2  This cover applies only to improvements the Policyholder paid for, not to items provided by the landlord.

PART XXXII: Arbitration
XXXII.1  If the Insurer accepts a claim but disagree with the Policyholder about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.

XXXIII.1  If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Insurer will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.

ELECTRONICS CARE PLAN
Issued by Brightline Device Cover

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Accessories means cases, chargers and earbuds.
I.2  Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
I.3  Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
I.4  Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 12 months after the device was bought.

PART II: Limits and service fee
II.1  Accidental Damage: limit $800 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
II.2  Breakdown: limit $600 per incident; service fee $25 per claim.
II.3  Theft and Loss: limit $800 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
II.4  Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the service fee is then deducted from the result.

PART III: Instalment agreements
III.1  If the Customer pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
III.2  Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

PART IV: Optional cover: Theft and Loss
IV.1  The Provider will replace the Customer's device if it is stolen or lost.
IV.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Customer's schedule.
IV.3  The most the Provider will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.
IV.4  The Provider will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
IV.5  The Provider will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

PART V: Discounts
V.1  Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
V.2  If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Provider may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

PART VI: Transferring the plan
VI.1  The Customer may transfer the plan to a new owner of the device by telling the Provider in writing.
VI.2  The remaining term of the plan transfers with the device; the term does not restart.

PART VII: Repair process
VII.1  After a claim is accepted, the Provider will send a prepaid mailer or book a courier collection.
VII.2  The Provider aims to return repaired devices within 15 business days of receiving them.

PART VIII: Records and evidence
VIII.1  The Customer should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
VIII.2  Where proof of value is missing, the Provider may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
VIII.3  The Provider may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

PART IX: Breakdown
IX.1  The Provider will repair or replace the Customer's device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
IX.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 45 days after the policy start date.
IX.3  The most the Provider will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $80 per incident.
IX.4  The Provider will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
IX.5  The Provider will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

PART X: General exclusions
X.1  The Provider will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
X.2  The Provider will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Customer.

PART XI: Complaints
XI.1  If the Customer has a complaint, the Customer should first contact the Provider's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
XI.2  The Provider will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
XI.3  If the Customer remains dissatisfied, the Customer may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

PART XII: Making a claim
XII.1  The Customer must notify the Provider of a claim within 21 days of the incident. The Provider will not pay any claim notified after that time.
XII.2  The Customer must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
XII.3  The Provider may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

PART XIII: How to read this document
XIII.1  This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
XIII.2  Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
XIII.3  Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

PART XIV: Renewal
XIV.1  The Provider will write to the Customer at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
XIV.2  The Provider is not obliged to offer renewal.

PART XV: Severability
XV.1  If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

CASE PRESENTATION A
# Employee Health Benefits Plan: Summary Plan Description
Issued by the Staff Welfare Fund

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
- **1.2** Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
- **1.3** Dependant means your spouse or partner, or a child under 21 who is enrolled in the plan.
- **1.4** Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
- **1.5** Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
- **1.6** Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
- **1.7** Hearing aid replacement period means 36 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
- **1.8** Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
- **1.9** Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one treatment.
- **1.10** Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
- **1.11** Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
- **1.12** Network provider means a practitioner or clinic that has an agreement with us to provide treatment.
- **1.13** Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
- **1.14** Plan year means the twelve months starting on your coverage start date.
- **1.15** Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
- **1.16** Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
- **1.17** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.18** Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
- **1.19** Registered practitioner means a practitioner registered with the professional body for their discipline.
- **1.20** Replacement period means 24 months from the date of your last eyewear claim.
- **1.21** Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
- **1.22** Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

## 2. Limits and deductible
- **2.1** Dental Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
- **2.2** Vision Care: limit $400 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
- **2.3** Therapy Services: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
- **2.5** The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Accessibility
- **3.1** This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

## 4. Vision Care
- **4.1** We will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
- **4.2** The most we will pay for Frames under this section is $120 per treatment.
- **4.3** We will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
- **4.4** We will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

## 5. Currency
- **5.1** All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
- **5.2** Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

## 6. Reasonable precautions
- **6.1** You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
- **6.2** You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

## 7. Interpretation
- **7.1** Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
- **7.2** Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
- **7.3** Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

## 8. How to read this document
- **8.1** This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
- **8.2** Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
- **8.3** Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

## 9. Discounts
- **9.1** Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
- **9.2** If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

## 10. Renewal
- **10.1** We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
- **10.2** We are not obliged to offer renewal.

## 11. Geographical limits
- **11.1** Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
- **11.2** Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

## 12. Leaving the plan
- **12.1** Cover ends on the day your employment ends or the day you stop being eligible, whichever is earlier.
- **12.2** Claims for treatment received before cover ended may be submitted up to 90 days afterwards.

## 13. Sanctions
- **13.1** We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

## 14. Dependants
- **14.1** You may enrol dependants at the start of each plan year or within 30 days of a qualifying life event.
- **14.2** Benefits paid for dependants count towards the same annual limits as your own claims.

## 15. Salvage
- **15.1** When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
- **15.2** If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

## 16. Claims documents
- **16.1** You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
- **16.2** We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

## 17. Customer support
- **17.1** Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
- **17.2** Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

## 18. Therapy Services
- **18.1** We will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
- **18.2** The most we will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $300 per treatment.
- **18.3** We will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
- **18.4** We will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

## 19. Dental Care
- **19.1** We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
- **19.2** No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 90 days after the policy start date.
- **19.3** The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.
- **19.4** The most we will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $600 per treatment.
- **19.5** We will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
- **19.6** We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

## 20. Recovery of costs
- **20.1** If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

## 21. Records and evidence
- **21.1** You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
- **21.2** Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
- **21.3** We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

## 22. Electronic documents
- **22.1** We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
- **22.2** You must tell us if your email address changes.
- **22.3** Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

## 23. Coordination of benefits
- **23.1** If a treatment is also covered by another plan, we will pay only the part of the cost that the other plan does not pay.
- **23.2** You must tell us about any other plan that covers you or your dependants.

## 24. Automatic renewal
- **24.1** Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
- **24.2** You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

## 25. Notices
- **25.1** Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
- **25.2** Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

## 26. Inflation
- **26.1** We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
- **26.2** Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

## 27. Market conditions
- **27.1** If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

## 28. Subrogation
- **28.1** We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
- **28.2** We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

## 29. Waiver
- **29.1** If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

## 30. Communication
- **30.1** We will communicate with you in English.
- **30.2** We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

## 31. Interest
- **31.1** We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

## 32. Optional cover: Hearing Care
- **32.1** We will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
- **32.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **32.3** The most we will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $150 per treatment.
- **32.4** We will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

## 33. General exclusions
- **33.1** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
- **33.2** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
- **33.3** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
- **33.4** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
- **33.5** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
- **33.6** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

## 34. Wellness allowance
- **34.1** Each plan year you may claim up to $250 towards a gym membership or fitness class.
- **34.2** The wellness allowance is not subject to any deductible and does not count towards other limits.

## 35. Joint policyholders
- **35.1** Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
- **35.2** A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

## 36. Cancellation
- **36.1** You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
- **36.2** After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
- **36.3** We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

## 37. Third-party administrators
- **37.1** We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
- **37.2** Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

## 38. Duty of fair presentation
- **38.1** You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
- **38.2** If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
- **38.3** If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

## 39. Arbitration
- **39.1** If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
- **39.2** Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

## 40. Compensation scheme
- **40.1** We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
- **40.2** If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

## 41. Premium payment
- **41.1** You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
- **41.2** If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

## 42. Environmental commitment
- **42.1** Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
- **42.2** You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

## 43. Assignment
- **43.1** You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

## 44. Payment of claims
- **44.1** We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
- **44.2** We aim to pay accepted claims within 10 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

## 45. Other insurance
- **45.1** If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
- **45.2** You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

## 46. Governing law
- **46.1** This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
- **46.2** Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

## 47. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
- **47.1** A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

## 48. Exchange of information
- **48.1** To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
- **48.2** We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

## 49. Eligibility
- **49.1** Employees who work at least 20 hours a week are eligible to join the plan from their first day of employment.
- **49.2** Contractors, agency workers and employees on unpaid leave of more than three months are not eligible.

## 50. Changes in circumstances
- **50.1** You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
- **50.2** We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

## 51. Instalment agreements
- **51.1** If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
- **51.2** Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

## 52. Severability
- **52.1** If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

## 53. Fraud
- **53.1** If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
- **53.2** We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

## 54. Appeals
- **54.1** If we decline all or part of a claim, you may appeal in writing within 60 days of the decision.
- **54.2** An appeal will be reviewed by someone who was not involved in the original decision.
- **54.3** We will give you a written decision on the appeal within 30 days.

## 55. Making a claim
- **55.1** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **55.2** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **55.3** You must notify us of a claim within 30 days of the treatment. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

## 56. Cooperation
- **56.1** You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
- **56.2** You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

## 57. Complaints

Issued by Brightline Device Cover

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.

- **5.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 45 days after the policy start date.

- **5.4** We will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
- **5.5** We will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

- **6.1** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

- **6.4** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.

- **15.1** All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.

- **18.1** You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
- **18.2** We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

- **19.1** If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
- **19.2** Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

## 20. Recovery of costs
- **20.1** If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

## 21. Reasonable precautions
- **21.1** You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
- **21.2** You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

## 22. Other insurance
- **22.1** If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
- **22.2** You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

## 23. Duty of fair presentation
- **23.1** You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
- **23.2** If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
- **23.3** If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

## 24. Taxes
- **24.1** The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
- **24.2** If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

## 25. Communication
- **25.1** We will communicate with you in English.
- **25.2** We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

## 26. Geographical limits
- **26.1** Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
- **26.2** Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

## 27. Replacement devices
- **27.1** If we cannot repair your device economically, we will replace it with a replacement device.
- **27.2** Replacement devices may be a different colour and may be refurbished to an as-new standard.
- **27.3** Accessories are replaced only if they were lost or damaged in the same incident as the device.

## 28. Assignment
- **28.1** You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

## 29. Customer support
- **29.1** Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
- **29.2** Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

## 30. Records and evidence
- **30.1** You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
- **30.2** Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
- **30.3** We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

## 31. Interest
- **31.1** We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

## 32. Software support
- **32.1** Our helpline can give advice on setting up and using your device.
- **32.2** Software support does not include fixing problems caused by third-party apps or unofficial operating systems.

## 33. How to read this document
- **33.1** This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
- **33.2** Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
- **33.3** Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

## 34. Cancellation
- **34.1** You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
- **34.2** After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
- **34.3** We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

## 35. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
- **35.1** A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

## 36. Waiver
- **36.1** If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

## 37. Subrogation
- **37.1** We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
- **37.2** We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

## 38. Joint policyholders
- **38.1** Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
- **38.2** A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

## 39. Transferring the plan
- **39.1** You may transfer the plan to a new owner of the device by telling us in writing.
- **39.2** The remaining term of the plan transfers with the device; the term does not restart.

## 40. Arbitration
- **40.1** If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
- **40.2** Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

## 41. Environmental commitment
- **41.1** Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
- **41.2** You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

## 42. Electronic documents
- **42.1** We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
- **42.2** You must tell us if your email address changes.
- **42.3** Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

## 43. Sanctions
- **43.1** We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

## 44. Compensation scheme
- **44.1** We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
- **44.2** If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

- **45.1** Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
- **45.2** You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

## 46. Discounts
- **46.1** Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
- **46.2** If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

## 47. Premium payment
- **47.1** You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
- **47.2** If an instalment is not paid within 21 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

- **48.1** Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
- **48.2** Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.

CASE PRESENTATION A
ANNUAL MULTI-TRIP TRAVEL COVER
Issued by Meridian Travel Insurance Ltd

SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS
1.1 Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
1.2 Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
1.3 Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
1.4 Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
1.5 Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 3,000 metres.
1.6 Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
1.7 Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
1.8 Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
1.9 Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which you received treatment or advice in the 3 months before the policy start date.
1.10 Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
1.11 Public transport means any scheduled train, bus, coach, ferry or aircraft.
1.12 Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 8 hours.
1.13 Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
1.14 Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
1.15 Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
1.16 Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
1.17 Territory means the countries in which cover applies, as shown in the schedule.
1.18 Travelling companion means a person who has booked to travel with you on the same trip.
1.19 Trip means a journey that starts and ends in your home country during the policy period.
1.20 Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

SECTION 2 - LIMITS AND EXCESS
2.1 Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
2.2 Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $25,000 per incident; excess $150 per claim.
2.3 Trip Cancellation: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
2.4 Travel Delay: limit $500 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
2.5 The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

SECTION 3 - EMERGENCY MEDICAL EXPENSES
3.1 We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
3.2 The most we will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $250 per incident.
3.3 The most we will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $300 per incident.
3.4 We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
3.5 We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
3.6 We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

SECTION 4 - BAGGAGE AND PERSONAL BELONGINGS
4.1 We will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to your baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
4.2 The most we will pay for Valuables under this section is $250 per incident.
4.3 The most we will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $450 per incident.
4.4 We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
4.5 We will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
4.6 We will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

SECTION 5 - TRIP CANCELLATION
5.1 We will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if you must cancel the trip for a reason beyond your control.
5.2 No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 14 days after the policy start date.
5.3 The most we will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $300 per incident.
5.4 We will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before you bought the policy.
5.5 We will not pay for cancellation because you no longer wish to travel.

SECTION 6 - OPTIONAL COVER: TRAVEL DELAY
6.1 We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
6.2 This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
6.3 We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

SECTION 7 - GENERAL EXCLUSIONS
7.1 We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
7.2 We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
7.3 We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
7.4 We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
7.5 We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

SECTION 8 - MAKING A CLAIM
8.1 We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
8.2 You must notify us of a claim within 21 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
8.3 You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

SECTION 9 - EMERGENCY ASSISTANCE
9.1 Our emergency assistance service is available 24 hours a day on the number shown in the schedule.
9.2 You must contact the assistance service before being admitted to hospital as an in-patient, unless it is an emergency.
9.3 The assistance service can arrange payment guarantees, interpreters and transport home.

SECTION 10 - PAYMENT OF CLAIMS
10.1 We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
10.2 We aim to pay accepted claims within 15 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

SECTION 11 - CURRENCY
11.1 All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
11.2 Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

SECTION 12 - CUSTOMER SUPPORT
12.1 Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
12.2 Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

SECTION 13 - MARKET CONDITIONS
13.1 If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

SECTION 14 - RENEWAL
14.1 We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
14.2 We are not obliged to offer renewal.

SECTION 15 - SUBROGATION
15.1 We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
15.2 We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

SECTION 16 - PERSONAL LIABILITY
16.1 We will pay damages you become legally liable to pay for accidental injury to another person or accidental damage to their property during the trip.
16.2 This section does not cover liability arising from the use of motor vehicles, boats or aircraft.
16.3 The most we will pay under this section is $5,000,000 for all claims arising from one event.

SECTION 17 - ARBITRATION
17.1 If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
17.2 Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

SECTION 18 - INSTALMENT AGREEMENTS
18.1 If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
18.2 Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

SECTION 19 - COOPERATION
19.1 You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
19.2 You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

SECTION 20 - COMMUNICATION
20.1 We will communicate with you in English.
20.2 We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

SECTION 21 - ASSIGNMENT
21.1 You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

SECTION 22 - LEGAL EXPENSES ABROAD
22.1 We will pay legal costs to pursue compensation for your injury or death caused by a third party during the trip.
22.2 We will not pay legal costs unless our legal adviser agrees that the claim has a reasonable prospect of success.

SECTION 23 - CLAIMS DOCUMENTS
23.1 You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
23.2 We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

SECTION 24 - MISSED DEPARTURE
24.1 We will pay reasonable additional travel and accommodation costs to reach your destination if you arrive too late to board your booked transport because public transport fails.
24.2 You must allow enough time to reach the departure point, and must obtain written confirmation of the delay from the transport operator.

SECTION 25 - JOINT POLICYHOLDERS
25.1 Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
25.2 A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

SECTION 26 - CHANGE OF ADDRESS
26.1 You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
26.2 We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

SECTION 27 - ENVIRONMENTAL COMMITMENT
27.1 Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
27.2 You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

SECTION 28 - SANCTIONS
28.1 We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

SECTION 29 - CANCELLATION
29.1 You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
29.2 After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
29.3 We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

SECTION 30 - FRAUD
30.1 If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
30.2 We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

SECTION 31 - SEVERABILITY
31.1 If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

SECTION 32 - THIRD-PARTY ADMINISTRATORS
32.1 We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
32.2 Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

SECTION 33 - DUTY OF FAIR PRESENTATION
33.1 You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
33.2 If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
33.3 If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

SECTION 34 - CONTRACTS (RIGHTS OF THIRD PARTIES)
34.1 A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

SECTION 35 - COMPENSATION SCHEME
35.1 We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
35.2 If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

SECTION 36 - RECORDS AND EVIDENCE
36.1 You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
36.2 Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
36.3 We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

SECTION 37 - ACCESSIBILITY
37.1 This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

SECTION 38 - INFLATION
38.1 We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
38.2 Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

SECTION 39 - DISCOUNTS
39.1 Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
39.2 If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

SECTION 40 - OTHER INSURANCE
40.1 If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
40.2 You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

SECTION 41 - RECOVERY OF COSTS
41.1 If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

SECTION 42 - ELECTRONIC DOCUMENTS
42.1 We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
42.2 You must tell us if your email address changes.
42.3 Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

SECTION 43 - AUTOMATIC RENEWAL
43.1 Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
43.2 You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

SECTION 44 - NOTICES
44.1 Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
44.2 Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

SECTION 45 - DATA PROTECTION
45.1 We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
45.2 We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
45.3 You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

SECTION 46 - INTEREST
46.1 We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

SECTION 47 - GEOGRAPHICAL LIMITS
47.1 Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
47.2 Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

SECTION 48 - EXCHANGE OF INFORMATION
48.1 To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
48.2 We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

SECTION 49 - TAXES
49.1 The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
49.2 If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

SECTION 50 - HOW TO READ THIS DOCUMENT
50.1 This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
50.2 Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
50.3 Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

# Home Contents Insurance Policy
Issued by Lantern General Insurance

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
- **1.2** Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
- **1.3** Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
- **1.4** Contents means household goods and personal possessions that belong to you or your family.
- **1.5** Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
- **1.6** Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
- **1.7** High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
- **1.8** Home means the private residence at the address shown in the schedule.
- **1.9** Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
- **1.10** Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
- **1.11** Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
- **1.12** Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
- **1.13** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.14** Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
- **1.15** Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
- **1.16** Unoccupied means not lived in by you or a member of your family for more than 60 consecutive days.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Theft: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
- **2.2** Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
- **2.3** Accidental Damage: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
- **2.5** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Flood
- **3.1** We will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering your home.
- **3.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Garden items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for your area had been issued before the policy started.

## 4. Escape of Water
- **4.1** We will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
- **4.2** The most we will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.
- **4.3** We will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
- **4.4** We will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

## 5. Optional cover: Accidental Damage
- **5.1** We will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to your contents inside the home.
- **5.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **5.3** The most we will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $500 per incident.
- **5.4** We will not pay for damage caused by pets.
- **5.5** We will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

## 6. Theft
- **6.1** We will pay for contents stolen from your home.
- **6.2** The most we will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
- **6.3** The most we will pay for Bicycles under this section is $800 per incident.
- **6.4** We will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
- **6.5** We will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
- **6.6** We will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

## 7. General exclusions
- **7.1** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
- **7.2** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **7.3** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
- **7.4** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
- **7.5** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.

- **8.1** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
