CASE PRESENTATION B
ANNUAL MULTI-TRIP TRAVEL COVER
Issued by Meridian Travel Insurance Ltd

SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS
1.1 Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
1.2 Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
1.3 Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
1.4 Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
1.5 Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 3,000 metres.
1.6 Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
1.7 Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
1.8 Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
1.9 Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which you received treatment or advice in the 3 months before the policy start date.
1.10 Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
1.11 Public transport means any scheduled train, bus, coach, ferry or aircraft.
1.12 Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 8 hours.
1.13 Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
1.14 Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
1.15 Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
1.16 Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
1.17 Territory means the countries in which cover applies, as shown in the schedule.
1.18 Travelling companion means a person who has booked to travel with you on the same trip.
1.19 Trip means a journey that starts and ends in your home country during the policy period.
1.20 Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

SECTION 2 - LIMITS AND EXCESS
2.1 Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
2.2 Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $25,000 per incident; excess $150 per claim.
2.3 Trip Cancellation: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
2.4 Travel Delay: limit $500 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
2.5 The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

SECTION 3 - EMERGENCY MEDICAL EXPENSES
3.1 We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
3.2 The most we will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $250 per incident.
3.3 The most we will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $300 per incident.
3.4 We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
3.5 We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
3.6 We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

SECTION 4 - BAGGAGE AND PERSONAL BELONGINGS
4.1 We will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to your baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
4.2 The most we will pay for Valuables under this section is $250 per incident.
4.3 The most we will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $450 per incident.
4.4 We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
4.5 We will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
4.6 We will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

SECTION 5 - TRIP CANCELLATION
5.1 We will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if you must cancel the trip for a reason beyond your control.
5.2 No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 14 days after the policy start date.
5.3 The most we will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $300 per incident.
5.4 We will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before you bought the policy.
5.5 We will not pay for cancellation because you no longer wish to travel.

SECTION 6 - OPTIONAL COVER: TRAVEL DELAY
6.1 We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
6.2 This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
6.3 We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

SECTION 7 - GENERAL EXCLUSIONS
7.1 We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
7.2 We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
7.3 We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
7.4 We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
7.5 We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

SECTION 8 - MAKING A CLAIM
8.1 We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
8.2 You must notify us of a claim within 21 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
8.3 You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

SECTION 9 - EMERGENCY ASSISTANCE
9.1 Our emergency assistance service is available 24 hours a day on the number shown in the schedule.
9.2 You must contact the assistance service before being admitted to hospital as an in-patient, unless it is an emergency.
9.3 The assistance service can arrange payment guarantees, interpreters and transport home.

SECTION 10 - PAYMENT OF CLAIMS
10.1 We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
10.2 We aim to pay accepted claims within 15 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

SECTION 11 - CURRENCY
11.1 All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
11.2 Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

SECTION 12 - CUSTOMER SUPPORT
12.1 Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
12.2 Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

SECTION 13 - MARKET CONDITIONS
13.1 If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

SECTION 14 - RENEWAL
14.1 We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
14.2 We are not obliged to offer renewal.

SECTION 15 - SUBROGATION
15.1 We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
15.2 We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

SECTION 16 - PERSONAL LIABILITY
16.1 We will pay damages you become legally liable to pay for accidental injury to another person or accidental damage to their property during the trip.
16.2 This section does not cover liability arising from the use of motor vehicles, boats or aircraft.
16.3 The most we will pay under this section is $5,000,000 for all claims arising from one event.

SECTION 17 - ARBITRATION
17.1 If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
17.2 Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

SECTION 18 - INSTALMENT AGREEMENTS
18.1 If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
18.2 Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

SECTION 19 - COOPERATION
19.1 You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
19.2 You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

SECTION 20 - COMMUNICATION
20.1 We will communicate with you in English.
20.2 We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

SECTION 21 - ASSIGNMENT
21.1 You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

SECTION 22 - LEGAL EXPENSES ABROAD
22.1 We will pay legal costs to pursue compensation for your injury or death caused by a third party during the trip.
22.2 We will not pay legal costs unless our legal adviser agrees that the claim has a reasonable prospect of success.

SECTION 23 - CLAIMS DOCUMENTS
23.1 You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
23.2 We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

SECTION 24 - MISSED DEPARTURE
24.1 We will pay reasonable additional travel and accommodation costs to reach your destination if you arrive too late to board your booked transport because public transport fails.
24.2 You must allow enough time to reach the departure point, and must obtain written confirmation of the delay from the transport operator.

SECTION 25 - JOINT POLICYHOLDERS
25.1 Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
25.2 A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

SECTION 26 - CHANGE OF ADDRESS
26.1 You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
26.2 We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

SECTION 27 - ENVIRONMENTAL COMMITMENT
27.1 Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
27.2 You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

SECTION 28 - SANCTIONS
28.1 We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

SECTION 29 - CANCELLATION
29.1 You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
29.2 After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
29.3 We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

SECTION 30 - FRAUD
30.1 If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
30.2 We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

SECTION 31 - SEVERABILITY
31.1 If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

SECTION 32 - THIRD-PARTY ADMINISTRATORS
32.1 We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
32.2 Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

SECTION 33 - DUTY OF FAIR PRESENTATION
33.1 You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
33.2 If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
33.3 If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

SECTION 34 - CONTRACTS (RIGHTS OF THIRD PARTIES)
34.1 A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

SECTION 35 - COMPENSATION SCHEME
35.1 We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
35.2 If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

SECTION 36 - RECORDS AND EVIDENCE
36.1 You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
36.2 Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
36.3 We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

SECTION 37 - ACCESSIBILITY
37.1 This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

SECTION 38 - INFLATION
38.1 We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
38.2 Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

SECTION 39 - DISCOUNTS
39.1 Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
39.2 If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

SECTION 40 - OTHER INSURANCE
40.1 If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
40.2 You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

SECTION 41 - RECOVERY OF COSTS
41.1 If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

SECTION 42 - ELECTRONIC DOCUMENTS
42.1 We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
42.2 You must tell us if your email address changes.
42.3 Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

SECTION 43 - AUTOMATIC RENEWAL
43.1 Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
43.2 You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

SECTION 44 - NOTICES
44.1 Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
44.2 Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

SECTION 45 - DATA PROTECTION
45.1 We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
45.2 We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
45.3 You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

SECTION 46 - INTEREST
46.1 We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

SECTION 47 - GEOGRAPHICAL LIMITS
47.1 Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
47.2 Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

SECTION 48 - EXCHANGE OF INFORMATION
48.1 To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
48.2 We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

SECTION 49 - TAXES
49.1 The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
49.2 If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

SECTION 50 - HOW TO READ THIS DOCUMENT
50.1 This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
50.2 Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
50.3 Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

# Staff Health Reimbursement Plan Rules
Issued by the Benefits Trust

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
- **1.2** Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
- **1.3** Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
- **1.4** Hearing aid replacement period means 36 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
- **1.5** Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
- **1.6** Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one treatment.
- **1.7** Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
- **1.8** Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
- **1.9** Network provider means a practitioner or clinic that has an agreement with us to provide treatment.
- **1.10** Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
- **1.11** Plan year means the twelve months starting on your coverage start date.
- **1.12** Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
- **1.13** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.14** Replacement period means 12 months from the date of your last eyewear claim.
- **1.15** Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
- **1.16** Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

## 2. Limits and deductible
- **2.1** Dental Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
- **2.2** Vision Care: limit $500 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
- **2.3** Therapy Services: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Hearing Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
- **2.5** The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Sanctions
- **3.1** We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

## 4. Therapy Services
- **4.1** We will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
- **4.2** The most we will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $300 per treatment.
- **4.3** We will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
- **4.4** We will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

## 5. Dependants
- **5.1** You may enrol dependants at the start of each plan year or within 30 days of a qualifying life event.
- **5.2** Benefits paid for dependants count towards the same annual limits as your own claims.

## 6. Exchange of information
- **6.1** To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
- **6.2** We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

## 7. Recovery of costs
- **7.1** If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

## 8. Accessibility
- **8.1** This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

## 9. Dental Care
- **9.1** We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
- **9.2** No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
- **9.3** The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.
- **9.4** The most we will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $600 per treatment.
- **9.5** We will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
- **9.6** We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

## 10. Discounts
- **10.1** Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
- **10.2** If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

## 11. Severability
- **11.1** If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

## 12. Payment of claims
- **12.1** We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
- **12.2** We aim to pay accepted claims within 15 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

## 13. Claims documents
- **13.1** You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
- **13.2** We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

## 14. Records and evidence
- **14.1** You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
- **14.2** Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
- **14.3** We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

## 15. Other insurance
- **15.1** If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
- **15.2** You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

## 16. Reasonable precautions
- **16.1** You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
- **16.2** You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

## 17. Cancellation
- **17.1** You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
- **17.2** After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
- **17.3** We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

## 18. Complaints
- **18.1** If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
- **18.2** We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
- **18.3** If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

- **19.1** A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

## 20. Market conditions
- **20.1** If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

## 21. Notices
- **21.1** Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
- **21.2** Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

## 22. Wellness allowance
- **22.1** Each plan year you may claim up to $250 towards a gym membership or fitness class.
- **22.2** The wellness allowance is not subject to any deductible and does not count towards other limits.

## 23. Interest
- **23.1** We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

## 24. Data protection
- **24.1** We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
- **24.2** We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
- **24.3** You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

## 25. Third-party administrators
- **25.1** We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
- **25.2** Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

## 26. Vision Care
- **26.1** We will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
- **26.2** The most we will pay for Frames under this section is $150 per treatment.
- **26.3** We will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
- **26.4** We will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

## 27. Inflation
- **27.1** We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
- **27.2** Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

## 28. Appeals
- **28.1** If we decline all or part of a claim, you may appeal in writing within 60 days of the decision.
- **28.2** An appeal will be reviewed by someone who was not involved in the original decision.
- **28.3** We will give you a written decision on the appeal within 30 days.

## 29. Cooperation
- **29.1** You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
- **29.2** You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

## 30. Geographical limits
- **30.1** Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
- **30.2** Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

## 31. Coordination of benefits
- **31.1** If a treatment is also covered by another plan, we will pay only the part of the cost that the other plan does not pay.
- **31.2** You must tell us about any other plan that covers you or your dependants.

## 32. Currency
- **32.1** All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
- **32.2** Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

## 33. Optional cover: Hearing Care
- **33.1** We will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
- **33.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **33.3** The most we will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $100 per treatment.
- **33.4** We will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

## 34. Changes in circumstances
- **34.1** You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
- **34.2** We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

## 35. Customer support
- **35.1** Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
- **35.2** Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

## 36. Arbitration
- **36.1** If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
- **36.2** Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

## 37. General exclusions
- **37.1** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
- **37.2** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **37.3** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
- **37.4** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

## 38. Fraud
- **38.1** If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
- **38.2** We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

## 39. Electronic documents
- **39.1** We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
- **39.2** You must tell us if your email address changes.
- **39.3** Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

## 40. Salvage
- **40.1** When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
- **40.2** If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

## 41. Instalment agreements
- **41.1** If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
- **41.2** Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

## 42. Joint policyholders
- **42.1** Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
- **42.2** A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

## 43. Subrogation
- **43.1** We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
- **43.2** We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

## 44. Making a claim
- **44.1** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **44.2** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **44.3** You must notify us of a claim within 30 days of the treatment. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

## 45. Premium payment
- **45.1** You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
- **45.2** If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

## 46. Waiver
- **46.1** If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

## 47. How to read this document
- **47.1** This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
- **47.2** Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
- **47.3** Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

## 48. Interpretation
- **48.1** Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
- **48.2** Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
- **48.3** Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

## 49. Taxes
- **49.1** The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
- **49.2** If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

## 50. Change of address
- **50.1** You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
- **50.2** We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

## 51. Communication
- **51.1** We will communicate with you in English.
- **51.2** We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

## 52. Eligibility
- **52.1** Employees who work at least 20 hours a week are eligible to join the plan from their first day of employment.
- **52.2** Contractors, agency workers and employees on unpaid leave of more than three months are not eligible.

## 53. Assignment
- **53.1** You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

## 54. Compensation scheme
- **54.1** We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
- **54.2** If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

## 55. Renewal
- **55.1** We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
- **55.2** We are not obliged to offer renewal.

## 56. Environmental commitment
- **56.1** Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
- **56.2** You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

## 57. Leaving the plan
- **57.1** Cover ends on the day your employment ends or the day you stop being eligible, whichever is earlier.
- **57.2** Claims for treatment received before cover ended may be submitted up to 90 days afterwards.

## 58. Duty of fair presentation
- **58.1** You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
- **58.2** If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
- **58.3** If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

## 59. Governing law
- **59.1** This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
- **59.2** Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

## 60. Automatic renewal
- **60.1** Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
- **60.2** You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

Issued by Lantern General Insurance
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Lantern General Insurance and "the Policyholder" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
(b) Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Insurer, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
(c) Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
(d) Contents means household goods and personal possessions that belong to the Policyholder or the Policyholder's family.
(e) Family means the Policyholder's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Policyholder.
(f) Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
(g) Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
(h) High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
(i) Limit means the most the Insurer will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
(j) Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.
(k) Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Policyholder's schedule.
(l) Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
(m) Premium means the amount the Policyholder must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
(n) Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
(o) Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
(p) Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Policyholder's details, the covers the Policyholder bought and any extensions.
(q) Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
(r) Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 30 consecutive days.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Theft: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(b) Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
(c) Accidental Damage: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(d) Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
(e) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Escape of Water
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

Article 4. Flood
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

Article 5. Notices
(a) Any notice the Insurer gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Insurer holds.
(b) Notices from the Policyholder should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

Article 6. Severability
(a) If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

Article 7. Duty of fair presentation
(a) The Policyholder must answer all questions the Insurer asks honestly and to the best of the Policyholder's knowledge.
(b) If the Policyholder gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Insurer may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
(c) If the Policyholder gives incorrect information carelessly, the Insurer may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

Article 8. Payment of claims
(a) The Insurer will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Policyholder's name.
(b) The Insurer aims to pay accepted claims within 10 working days of receiving all the documents the Insurer needs.

Article 9. Customer support
(a) The Insurer's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
(b) Outside these hours the Policyholder can leave a message and the Insurer will call back on the next working day.

(a) This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
(b) Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
(c) Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

Article 11. Theft
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,500 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $800 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

Article 12. Arbitration

(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

Article 27. Sanctions
(a) The Insurer will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Insurer to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

Article 28. Discounts
(a) Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.

STAFF HEALTH REIMBURSEMENT PLAN RULES
Issued by Cedar Benefits Services

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
I.2  Hearing aid replacement period means 36 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
I.3  Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
I.4  Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
I.5  Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
I.6  Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
I.7  Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
I.8  Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

PART II: Limits and deductible
II.1  Dental Care: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
II.2  Vision Care: limit $400 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
II.3  Therapy Services: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
II.4  Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
II.5  The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Dental Care
III.1  The Plan will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
III.2  No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
III.3  The most the Plan will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $750 per treatment.
III.4  The most the Plan will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $600 per treatment.
III.5  The Plan will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
III.6  The Plan will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

PART IV: Optional cover: Hearing Care
IV.1  The Plan will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
IV.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Member's schedule.
IV.3  The most the Plan will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $150 per treatment.
IV.4  The Plan will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

PART V: Therapy Services
V.1  The Plan will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
V.2  The most the Plan will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $200 per treatment.
V.3  The Plan will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
V.4  The Plan will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

PART VI: General exclusions
VI.1  The Plan will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Plan from paying.
VI.2  The Plan will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
VI.3  The Plan will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

PART VII: Making a claim
VII.1  The Member must notify the Plan of a claim within 90 days of the treatment. The Plan will not pay any claim notified after that time.
VII.2  The Plan may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
VII.3  The Member must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

PART VIII: Coordination of benefits
VIII.1  If a treatment is also covered by another plan, the Plan will pay only the part of the cost that the other plan does not pay.
VIII.2  The Member must tell the Plan about any other plan that covers the Member or the Member's dependants.

II.3  Accidental Damage: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.4  Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
II.5  The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Theft
III.1  The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
III.2  The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,500 per incident.
III.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $500 per incident.
III.4  The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
III.5  The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
III.6  The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

PART IV: Flood
IV.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
IV.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
IV.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
IV.4  The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

PART V: Optional cover: Accidental Damage
V.1  The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
V.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
V.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $500 per incident.
V.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
V.5  The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

PART VI: Escape of Water
VI.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
VI.2  The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.
VI.3  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
VI.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

PART VII: General exclusions
VII.1  The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
VII.2  The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
VII.3  The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.
VII.4  The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

VIII.1  The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

VIII.3  The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 60 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

PART IX: Interpretation
IX.1  Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
IX.2  Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
IX.3  Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

XVI.1  The Policyholder cannot transfer the Policyholder's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Insurer's written consent.

PART XVII: Salvage
XVII.1  When the Insurer replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Insurer's property.
XVII.2  If stolen property is recovered after the Insurer has paid a claim, the Policyholder must tell the Insurer and either return the payment or give the Insurer the property.

PART XVIII: Waiver
XVIII.1  If the Insurer does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Insurer has given up the right to enforce it later.

PART XIX: Other insurance
XIX.1  If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Insurer will pay only the Insurer's proportionate share.
XIX.2  The Policyholder must tell the Insurer about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Policyholder makes a claim.

PART XX: Accessibility
XX.1  This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

PART XXI: Locks and keys
XXI.1  If the keys to the Policyholder's home are lost or stolen, the Insurer will pay the cost of replacing the locks to the outside doors.
XXI.2  The most the Insurer will pay under this clause is $500 for any one claim.

PART XXII: Notices
XXII.1  Any notice the Insurer gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Insurer holds.
XXII.2  Notices from the Policyholder should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

PART XXIII: Sanctions
XXIII.1  The Insurer will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Insurer to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

PART XXIV: Tenant's improvements
XXIV.1  If the Policyholder rents the home, the Insurer will pay for damage to fixtures and fittings that the Policyholder installed and are responsible for.

HOME CONTENTS INSURANCE POLICY
Issued by Oakfield Assurance

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
I.2  Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Insurer, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
I.3  Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
I.4  Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
I.5  Contents means household goods and personal possessions that belong to the Policyholder or the Policyholder's family.
I.6  Family means the Policyholder's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Policyholder.
I.7  Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
I.8  Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
I.9  High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
I.10  Home means the private residence at the address shown in the schedule.
I.11  Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
I.12  Limit means the most the Insurer will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
I.13  Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Policyholder's schedule.
I.14  Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
I.15  Premium means the amount the Policyholder must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
I.16  Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
I.17  Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Policyholder's details, the covers the Policyholder bought and any extensions.
I.18  Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
I.19  Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 30 consecutive days.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Theft: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.2  Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.3  Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.4  Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.5  The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Theft
III.1  The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
III.2  The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $2,500 per incident.
III.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $500 per incident.
III.4  The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
III.5  The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
III.6  The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

PART IV: Escape of Water
IV.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
IV.2  The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.
IV.3  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
IV.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

PART V: Changes in circumstances
V.1  The Policyholder must tell the Insurer as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
V.2  The Insurer may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

PART VI: Geographical limits
VI.1  Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
VI.2  Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

PART VII: Instalment agreements
VII.1  If the Policyholder pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
VII.2  Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

PART VIII: Currency
VIII.1  All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
VIII.2  Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

PART IX: Cancellation
IX.1  The Policyholder can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
IX.2  After the first 14 days the Policyholder can cancel at any time; the Insurer will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
IX.3  The Insurer can cancel this policy by giving the Policyholder 30 days' written notice to the last address the Insurer holds.

PART X: Notices
X.1  Any notice the Insurer gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Insurer holds.
X.2  Notices from the Policyholder should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

PART XI: Accessibility
XI.1  This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

PART XII: Complaints
XII.1  If the Policyholder has a complaint, the Policyholder should first contact the Insurer's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
XII.2  The Insurer will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
XII.3  If the Policyholder remains dissatisfied, the Policyholder may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

PART XIII: Optional cover: Accidental Damage
XIII.1  The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
XIII.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
XIII.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $500 per incident.
XIII.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
XIII.5  The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

PART XIV: Recovery of costs
XIV.1  If the Insurer pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Insurer may ask the Policyholder to repay the amount.

PART XV: Interest
XV.1  The Insurer will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

PART XVI: Waiver
XVI.1  If the Insurer does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Insurer has given up the right to enforce it later.

PART XVII: How to read this document
XVII.1  This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
XVII.2  Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
XVII.3  Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

PART XVIII: Flood
XVIII.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
XVIII.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
XVIII.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
XVIII.4  The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

PART XIX: Freezer contents
XIX.1  The Insurer will pay for food in a domestic freezer that spoils because of a rise or fall in temperature.
XIX.2  The Insurer will not pay if the freezer is more than fifteen years old, or if the electricity supplier cut the supply deliberately.

PART XX: Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
XX.1  A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

PART XXI: Customer support
XXI.1  The Insurer's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
XXI.2  Outside these hours the Policyholder can leave a message and the Insurer will call back on the next working day.

PART XXII: General exclusions
XXII.1  The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
XXII.2  The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
XXII.3  The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
XXII.4  The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.
XXII.5  The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
XXII.6  The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.

PART XXIII: Fraud
XXIII.1  If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Insurer will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
XXIII.2  The Insurer may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

PART XXIV: Governing law
XXIV.1  This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
XXIV.2  Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

PART XXV: Making a claim
XXV.1  The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 30 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
XXV.2  The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
XXV.3  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

I.11  Wearables means smartwatches and fitness trackers.

PART II: Limits and service fee
II.1  Accidental Damage: limit $1,500 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
II.2  Breakdown: limit $1,000 per incident; service fee $25 per claim.
II.3  Theft and Loss: limit $800 per incident; service fee $149 per claim.
II.4  Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the service fee is then deducted from the result.

PART III: Compensation scheme
III.1  The Provider is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
III.2  If the Provider cannot meet the Provider's obligations, the Customer may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

PART IV: Exchange of information
IV.1  To prevent fraud, the Provider may check the details the Customer gives against public records and industry databases.
IV.2  The Provider may contact previous insurers to confirm the Customer's claims history.

PART V: Transferring the plan
V.1  The Customer may transfer the plan to a new owner of the device by telling the Provider in writing.
V.2  The remaining term of the plan transfers with the device; the term does not restart.

PART VI: Fraud
VI.1  If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Provider will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
VI.2  The Provider may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

PART VII: Renewal
VII.1  The Provider will write to the Customer at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
VII.2  The Provider is not obliged to offer renewal.

PART VIII: Subrogation
VIII.1  The Provider will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Customer's name the defence or settlement of any claim.
VIII.2  The Provider can take action in the Customer's name to recover any payment the Provider makes from anyone responsible for the loss.

PART IX: How to read this document
IX.1  This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
IX.2  Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
IX.3  Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

PART X: Notices
X.1  Any notice the Provider gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Provider holds.
X.2  Notices from the Customer should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

PART XI: Assignment
XI.1  The Customer cannot transfer the Customer's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Provider's written consent.

PART XII: Discounts
XII.1  Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
XII.2  If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Provider may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

PART XIII: Interpretation
XIII.1  Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
XIII.2  Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
XIII.3  Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

PART XIV: Third-party administrators
XIV.1  The Provider may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Provider's behalf.
XIV.2  Any company the Provider appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

PART XV: Premium payment
XV.1  The Customer must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
XV.2  If an instalment is not paid within 21 days of its due date, the Provider may cancel the policy after giving notice.

PART XVI: Other insurance
XVI.1  If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Provider will pay only the Provider's proportionate share.
XVI.2  The Customer must tell the Provider about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Customer makes a claim.

PART XVII: Repair process
XVII.1  After a claim is accepted, the Provider will send a prepaid mailer or book a courier collection.
XVII.2  The Provider aims to return repaired devices within 5 business days of receiving them.

PART XVIII: Breakdown
XVIII.1  The Provider will repair or replace the Customer's device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
XVIII.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 45 days after the policy start date.
XVIII.3  The most the Provider will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $80 per incident.
XVIII.4  The Provider will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
XVIII.5  The Provider will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

PART XIX: Sanctions
XIX.1  The Provider will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Provider to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

PART XX: Recovery of costs
XX.1  If the Provider pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Provider may ask the Customer to repay the amount.

PART XXI: Optional cover: Theft and Loss
XXI.1  The Provider will replace the Customer's device if it is stolen or lost.
XXI.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Customer's schedule.
XXI.3  The most the Provider will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
XXI.4  The Provider will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
XXI.5  The Provider will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

PART XXII: Duty of fair presentation
XXII.1  The Customer must answer all questions the Provider asks honestly and to the best of the Customer's knowledge.
XXII.2  If the Customer gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Provider may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
XXII.3  If the Customer gives incorrect information carelessly, the Provider may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

PART XXIII: Changes in circumstances
XXIII.1  The Customer must tell the Provider as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
XXIII.2  The Provider may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

PART XXIV: Salvage
XXIV.1  When the Provider replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Provider's property.
XXIV.2  If stolen property is recovered after the Provider has paid a claim, the Customer must tell the Provider and either return the payment or give the Provider the property.

PART XXV: Currency
XXV.1  All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
XXV.2  Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

PART XXVI: Accidental Damage
XXVI.1  The Provider will repair or replace the Customer's device if it is accidentally damaged.
XXVI.2  The most the Provider will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
XXVI.3  The most the Provider will pay for Wearables under this section is $250 per incident.
XXVI.4  The Provider will not pay for cosmetic damage, such as scratches or dents, that does not affect how the device works.
XXVI.5  The Provider will not pay for damage following a repair by anyone other than the Provider or an authorised repairer. This exclusion does not apply if the Provider approved the repair in writing beforehand.

PART XXVII: Communication
XXVII.1  The Provider will communicate with the Customer in English.
XXVII.2  The Provider may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

PART XXVIII: Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
XXVIII.1  A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

PART XXIX: Cooperation
XXIX.1  The Customer must give the Provider all the help and information the Provider reasonably need to settle a claim.
XXIX.2  The Customer must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Provider's written permission.

PART XXX: Governing law
XXX.1  This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
XXX.2  Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

PART XXXI: General exclusions
XXXI.1  The Provider will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
XXXI.2  The Provider will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
XXXI.3  The Provider will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Provider from paying.

PART XXXII: Data and backups
XXXII.1  The Provider is not responsible for recovering or restoring any data, software or settings stored on the Customer's device.
XXXII.2  The Customer should back up the Customer's data regularly and before sending the device for repair.

PART XXXIII: Interest
XXXIII.1  The Provider will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

PART XXXIV: Making a claim
XXXIV.1  The Provider may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
XXXIV.2  The Customer must notify the Provider of a claim within 30 days of the incident. The Provider will not pay any claim notified after that time.
XXXIV.3  The Customer must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

PART XXXV: Payment of claims
XXXV.1  The Provider will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Customer's name.
XXXV.2  The Provider aims to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents the Provider needs.

PART XXXVI: Change of address
XXXVI.1  The Customer must tell the Provider within 30 days if the Customer changes the Customer's address.
XXXVI.2  The Provider may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

PART XXXVII: Accessibility
XXXVII.1  This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

PART XXXVIII: Reasonable precautions
XXXVIII.1  The Customer must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
XXXVIII.2  The Customer must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

PART XXXIX: Arbitration
XXXIX.1  If the Provider accepts a claim but disagree with the Customer about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
XXXIX.2  Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against the Provider.

PART XXXX: Joint policyholders
XXXX.1  Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.

PART XXXXI: Claims documents
XXXXI.1  The Customer must provide, at the Customer's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Provider reasonably ask for.
XXXXI.2  The Provider may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

PART XXXXII: Records and evidence
XXXXII.1  The Customer should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
XXXXII.2  Where proof of value is missing, the Provider may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.

XXXXIV.1  If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

- **23.1** Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
