In this policy, "the Insurer" means Lantern General Insurance and "the Policyholder" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
(b) Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
(c) Family means the Policyholder's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Policyholder.
(d) Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
(e) Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
(f) High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
(g) Limit means the most the Insurer will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
(h) Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Policyholder's schedule.
(i) Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
(j) Premium means the amount the Policyholder must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
(k) Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
(l) Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
(m) Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 45 consecutive days.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Theft: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
(b) Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(c) Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(d) Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(e) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Flood
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 14 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

Article 4. Customer support
(a) The Insurer's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
(b) Outside these hours the Policyholder can leave a message and the Insurer will call back on the next working day.

Article 5. Sanctions
(a) The Insurer will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Insurer to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

Article 6. Theft
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $800 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

Article 7. Claims documents
(a) The Policyholder must provide, at the Policyholder's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Insurer reasonably ask for.
(b) The Insurer may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

Article 8. Optional cover: Accidental Damage
(a) The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $750 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

Article 9. Severability
(a) If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

Article 10. Freezer contents
(a) The Insurer will pay for food in a domestic freezer that spoils because of a rise or fall in temperature.
(b) The Insurer will not pay if the freezer is more than fifteen years old, or if the electricity supplier cut the supply deliberately.

Article 11. Garden and outdoor cover
(a) The Insurer will pay for plants, trees and shrubs in the garden of the home that are damaged by fire, lightning or theft.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by frost, storms, drought or animals.

Article 12. Cooperation
(a) The Policyholder must give the Insurer all the help and information the Insurer reasonably need to settle a claim.
(b) The Policyholder must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Insurer's written permission.

Article 13. Recovery of costs
(a) If the Insurer pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Insurer may ask the Policyholder to repay the amount.

Article 14. Escape of Water
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $2,000 per incident.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

Article 15. Records and evidence
(a) The Policyholder should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
(b) Where proof of value is missing, the Insurer may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
(c) The Insurer may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

Article 16. Change of address
(a) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer within 30 days if the Policyholder changes the Policyholder's address.
(b) The Insurer may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

Article 17. Assignment
(a) The Policyholder cannot transfer the Policyholder's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Insurer's written consent.

Article 18. Waiver
(a) If the Insurer does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Insurer has given up the right to enforce it later.

Article 19. Reasonable precautions
(a) The Policyholder must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
(b) The Policyholder must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

Article 20. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
(a) A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

Article 21. How to read this document
(a) This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
(b) Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
(c) Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

Article 22. Cancellation
(a) The Policyholder can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
(b) After the first 14 days the Policyholder can cancel at any time; the Insurer will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
(c) The Insurer can cancel this policy by giving the Policyholder 30 days' written notice to the last address the Insurer holds.

Article 23. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

Article 24. Complaints
(a) If the Policyholder has a complaint, the Policyholder should first contact the Insurer's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
(b) The Insurer will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
(c) If the Policyholder remains dissatisfied, the Policyholder may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

Article 25. Making a claim
(a) The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 14 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(b) The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(c) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

Article 26. Automatic renewal
(a) Unless the Policyholder tells the Insurer otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Insurer holds.
(b) The Policyholder can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Insurer's helpline.

Article 27. Other insurance
(a) If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Insurer will pay only the Insurer's proportionate share.
(b) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Policyholder makes a claim.

Article 28. Third-party administrators
(a) The Insurer may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Insurer's behalf.
(b) Any company the Insurer appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

Article 29. Market conditions
(a) If the replacement item is no longer available, the Insurer will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

Article 30. Currency
(a) All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
(b) Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

Article 31. Discounts
(a) Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
(b) If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Insurer may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

Article 32. Subrogation
(a) The Insurer will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Policyholder's name the defence or settlement of any claim.
(b) The Insurer can take action in the Policyholder's name to recover any payment the Insurer makes from anyone responsible for the loss.

Article 33. Compensation scheme
(a) The Insurer is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
(b) If the Insurer cannot meet the Insurer's obligations, the Policyholder may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

Article 34. Communication
(a) The Insurer will communicate with the Policyholder in English.
(b) The Insurer may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

Article 35. Accessibility
(a) This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

Article 36. Interpretation
(a) Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
(b) Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
(c) Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

Article 37. Alternative accommodation
(a) If the Policyholder's home cannot be lived in after damage covered by this policy, the Insurer will pay the reasonable cost of comparable temporary accommodation.
(b) The Insurer will also pay for the temporary housing of pets that live with the Policyholder.
(c) Cover ends when the home is fit to live in again or after twelve months, whichever is sooner.

Article 38. Interest
(a) The Insurer will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

Article 39. Electronic documents
(a) The Insurer will send documents by email unless the Policyholder asks for paper copies.
(b) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer if the Policyholder's email address changes.
(c) Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

Article 40. Governing law
(a) This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
(b) Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

- **1.18** Territory means the countries in which cover applies, as shown in the schedule.
- **1.19** Travelling companion means a person who has booked to travel with you on the same trip.

- **3.1** We will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to your baggage and personal belongings during the trip.

- **3.6** We will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

- **32.1** If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

- **34.1** Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
- **34.2** Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

- **35.2** We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

- **36.1** You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.

HOME CONTENTS INSURANCE POLICY
Issued by Lantern General Insurance

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
I.2  Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.
I.3  Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
I.4  Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Policyholder's details, the covers the Policyholder bought and any extensions.
I.5  Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Theft: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
II.2  Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.3  Accidental Damage: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.4  Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
II.5  The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Freezer contents
III.1  The Insurer will pay for food in a domestic freezer that spoils because of a rise or fall in temperature.
III.2  The Insurer will not pay if the freezer is more than fifteen years old, or if the electricity supplier cut the supply deliberately.

PART IV: Reasonable precautions
IV.1  The Policyholder must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
IV.2  The Policyholder must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

PART V: Changes in circumstances
V.1  The Policyholder must tell the Insurer as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
V.2  The Insurer may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

PART VI: Taxes
VI.1  The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
VI.2  If the tax rate changes, the Insurer may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

PART VII: Payment of claims
VII.1  The Insurer will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Policyholder's name.
VII.2  The Insurer aims to pay accepted claims within 10 working days of receiving all the documents the Insurer needs.

PART VIII: Fraud
VIII.1  If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Insurer will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
VIII.2  The Insurer may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

PART IX: Optional cover: Accidental Damage
IX.1  The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
IX.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
IX.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $750 per incident.
IX.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
IX.5  The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

PART X: Flood
X.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
X.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
X.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
X.4  The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

PART XI: Cooperation
XI.1  The Policyholder must give the Insurer all the help and information the Insurer reasonably need to settle a claim.
XI.2  The Policyholder must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Insurer's written permission.

PART XII: Currency
XII.1  All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
XII.2  Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

PART XIII: Customer support
XIII.1  The Insurer's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
XIII.2  Outside these hours the Policyholder can leave a message and the Insurer will call back on the next working day.

PART XIV: General exclusions
XIV.1  The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.
XIV.2  The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

PART XV: Duty of fair presentation
XV.1  The Policyholder must answer all questions the Insurer asks honestly and to the best of the Policyholder's knowledge.
XV.2  If the Policyholder gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Insurer may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
XV.3  If the Policyholder gives incorrect information carelessly, the Insurer may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

PART XVI: Cancellation
XVI.1  The Policyholder can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
XVI.2  After the first 14 days the Policyholder can cancel at any time; the Insurer will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
XVI.3  The Insurer can cancel this policy by giving the Policyholder 30 days' written notice to the last address the Insurer holds.

PART XVII: Compensation scheme
XVII.1  The Insurer is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
XVII.2  If the Insurer cannot meet the Insurer's obligations, the Policyholder may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

PART XVIII: Salvage
XVIII.1  When the Insurer replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Insurer's property.
XVIII.2  If stolen property is recovered after the Insurer has paid a claim, the Policyholder must tell the Insurer and either return the payment or give the Insurer the property.

PART XIX: Exchange of information
XIX.1  To prevent fraud, the Insurer may check the details the Policyholder gives against public records and industry databases.
XIX.2  The Insurer may contact previous insurers to confirm the Policyholder's claims history.

PART XX: Assignment
XX.1  The Policyholder cannot transfer the Policyholder's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Insurer's written consent.

PART XXI: Environmental commitment
XXI.1  Where practical, the Insurer will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
XXI.2  The Policyholder may ask for a new part instead, and the Insurer will tell the Policyholder whether any additional cost would apply.

PART XXII: Recovery of costs
XXII.1  If the Insurer pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Insurer may ask the Policyholder to repay the amount.

PART XXIII: Claims documents
XXIII.1  The Policyholder must provide, at the Policyholder's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Insurer reasonably ask for.
XXIII.2  The Insurer may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

PART XXIV: Making a claim
XXIV.1  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
XXIV.2  The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
XXIV.3  The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 60 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

PART XXV: Instalment agreements
XXV.1  If the Policyholder pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
XXV.2  Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

PART XXVI: Inflation
XXVI.1  The Insurer may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
XXVI.2  Any adjustment will be shown in the Policyholder's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

PART XXVII: Sanctions
XXVII.1  The Insurer will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Insurer to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

PART XXVIII: Data protection
XXVIII.1  The Insurer will use the personal information the Policyholder provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
XXVIII.2  The Insurer will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
XXVIII.3  The Policyholder can ask for a copy of the personal information the Insurer holds by writing to the Insurer's data protection officer.

CASE PRESENTATION A
# Staff Health Reimbursement Plan Rules
Issued by Wellspring Benefits Administration

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
- **1.2** Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
- **1.3** Dependant means your spouse or partner, or a child under 21 who is enrolled in the plan.
- **1.4** Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
- **1.5** Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
- **1.6** Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
- **1.7** Hearing aid replacement period means 24 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
- **1.8** Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
- **1.9** Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one treatment.
- **1.10** Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
- **1.11** Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
- **1.12** Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
- **1.13** Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
- **1.14** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.15** Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
- **1.16** Replacement period means 24 months from the date of your last eyewear claim.
- **1.17** Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
- **1.18** Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

## 2. Limits and deductible
- **2.1** Dental Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
- **2.2** Vision Care: limit $300 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
- **2.3** Therapy Services: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
- **2.5** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Wellness allowance
- **3.1** Each plan year you may claim up to $100 towards a gym membership or fitness class.
- **3.2** The wellness allowance is not subject to any deductible and does not count towards other limits.

## 4. Assignment
- **4.1** You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

## 5. Therapy Services
- **5.1** We will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
- **5.2** The most we will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $200 per treatment.
- **5.3** We will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
- **5.4** We will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

## 6. Vision Care
- **6.1** We will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
- **6.2** The most we will pay for Frames under this section is $150 per treatment.
- **6.3** We will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
- **6.4** We will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

## 7. Arbitration
- **7.1** If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
- **7.2** Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

## 8. Cancellation
- **8.1** You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
- **8.2** After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $30.
- **8.3** We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

## 9. Other insurance
- **9.1** If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
- **9.2** You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

## 10. Automatic renewal
- **10.1** Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
- **10.2** You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

## 11. Duty of fair presentation
- **11.1** You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
- **11.2** If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
- **11.3** If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

## 12. Recovery of costs
- **12.1** If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

## 13. Optional cover: Hearing Care
- **13.1** We will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
- **13.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **13.3** The most we will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $100 per treatment.
- **13.4** We will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

## 14. Compensation scheme
- **14.1** We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
- **14.2** If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

## 15. Instalment agreements
- **15.1** If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
- **15.2** Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

## 16. Changes in circumstances
- **16.1** You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
- **16.2** We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

## 17. Accessibility
- **17.1** This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

## 18. Salvage
- **18.1** When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
- **18.2** If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

## 19. Communication
- **19.1** We will communicate with you in English.
- **19.2** We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

## 20. Dental Care
- **20.1** We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
- **20.2** No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
- **20.3** The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.
- **20.4** The most we will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $600 per treatment.
- **20.5** We will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
- **20.6** We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

## 21. Subrogation
- **21.1** We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
- **21.2** We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

## 22. Fraud
- **22.1** If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
- **22.2** We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

## 23. Exchange of information
- **23.1** To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
- **23.2** We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

## 24. Leaving the plan
- **24.1** Cover ends on the day your employment ends or the day you stop being eligible, whichever is earlier.
- **24.2** Claims for treatment received before cover ended may be submitted up to 90 days afterwards.

## 25. Governing law
- **25.1** This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
- **25.2** Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

## 26. Inflation
- **26.1** We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
- **26.2** Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

## 27. Severability
- **27.1** If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

## 28. Interest
- **28.1** We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

## 29. Currency
- **29.1** All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
- **29.2** Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

## 30. Environmental commitment
- **30.1** Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
- **30.2** You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

## 31. Reasonable precautions
- **31.1** You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
- **31.2** You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

## 32. Records and evidence
- **32.1** You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
- **32.2** Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
- **32.3** We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

## 33. Renewal
- **33.1** We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
- **33.2** We are not obliged to offer renewal.

## 34. General exclusions
- **34.1** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
- **34.2** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **34.3** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
- **34.4** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
- **34.5** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
- **34.6** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

## 35. Joint policyholders
- **35.1** Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
- **35.2** A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

## 36. Electronic documents
- **36.1** We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
- **36.2** You must tell us if your email address changes.
- **36.3** Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

## 37. Making a claim
- **37.1** You must notify us of a claim within 30 days of the treatment. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **37.2** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **37.3** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

## 38. How to read this document
- **38.1** This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
- **38.2** Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
- **38.3** Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

## 39. Interpretation
- **39.1** Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
- **39.2** Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
- **39.3** Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

## 40. Appeals
- **40.1** If we decline all or part of a claim, you may appeal in writing within 60 days of the decision.
- **40.2** An appeal will be reviewed by someone who was not involved in the original decision.
- **40.3** We will give you a written decision on the appeal within 30 days.

# Single-Trip Travel Protection Plan
Issued by Compass Mutual

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
- **1.2** Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
- **1.3** Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
- **1.4** Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
- **1.5** Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
- **1.6** Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 3,000 metres.
- **1.7** Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
- **1.8** Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
- **1.9** Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
- **1.10** Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which you received treatment or advice in the 3 months before the policy start date.
- **1.11** Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
- **1.12** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.13** Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 12 hours.
- **1.14** Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
- **1.15** Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
- **1.16** Travelling companion means a person who has booked to travel with you on the same trip.
- **1.17** Trip means a journey that starts and ends in your home country during the policy period.
- **1.18** Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.2** Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $150 per claim.
- **2.3** Trip Cancellation: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Travel Delay: limit $300 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
- **2.5** The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Baggage and Personal Belongings
- **3.1** We will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to your baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
- **3.2** The most we will pay for Valuables under this section is $400 per incident.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $450 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
- **3.5** We will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
- **3.6** We will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

## 4. Optional cover: Travel Delay
- **4.1** We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
- **4.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **4.3** We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

## 5. Emergency Medical Expenses
- **5.1** We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
- **5.2** The most we will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $400 per incident.
- **5.3** The most we will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $500 per incident.
- **5.4** We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
- **5.5** We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
- **5.6** We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

## 6. Trip Cancellation
- **6.1** We will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if you must cancel the trip for a reason beyond your control.
- **6.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 14 days after the policy start date.
- **6.3** The most we will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $200 per incident.
- **6.4** We will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before you bought the policy.
- **6.5** We will not pay for cancellation because you no longer wish to travel.

## 7. General exclusions
- **7.1** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **7.2** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
- **7.3** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
- **7.4** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
- **7.5** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
- **7.6** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.

## 8. Making a claim
- **8.1** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **8.2** You must notify us of a claim within 90 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **8.3** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

## 9. Cancellation
- **9.1** You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
- **9.2** After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
- **9.3** We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

## 10. Sanctions
- **10.1** We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

## 11. Customer support
- **11.1** Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
- **11.2** Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

## 12. Cooperation
- **12.1** You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
- **12.2** You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

## 13. Accessibility
- **13.1** This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

## 14. Fraud
- **14.1** If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
- **14.2** We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

## 15. Repatriation
- **15.1** If our medical adviser agrees it is necessary, we will arrange and pay for you to be brought home.
- **15.2** We will decide the method of transport and the time of repatriation after speaking to the treating doctor.

## 16. Recovery of costs
- **16.1** If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

## 17. Salvage
- **17.1** When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
- **17.2** If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

## 18. Data protection
- **18.1** We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
- **18.2** We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
- **18.3** You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

## 19. Records and evidence
- **19.1** You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
- **19.2** Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
- **19.3** We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

## 20. Reasonable precautions
- **20.1** You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
- **20.2** You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

## 21. Instalment agreements
- **21.1** If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
- **21.2** Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

## 22. Other insurance
- **22.1** If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
- **22.2** You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

## 23. Joint policyholders
- **23.1** Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
- **23.2** A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

## 24. Arbitration
- **24.1** If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
- **24.2** Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

## 25. Changes in circumstances
- **25.1** You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
- **25.2** We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

## 26. Governing law
- **26.1** This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
- **26.2** Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

## 27. Compensation scheme
- **27.1** We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
- **27.2** If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

## 28. Change of address
- **28.1** You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
- **28.2** We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

## 29. Communication
- **29.1** We will communicate with you in English.
- **29.2** We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

## 30. Assignment
- **30.1** You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

## 31. Inflation
- **31.1** We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
- **31.2** Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

## 32. Claims documents
- **32.1** You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
- **32.2** We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

## 33. Premium payment
- **33.1** You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
- **33.2** If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

## 34. Automatic renewal
- **34.1** Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
- **34.2** You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

## 35. Third-party administrators
- **35.1** We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
- **35.2** Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

## 36. Environmental commitment
- **36.1** Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
- **36.2** You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

## 37. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
- **37.1** A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

## 38. Taxes
- **38.1** The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
- **38.2** If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

## 39. Complaints
- **39.1** If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
- **39.2** We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
- **39.3** If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

## 40. Severability
- **40.1** If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

## 41. Emergency assistance
- **41.1** Our emergency assistance service is available 24 hours a day on the number shown in the schedule.
- **41.2** You must contact the assistance service before being admitted to hospital as an in-patient, unless it is an emergency.
- **41.3** The assistance service can arrange payment guarantees, interpreters and transport home.

## 42. Electronic documents
- **42.1** We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
- **42.2** You must tell us if your email address changes.
- **42.3** Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

## 43. How to read this document
- **43.1** This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
- **43.2** Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
- **43.3** Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

## 44. Interpretation
- **44.1** Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
- **44.2** Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
- **44.3** Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

## 45. Renewal
- **45.1** We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
- **45.2** We are not obliged to offer renewal.

## 46. Notices
- **46.1** Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
- **46.2** Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

## 47. Discounts
- **47.1** Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
- **47.2** If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

## 48. Personal liability
- **48.1** We will pay damages you become legally liable to pay for accidental injury to another person or accidental damage to their property during the trip.
- **48.2** This section does not cover liability arising from the use of motor vehicles, boats or aircraft.
- **48.3** The most we will pay under this section is $2,000,000 for all claims arising from one event.

## 49. Subrogation
- **49.1** We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
- **49.2** We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

## 50. Duty of fair presentation
- **50.1** You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
- **50.2** If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
- **50.3** If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

## 51. Interest
- **51.1** We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

## 52. Legal expenses abroad
- **52.1** We will pay legal costs to pursue compensation for your injury or death caused by a third party during the trip.
- **52.2** We will not pay legal costs unless our legal adviser agrees that the claim has a reasonable prospect of success.

## 53. Exchange of information
- **53.1** To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
- **53.2** We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

## 54. Waiver
- **54.1** If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

## 55. Currency
- **55.1** All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
- **55.2** Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

## 56. Geographical limits
- **56.1** Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
- **56.2** Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

## 57. Missed departure
- **57.1** We will pay reasonable additional travel and accommodation costs to reach your destination if you arrive too late to board your booked transport because public transport fails.
- **57.2** You must allow enough time to reach the departure point, and must obtain written confirmation of the delay from the transport operator.

--- a/tests/test_engines.py
+++ b/tests/test_engines.py
@@ -83 +83,103 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python
 
+from __future__ import print_function
+
+import unittest
+
+try:
+    from unittest import mock
+except ImportError:
+    import mock
+
+import imp
+import os.path
+
+
+import engines
+
+
+class TestInit(unittest.TestCase):
+
+    def test_init(self):
+        mock_engines = {}
+
+        mock_listdir = mock.Mock(return_value=(
+                'text_engine.txt',
+                '0_engine.py',
+                '.period_engine.py',
+                '@at_engine.py',
+                '__init__.py',
+                '_underscore_engine.py',
+                'normal_engine.py',
+                'compiled_engine.pyc',
+                'optimized_engine.pyo',
+            ))
+
+        valid_engines = {
+                '_underscore_engine':   ('UnderscoreEngine', 'underscore'),
+                'normal_engine':        ('NormalEngine',     'normal'),
+                'compiled_engine':      ('CompiledEngine',   'compiled'),
+                'optimized_engine':     ('OptimizedEngine',  'optimized'),
+            }
+
+        result_dict = {handle: None for __, (__, handle) in valid_engines.items()}
+
+        def mock_import_module(name, package):
+            self.assertEqual(package, 'engines')
+
+            assert name.startswith('.')
+            name = name[1:]
+
+            module = imp.new_module('%s.%s' % (package, name))
+
+            if name == '__init__':
+                module.Engine = engines.Engine
+            else:
+                self.assertIn(name, valid_engines)
+                class_name, engine_handle = valid_engines[name]
+
+                class MockEngine(engines.Engine):
+                    handle = engine_handle
+
+                MockEngine.__name__ = class_name
+                MockEngine.__qualname__ = class_name
+
+                result_dict[engine_handle] = MockEngine
+                setattr(module, class_name, MockEngine)
+
+            return module
+
+        with mock.patch.object(engines, 'engines', mock_engines), \
+             mock.patch('os.listdir', mock_listdir), \
+             mock.patch('importlib.import_module', mock_import_module):
+            engines._init()
+
+        mock_listdir.assert_called_once_with(os.path.dirname(engines.__file__))
+        self.assertDictEqual(mock_engines, result_dict)
+
+
+class TestEngine(unittest.TestCase):
+
+    def test_not_instantiable(self):
+        self.assertRaises(AssertionError, engines.Engine, dirname='/tmp/', tolerant=False)
+
+    def test_handle_is_none(self):
+        class TestEngine(engines.Engine):
+            pass
+
+        engine = TestEngine(dirname='/tmp/', tolerant=False)
+
+        self.assertIsNone(engine.handle)
+
+    def test_apply_not_implemented(self):
+        class TestEngine(engines.Engine):
+            pass
+
+        engine = TestEngine(dirname='/tmp/', tolerant=False)
+
+        self.assertRaises(NotImplementedError, engine.apply, {})
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    unittest.main()
+

2.1 Accidental Damage: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
2.2 Breakdown: limit $600 per incident; service fee $25 per claim.

3.2 No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
3.3 The most we will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $80 per incident.
3.4 We will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
3.5 We will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

RENTERS CONTENTS PROTECTION
Issued by Lantern General Insurance

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
I.2  Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Insurer, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
I.3  Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
I.4  Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
I.5  Contents means household goods and personal possessions that belong to the Policyholder or the Policyholder's family.
I.6  Family means the Policyholder's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Policyholder.
I.7  Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
I.8  High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
I.9  Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
I.10  Limit means the most the Insurer will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
I.11  Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Policyholder's schedule.
I.12  Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
I.13  Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
I.14  Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
I.15  Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 45 consecutive days.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.2  Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.3  Accidental Damage: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.4  Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.5  The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Cooperation
III.1  The Policyholder must give the Insurer all the help and information the Insurer reasonably need to settle a claim.
III.2  The Policyholder must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Insurer's written permission.

PART IV: Flood
IV.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
IV.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
IV.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
IV.4  The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

PART V: Communication
V.1  The Insurer will communicate with the Policyholder in English.
V.2  The Insurer may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

PART VI: Locks and keys
VI.1  If the keys to the Policyholder's home are lost or stolen, the Insurer will pay the cost of replacing the locks to the outside doors.
VI.2  The most the Insurer will pay under this clause is $500 for any one claim.

PART VII: Garden and outdoor cover
VII.1  The Insurer will pay for plants, trees and shrubs in the garden of the home that are damaged by fire, lightning or theft.
VII.2  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by frost, storms, drought or animals.

PART VIII: Complaints
VIII.1  If the Policyholder has a complaint, the Policyholder should first contact the Insurer's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
VIII.2  The Insurer will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
VIII.3  If the Policyholder remains dissatisfied, the Policyholder may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

PART IX: Subrogation
IX.1  The Insurer will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Policyholder's name the defence or settlement of any claim.
IX.2  The Insurer can take action in the Policyholder's name to recover any payment the Insurer makes from anyone responsible for the loss.

PART X: Assignment
X.1  The Policyholder cannot transfer the Policyholder's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Insurer's written consent.

PART XI: Payment of claims
XI.1  The Insurer will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Policyholder's name.
XI.2  The Insurer aims to pay accepted claims within 15 working days of receiving all the documents the Insurer needs.

PART XII: Geographical limits
XII.1  Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
XII.2  Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

PART XIII: Automatic renewal
XIII.1  Unless the Policyholder tells the Insurer otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Insurer holds.
XIII.2  The Policyholder can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Insurer's helpline.

PART XIV: Fraud
XIV.1  If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Insurer will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
XIV.2  The Insurer may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

PART XV: Recovery of costs
XV.1  If the Insurer pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Insurer may ask the Policyholder to repay the amount.

PART XVI: How to read this document
XVI.1  This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
XVI.2  Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
XVI.3  Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

XVII.1  All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
XVII.2  Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

XVIII.1  The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
XVIII.2  The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $2,500 per incident.
XVIII.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $800 per incident.
XVIII.4  The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
XVIII.5  The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.

XIX.1  This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

XX.1  The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
XX.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.

XXI.1  Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
- **1.2** Hearing aid replacement period means 24 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
- **1.3** Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.

## 2. Limits and deductible
- **2.1** Dental Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
- **2.2** Vision Care: limit $300 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
- **2.3** Therapy Services: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Hearing Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
- **2.5** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Inflation
- **3.1** We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
- **3.2** Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

## 4. Dental Care
- **4.1** We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
- **4.2** No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 90 days after the policy start date.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.
- **4.4** The most we will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $800 per treatment.
- **4.5** We will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
- **4.6** We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

## 5. Geographical limits
- **5.1** Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
- **5.2** Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

## 6. Leaving the plan

- **6.2** Claims for treatment received before cover ended may be submitted up to 90 days afterwards.

- **7.1** Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
- **7.2** Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

- **29.1** You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.

- **30.1** We will communicate with you in English.

- **31.1** If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.

+        :type nums1: List[int]
+        :type nums2: List[int]
+        :rtype: float

+        if m > n:
+            nums1, nums2, m, n = nums2, nums1, n, m
