CASE PRESENTATION B
GROUP HEALTH CASH PLAN
Issued by the Benefits Trust

SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS
1.1 Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
1.2 Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
1.3 Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
1.4 Hearing aid replacement period means 24 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
1.5 Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
1.6 Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one treatment.
1.7 Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
1.8 Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
1.9 Network provider means a practitioner or clinic that has an agreement with us to provide treatment.
1.10 Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
1.11 Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
1.12 Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
1.13 Replacement period means 24 months from the date of your last eyewear claim.

SECTION 2 - LIMITS AND DEDUCTIBLE
2.1 Dental Care: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
2.2 Vision Care: limit $300 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
2.3 Therapy Services: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
2.4 Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
2.5 Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

SECTION 3 - VISION CARE
3.1 We will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
3.2 The most we will pay for Frames under this section is $150 per treatment.
3.3 We will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
3.4 We will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

SECTION 4 - DENTAL CARE
4.1 We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
4.2 No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
4.3 The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.
4.4 The most we will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $800 per treatment.
4.5 We will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
4.6 We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

SECTION 5 - THERAPY SERVICES
5.1 We will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
5.2 The most we will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $300 per treatment.
5.3 We will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
5.4 We will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

SECTION 6 - OPTIONAL COVER: HEARING CARE
6.1 We will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
6.2 This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
6.3 The most we will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $100 per treatment.
6.4 We will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

SECTION 7 - GENERAL EXCLUSIONS
7.1 We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
7.2 We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
7.3 We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

SECTION 8 - MAKING A CLAIM
8.1 You must notify us of a claim within 14 days of the treatment. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
8.2 We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
8.3 You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

SECTION 9 - FRAUD
9.1 If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
9.2 We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

SECTION 10 - JOINT POLICYHOLDERS
10.1 Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
10.2 A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

SECTION 11 - ACCESSIBILITY
11.1 This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

SECTION 12 - ENVIRONMENTAL COMMITMENT
12.1 Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
12.2 You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

SECTION 13 - PREMIUM PAYMENT
13.1 You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
13.2 If an instalment is not paid within 21 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

SECTION 14 - COMPLAINTS
14.1 If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
14.2 We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
14.3 If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

SECTION 15 - DISCOUNTS
15.1 Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
15.2 If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

SECTION 16 - ASSIGNMENT
16.1 You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

SECTION 17 - DATA PROTECTION
17.1 We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
17.2 We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
17.3 You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

SECTION 18 - CUSTOMER SUPPORT
18.1 Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
18.2 Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

SECTION 19 - CHANGE OF ADDRESS
19.1 You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
19.2 We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

SECTION 20 - CURRENCY
20.1 All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
20.2 Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

SECTION 21 - DUTY OF FAIR PRESENTATION
21.1 You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
21.2 If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
21.3 If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

SECTION 22 - THIRD-PARTY ADMINISTRATORS
22.1 We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
22.2 Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

SECTION 23 - EXCHANGE OF INFORMATION
23.1 To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
23.2 We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

SECTION 24 - SANCTIONS
24.1 We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

SECTION 25 - NOTICES
25.1 Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
25.2 Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

SECTION 26 - RECORDS AND EVIDENCE
26.1 You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
26.2 Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
26.3 We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

SECTION 27 - PAYMENT OF CLAIMS
27.1 We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
27.2 We aim to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

SECTION 28 - GOVERNING LAW
28.1 This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
28.2 Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

SECTION 29 - SALVAGE
29.1 When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
29.2 If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

SECTION 30 - INSTALMENT AGREEMENTS
30.1 If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
30.2 Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

SECTION 31 - RECOVERY OF COSTS
31.1 If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

SECTION 32 - CONTRACTS (RIGHTS OF THIRD PARTIES)
32.1 A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

SECTION 33 - MARKET CONDITIONS
33.1 If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

SECTION 34 - COORDINATION OF BENEFITS
34.1 If a treatment is also covered by another plan, we will pay only the part of the cost that the other plan does not pay.
34.2 You must tell us about any other plan that covers you or your dependants.

SECTION 35 - ARBITRATION
35.1 If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
35.2 Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

SECTION 36 - INFLATION
36.1 We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
36.2 Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

SECTION 37 - COMPENSATION SCHEME
37.1 We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
37.2 If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

SECTION 38 - HOW TO READ THIS DOCUMENT
38.1 This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
38.2 Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
38.3 Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

SECTION 39 - COMMUNICATION
39.1 We will communicate with you in English.
39.2 We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

SECTION 40 - TAXES
40.1 The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
40.2 If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

SECTION 41 - ELECTRONIC DOCUMENTS
41.1 We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
41.2 You must tell us if your email address changes.
41.3 Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

SECTION 42 - SUBROGATION
42.1 We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
42.2 We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

SECTION 43 - CLAIMS DOCUMENTS
43.1 You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
43.2 We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

SECTION 44 - DEPENDANTS
44.1 You may enrol dependants at the start of each plan year or within 30 days of a qualifying life event.
44.2 Benefits paid for dependants count towards the same annual limits as your own claims.

SECTION 45 - RENEWAL
45.1 We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
45.2 We are not obliged to offer renewal.

SECTION 46 - INTERPRETATION
46.1 Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
46.2 Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
46.3 Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

SECTION 47 - OTHER INSURANCE
47.1 If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
47.2 You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

SECTION 48 - WELLNESS ALLOWANCE
48.1 Each plan year you may claim up to $150 towards a gym membership or fitness class.
48.2 The wellness allowance is not subject to any deductible and does not count towards other limits.

SECTION 49 - LEAVING THE PLAN
49.1 Cover ends on the day your employment ends or the day you stop being eligible, whichever is earlier.
49.2 Claims for treatment received before cover ended may be submitted up to 90 days afterwards.

SECTION 50 - AUTOMATIC RENEWAL
50.1 Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
50.2 You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

SECTION 51 - CHANGES IN CIRCUMSTANCES
51.1 You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
51.2 We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

SECTION 52 - INTEREST
52.1 We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

SECTION 53 - GEOGRAPHICAL LIMITS
53.1 Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
53.2 Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

SECTION 54 - COOPERATION
54.1 You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
54.2 You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

SECTION 55 - REASONABLE PRECAUTIONS
55.1 You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
55.2 You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

SECTION 56 - ELIGIBILITY
56.1 Employees who work at least 20 hours a week are eligible to join the plan from their first day of employment.
56.2 Contractors, agency workers and employees on unpaid leave of more than three months are not eligible.

SECTION 57 - SEVERABILITY
57.1 If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

SECTION 58 - WAIVER
58.1 If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

SECTION 59 - APPEALS
59.1 If we decline all or part of a claim, you may appeal in writing within 60 days of the decision.
59.2 An appeal will be reviewed by someone who was not involved in the original decision.
59.3 We will give you a written decision on the appeal within 30 days.

SECTION 60 - CANCELLATION
60.1 You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
60.2 After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
60.3 We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

HOUSEHOLD CONTENTS COVER: POLICY BOOKLET
Issued by Keystone Home Mutual
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Keystone Home Mutual and "the Policyholder" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
(b) Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Insurer, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
(c) Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
(d) Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
(e) Contents means household goods and personal possessions that belong to the Policyholder or the Policyholder's family.
(f) Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
(g) Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
(h) High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
(i) Home means the private residence at the address shown in the schedule.
(j) Limit means the most the Insurer will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
(k) Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.
(l) Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Policyholder's schedule.
(m) Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
(n) Premium means the amount the Policyholder must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
(o) Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
(p) Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Policyholder's details, the covers the Policyholder bought and any extensions.
(q) Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
(r) Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 60 consecutive days.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(b) Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(c) Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(d) Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
(e) The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

Article 3. Optional cover: Accidental Damage
(a) The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $750 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

Article 4. Escape of Water
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $2,000 per incident.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

Article 5. Flood
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

Article 6. Theft
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,500 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $800 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

Article 7. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

Article 8. Making a claim
(a) The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(b) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(c) The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 14 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

Article 9. Arbitration
(a) If the Insurer accepts a claim but disagree with the Policyholder about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
(b) Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against the Insurer.

Article 10. Tenant's improvements
(a) If the Policyholder rents the home, the Insurer will pay for damage to fixtures and fittings that the Policyholder installed and are responsible for.
(b) This cover applies only to improvements the Policyholder paid for, not to items provided by the landlord.

Article 11. Records and evidence
(a) The Policyholder should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
(b) Where proof of value is missing, the Insurer may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
(c) The Insurer may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

Article 12. Data protection
(a) The Insurer will use the personal information the Policyholder provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
(b) The Insurer will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
(c) The Policyholder can ask for a copy of the personal information the Insurer holds by writing to the Insurer's data protection officer.

Article 13. Changes in circumstances
(a) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
(b) The Insurer may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

Article 14. Alternative accommodation
(a) If the Policyholder's home cannot be lived in after damage covered by this policy, the Insurer will pay the reasonable cost of comparable temporary accommodation.
(b) The Insurer will also pay for the temporary housing of pets that live with the Policyholder.
(c) Cover ends when the home is fit to live in again or after twelve months, whichever is sooner.

Article 15. Sanctions
(a) The Insurer will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Insurer to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

Article 16. Claims documents
(a) The Policyholder must provide, at the Policyholder's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Insurer reasonably ask for.
(b) The Insurer may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

Article 17. Inflation
(a) The Insurer may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
(b) Any adjustment will be shown in the Policyholder's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

Article 18. Renewal
(a) The Insurer will write to the Policyholder at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
(b) The Insurer is not obliged to offer renewal.

Article 19. Contents temporarily removed
(a) The Policyholder's contents are covered while temporarily removed from the home to another building in the same country, for up to 60 days.
(b) Contents in a student hall of residence are covered only if the student is a member of the Policyholder's family.

Article 20. Third-party administrators
(a) The Insurer may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Insurer's behalf.
(b) Any company the Insurer appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

Article 21. Salvage
(a) When the Insurer replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Insurer's property.
(b) If stolen property is recovered after the Insurer has paid a claim, the Policyholder must tell the Insurer and either return the payment or give the Insurer the property.

Article 22. Customer support
(a) The Insurer's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
(b) Outside these hours the Policyholder can leave a message and the Insurer will call back on the next working day.

Article 23. Environmental commitment
(a) Where practical, the Insurer will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
(b) The Policyholder may ask for a new part instead, and the Insurer will tell the Policyholder whether any additional cost would apply.

Article 24. Interest
(a) The Insurer will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

Article 25. Assignment
(a) The Policyholder cannot transfer the Policyholder's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Insurer's written consent.

Article 26. Waiver
(a) If the Insurer does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Insurer has given up the right to enforce it later.

Article 27. Geographical limits
(a) Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
(b) Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

Article 28. Premium payment
(a) The Policyholder must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
(b) If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, the Insurer may cancel the policy after giving notice.

Article 29. How to read this document
(a) This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
(b) Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
(c) Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

Article 30. Reasonable precautions
(a) The Policyholder must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
(b) The Policyholder must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

Article 31. Joint policyholders
(a) Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
(b) A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

(a) This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
(b) Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

Article 33. Severability
(a) If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

Article 34. Interpretation
(a) Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
(b) Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
(c) Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

Article 35. Fraud
(a) If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Insurer will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
(b) The Insurer may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

Article 36. Cancellation
(a) The Policyholder can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
(b) After the first 14 days the Policyholder can cancel at any time; the Insurer will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $30.
(c) The Insurer can cancel this policy by giving the Policyholder 30 days' written notice to the last address the Insurer holds.

Article 37. Electronic documents
(a) The Insurer will send documents by email unless the Policyholder asks for paper copies.
(b) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer if the Policyholder's email address changes.
(c) Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

Article 38. Recovery of costs
(a) If the Insurer pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Insurer may ask the Policyholder to repay the amount.

# Group Health Cash Plan

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
- **1.2** Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
- **1.3** Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
- **1.4** Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
- **1.5** Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
- **1.6** Hearing aid replacement period means 36 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
- **1.7** Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
- **1.8** Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one treatment.
- **1.9** Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
- **1.10** Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
- **1.11** Network provider means a practitioner or clinic that has an agreement with us to provide treatment.
- **1.12** Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
- **1.13** Plan year means the twelve months starting on your coverage start date.
- **1.14** Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
- **1.15** Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
- **1.16** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.17** Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
- **1.18** Registered practitioner means a practitioner registered with the professional body for their discipline.
- **1.19** Replacement period means 12 months from the date of your last eyewear claim.
- **1.20** Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
- **1.21** Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

## 2. Limits and deductible
- **2.1** Dental Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
- **2.2** Vision Care: limit $300 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
- **2.3** Therapy Services: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Hearing Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
- **2.5** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Records and evidence
- **3.1** You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
- **3.2** Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
- **3.3** We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

## 4. Cancellation
- **4.1** You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
- **4.2** After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $30.
- **4.3** We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

## 5. Communication
- **5.1** We will communicate with you in English.
- **5.2** We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

## 6. Interest
- **6.1** We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

## 7. Payment of claims
- **7.1** We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
- **7.2** We aim to pay accepted claims within 15 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

## 8. Sanctions
- **8.1** We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

## 9. Arbitration
- **9.1** If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
- **9.2** Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

## 10. Eligibility
- **10.1** Employees who work at least 20 hours a week are eligible to join the plan from their first day of employment.
- **10.2** Contractors, agency workers and employees on unpaid leave of more than three months are not eligible.

## 11. Other insurance
- **11.1** If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
- **11.2** You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

## 12. Therapy Services
- **12.1** We will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
- **12.2** The most we will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $300 per treatment.
- **12.3** We will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
- **12.4** We will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

## 13. Cooperation
- **13.1** You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
- **13.2** You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

## 14. Optional cover: Hearing Care
- **14.1** We will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
- **14.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **14.3** The most we will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $100 per treatment.
- **14.4** We will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

## 15. Currency
- **15.1** All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
- **15.2** Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

## 16. Vision Care
- **16.1** We will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
- **16.2** The most we will pay for Frames under this section is $120 per treatment.
- **16.3** We will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
- **16.4** We will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

## 17. Market conditions
- **17.1** If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

## 18. Governing law
- **18.1** This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
- **18.2** Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

## 19. Taxes
- **19.1** The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
- **19.2** If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

## 20. Electronic documents
- **20.1** We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
- **20.2** You must tell us if your email address changes.
- **20.3** Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

## 21. Fraud
- **21.1** If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
- **21.2** We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

## 22. Wellness allowance
- **22.1** Each plan year you may claim up to $150 towards a gym membership or fitness class.
- **22.2** The wellness allowance is not subject to any deductible and does not count towards other limits.

## 23. Compensation scheme
- **23.1** We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
- **23.2** If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

## 24. Severability
- **24.1** If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

## 25. Exchange of information
- **25.1** To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
- **25.2** We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

## 26. Appeals
- **26.1** If we decline all or part of a claim, you may appeal in writing within 60 days of the decision.
- **26.2** An appeal will be reviewed by someone who was not involved in the original decision.
- **26.3** We will give you a written decision on the appeal within 30 days.

## 27. Accessibility
- **27.1** This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

## 28. Joint policyholders
- **28.1** Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
- **28.2** A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

## 29. Coordination of benefits
- **29.1** If a treatment is also covered by another plan, we will pay only the part of the cost that the other plan does not pay.
- **29.2** You must tell us about any other plan that covers you or your dependants.

## 30. Customer support
- **30.1** Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
- **30.2** Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

## 31. Subrogation
- **31.1** We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
- **31.2** We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

## 32. Waiver
- **32.1** If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

## 33. Notices
- **33.1** Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
- **33.2** Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

## 34. How to read this document
- **34.1** This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
- **34.2** Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
- **34.3** Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

## 35. Dental Care
- **35.1** We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
- **35.2** No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
- **35.3** The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.
- **35.4** The most we will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $800 per treatment.
- **35.5** We will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
- **35.6** We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

## 36. Change of address
- **36.1** You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
- **36.2** We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

## 37. General exclusions
- **37.1** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
- **37.2** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
- **37.3** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

## 38. Leaving the plan
- **38.1** Cover ends on the day your employment ends or the day you stop being eligible, whichever is earlier.
- **38.2** Claims for treatment received before cover ended may be submitted up to 90 days afterwards.

## 39. Complaints
- **39.1** If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
- **39.2** We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
- **39.3** If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

## 40. Assignment
- **40.1** You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

## 41. Instalment agreements
- **41.1** If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
- **41.2** Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

## 42. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
- **42.1** A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

## 43. Renewal
- **43.1** We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
- **43.2** We are not obliged to offer renewal.

## 44. Changes in circumstances
- **44.1** You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
- **44.2** We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

## 45. Automatic renewal
- **45.1** Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
- **45.2** You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

## 46. Inflation
- **46.1** We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
- **46.2** Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

## 47. Environmental commitment
- **47.1** Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
- **47.2** You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

## 48. Third-party administrators
- **48.1** We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
- **48.2** Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

## 49. Premium payment
- **49.1** You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
- **49.2** If an instalment is not paid within 21 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

## 50. Claims documents
- **50.1** You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
- **50.2** We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

## 51. Reasonable precautions
- **51.1** You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
- **51.2** You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

## 52. Geographical limits
- **52.1** Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
- **52.2** Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

## 53. Duty of fair presentation
- **53.1** You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
- **53.2** If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
- **53.3** If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

## 54. Discounts
- **54.1** Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
- **54.2** If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

## 55. Dependants
- **55.1** You may enrol dependants at the start of each plan year or within 30 days of a qualifying life event.
- **55.2** Benefits paid for dependants count towards the same annual limits as your own claims.

## 56. Salvage
- **56.1** When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
- **56.2** If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

## 57. Interpretation
- **57.1** Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
- **57.2** Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
- **57.3** Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

## 58. Recovery of costs
- **58.1** If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

## 59. Data protection
- **59.1** We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
- **59.2** We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
- **59.3** You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

## 60. Making a claim
- **60.1** You must notify us of a claim within 21 days of the treatment. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **60.2** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **60.3** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

GADGET COVER: TERMS AND CONDITIONS
Issued by Circuit Care Services

SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS
1.1 Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.
1.2 Device means the item shown in the schedule, bought new from an authorised retailer.
1.3 Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
1.4 Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
1.5 Wearables means smartwatches and fitness trackers.

SECTION 2 - LIMITS AND SERVICE FEE
2.1 Accidental Damage: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
2.2 Breakdown: limit $600 per incident; service fee $25 per claim.
2.3 Theft and Loss: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $149 per claim.
2.4 Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the service fee is then deducted from the result.

SECTION 3 - ACCIDENTAL DAMAGE
3.1 We will repair or replace your device if it is accidentally damaged.
3.2 The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
3.3 The most we will pay for Wearables under this section is $300 per incident.
3.4 We will not pay for cosmetic damage, such as scratches or dents, that does not affect how the device works.
3.5 We will not pay for damage following a repair by anyone other than us or an authorised repairer. This exclusion does not apply if we approved the repair in writing beforehand.

SECTION 4 - GENERAL EXCLUSIONS
4.1 We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
4.2 We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

SECTION 5 - MAKING A CLAIM
5.1 You must notify us of a claim within 60 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
5.2 You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
5.3 We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

SECTION 6 - INTEREST
6.1 We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

SECTION 7 - REPAIR PROCESS
7.1 After a claim is accepted, we will send a prepaid mailer or book a courier collection.
7.2 We aim to return repaired devices within 15 business days of receiving them.

SECTION 8 - RECOVERY OF COSTS
8.1 If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

SECTION 9 - CHANGE OF ADDRESS
9.1 You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
9.2 We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

SECTION 10 - PREMIUM PAYMENT
10.1 You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
10.2 If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

SECTION 11 - COOPERATION
11.1 You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
11.2 You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

SECTION 12 - TRANSFERRING THE PLAN
12.1 You may transfer the plan to a new owner of the device by telling us in writing.
12.2 The remaining term of the plan transfers with the device; the term does not restart.

SECTION 13 - CUSTOMER SUPPORT
13.1 Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
13.2 Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

SECTION 14 - CONTRACTS (RIGHTS OF THIRD PARTIES)
14.1 A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

SECTION 15 - FRAUD
15.1 If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
15.2 We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

SECTION 16 - CLAIMS DOCUMENTS
16.1 You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
16.2 We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

SECTION 17 - REASONABLE PRECAUTIONS
17.1 You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
17.2 You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

SECTION 18 - DATA AND BACKUPS
18.1 We are not responsible for recovering or restoring any data, software or settings stored on your device.

SECTION 19 - SALVAGE

SECTION 21 - MARKET CONDITIONS

SECTION 22 - COMPENSATION SCHEME

CASE PRESENTATION B
# Staff Health Reimbursement Plan Rules
Issued by the Benefits Trust

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
- **1.2** Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
- **1.3** Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
- **1.4** Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
- **1.5** Plan year means the twelve months starting on your coverage start date.

## 2. Limits and deductible
- **2.1** Dental Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
- **2.2** Vision Care: limit $400 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
- **2.3** Therapy Services: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
- **2.5** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Currency
- **3.1** All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
- **3.2** Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

## 4. Dental Care
- **4.1** We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
- **4.2** No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $750 per treatment.
- **4.4** The most we will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $800 per treatment.
- **4.5** We will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
- **4.6** We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

## 5. Changes in circumstances
- **5.1** You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
- **5.2** We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

## 6. Salvage
- **6.1** When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
- **6.2** If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

## 7. Exchange of information
- **7.1** To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
- **7.2** We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

## 8. Data protection
- **8.1** We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
- **8.2** We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
- **8.3** You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

## 9. Wellness allowance
- **9.1** Each plan year you may claim up to $100 towards a gym membership or fitness class.
- **9.2** The wellness allowance is not subject to any deductible and does not count towards other limits.

## 10. Joint policyholders
- **10.1** Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
- **10.2** A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

## 11. Payment of claims
- **11.1** We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
- **11.2** We aim to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

## 12. Communication
- **12.1** We will communicate with you in English.
- **12.2** We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

## 13. Eligibility
- **13.1** Employees who work at least 20 hours a week are eligible to join the plan from their first day of employment.
- **13.2** Contractors, agency workers and employees on unpaid leave of more than three months are not eligible.

## 14. Appeals
- **14.1** If we decline all or part of a claim, you may appeal in writing within 60 days of the decision.
- **14.2** An appeal will be reviewed by someone who was not involved in the original decision.
- **14.3** We will give you a written decision on the appeal within 30 days.

## 15. Duty of fair presentation
- **15.1** You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
- **15.2** If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
- **15.3** If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

## 16. Therapy Services
- **16.1** We will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
- **16.2** The most we will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $300 per treatment.
- **16.3** We will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
- **16.4** We will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

## 17. Leaving the plan
- **17.1** Cover ends on the day your employment ends or the day you stop being eligible, whichever is earlier.
- **17.2** Claims for treatment received before cover ended may be submitted up to 90 days afterwards.

## 18. Compensation scheme
- **18.1** We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
- **18.2** If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

## 19. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
- **19.1** A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

## 20. Geographical limits
- **20.1** Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
- **20.2** Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

## 21. General exclusions
- **21.1** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
- **21.2** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **21.3** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

## 22. Environmental commitment
- **22.1** Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
- **22.2** You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

## 23. Reasonable precautions
- **23.1** You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
- **23.2** You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

## 24. Waiver
- **24.1** If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

IV.4  The Plan will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

PART V: Therapy Services
V.1  The Plan will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
V.2  The most the Plan will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $200 per treatment.

V.4  The Plan will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

PART II: Limits and service fee
II.1  Accidental Damage: limit $1,500 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
II.2  Breakdown: limit $1,000 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
II.3  Theft and Loss: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $149 per claim.
II.4  The service fee is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Sanctions
III.1  The Provider will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Provider to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

PART IV: Unrecoverable devices
IV.1  If a device is found after the Provider has replaced it, the found device becomes the Provider's property and must be sent to the Provider.
IV.2  The Provider may block devices reported as lost or stolen so that they cannot be used on mobile networks.

PART V: Interpretation
V.1  Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
V.2  Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
V.3  Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

PART VI: Third-party administrators
VI.1  The Provider may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Provider's behalf.
VI.2  Any company the Provider appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

PART VII: Communication
VII.1  The Provider will communicate with the Customer in English.
VII.2  The Provider may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

PART VIII: How to read this document
VIII.1  This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
VIII.2  Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
VIII.3  Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

IX.1  The Provider will replace the Customer's device if it is stolen or lost.
IX.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Customer's schedule.
IX.3  The most the Provider will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.
IX.4  The Provider will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
IX.5  The Provider will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

PART X: Records and evidence
X.1  The Customer should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
X.2  Where proof of value is missing, the Provider may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
X.3  The Provider may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

PART XI: Accidental Damage
XI.1  The Provider will repair or replace the Customer's device if it is accidentally damaged.
XI.2  The most the Provider will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
XI.3  The most the Provider will pay for Wearables under this section is $300 per incident.
XI.4  The Provider will not pay for cosmetic damage, such as scratches or dents, that does not affect how the device works.
XI.5  The Provider will not pay for damage following a repair by anyone other than the Provider or an authorised repairer. This exclusion does not apply if the Provider approved the repair in writing beforehand.

PART XII: Change of address
XII.1  The Customer must tell the Provider within 30 days if the Customer changes the Customer's address.
XII.2  The Provider may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

PART XIII: Breakdown
XIII.1  The Provider will repair or replace the Customer's device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
XIII.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
XIII.3  The most the Provider will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $80 per incident.
XIII.4  The Provider will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
XIII.5  The Provider will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

PART XIV: Changes in circumstances
XIV.1  The Customer must tell the Provider as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
XIV.2  The Provider may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

PART XV: Compensation scheme
XV.1  The Provider is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
XV.2  If the Provider cannot meet the Provider's obligations, the Customer may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

PART XVI: General exclusions
XVI.1  The Provider will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
XVI.2  The Provider will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
XVI.3  The Provider will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
XVI.4  The Provider will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Provider from paying.

PART XVII: Making a claim
XVII.1  The Provider may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
XVII.2  The Customer must notify the Provider of a claim within 30 days of the incident. The Provider will not pay any claim notified after that time.
XVII.3  The Customer must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

PART XVIII: Claims documents
XVIII.1  The Customer must provide, at the Customer's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Provider reasonably ask for.
XVIII.2  The Provider may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

PART XIX: Data protection
XIX.1  The Provider will use the personal information the Customer provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
XIX.2  The Provider will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
XIX.3  The Customer can ask for a copy of the personal information the Provider holds by writing to the Provider's data protection officer.

PART XX: Premium payment
XX.1  The Customer must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
XX.2  If an instalment is not paid within 21 days of its due date, the Provider may cancel the policy after giving notice.

PART XXI: Cancellation
XXI.1  The Customer can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
XXI.2  After the first 14 days the Customer can cancel at any time; the Provider will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
XXI.3  The Provider can cancel this policy by giving the Customer 30 days' written notice to the last address the Provider holds.

PART XXII: Environmental commitment
XXII.1  Where practical, the Provider will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
XXII.2  The Customer may ask for a new part instead, and the Provider will tell the Customer whether any additional cost would apply.

PART XXIII: Replacement devices
XXIII.1  If the Provider cannot repair the Customer's device economically, the Provider will replace it with a replacement device.
XXIII.2  Replacement devices may be a different colour and may be refurbished to an as-new standard.
XXIII.3  Accessories are replaced only if they were lost or damaged in the same incident as the device.

CASE PRESENTATION A
HOUSEHOLD CONTENTS COVER: POLICY BOOKLET
Issued by Keystone Home Mutual

SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS
1.1 Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
1.2 Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
1.3 Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
1.4 Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
1.5 Contents means household goods and personal possessions that belong to you or your family.
1.6 Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
1.7 Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
1.8 Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
1.9 High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
1.10 Home means the private residence at the address shown in the schedule.
1.11 Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
1.12 Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
1.13 Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.
1.14 Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
1.15 Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
1.16 Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
1.17 Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
1.18 Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
1.19 Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
1.20 Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
1.21 Unoccupied means not lived in by you or a member of your family for more than 30 consecutive days.

SECTION 2 - LIMITS AND EXCESS
2.1 Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
2.2 Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
2.3 Accidental Damage: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.4 Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
2.5 The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

SECTION 3 - THEFT
3.1 We will pay for contents stolen from your home.
3.2 The most we will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,500 per incident.
3.3 The most we will pay for Bicycles under this section is $500 per incident.
3.4 We will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
3.5 We will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
3.6 We will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

SECTION 4 - FLOOD
4.1 We will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering your home.
4.2 No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
4.3 The most we will pay for Garden items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
4.4 We will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for your area had been issued before the policy started.

SECTION 5 - ESCAPE OF WATER
5.1 We will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
5.2 The most we will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $2,000 per incident.
5.3 We will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
5.4 We will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

SECTION 6 - OPTIONAL COVER: ACCIDENTAL DAMAGE
6.1 We will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to your contents inside the home.
6.2 This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
6.3 The most we will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $500 per incident.
6.4 We will not pay for damage caused by pets.
6.5 We will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

SECTION 7 - GENERAL EXCLUSIONS
7.1 We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
7.2 We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
7.3 We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
7.4 We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
7.5 We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

SECTION 8 - MAKING A CLAIM
8.1 You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
8.2 We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
8.3 You must notify us of a claim within 60 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

SECTION 9 - TENANT'S IMPROVEMENTS
9.1 If you rent the home, we will pay for damage to fixtures and fittings that you installed and are responsible for.
9.2 This cover applies only to improvements you paid for, not to items provided by the landlord.

SECTION 10 - RECORDS AND EVIDENCE
10.1 You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
10.2 Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
10.3 We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

SECTION 11 - CHANGE OF ADDRESS
11.1 You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
11.2 We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

SECTION 12 - ACCESSIBILITY
12.1 This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

SECTION 13 - RENEWAL
13.1 We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
13.2 We are not obliged to offer renewal.

SECTION 14 - REASONABLE PRECAUTIONS
14.1 You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
14.2 You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

SECTION 15 - THIRD-PARTY ADMINISTRATORS
15.1 We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
15.2 Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

SECTION 16 - ASSIGNMENT
16.1 You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

SECTION 17 - COMMUNICATION
17.1 We will communicate with you in English.
17.2 We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

SECTION 18 - COMPENSATION SCHEME
18.1 We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
18.2 If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

SECTION 19 - AUTOMATIC RENEWAL
19.1 Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
19.2 You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

SECTION 20 - COMPLAINTS
20.1 If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
20.2 We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
20.3 If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

SECTION 21 - FRAUD
21.1 If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
21.2 We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

SECTION 22 - SANCTIONS
22.1 We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

SECTION 23 - DISCOUNTS
23.1 Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
23.2 If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

SECTION 24 - INTEREST
24.1 We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

SECTION 25 - CURRENCY
25.1 All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
25.2 Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

SECTION 26 - DUTY OF FAIR PRESENTATION
26.1 You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
26.2 If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
26.3 If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

SECTION 27 - CUSTOMER SUPPORT
27.1 Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
27.2 Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

SECTION 28 - CLAIMS DOCUMENTS
28.1 You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
28.2 We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

SECTION 29 - CONTENTS TEMPORARILY REMOVED
29.1 Your contents are covered while temporarily removed from the home to another building in the same country, for up to 60 days.
29.2 Contents in a student hall of residence are covered only if the student is a member of your family.

SECTION 30 - ELECTRONIC DOCUMENTS
30.1 We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
30.2 You must tell us if your email address changes.
30.3 Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

SECTION 31 - SUBROGATION
31.1 We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
31.2 We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

SECTION 32 - PAYMENT OF CLAIMS
32.1 We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
32.2 We aim to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

SECTION 33 - SEVERABILITY
33.1 If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

SECTION 34 - MARKET CONDITIONS
34.1 If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

SECTION 35 - SALVAGE
35.1 When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
35.2 If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

SECTION 36 - CANCELLATION
36.1 You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
36.2 After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $30.
36.3 We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

SECTION 37 - WAIVER
37.1 If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

SECTION 38 - ARBITRATION
38.1 If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
38.2 Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

SECTION 39 - ENVIRONMENTAL COMMITMENT
39.1 Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
39.2 You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.
