# Group Health Cash Plan
Issued by Wellspring Benefits Administration

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
- **1.2** Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
- **1.3** Dependant means your spouse or partner, or a child under 21 who is enrolled in the plan.
- **1.4** Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
- **1.5** Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
- **1.6** Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
- **1.7** Hearing aid replacement period means 24 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
- **1.8** Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
- **1.9** Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one treatment.
- **1.10** Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
- **1.11** Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
- **1.12** Network provider means a practitioner or clinic that has an agreement with us to provide treatment.
- **1.13** Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
- **1.14** Plan year means the twelve months starting on your coverage start date.
- **1.15** Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
- **1.16** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.17** Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
- **1.18** Registered practitioner means a practitioner registered with the professional body for their discipline.
- **1.19** Replacement period means 24 months from the date of your last eyewear claim.
- **1.20** Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
- **1.21** Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

## 2. Limits and deductible
- **2.1** Dental Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
- **2.2** Vision Care: limit $300 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
- **2.3** Therapy Services: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
- **2.5** The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Governing law
- **3.1** This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
- **3.2** Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

## 4. Claims documents
- **4.1** You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
- **4.2** We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

## 5. Dental Care
- **5.1** We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
- **5.2** No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 90 days after the policy start date.
- **5.3** The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.
- **5.4** The most we will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $800 per treatment.
- **5.5** We will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
- **5.6** We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

## 6. Waiver
- **6.1** If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

## 7. Inflation
- **7.1** We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
- **7.2** Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

## 8. Notices
- **8.1** Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
- **8.2** Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

## 9. Duty of fair presentation
- **9.1** You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
- **9.2** If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
- **9.3** If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

## 10. Premium payment
- **10.1** You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
- **10.2** If an instalment is not paid within 21 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

## 11. Joint policyholders
- **11.1** Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
- **11.2** A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

## 12. Taxes
- **12.1** The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
- **12.2** If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

## 13. Electronic documents
- **13.1** We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
- **13.2** You must tell us if your email address changes.
- **13.3** Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

## 14. Vision Care
- **14.1** We will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
- **14.2** The most we will pay for Frames under this section is $150 per treatment.
- **14.3** We will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
- **14.4** We will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

## 15. Optional cover: Hearing Care
- **15.1** We will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
- **15.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **15.3** The most we will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $100 per treatment.
- **15.4** We will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

## 16. Subrogation
- **16.1** We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
- **16.2** We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

## 17. Complaints
- **17.1** If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
- **17.2** We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
- **17.3** If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

## 18. Reasonable precautions
- **18.1** You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
- **18.2** You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

## 19. Payment of claims
- **19.1** We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
- **19.2** We aim to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

## 20. Sanctions
- **20.1** We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

## 21. Therapy Services
- **21.1** We will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
- **21.2** The most we will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $300 per treatment.
- **21.3** We will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
- **21.4** We will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

## 22. Cooperation
- **22.1** You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
- **22.2** You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

## 23. Dependants
- **23.1** You may enrol dependants at the start of each plan year or within 30 days of a qualifying life event.
- **23.2** Benefits paid for dependants count towards the same annual limits as your own claims.

## 24. General exclusions
- **24.1** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
- **24.2** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
- **24.3** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **24.4** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
- **24.5** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

## 25. Arbitration
- **25.1** If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
- **25.2** Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

## 26. Currency
- **26.1** All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
- **26.2** Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

## 27. Records and evidence
- **27.1** You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
- **27.2** Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
- **27.3** We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

## 28. Geographical limits
- **28.1** Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
- **28.2** Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

## 29. Making a claim
- **29.1** You must notify us of a claim within 90 days of the treatment. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **29.2** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **29.3** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

# Household Contents Cover: Policy Booklet
Issued by Hearthstone Insurance plc

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
- **1.2** Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
- **1.3** Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
- **1.4** High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
- **1.5** Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
- **1.6** Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
- **1.7** Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
- **1.8** Unoccupied means not lived in by you or a member of your family for more than 45 consecutive days.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
- **2.2** Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
- **2.3** Accidental Damage: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
- **2.5** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Theft
- **3.1** We will pay for contents stolen from your home.
- **3.2** The most we will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,500 per incident.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Bicycles under this section is $500 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
- **3.5** We will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
- **3.6** We will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

## 4. Escape of Water
- **4.1** We will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
- **4.2** The most we will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $2,000 per incident.
- **4.3** We will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
- **4.4** We will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

## 5. Flood
- **5.1** We will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering your home.
- **5.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
- **5.3** The most we will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
- **5.4** We will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for your area had been issued before the policy started.

## 6. General exclusions
- **6.1** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **6.2** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
- **6.3** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.

## 7. Making a claim
- **7.1** You must notify us of a claim within 30 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **7.2** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **7.3** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

## 8. Third-party administrators
- **8.1** We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
- **8.2** Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

## 9. Instalment agreements
- **9.1** If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
- **9.2** Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

## 10. Fraud
- **10.1** If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
- **10.2** We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

## 11. Market conditions
- **11.1** If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

## 12. Freezer contents
- **12.1** We will pay for food in a domestic freezer that spoils because of a rise or fall in temperature.
- **12.2** We will not pay if the freezer is more than fifteen years old, or if the electricity supplier cut the supply deliberately.

## 13. Communication
- **13.1** We will communicate with you in English.
- **13.2** We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

## 14. Accessibility
- **14.1** This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

## 15. Other insurance
- **15.1** If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
- **15.2** You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

## 16. Contents temporarily removed
- **16.1** Your contents are covered while temporarily removed from the home to another building in the same country, for up to 60 days.
- **16.2** Contents in a student hall of residence are covered only if the student is a member of your family.

## 17. Premium payment
- **17.1** You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
- **17.2** If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

## 18. Governing law
- **18.1** This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
- **18.2** Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

## 19. Records and evidence
- **19.1** You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
- **19.2** Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
- **19.3** We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

## 20. Exchange of information
- **20.1** To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
- **20.2** We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

## 21. Inflation
- **21.1** We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
- **21.2** Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

## 22. Severability
- **22.1** If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

Issued by Keystone Home Mutual

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.

- **1.5** Contents means household goods and personal possessions that belong to you or your family.

- **1.7** Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
- **1.8** Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
- **1.9** High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
- **1.10** Home means the private residence at the address shown in the schedule.
- **1.11** Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
- **1.12** Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
- **1.13** Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.

- **1.15** Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
- **1.16** Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
- **1.17** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.18** Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
- **1.19** Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
- **1.20** Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
- **1.21** Unoccupied means not lived in by you or a member of your family for more than 30 consecutive days.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
- **2.2** Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
- **2.3** Accidental Damage: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.4** Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
- **2.5** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

- **3.1** We will pay for contents stolen from your home.

- **3.3** The most we will pay for Bicycles under this section is $800 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
- **3.5** We will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
- **3.6** We will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

- **4.4** We will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for your area had been issued before the policy started.

- **5.4** We will not pay for damage caused by pets.

Issued by Northstar Underwriting

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Insured Person's schedule.

I.3  Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $1,500 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.2  Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $25,000 per incident; excess $150 per claim.
II.3  Trip Cancellation: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.4  Travel Delay: limit $500 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.5  The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Baggage and Personal Belongings
III.1  The Insurer will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to the Insured Person's baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
III.2  The most the Insurer will pay for Valuables under this section is $500 per incident.
III.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $300 per incident.
III.4  The Insurer will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
III.5  The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
III.6  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

PART IV: General exclusions
IV.1  The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
IV.2  The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.

PART V: Making a claim
V.1  The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
V.2  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
V.3  The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 90 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

PART VI: Personal liability
VI.1  The Insurer will pay damages the Insured Person becomes legally liable to pay for accidental injury to another person or accidental damage to their property during the trip.
VI.2  This section does not cover liability arising from the use of motor vehicles, boats or aircraft.
VI.3  The most the Insurer will pay under this section is $5,000,000 for all claims arising from one event.

PART VII: Customer support
VII.1  The Insurer's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
VII.2  Outside these hours the Insured Person can leave a message and the Insurer will call back on the next working day.

PART VIII: Change of address
VIII.1  The Insured Person must tell the Insurer within 30 days if the Insured Person changes the Insured Person's address.
VIII.2  The Insurer may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

PART IX: Renewal
IX.1  The Insurer will write to the Insured Person at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
IX.2  The Insurer is not obliged to offer renewal.

PART X: Taxes
X.1  The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
X.2  If the tax rate changes, the Insurer may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

PART XI: Exchange of information
XI.1  To prevent fraud, the Insurer may check the details the Insured Person gives against public records and industry databases.
XI.2  The Insurer may contact previous insurers to confirm the Insured Person's claims history.

PART XII: Other insurance
XII.1  If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Insurer will pay only the Insurer's proportionate share.
XII.2  The Insured Person must tell the Insurer about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Insured Person makes a claim.

PART XIII: Fraud
XIII.1  If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Insurer will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
XIII.2  The Insurer may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

PART XIV: Salvage
XIV.1  When the Insurer replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Insurer's property.
XIV.2  If stolen property is recovered after the Insurer has paid a claim, the Insured Person must tell the Insurer and either return the payment or give the Insurer the property.

PART XV: Cancellation
XV.1  The Insured Person can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
XV.2  After the first 14 days the Insured Person can cancel at any time; the Insurer will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
XV.3  The Insurer can cancel this policy by giving the Insured Person 30 days' written notice to the last address the Insurer holds.

PART XVI: Missed departure
XVI.1  The Insurer will pay reasonable additional travel and accommodation costs to reach the Insured Person's destination if the Insured Person arrives too late to board the Insured Person's booked transport because public transport fails.
XVI.2  The Insured Person must allow enough time to reach the departure point, and must obtain written confirmation of the delay from the transport operator.

PART XVII: Automatic renewal
XVII.1  Unless the Insured Person tells the Insurer otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Insurer holds.
XVII.2  The Insured Person can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Insurer's helpline.

PART XVIII: Rental car excess
XVIII.1  If the Insured Person hires a car during the trip, the Insurer will reimburse any excess the Insured Person must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.
XVIII.2  This section applies only to cars hired from a licensed rental company under a written agreement.

PART XIX: Data protection
XIX.1  The Insurer will use the personal information the Insured Person provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
XIX.2  The Insurer will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
XIX.3  The Insured Person can ask for a copy of the personal information the Insurer holds by writing to the Insurer's data protection officer.

PART XX: Arbitration
XX.1  If the Insurer accepts a claim but disagree with the Insured Person about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
XX.2  Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against the Insurer.

PART XXI: Accessibility
XXI.1  This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

PART XXII: Discounts
XXII.1  Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
XXII.2  If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Insurer may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

PART XXIII: Environmental commitment
XXIII.1  Where practical, the Insurer will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
XXIII.2  The Insured Person may ask for a new part instead, and the Insurer will tell the Insured Person whether any additional cost would apply.

PART XXIV: Reasonable precautions
XXIV.1  The Insured Person must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
XXIV.2  The Insured Person must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

PART XXV: Sanctions
XXV.1  The Insurer will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Insurer to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

PART XXVI: Severability
XXVI.1  If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS
1.1 Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
1.2 Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
1.3 Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
1.4 Contents means household goods and personal possessions that belong to you or your family.
1.5 Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
1.6 Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
1.7 Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
1.8 High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
1.9 Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.
1.10 Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
1.11 Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
1.12 Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
1.13 Unoccupied means not lived in by you or a member of your family for more than 30 consecutive days.

SECTION 2 - LIMITS AND EXCESS
2.1 Theft: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.2 Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
2.3 Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.4 Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
2.5 Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

SECTION 3 - ESCAPE OF WATER
3.1 We will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
3.2 The most we will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.
3.3 We will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
3.4 We will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

SECTION 4 - FLOOD
4.1 We will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering your home.
4.2 No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
4.3 The most we will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
4.4 We will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for your area had been issued before the policy started.

SECTION 5 - OPTIONAL COVER: ACCIDENTAL DAMAGE
5.1 We will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to your contents inside the home.
5.2 This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
5.3 The most we will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $750 per incident.
5.4 We will not pay for damage caused by pets.
5.5 We will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

SECTION 6 - THEFT
6.1 We will pay for contents stolen from your home.
6.2 The most we will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
6.3 The most we will pay for Bicycles under this section is $800 per incident.
6.4 We will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
6.5 We will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
6.6 We will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

SECTION 7 - GENERAL EXCLUSIONS
7.1 We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
7.2 We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
7.3 We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
7.4 We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
7.5 We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
7.6 We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

SECTION 8 - MAKING A CLAIM
8.1 We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
8.2 You must notify us of a claim within 30 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
8.3 You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

SECTION 9 - ELECTRONIC DOCUMENTS
9.1 We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
9.2 You must tell us if your email address changes.
9.3 Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

SECTION 10 - ALTERNATIVE ACCOMMODATION
10.1 If your home cannot be lived in after damage covered by this policy, we will pay the reasonable cost of comparable temporary accommodation.
10.2 We will also pay for the temporary housing of pets that live with you.
10.3 Cover ends when the home is fit to live in again or after twelve months, whichever is sooner.

SECTION 11 - AUTOMATIC RENEWAL
11.1 Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
11.2 You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

SECTION 12 - COMPENSATION SCHEME
12.1 We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
12.2 If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

SECTION 13 - GOVERNING LAW
13.1 This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.

SECTION 15 - MARKET CONDITIONS

SECTION 16 - PAYMENT OF CLAIMS
16.1 We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.

17.1 If you rent the home, we will pay for damage to fixtures and fittings that you installed and are responsible for.

18.1 Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.

19.1 We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.

20.1 We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.

23.1 A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

24.1 We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.

25.1 We will communicate with you in English.

26.1 Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.

27.1 When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.

SECTION 28 - OTHER INSURANCE
28.1 If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.

SECTION 29 - EXCHANGE OF INFORMATION
29.1 To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.

30.1 You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.

SECTION 31 - NOTICES
31.1 Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
31.2 Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

SECTION 32 - CLAIMS DOCUMENTS
32.1 You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
32.2 We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

SECTION 33 - DISCOUNTS
33.1 Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
33.2 If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

SECTION 34 - REASONABLE PRECAUTIONS
34.1 You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
34.2 You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

SECTION 35 - GEOGRAPHICAL LIMITS
35.1 Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
35.2 Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

SECTION 36 - SANCTIONS
36.1 We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

SECTION 37 - CURRENCY
37.1 All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.

SECTION 38 - INSTALMENT AGREEMENTS
38.1 If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.

SECTION 39 - DATA PROTECTION
39.1 We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
39.2 We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
39.3 You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

SECTION 40 - COOPERATION
40.1 You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
40.2 You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

41.1 You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

SECTION 42 - ACCESSIBILITY
42.1 This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

43.1 We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

44.1 You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.

46.1 If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

47.1 If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

52.1 You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.

53.1 If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.

2.2 Breakdown: limit $1,000 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.

SECTION 5 - BREAKDOWN
5.1 We will repair or replace your device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
5.2 No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.

5.4 We will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
5.5 We will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

SECTION 6 - GENERAL EXCLUSIONS
6.1 We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
6.2 We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
6.3 We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
6.4 We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
6.5 We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
6.6 We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.

9.1 We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

10.1 We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.

11.1 You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.

11.3 We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

12.2 The remaining term of the plan transfers with the device; the term does not restart.

13.1 You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
13.2 We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

14.1 Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
14.2 You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

SECTION 15 - GEOGRAPHICAL LIMITS
15.1 Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.

17.1 When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
17.2 If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

18.1 You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
18.2 We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

SECTION 19 - SANCTIONS
19.1 We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

20.1 If we cannot repair your device economically, we will replace it with a replacement device.
20.2 Replacement devices may be a different colour and may be refurbished to an as-new standard.
20.3 Accessories are replaced only if they were lost or damaged in the same incident as the device.

SECTION 21 - OTHER INSURANCE
21.1 If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
21.2 You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

SECTION 22 - PAYMENT OF CLAIMS
22.1 We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
22.2 We aim to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

SECTION 23 - DATA AND BACKUPS
23.1 We are not responsible for recovering or restoring any data, software or settings stored on your device.
23.2 You should back up your data regularly and before sending the device for repair.

SECTION 24 - SEVERABILITY
24.1 If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

SECTION 25 - ACCESSIBILITY
25.1 This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

SECTION 26 - COMPENSATION SCHEME
26.1 We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
26.2 If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

27.1 You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
27.2 After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
27.3 We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

28.1 This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
28.2 Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

29.1 If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
29.2 Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

SECTION 30 - NOTICES
30.1 Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
30.2 Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

SECTION 31 - MARKET CONDITIONS
31.1 If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

SECTION 32 - CURRENCY
32.1 All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
32.2 Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

SECTION 33 - ASSIGNMENT
33.1 You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

SECTION 34 - DUTY OF FAIR PRESENTATION
34.1 You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
34.2 If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
34.3 If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

SECTION 35 - ARBITRATION
35.1 If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
35.2 Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

SECTION 36 - RECOVERY OF COSTS
36.1 If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

SECTION 37 - JOINT POLICYHOLDERS
37.1 Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
37.2 A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

SECTION 38 - PREMIUM PAYMENT
38.1 You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
38.2 If an instalment is not paid within 21 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

SECTION 39 - HOW TO READ THIS DOCUMENT
39.1 This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
39.2 Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
39.3 Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

SECTION 40 - REASONABLE PRECAUTIONS
40.1 You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
40.2 You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

SECTION 41 - DATA PROTECTION
41.1 We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
41.2 We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
41.3 You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

SECTION 42 - CONTRACTS (RIGHTS OF THIRD PARTIES)
42.1 A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

SECTION 43 - INFLATION
43.1 We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
43.2 Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

SECTION 44 - FRAUD
44.1 If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
44.2 We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

SECTION 45 - AUTOMATIC RENEWAL
45.1 Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
45.2 You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

SECTION 46 - SOFTWARE SUPPORT
46.1 Our helpline can give advice on setting up and using your device.
46.2 Software support does not include fixing problems caused by third-party apps or unofficial operating systems.

SECTION 47 - REPAIR PROCESS
47.1 After a claim is accepted, we will send a prepaid mailer or book a courier collection.
47.2 We aim to return repaired devices within 5 business days of receiving them.

SECTION 48 - COMMUNICATION
48.1 We will communicate with you in English.
48.2 We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

SECTION 49 - RENEWAL
49.1 We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
49.2 We are not obliged to offer renewal.

SECTION 50 - EXCHANGE OF INFORMATION
50.1 To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
50.2 We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

SECTION 51 - CUSTOMER SUPPORT
51.1 Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
51.2 Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

SECTION 52 - WAIVER
52.1 If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

SECTION 53 - TAXES
53.1 The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
53.2 If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

SECTION 54 - ELECTRONIC DOCUMENTS
54.1 We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
54.2 You must tell us if your email address changes.
54.3 Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

SECTION 55 - THIRD-PARTY ADMINISTRATORS
55.1 We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.

56.2 We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.

57.1 You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.

58.1 If a device is found after we have replaced it, the found device becomes our property and must be sent to us.

STAFF HEALTH REIMBURSEMENT PLAN RULES
Issued by Wellspring Benefits Administration

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Plan, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
I.2  Dependant means the Member's spouse or partner, or a child under 21 who is enrolled in the plan.
I.3  Family means the Member's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Member.
I.4  Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
I.5  Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
I.6  Hearing aid replacement period means 24 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
I.7  Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
I.8  Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
I.9  Network provider means a practitioner or clinic that has an agreement with the Plan to provide treatment.
I.10  Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
I.11  Plan year means the twelve months starting on the Member's coverage start date.
I.12  Premium means the amount the Member must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
I.13  Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
I.14  Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
I.15  Registered practitioner means a practitioner registered with the professional body for their discipline.
I.16  Replacement period means 24 months from the date of the Member's last eyewear claim.

PART II: Limits and deductible
II.1  Dental Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
II.2  Vision Care: limit $300 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
II.3  Therapy Services: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
II.4  Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
II.5  The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Vision Care
III.1  The Plan will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
III.2  The most the Plan will pay for Frames under this section is $120 per treatment.
III.3  The Plan will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
III.4  The Plan will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

PART IV: Therapy Services
IV.1  The Plan will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
IV.2  The most the Plan will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $200 per treatment.
IV.3  The Plan will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
IV.4  The Plan will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

PART V: Optional cover: Hearing Care
V.1  The Plan will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
V.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Member's schedule.
V.3  The most the Plan will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $100 per treatment.
V.4  The Plan will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

PART VI: Dental Care
VI.1  The Plan will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
VI.2  No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
VI.3  The most the Plan will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $750 per treatment.
VI.4  The most the Plan will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $600 per treatment.
VI.5  The Plan will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
VI.6  The Plan will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

PART VII: General exclusions
VII.1  The Plan will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
VII.2  The Plan will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
VII.3  The Plan will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
VII.4  The Plan will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

PART VIII: Making a claim
VIII.1  The Member must notify the Plan of a claim within 30 days of the treatment. The Plan will not pay any claim notified after that time.
VIII.2  The Plan may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
VIII.3  The Member must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

PART IX: Communication
IX.1  The Plan will communicate with the Member in English.
IX.2  The Plan may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

PART X: Payment of claims
X.1  The Plan will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Member's name.
X.2  The Plan aims to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents the Plan needs.

PART XI: Third-party administrators
XI.1  The Plan may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Plan's behalf.
XI.2  Any company the Plan appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

PART XII: Eligibility
XII.1  Employees who work at least 20 hours a week are eligible to join the plan from their first day of employment.
XII.2  Contractors, agency workers and employees on unpaid leave of more than three months are not eligible.

PART XIII: Environmental commitment
XIII.1  Where practical, the Plan will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
XIII.2  The Member may ask for a new part instead, and the Plan will tell the Member whether any additional cost would apply.

PART XIV: Automatic renewal
XIV.1  Unless the Member tells the Plan otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Plan holds.
XIV.2  The Member can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Plan's helpline.

PART XV: Instalment agreements
XV.1  If the Member pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
XV.2  Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

PART XVI: Fraud
XVI.1  If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Plan will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
XVI.2  The Plan may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

PART XVII: Reasonable precautions
XVII.1  The Member must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
XVII.2  The Member must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

PART XVIII: Duty of fair presentation
XVIII.1  The Member must answer all questions the Plan asks honestly and to the best of the Member's knowledge.
XVIII.2  If the Member gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Plan may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
XVIII.3  If the Member gives incorrect information carelessly, the Plan may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

PART XIX: Exchange of information
XIX.1  To prevent fraud, the Plan may check the details the Member gives against public records and industry databases.
XIX.2  The Plan may contact previous insurers to confirm the Member's claims history.

PART XX: Recovery of costs
XX.1  If the Plan pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Plan may ask the Member to repay the amount.

PART XXI: Wellness allowance
XXI.1  Each plan year the Member may claim up to $100 towards a gym membership or fitness class.
XXI.2  The wellness allowance is not subject to any deductible and does not count towards other limits.

PART XXII: Cooperation
XXII.1  The Member must give the Plan all the help and information the Plan reasonably need to settle a claim.
XXII.2  The Member must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Plan's written permission.

PART XXIII: Customer support
XXIII.1  The Plan's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
XXIII.2  Outside these hours the Member can leave a message and the Plan will call back on the next working day.

PART XXIV: Complaints
XXIV.1  If the Member has a complaint, the Member should first contact the Plan's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
XXIV.2  The Plan will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
XXIV.3  If the Member remains dissatisfied, the Member may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

PART XXV: Accessibility
XXV.1  This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

PART XXVI: Dependants
XXVI.1  The Member may enrol dependants at the start of each plan year or within 30 days of a qualifying life event.
XXVI.2  Benefits paid for dependants count towards the same annual limits as the Member's own claims.

PART XXVII: Change of address
XXVII.1  The Member must tell the Plan within 30 days if the Member changes the Member's address.
XXVII.2  The Plan may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

PART XXVIII: Compensation scheme
XXVIII.1  The Plan is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
XXVIII.2  If the Plan cannot meet the Plan's obligations, the Member may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

PART XXIX: Interest
XXIX.1  The Plan will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

PART XXX: Assignment
XXX.1  The Member cannot transfer the Member's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Plan's written consent.

PART XXXI: Salvage
XXXI.1  When the Plan replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Plan's property.
XXXI.2  If stolen property is recovered after the Plan has paid a claim, the Member must tell the Plan and either return the payment or give the Plan the property.

PART XXXII: Claims documents
XXXII.1  The Member must provide, at the Member's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Plan reasonably ask for.
XXXII.2  The Plan may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

PART XXXIII: Premium payment
XXXIII.1  The Member must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
XXXIII.2  If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, the Plan may cancel the policy after giving notice.

PART XXXIV: Subrogation
XXXIV.1  The Plan will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Member's name the defence or settlement of any claim.
XXXIV.2  The Plan can take action in the Member's name to recover any payment the Plan makes from anyone responsible for the loss.

PART XXXV: Inflation
XXXV.1  The Plan may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
XXXV.2  Any adjustment will be shown in the Member's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

state.policy:
TRAVEL INSURANCE POLICY WORDING
Issued by Northstar Underwriting

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
I.2  Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
I.3  Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $1,500 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.2  Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $25,000 per incident; excess $150 per claim.
II.3  Trip Cancellation: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.4  Travel Delay: limit $500 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.5  The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Baggage and Personal Belongings
III.1  The Insurer will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to the Insured Person's baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
III.2  The most the Insurer will pay for Valuables under this section is $500 per incident.
III.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $300 per incident.
III.4  The Insurer will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
III.5  The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
III.6  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

PART IV: General exclusions
IV.1  The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
IV.2  The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.

PART V: Making a claim
V.1  The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
V.2  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
V.3  The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 90 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

PART VI: Personal liability
VI.1  The Insurer will pay damages the Insured Person becomes legally liable to pay for accidental injury to another person or accidental damage to their property during the trip.
VI.2  This section does not cover liability arising from the use of motor vehicles, boats or aircraft.
VI.3  The most the Insurer will pay under this section is $5,000,000 for all claims arising from one event.

PART VII: Customer support
VII.1  The Insurer's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
VII.2  Outside these hours the Insured Person can leave a message and the Insurer will call back on the next working day.

PART VIII: Change of address
VIII.1  The Insured Person must tell the Insurer within 30 days if the Insured Person changes the Insured Person's address.
VIII.2  The Insurer may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

PART IX: Renewal
IX.1  The Insurer will write to the Insured Person at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
IX.2  The Insurer is not obliged to offer renewal.

PART X: Taxes
X.1  The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
X.2  If the tax rate changes, the Insurer may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

PART XI: Exchange of information
XI.1  To prevent fraud, the Insurer may check the details the Insured Person gives against public records and industry databases.
XI.2  The Insurer may contact previous insurers to confirm the Insured Person's claims history.

PART XII: Other insurance
XII.1  If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Insurer will pay only the Insurer's proportionate share.
XII.2  The Insured Person must tell the Insurer about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Insured Person makes a claim.

PART XIII: Fraud
XIII.1  If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Insurer will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
XIII.2  The Insurer may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

PART XIV: Salvage
XIV.1  When the Insurer replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Insurer's property.
XIV.2  If stolen property is recovered after the Insurer has paid a claim, the Insured Person must tell the Insurer and either return the payment or give the Insurer the property.

PART XV: Cancellation
XV.1  The Insured Person can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
XV.2  After the first 14 days the Insured Person can cancel at any time; the Insurer will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
XV.3  The Insurer can cancel this policy by giving the Insured Person 30 days' written notice to the last address the Insurer holds.

PART XVI: Missed departure
XVI.1  The Insurer will pay reasonable additional travel and accommodation costs to reach the Insured Person's destination if the Insured Person arrives too late to board the Insured Person's booked transport because public transport fails.
XVI.2  The Insured Person must allow enough time to reach the departure point, and must obtain written confirmation of the delay from the transport operator.

PART XVII: Automatic renewal
XVII.1  Unless the Insured Person tells the Insurer otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Insurer holds.
XVII.2  The Insured Person can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Insurer's helpline.

PART XVIII: Rental car excess
XVIII.1  If the Insured Person hires a car during the trip, the Insurer will reimburse any excess the Insured Person must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.
XVIII.2  This section applies only to cars hired from a licensed rental company under a written agreement.

PART XIX: Data protection
XIX.1  The Insurer will use the personal information the Insured Person provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
XIX.2  The Insurer will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
XIX.3  The Insured Person can ask for a copy of the personal information the Insurer holds by writing to the Insurer's data protection officer.

PART XX: Arbitration
XX.1  If the Insurer accepts a claim but disagree with the Insured Person about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
XX.2  Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against the Insurer.

PART XXI: Accessibility
XXI.1  This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

PART XXII: Discounts
XXII.1  Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
XXII.2  If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Insurer may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

PART XXIII: Environmental commitment
XXIII.1  Where practical, the Insurer will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
XXIII.2  The Insured Person may ask for a new part instead, and the Insurer will tell the Insured Person whether any additional cost would apply.

PART XXIV: Reasonable precautions
XXIV.1  The Insured Person must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
XXIV.2  The Insured Person must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

PART XXV: Sanctions
XXV.1  The Insurer will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Insurer to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

PART XXVI: Severability
XXVI.1  If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

HOME CONTENTS INSURANCE POLICY
Issued by Oakfield Assurance

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
I.2  Family means the Policyholder's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Policyholder.
I.3  Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
I.4  Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Theft: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
II.2  Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
II.3  Accidental Damage: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.4  Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.5  Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

PART III: Optional cover: Accidental Damage
III.1  The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
III.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
III.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $750 per incident.
III.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
III.5  The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

PART IV: Escape of Water
IV.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
IV.2  The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.
IV.3  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
IV.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

PART V: Flood
V.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
V.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
V.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
V.4  The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

PART VI: General exclusions
VI.1  The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
VI.2  The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
VI.3  The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.

PART VII: Making a claim
VII.1  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
VII.2  The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
VII.3  The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 14 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

PART VIII: Taxes
VIII.1  The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
VIII.2  If the tax rate changes, the Insurer may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

PART IX: Discounts
IX.1  Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
IX.2  If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Insurer may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

PART X: Currency
X.1  All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
X.2  Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

PART XI: Exchange of information
XI.1  To prevent fraud, the Insurer may check the details the Policyholder gives against public records and industry databases.
XI.2  The Insurer may contact previous insurers to confirm the Policyholder's claims history.

PART XII: Cancellation
XII.1  The Policyholder can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
XII.2  After the first 14 days the Policyholder can cancel at any time; the Insurer will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
XII.3  The Insurer can cancel this policy by giving the Policyholder 30 days' written notice to the last address the Insurer holds.

PART XIII: Data protection
XIII.1  The Insurer will use the personal information the Policyholder provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
XIII.2  The Insurer will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
XIII.3  The Policyholder can ask for a copy of the personal information the Insurer holds by writing to the Insurer's data protection officer.

PART XIV: Complaints
XIV.1  If the Policyholder has a complaint, the Policyholder should first contact the Insurer's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
XIV.2  The Insurer will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
XIV.3  If the Policyholder remains dissatisfied, the Policyholder may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

PART XV: Duty of fair presentation
XV.1  The Policyholder must answer all questions the Insurer asks honestly and to the best of the Policyholder's knowledge.
XV.2  If the Policyholder gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Insurer may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
XV.3  If the Policyholder gives incorrect information carelessly, the Insurer may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

PART XVI: Reasonable precautions
XVI.1  The Policyholder must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
XVI.2  The Policyholder must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

PART XVII: Market conditions
XVII.1  If the replacement item is no longer available, the Insurer will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

PART XVIII: Claims documents
XVIII.1  The Policyholder must provide, at the Policyholder's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Insurer reasonably ask for.
XVIII.2  The Insurer may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

PART XIX: Contents temporarily removed
XIX.1  The Policyholder's contents are covered while temporarily removed from the home to another building in the same country, for up to 60 days.
XIX.2  Contents in a student hall of residence are covered only if the student is a member of the Policyholder's family.

PART XX: Alternative accommodation
XX.1  If the Policyholder's home cannot be lived in after damage covered by this policy, the Insurer will pay the reasonable cost of comparable temporary accommodation.
XX.2  The Insurer will also pay for the temporary housing of pets that live with the Policyholder.
XX.3  Cover ends when the home is fit to live in again or after twelve months, whichever is sooner.

PART XXI: Payment of claims
XXI.1  The Insurer will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Policyholder's name.
XXI.2  The Insurer aims to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents the Insurer needs.

PART XXII: Interpretation
XXII.1  Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
XXII.2  Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
XXII.3  Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

PART XXIII: Communication
XXIII.1  The Insurer will communicate with the Policyholder in English.
XXIII.2  The Insurer may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

PART XXIV: Subrogation
XXIV.1  The Insurer will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Policyholder's name the defence or settlement of any claim.
XXIV.2  The Insurer can take action in the Policyholder's name to recover any payment the Insurer makes from anyone responsible for the loss.

PART XXV: Salvage
XXV.1  When the Insurer replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Insurer's property.
XXV.2  If stolen property is recovered after the Insurer has paid a claim, the Policyholder must tell the Insurer and either return the payment or give the Insurer the property.
