DEVICE PROTECTION PLAN TERMS
Issued by Brightline Device Cover

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.
I.2  Accessories means cases, chargers and earbuds.
I.3  Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Provider, before any service fee, limit or sublimit is applied.
I.4  Authorised repairer means a repairer approved in writing by the Provider.
I.5  Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
I.6  Breakdown means the failure of a part to work as the manufacturer intended, from an internal electrical or mechanical fault.
I.7  Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
I.8  Device means the item shown in the schedule, bought new from an authorised retailer.
I.9  Family means the Customer's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Customer.
I.10  Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
I.11  Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 24 months after the device was bought.
I.12  Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Customer's schedule.
I.13  Premium means the amount the Customer must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
I.14  Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
I.15  Replacement device means a device of the same or similar specification, which may be refurbished.
I.16  Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Customer's details, the covers the Customer bought and any extensions.
I.17  Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
I.18  Wearables means smartwatches and fitness trackers.

PART II: Limits and service fee
II.1  Accidental Damage: limit $800 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
II.2  Breakdown: limit $600 per incident; service fee $25 per claim.
II.3  Theft and Loss: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
II.4  Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the service fee is then deducted from the result.

PART III: Data and backups
III.1  The Provider is not responsible for recovering or restoring any data, software or settings stored on the Customer's device.
III.2  The Customer should back up the Customer's data regularly and before sending the device for repair.

PART IV: Claims documents
IV.1  The Customer must provide, at the Customer's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Provider reasonably ask for.
IV.2  The Provider may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

PART V: Discounts
V.1  Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
V.2  If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Provider may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

PART VI: Customer support
VI.1  The Provider's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
VI.2  Outside these hours the Customer can leave a message and the Provider will call back on the next working day.

PART VII: Change of address
VII.1  The Customer must tell the Provider within 30 days if the Customer changes the Customer's address.
VII.2  The Provider may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

PART VIII: Third-party administrators
VIII.1  The Provider may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Provider's behalf.
VIII.2  Any company the Provider appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

PART IX: Currency
IX.1  All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
IX.2  Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

PART X: Sanctions
X.1  The Provider will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Provider to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

PART XI: Records and evidence
XI.1  The Customer should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
XI.2  Where proof of value is missing, the Provider may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
XI.3  The Provider may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

PART XII: Market conditions
XII.1  If the replacement item is no longer available, the Provider will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

PART XIII: Transferring the plan
XIII.1  The Customer may transfer the plan to a new owner of the device by telling the Provider in writing.
XIII.2  The remaining term of the plan transfers with the device; the term does not restart.

PART XIV: Interpretation
XIV.1  Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
XIV.2  Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
XIV.3  Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

PART XV: Instalment agreements
XV.1  If the Customer pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
XV.2  Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

PART XVI: Salvage
XVI.1  When the Provider replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Provider's property.
XVI.2  If stolen property is recovered after the Provider has paid a claim, the Customer must tell the Provider and either return the payment or give the Provider the property.

PART XVII: Joint policyholders
XVII.1  Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
XVII.2  A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

PART XVIII: Geographical limits
XVIII.1  Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
XVIII.2  Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

PART XIX: Communication
XIX.1  The Provider will communicate with the Customer in English.
XIX.2  The Provider may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

PART XX: How to read this document
XX.1  This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
XX.2  Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
XX.3  Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

PART XXI: Repair process
XXI.1  After a claim is accepted, the Provider will send a prepaid mailer or book a courier collection.
XXI.2  The Provider aims to return repaired devices within 10 business days of receiving them.

PART XXII: Waiver
XXII.1  If the Provider does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Provider has given up the right to enforce it later.

PART XXIII: Automatic renewal
XXIII.1  Unless the Customer tells the Provider otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Provider holds.
XXIII.2  The Customer can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Provider's helpline.

PART XXIV: Premium payment
XXIV.1  The Customer must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
XXIV.2  If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, the Provider may cancel the policy after giving notice.

PART XXV: Accidental Damage
XXV.1  The Provider will repair or replace the Customer's device if it is accidentally damaged.
XXV.2  The most the Provider will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.
XXV.3  The most the Provider will pay for Wearables under this section is $300 per incident.
XXV.4  The Provider will not pay for cosmetic damage, such as scratches or dents, that does not affect how the device works.
XXV.5  The Provider will not pay for damage following a repair by anyone other than the Provider or an authorised repairer. This exclusion does not apply if the Provider approved the repair in writing beforehand.

PART XXVI: Renewal
XXVI.1  The Provider will write to the Customer at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
XXVI.2  The Provider is not obliged to offer renewal.

PART XXVII: Severability
XXVII.1  If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

PART XXVIII: Unrecoverable devices
XXVIII.1  If a device is found after the Provider has replaced it, the found device becomes the Provider's property and must be sent to the Provider.
XXVIII.2  The Provider may block devices reported as lost or stolen so that they cannot be used on mobile networks.

PART XXIX: Subrogation
XXIX.1  The Provider will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Customer's name the defence or settlement of any claim.
XXIX.2  The Provider can take action in the Customer's name to recover any payment the Provider makes from anyone responsible for the loss.

PART XXX: Accessibility
XXX.1  This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

PART XXXI: Arbitration
XXXI.1  If the Provider accepts a claim but disagree with the Customer about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
XXXI.2  Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against the Provider.

PART XXXII: Assignment
XXXII.1  The Customer cannot transfer the Customer's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Provider's written consent.

PART XXXIII: Notices
XXXIII.1  Any notice the Provider gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Provider holds.
XXXIII.2  Notices from the Customer should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

PART XXXIV: Replacement devices
XXXIV.1  If the Provider cannot repair the Customer's device economically, the Provider will replace it with a replacement device.
XXXIV.2  Replacement devices may be a different colour and may be refurbished to an as-new standard.
XXXIV.3  Accessories are replaced only if they were lost or damaged in the same incident as the device.

PART XXXV: Recovery of costs
XXXV.1  If the Provider pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Provider may ask the Customer to repay the amount.

PART XXXVI: Inflation
XXXVI.1  The Provider may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
XXXVI.2  Any adjustment will be shown in the Customer's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

PART XXXVII: Software support
XXXVII.1  The Provider's helpline can give advice on setting up and using the Customer's device.
XXXVII.2  Software support does not include fixing problems caused by third-party apps or unofficial operating systems.

PART XXXVIII: Reasonable precautions
XXXVIII.1  The Customer must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
XXXVIII.2  The Customer must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

PART XXXIX: Optional cover: Theft and Loss
XXXIX.1  The Provider will replace the Customer's device if it is stolen or lost.
XXXIX.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Customer's schedule.
XXXIX.3  The most the Provider will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.
XXXIX.4  The Provider will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
XXXIX.5  The Provider will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

PART XXXX: Compensation scheme
XXXX.1  The Provider is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
XXXX.2  If the Provider cannot meet the Provider's obligations, the Customer may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

PART XXXXI: Payment of claims
XXXXI.1  The Provider will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Customer's name.
XXXXI.2  The Provider aims to pay accepted claims within 10 working days of receiving all the documents the Provider needs.

PART XXXXII: Data protection
XXXXII.1  The Provider will use the personal information the Customer provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
XXXXII.2  The Provider will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
XXXXII.3  The Customer can ask for a copy of the personal information the Provider holds by writing to the Provider's data protection officer.

PART XXXXIII: Fraud
XXXXIII.1  If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Provider will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
XXXXIII.2  The Provider may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

PART XXXXIV: Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
XXXXIV.1  A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

PART XXXXV: Exchange of information
XXXXV.1  To prevent fraud, the Provider may check the details the Customer gives against public records and industry databases.
XXXXV.2  The Provider may contact previous insurers to confirm the Customer's claims history.

PART XXXXVI: Cooperation
XXXXVI.1  The Customer must give the Provider all the help and information the Provider reasonably need to settle a claim.
XXXXVI.2  The Customer must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Provider's written permission.

PART XXXXVII: Governing law
XXXXVII.1  This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
XXXXVII.2  Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

PART XXXXVIII: Breakdown
XXXXVIII.1  The Provider will repair or replace the Customer's device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
XXXXVIII.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 45 days after the policy start date.
XXXXVIII.3  The most the Provider will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $120 per incident.
XXXXVIII.4  The Provider will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
XXXXVIII.5  The Provider will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

PART XXXXIX: Changes in circumstances
XXXXIX.1  The Customer must tell the Provider as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
XXXXIX.2  The Provider may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

PART XXXXX: Interest
XXXXX.1  The Provider will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

PART XXXXXI: Other insurance
XXXXXI.1  If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Provider will pay only the Provider's proportionate share.
XXXXXI.2  The Customer must tell the Provider about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Customer makes a claim.

PART XXXXXII: General exclusions
XXXXXII.1  The Provider will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
XXXXXII.2  The Provider will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Provider from paying.
XXXXXII.3  The Provider will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Customer.
XXXXXII.4  The Provider will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
XXXXXII.5  The Provider will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

PART XXXXXIII: Electronic documents
XXXXXIII.1  The Provider will send documents by email unless the Customer asks for paper copies.
XXXXXIII.2  The Customer must tell the Provider if the Customer's email address changes.
XXXXXIII.3  Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

PART XXXXXIV: Taxes
XXXXXIV.1  The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
XXXXXIV.2  If the tax rate changes, the Provider may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

PART XXXXXV: Making a claim
XXXXXV.1  The Customer must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
XXXXXV.2  The Customer must notify the Provider of a claim within 60 days of the incident. The Provider will not pay any claim notified after that time.
XXXXXV.3  The Provider may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

PART XXXXXVI: Cancellation
XXXXXVI.1  The Customer can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
XXXXXVI.2  After the first 14 days the Customer can cancel at any time; the Provider will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
XXXXXVI.3  The Provider can cancel this policy by giving the Customer 30 days' written notice to the last address the Provider holds.

PART XXXXXVII: Environmental commitment
XXXXXVII.1  Where practical, the Provider will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.

PART XXXXXVIII: Complaints
XXXXXVIII.1  If the Customer has a complaint, the Customer should first contact the Provider's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
XXXXXVIII.2  The Provider will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
XXXXXVIII.3  If the Customer remains dissatisfied, the Customer may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

XXXXXIX.1  The Customer must answer all questions the Provider asks honestly and to the best of the Customer's knowledge.
XXXXXIX.2  If the Customer gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Provider may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.

# Annual Multi-Trip Travel Cover
Issued by Northstar Underwriting

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
- **1.2** Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
- **1.3** Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
- **1.4** Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
- **1.5** Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,500 metres.
- **1.6** Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
- **1.7** Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
- **1.8** Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
- **1.9** Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
- **1.10** Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which you received treatment or advice in the 6 months before the policy start date.

- **1.14** Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 8 hours.

- **1.17** Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
- **1.18** Territory means the countries in which cover applies, as shown in the schedule.
- **1.19** Travelling companion means a person who has booked to travel with you on the same trip.

- **2.1** Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.2** Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $150 per claim.

- **2.4** Travel Delay: limit $750 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
- **2.5** The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Changes in circumstances
- **3.1** You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
- **3.2** We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

## 4. Assignment

## 5. Interpretation
- **5.1** Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
- **5.2** Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
- **5.3** Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

- **6.2** We will decide the method of transport and the time of repatriation after speaking to the treating doctor.

- **7.1** We will communicate with you in English.
- **7.2** We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

## 8. Inflation
- **8.1** We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.

## 9. Payment of claims
- **9.1** We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
- **9.2** We aim to pay accepted claims within 15 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

## 10. Salvage
- **10.1** When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
- **10.2** If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

## 11. Baggage and Personal Belongings
- **11.1** We will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to your baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
- **11.2** The most we will pay for Valuables under this section is $400 per incident.
- **11.3** The most we will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $450 per incident.
- **11.4** We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
- **11.5** We will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.

## 12. Discounts
- **12.1** Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
- **12.2** If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

## 13. Data protection

- **14.3** The most we will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $300 per incident.
- **14.4** We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
- **14.5** We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
- **14.6** We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

- **15.1** We will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if you must cancel the trip for a reason beyond your control.
- **15.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 10 days after the policy start date.
- **15.3** The most we will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $300 per incident.
- **15.4** We will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before you bought the policy.
- **15.5** We will not pay for cancellation because you no longer wish to travel.

## 18. Currency

- **18.2** Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

Article 5. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

Article 6. Making a claim

(b) The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

In this policy, "the Plan" means the Staff Welfare Fund and "the Member" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Plan, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
(b) Family means the Member's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Member.
(c) Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
(d) Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Member's details, the covers the Member bought and any extensions.

Article 2. Limits and deductible
(a) Dental Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
(b) Vision Care: limit $300 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
(c) Therapy Services: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
(d) Hearing Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
(e) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

Article 3. Therapy Services
(a) The Plan will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
(b) The most the Plan will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $300 per treatment.
(c) The Plan will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
(d) The Plan will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

Article 4. General exclusions
(a) The Plan will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
(b) The Plan will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Plan from paying.

Article 5. Making a claim
(a) The Member must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(b) The Member must notify the Plan of a claim within 14 days of the treatment. The Plan will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(c) The Plan may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

Article 6. Fraud
(a) If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Plan will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
(b) The Plan may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

Article 7. Recovery of costs
(a) If the Plan pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Plan may ask the Member to repay the amount.

Article 8. Leaving the plan
(a) Cover ends on the day the Member's employment ends or the day the Member stops being eligible, whichever is earlier.
(b) Claims for treatment received before cover ended may be submitted up to 90 days afterwards.

Article 9. Duty of fair presentation
(a) The Member must answer all questions the Plan asks honestly and to the best of the Member's knowledge.
(b) If the Member gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Plan may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
(c) If the Member gives incorrect information carelessly, the Plan may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

Article 10. Claims documents
(a) The Member must provide, at the Member's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Plan reasonably ask for.
(b) The Plan may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

Article 11. Compensation scheme
(a) The Plan is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
(b) If the Plan cannot meet the Plan's obligations, the Member may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

Article 12. Market conditions
(a) If the replacement item is no longer available, the Plan will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

Article 13. Exchange of information
(a) To prevent fraud, the Plan may check the details the Member gives against public records and industry databases.
(b) The Plan may contact previous insurers to confirm the Member's claims history.

Article 14. Third-party administrators
(a) The Plan may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Plan's behalf.
(b) Any company the Plan appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

Article 15. Customer support
(a) The Plan's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
(b) Outside these hours the Member can leave a message and the Plan will call back on the next working day.

Article 16. Interpretation
(a) Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
(b) Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
(c) Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

Article 17. Instalment agreements
(a) If the Member pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
(b) Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

GROUP HEALTH CASH PLAN
Issued by Cedar Benefits Services

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Plan, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
I.2  Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
I.3  Dependant means the Member's spouse or partner, or a child under 21 who is enrolled in the plan.
I.4  Family means the Member's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Member.
I.5  Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
I.6  Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
I.7  Hearing aid replacement period means 24 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
I.8  Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
I.9  Limit means the most the Plan will pay for all claims under a section arising from one treatment.
I.10  Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
I.11  Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
I.12  Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
I.13  Plan year means the twelve months starting on the Member's coverage start date.
I.14  Premium means the amount the Member must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
I.15  Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
I.16  Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
I.17  Registered practitioner means a practitioner registered with the professional body for their discipline.
I.18  Replacement period means 12 months from the date of the Member's last eyewear claim.

PART II: Limits and deductible
II.1  Dental Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
II.2  Vision Care: limit $500 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
II.3  Therapy Services: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
II.4  Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
II.5  Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

PART III: Therapy Services
III.1  The Plan will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
III.2  The most the Plan will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $200 per treatment.
III.3  The Plan will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
III.4  The Plan will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

PART IV: Vision Care
IV.1  The Plan will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
IV.2  The most the Plan will pay for Frames under this section is $120 per treatment.
IV.3  The Plan will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
IV.4  The Plan will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

PART V: Dental Care
V.1  The Plan will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
V.2  No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 90 days after the policy start date.
V.3  The most the Plan will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.
V.4  The most the Plan will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $800 per treatment.
V.5  The Plan will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
V.6  The Plan will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

PART VI: Optional cover: Hearing Care
VI.1  The Plan will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
VI.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Member's schedule.
VI.3  The most the Plan will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $100 per treatment.
VI.4  The Plan will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

PART VII: General exclusions
VII.1  The Plan will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
VII.2  The Plan will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
VII.3  The Plan will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Member.
VII.4  The Plan will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Plan from paying.
VII.5  The Plan will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
VII.6  The Plan will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

PART VIII: Making a claim
VIII.1  The Plan may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
VIII.2  The Member must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
VIII.3  The Member must notify the Plan of a claim within 30 days of the treatment. The Plan will not pay any claim notified after that time.

PART IX: Governing law
IX.1  This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
IX.2  Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

PART X: Interpretation
X.1  Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
X.2  Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
X.3  Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

PART XI: Discounts
XI.1  Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
XI.2  If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Plan may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

PART XII: Market conditions
XII.1  If the replacement item is no longer available, the Plan will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

PART XIII: Records and evidence
XIII.1  The Member should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
XIII.2  Where proof of value is missing, the Plan may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
XIII.3  The Plan may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

PART XIV: Environmental commitment
XIV.1  Where practical, the Plan will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
XIV.2  The Member may ask for a new part instead, and the Plan will tell the Member whether any additional cost would apply.

PART XV: Geographical limits
XV.1  Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
XV.2  Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

PART XVI: Automatic renewal
XVI.1  Unless the Member tells the Plan otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Plan holds.
XVI.2  The Member can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Plan's helpline.

PART XVII: How to read this document
XVII.1  This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
XVII.2  Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
XVII.3  Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

PART XVIII: Accessibility
XVIII.1  This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

PART XIX: Sanctions
XIX.1  The Plan will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Plan to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

PART XX: Premium payment
XX.1  The Member must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
XX.2  If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, the Plan may cancel the policy after giving notice.

PART XXI: Salvage
XXI.1  When the Plan replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Plan's property.
XXI.2  If stolen property is recovered after the Plan has paid a claim, the Member must tell the Plan and either return the payment or give the Plan the property.

PART XXII: Leaving the plan
XXII.1  Cover ends on the day the Member's employment ends or the day the Member stops being eligible, whichever is earlier.
XXII.2  Claims for treatment received before cover ended may be submitted up to 90 days afterwards.

PART XXIII: Communication
XXIII.1  The Plan will communicate with the Member in English.
XXIII.2  The Plan may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

PART XXIV: Notices
XXIV.1  Any notice the Plan gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Plan holds.
XXIV.2  Notices from the Member should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

PART XXV: Electronic documents
XXV.1  The Plan will send documents by email unless the Member asks for paper copies.
XXV.2  The Member must tell the Plan if the Member's email address changes.
XXV.3  Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

PART XXVI: Duty of fair presentation
XXVI.1  The Member must answer all questions the Plan asks honestly and to the best of the Member's knowledge.
XXVI.2  If the Member gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Plan may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
XXVI.3  If the Member gives incorrect information carelessly, the Plan may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

PART XXVII: Appeals
XXVII.1  If the Plan declines all or part of a claim, the Member may appeal in writing within 60 days of the decision.
XXVII.2  An appeal will be reviewed by someone who was not involved in the original decision.
XXVII.3  The Plan will give the Member a written decision on the appeal within 30 days.

PART XXVIII: Changes in circumstances
XXVIII.1  The Member must tell the Plan as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
XXVIII.2  The Plan may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

PART XXIX: Instalment agreements
XXIX.1  If the Member pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
XXIX.2  Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

PART XXX: Renewal
XXX.1  The Plan will write to the Member at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
XXX.2  The Plan is not obliged to offer renewal.

PART XXXI: Inflation
XXXI.1  The Plan may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
XXXI.2  Any adjustment will be shown in the Member's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

PART XXXII: Fraud
XXXII.1  If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Plan will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
XXXII.2  The Plan may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

PART XXXIII: Subrogation
XXXIII.1  The Plan will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Member's name the defence or settlement of any claim.
XXXIII.2  The Plan can take action in the Member's name to recover any payment the Plan makes from anyone responsible for the loss.

PART XXXIV: Payment of claims
XXXIV.1  The Plan will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Member's name.
XXXIV.2  The Plan aims to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents the Plan needs.

PART XXXV: Coordination of benefits
XXXV.1  If a treatment is also covered by another plan, the Plan will pay only the part of the cost that the other plan does not pay.
XXXV.2  The Member must tell the Plan about any other plan that covers the Member or the Member's dependants.

PART XXXVI: Severability
XXXVI.1  If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

PART XXXVII: Wellness allowance
XXXVII.1  Each plan year the Member may claim up to $250 towards a gym membership or fitness class.
XXXVII.2  The wellness allowance is not subject to any deductible and does not count towards other limits.

PART XXXVIII: Compensation scheme
XXXVIII.1  The Plan is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
XXXVIII.2  If the Plan cannot meet the Plan's obligations, the Member may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

PART XXXIX: Arbitration
XXXIX.1  If the Plan accepts a claim but disagree with the Member about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
XXXIX.2  Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against the Plan.

PART XXXX: Data protection
XXXX.1  The Plan will use the personal information the Member provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
XXXX.2  The Plan will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
XXXX.3  The Member can ask for a copy of the personal information the Plan holds by writing to the Plan's data protection officer.

PART XXXXI: Eligibility
XXXXI.1  Employees who work at least 20 hours a week are eligible to join the plan from their first day of employment.
XXXXI.2  Contractors, agency workers and employees on unpaid leave of more than three months are not eligible.

PART XXXXII: Assignment
XXXXII.1  The Member cannot transfer the Member's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Plan's written consent.

PART XXXXIII: Complaints
XXXXIII.1  If the Member has a complaint, the Member should first contact the Plan's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
XXXXIII.2  The Plan will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
XXXXIII.3  If the Member remains dissatisfied, the Member may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

PART XXXXIV: Interest
XXXXIV.1  The Plan will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

PART XXXXV: Recovery of costs
XXXXV.1  If the Plan pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Plan may ask the Member to repay the amount.

PART XXXXVI: Exchange of information
XXXXVI.1  To prevent fraud, the Plan may check the details the Member gives against public records and industry databases.
XXXXVI.2  The Plan may contact previous insurers to confirm the Member's claims history.

HOME CONTENTS INSURANCE POLICY
Issued by Oakfield Assurance

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
I.2  Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Insurer, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
I.3  Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
I.4  Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
I.5  Contents means household goods and personal possessions that belong to the Policyholder or the Policyholder's family.
I.6  Family means the Policyholder's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Policyholder.
I.7  Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
I.8  Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
I.9  High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
I.10  Home means the private residence at the address shown in the schedule.
I.11  Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
I.12  Limit means the most the Insurer will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
I.13  Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Policyholder's schedule.
I.14  Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
I.15  Premium means the amount the Policyholder must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
I.16  Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
I.17  Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Policyholder's details, the covers the Policyholder bought and any extensions.
I.18  Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
I.19  Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 30 consecutive days.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Theft: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
II.2  Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.3  Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.4  Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.5  The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Theft
III.1  The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
III.2  The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $2,500 per incident.
III.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $500 per incident.
III.4  The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
III.5  The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
III.6  The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

PART IV: Escape of Water
IV.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
IV.2  The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.
IV.3  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
IV.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

PART V: Changes in circumstances
V.1  The Policyholder must tell the Insurer as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
V.2  The Insurer may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

PART VI: Geographical limits
VI.1  Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
VI.2  Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

PART VII: Instalment agreements
VII.1  If the Policyholder pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
VII.2  Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

PART VIII: Currency
VIII.1  All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
VIII.2  Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

PART IX: Cancellation
IX.1  The Policyholder can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
IX.2  After the first 14 days the Policyholder can cancel at any time; the Insurer will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
IX.3  The Insurer can cancel this policy by giving the Policyholder 30 days' written notice to the last address the Insurer holds.

PART X: Notices
X.1  Any notice the Insurer gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Insurer holds.
X.2  Notices from the Policyholder should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

PART XI: Accessibility
XI.1  This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

PART XII: Complaints
XII.1  If the Policyholder has a complaint, the Policyholder should first contact the Insurer's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
XII.2  The Insurer will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
XII.3  If the Policyholder remains dissatisfied, the Policyholder may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

PART XIII: Optional cover: Accidental Damage
XIII.1  The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
XIII.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
XIII.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $500 per incident.
XIII.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
XIII.5  The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

PART XIV: Recovery of costs
XIV.1  If the Insurer pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Insurer may ask the Policyholder to repay the amount.

PART XV: Interest
XV.1  The Insurer will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

PART XVI: Waiver
XVI.1  If the Insurer does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Insurer has given up the right to enforce it later.

PART XVII: How to read this document
XVII.1  This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
XVII.2  Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
XVII.3  Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

PART XVIII: Flood
XVIII.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
XVIII.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
XVIII.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
XVIII.4  The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

PART XIX: Freezer contents
XIX.1  The Insurer will pay for food in a domestic freezer that spoils because of a rise or fall in temperature.
XIX.2  The Insurer will not pay if the freezer is more than fifteen years old, or if the electricity supplier cut the supply deliberately.

PART XX: Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
XX.1  A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

PART XXI: Customer support
XXI.1  The Insurer's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
XXI.2  Outside these hours the Policyholder can leave a message and the Insurer will call back on the next working day.

PART XXII: General exclusions
XXII.1  The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
XXII.2  The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
XXII.3  The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
XXII.4  The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.
XXII.5  The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
XXII.6  The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.

PART XXIII: Fraud
XXIII.1  If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Insurer will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
XXIII.2  The Insurer may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

PART XXIV: Governing law
XXIV.1  This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
XXIV.2  Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

PART XXV: Making a claim
XXV.1  The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 30 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
XXV.2  The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
XXV.3  The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Plan, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.

I.5  Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.

I.7  Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
I.8  Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
I.9  Network provider means a practitioner or clinic that has an agreement with the Plan to provide treatment.
I.10  Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
I.11  Plan year means the twelve months starting on the Member's coverage start date.
I.12  Premium means the amount the Member must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
I.13  Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
I.14  Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
I.15  Registered practitioner means a practitioner registered with the professional body for their discipline.
I.16  Replacement period means 24 months from the date of the Member's last eyewear claim.

PART II: Limits and deductible
II.1  Dental Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
II.2  Vision Care: limit $300 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
II.3  Therapy Services: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
II.4  Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
II.5  The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Vision Care
III.1  The Plan will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
III.2  The most the Plan will pay for Frames under this section is $120 per treatment.
III.3  The Plan will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
III.4  The Plan will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

PART IV: Therapy Services
IV.1  The Plan will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
IV.2  The most the Plan will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $200 per treatment.
IV.3  The Plan will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
IV.4  The Plan will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

PART V: Optional cover: Hearing Care
V.1  The Plan will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
V.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Member's schedule.
V.3  The most the Plan will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $100 per treatment.
V.4  The Plan will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

PART VI: Dental Care
VI.1  The Plan will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.

VII.1  The Plan will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
VII.2  The Plan will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
VII.3  The Plan will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

X.2  The Plan aims to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents the Plan needs.

XI.1  The Plan may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Plan's behalf.
XI.2  Any company the Plan appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

XII.1  Employees who work at least 20 hours a week are eligible to join the plan from their first day of employment.
XII.2  Contractors, agency workers and employees on unpaid leave of more than three months are not eligible.

XVI.2  The Plan may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

PART XVII: Reasonable precautions
XVII.1  The Member must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
XVII.2  The Member must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

XVIII.1  The Member must answer all questions the Plan asks honestly and to the best of the Member's knowledge.

XVIII.3  If the Member gives incorrect information carelessly, the Plan may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

PART XIX: Exchange of information
XIX.1  To prevent fraud, the Plan may check the details the Member gives against public records and industry databases.
XIX.2  The Plan may contact previous insurers to confirm the Member's claims history.

PART XX: Recovery of costs
XX.1  If the Plan pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Plan may ask the Member to repay the amount.

PART XXI: Wellness allowance
XXI.1  Each plan year the Member may claim up to $100 towards a gym membership or fitness class.
XXI.2  The wellness allowance is not subject to any deductible and does not count towards other limits.

PART XXII: Cooperation
XXII.1  The Member must give the Plan all the help and information the Plan reasonably need to settle a claim.
XXII.2  The Member must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Plan's written permission.

XXIII.2  Outside these hours the Member can leave a message and the Plan will call back on the next working day.

# Group Health Cash Plan
Issued by the Staff Welfare Fund

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
- **1.2** Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
- **1.3** Dependant means your spouse or partner, or a child under 21 who is enrolled in the plan.
- **1.4** Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
- **1.5** Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
- **1.6** Hearing aid replacement period means 36 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
- **1.7** Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one treatment.
- **1.8** Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
- **1.9** Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
- **1.10** Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
- **1.11** Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
- **1.12** Replacement period means 12 months from the date of your last eyewear claim.
- **1.13** Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

## 2. Limits and deductible
- **2.1** Dental Care: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
- **2.2** Vision Care: limit $300 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
- **2.3** Therapy Services: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
- **2.5** Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

## 3. Changes in circumstances
- **3.1** You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
- **3.2** We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

## 4. Optional cover: Hearing Care
- **4.1** We will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
- **4.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $100 per treatment.
- **4.4** We will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

## 5. Arbitration
- **5.1** If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
- **5.2** Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

## 6. Inflation
- **6.1** We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
- **6.2** Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

## 7. Vision Care
- **7.1** We will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
- **7.2** The most we will pay for Frames under this section is $120 per treatment.
- **7.3** We will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
- **7.4** We will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

## 8. Cancellation
- **8.1** You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
- **8.2** After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $30.
- **8.3** We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

## 9. Data protection
- **9.1** We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
- **9.2** We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
- **9.3** You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

## 10. Waiver
- **10.1** If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

## 11. Claims documents
- **11.1** You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
- **11.2** We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

## 12. Governing law
- **12.1** This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
- **12.2** Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

## 13. Fraud
- **13.1** If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
- **13.2** We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

## 14. Instalment agreements
- **14.1** If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
- **14.2** Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

## 15. Eligibility
- **15.1** Employees who work at least 20 hours a week are eligible to join the plan from their first day of employment.
- **15.2** Contractors, agency workers and employees on unpaid leave of more than three months are not eligible.

## 16. Leaving the plan
- **16.1** Cover ends on the day your employment ends or the day you stop being eligible, whichever is earlier.
- **16.2** Claims for treatment received before cover ended may be submitted up to 90 days afterwards.

## 17. Communication
- **17.1** We will communicate with you in English.
- **17.2** We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

## 18. Premium payment
- **18.1** You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
- **18.2** If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

## 19. Subrogation
- **19.1** We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
- **19.2** We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

## 20. Sanctions
- **20.1** We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

## 21. Cooperation
- **21.1** You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
- **21.2** You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

## 22. Taxes
- **22.1** The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
- **22.2** If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

## 23. Dental Care
- **23.1** We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
- **23.2** No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 90 days after the policy start date.
- **23.3** The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $750 per treatment.
- **23.4** The most we will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $600 per treatment.
- **23.5** We will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
- **23.6** We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

## 24. Therapy Services
- **24.1** We will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
- **24.2** The most we will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $300 per treatment.
- **24.3** We will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
- **24.4** We will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

## 25. Interest
- **25.1** We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

## 26. Other insurance
- **26.1** If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
- **26.2** You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

## 27. Interpretation
- **27.1** Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
- **27.2** Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
- **27.3** Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

## 28. Accessibility
- **28.1** This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

## 29. Assignment
- **29.1** You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

## 30. Customer support
- **30.1** Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
- **30.2** Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

## 31. Electronic documents
- **31.1** We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
- **31.2** You must tell us if your email address changes.
- **31.3** Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

## 32. Appeals
- **32.1** If we decline all or part of a claim, you may appeal in writing within 60 days of the decision.
- **32.2** An appeal will be reviewed by someone who was not involved in the original decision.
- **32.3** We will give you a written decision on the appeal within 30 days.

## 33. Third-party administrators
- **33.1** We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
- **33.2** Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

## 34. Geographical limits
- **34.1** Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
- **34.2** Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

## 35. Salvage
- **35.1** When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
- **35.2** If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

## 36. Discounts
- **36.1** Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
- **36.2** If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

## 37. Recovery of costs
- **37.1** If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

## 38. Renewal
- **38.1** We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
- **38.2** We are not obliged to offer renewal.

## 39. Notices
- **39.1** Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
- **39.2** Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

## 40. Coordination of benefits
- **40.1** If a treatment is also covered by another plan, we will pay only the part of the cost that the other plan does not pay.
- **40.2** You must tell us about any other plan that covers you or your dependants.

## 41. Wellness allowance
- **41.1** Each plan year you may claim up to $100 towards a gym membership or fitness class.
- **41.2** The wellness allowance is not subject to any deductible and does not count towards other limits.

## 42. Reasonable precautions
- **42.1** You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
- **42.2** You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

## 43. Environmental commitment
- **43.1** Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
- **43.2** You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

## 44. Compensation scheme
- **44.1** We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
- **44.2** If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

## 45. General exclusions
- **45.1** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **45.2** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
- **45.3** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
- **45.4** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
- **45.5** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.

## 46. Currency
- **46.1** All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
- **46.2** Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

## 47. Automatic renewal
- **47.1** Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
- **47.2** You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

## 48. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
- **48.1** A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

## 49. Making a claim
- **49.1** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **49.2** You must notify us of a claim within 14 days of the treatment. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **49.3** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

## 50. Change of address
- **50.1** You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
- **50.2** We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

## 51. Records and evidence
- **51.1** You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
- **51.2** Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
- **51.3** We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

## 52. Duty of fair presentation
- **52.1** You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
- **52.2** If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
- **52.3** If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

## 53. Payment of claims
- **53.1** We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
- **53.2** We aim to pay accepted claims within 10 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

## 54. Severability
- **54.1** If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

## 55. Dependants
- **55.1** You may enrol dependants at the start of each plan year or within 30 days of a qualifying life event.
- **55.2** Benefits paid for dependants count towards the same annual limits as your own claims.

## 56. How to read this document
- **56.1** This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
- **56.2** Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
- **56.3** Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

## 57. Exchange of information
- **57.1** To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
- **57.2** We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

## 58. Complaints
- **58.1** If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
- **58.2** We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
- **58.3** If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

## 59. Market conditions
- **59.1** If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

## 60. Joint policyholders
- **60.1** Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
- **60.2** A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

+#!/bin/bash
+set -e
 
+if [ "$#" -ne 1 ]; then
+  echo "Usage: scripts/hackage-docs.sh HACKAGE_USER"
+  exit 1
+fi
+
+user=$1
+
+cabal_file=$(find . -maxdepth 1 -name "*.cabal" -print -quit)
+if [ ! -f "$cabal_file" ]; then
+  echo "Run this script in the top-level package directory"
+  exit 1
+fi
+
+pkg=$(awk -F ":[[:space:]]*" 'tolower($1)=="name"    { print $2 }' < "$cabal_file")
+ver=$(awk -F ":[[:space:]]*" 'tolower($1)=="version" { print $2 }' < "$cabal_file")
+
+if [ -z "$pkg" ]; then
+  echo "Unable to determine package name"
+  exit 1
+fi
+
+if [ -z "$ver" ]; then
+  echo "Unable to determine package version"
+  exit 1
+fi
+
+echo "Detected package: $pkg-$ver"
+
+dir=$(mktemp -d build-docs.XXXXXX)
+trap 'rm -r "$dir"' EXIT
+
+cabal haddock --hoogle --hyperlink-source --html-location='/package/$pkg-$version/docs' --contents-location='/package/$pkg-$version' --haddock-options="--hyperlinked-source"
+
+cp -R dist/doc/html/$pkg/ $dir/$pkg-$ver-docs
+
+tar cvz -C $dir --format=ustar -f $dir/$pkg-$ver-docs.tar.gz $pkg-$ver-docs
+
+curl -X PUT \
+     -H 'Content-Type: application/x-tar' \
+     -H 'Content-Encoding: gzip' \
+     -u "$user" \
+     --data-binary "@$dir/$pkg-$ver-docs.tar.gz" \
+     "https://hackage.haskell.org/package/$pkg-$ver/docs"
+
