state.policy:
HOME CONTENTS INSURANCE POLICY
Issued by Hearthstone Insurance plc

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
I.2  Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Insurer, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
I.3  Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
I.4  Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
I.5  Contents means household goods and personal possessions that belong to the Policyholder or the Policyholder's family.
I.6  Family means the Policyholder's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Policyholder.
I.7  Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
I.8  Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
I.9  High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
I.10  Home means the private residence at the address shown in the schedule.
I.11  Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
I.12  Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.
I.13  Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Policyholder's schedule.
I.14  Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
I.15  Premium means the amount the Policyholder must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
I.16  Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
I.17  Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
I.18  Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Policyholder's details, the covers the Policyholder bought and any extensions.
I.19  Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
I.20  Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 60 consecutive days.

PART II: Limits and excess
II.1  Theft: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
II.2  Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
II.3  Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
II.4  Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
II.5  The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

PART III: Claims documents
III.1  The Policyholder must provide, at the Policyholder's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Insurer reasonably ask for.
III.2  The Insurer may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

PART IV: Salvage
IV.1  When the Insurer replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Insurer's property.
IV.2  If stolen property is recovered after the Insurer has paid a claim, the Policyholder must tell the Insurer and either return the payment or give the Insurer the property.

PART V: Complaints
V.1  If the Policyholder has a complaint, the Policyholder should first contact the Insurer's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
V.2  The Insurer will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
V.3  If the Policyholder remains dissatisfied, the Policyholder may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

PART VI: Governing law
VI.1  This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
VI.2  Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

PART VII: Sanctions
VII.1  The Insurer will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Insurer to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

PART VIII: Theft
VIII.1  The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
VIII.2  The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
VIII.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $800 per incident.
VIII.4  The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
VIII.5  The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
VIII.6  The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

PART IX: Freezer contents
IX.1  The Insurer will pay for food in a domestic freezer that spoils because of a rise or fall in temperature.
IX.2  The Insurer will not pay if the freezer is more than fifteen years old, or if the electricity supplier cut the supply deliberately.

PART X: Records and evidence
X.1  The Policyholder should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
X.2  Where proof of value is missing, the Insurer may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
X.3  The Insurer may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

PART XI: Alternative accommodation
XI.1  If the Policyholder's home cannot be lived in after damage covered by this policy, the Insurer will pay the reasonable cost of comparable temporary accommodation.
XI.2  The Insurer will also pay for the temporary housing of pets that live with the Policyholder.
XI.3  Cover ends when the home is fit to live in again or after twelve months, whichever is sooner.

PART XII: Cooperation
XII.1  The Policyholder must give the Insurer all the help and information the Insurer reasonably need to settle a claim.
XII.2  The Policyholder must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Insurer's written permission.

PART XIII: Interest
XIII.1  The Insurer will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

PART XIV: Escape of Water
XIV.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
XIV.2  The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.
XIV.3  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
XIV.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

PART XV: Data protection
XV.1  The Insurer will use the personal information the Policyholder provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
XV.2  The Insurer will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
XV.3  The Policyholder can ask for a copy of the personal information the Insurer holds by writing to the Insurer's data protection officer.

PART XVI: Garden and outdoor cover
XVI.1  The Insurer will pay for plants, trees and shrubs in the garden of the home that are damaged by fire, lightning or theft.
XVI.2  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by frost, storms, drought or animals.

PART XVII: Accessibility
XVII.1  This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

PART XVIII: Joint policyholders
XVIII.1  Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
XVIII.2  A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

PART XIX: How to read this document
XIX.1  This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
XIX.2  Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
XIX.3  Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

PART XX: Optional cover: Accidental Damage
XX.1  The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
XX.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
XX.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $500 per incident.
XX.4  The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
XX.5  The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

PART XXI: Third-party administrators
XXI.1  The Insurer may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Insurer's behalf.
XXI.2  Any company the Insurer appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

PART XXII: Interpretation
XXII.1  Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
XXII.2  Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
XXII.3  Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

PART XXIII: Flood
XXIII.1  The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
XXIII.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
XXIII.3  The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
XXIII.4  The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

PART XXIV: General exclusions
XXIV.1  The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
XXIV.2  The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
XXIV.3  The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.

PART XXV: Subrogation
XXV.1  The Insurer will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Policyholder's name the defence or settlement of any claim.
XXV.2  The Insurer can take action in the Policyholder's name to recover any payment the Insurer makes from anyone responsible for the loss.

PART XXVI: Communication
XXVI.1  The Insurer will communicate with the Policyholder in English.
XXVI.2  The Insurer may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

PART XXVII: Locks and keys
XXVII.1  If the keys to the Policyholder's home are lost or stolen, the Insurer will pay the cost of replacing the locks to the outside doors.
XXVII.2  The most the Insurer will pay under this clause is $500 for any one claim.

PART XXVIII: Change of address
XXVIII.1  The Policyholder must tell the Insurer within 30 days if the Policyholder changes the Policyholder's address.
XXVIII.2  The Insurer may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

PART XXIX: Currency
XXIX.1  All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
XXIX.2  Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

PART XXX: Inflation
XXX.1  The Insurer may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
XXX.2  Any adjustment will be shown in the Policyholder's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

PART XXXI: Tenant's improvements
XXXI.1  If the Policyholder rents the home, the Insurer will pay for damage to fixtures and fittings that the Policyholder installed and are responsible for.
XXXI.2  This cover applies only to improvements the Policyholder paid for, not to items provided by the landlord.

PART XXXII: Arbitration
XXXII.1  If the Insurer accepts a claim but disagree with the Policyholder about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
XXXII.2  Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against the Insurer.

PART XXXIII: Fraud
XXXIII.1  If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Insurer will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
XXXIII.2  The Insurer may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

PART XXXIV: Payment of claims
XXXIV.1  The Insurer will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Policyholder's name.
XXXIV.2  The Insurer aims to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents the Insurer needs.

PART XXXV: Market conditions
XXXV.1  If the replacement item is no longer available, the Insurer will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

PART XXXVI: Contents temporarily removed
XXXVI.1  The Policyholder's contents are covered while temporarily removed from the home to another building in the same country, for up to 60 days.
XXXVI.2  Contents in a student hall of residence are covered only if the student is a member of the Policyholder's family.

PART XXXVII: Taxes
XXXVII.1  The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
XXXVII.2  If the tax rate changes, the Insurer may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

CASE PRESENTATION A
# Annual Multi-Trip Travel Cover
Issued by Northstar Underwriting

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
- **1.2** Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
- **1.3** Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
- **1.4** Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
- **1.5** Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,500 metres.
- **1.6** Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
- **1.7** Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
- **1.8** Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
- **1.9** Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
- **1.10** Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which you received treatment or advice in the 6 months before the policy start date.
- **1.11** Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
- **1.12** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.13** Public transport means any scheduled train, bus, coach, ferry or aircraft.
- **1.14** Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 8 hours.
- **1.15** Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
- **1.16** Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
- **1.17** Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
- **1.18** Territory means the countries in which cover applies, as shown in the schedule.
- **1.19** Travelling companion means a person who has booked to travel with you on the same trip.
- **1.20** Trip means a journey that starts and ends in your home country during the policy period.
- **1.21** Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.2** Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $150 per claim.
- **2.3** Trip Cancellation: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
- **2.4** Travel Delay: limit $750 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
- **2.5** The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Changes in circumstances
- **3.1** You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
- **3.2** We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

## 4. Assignment
- **4.1** You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

## 5. Interpretation
- **5.1** Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
- **5.2** Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
- **5.3** Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

## 6. Repatriation
- **6.1** If our medical adviser agrees it is necessary, we will arrange and pay for you to be brought home.
- **6.2** We will decide the method of transport and the time of repatriation after speaking to the treating doctor.

## 7. Communication
- **7.1** We will communicate with you in English.
- **7.2** We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

## 8. Inflation
- **8.1** We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
- **8.2** Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

## 9. Payment of claims
- **9.1** We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
- **9.2** We aim to pay accepted claims within 15 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

## 10. Salvage
- **10.1** When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
- **10.2** If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

## 11. Baggage and Personal Belongings
- **11.1** We will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to your baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
- **11.2** The most we will pay for Valuables under this section is $400 per incident.
- **11.3** The most we will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $450 per incident.
- **11.4** We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
- **11.5** We will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
- **11.6** We will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

## 12. Discounts
- **12.1** Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
- **12.2** If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

## 13. Data protection
- **13.1** We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
- **13.2** We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
- **13.3** You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

## 14. Emergency Medical Expenses
- **14.1** We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
- **14.2** The most we will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $400 per incident.
- **14.3** The most we will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $300 per incident.
- **14.4** We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
- **14.5** We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
- **14.6** We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

## 15. Trip Cancellation
- **15.1** We will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if you must cancel the trip for a reason beyond your control.
- **15.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 10 days after the policy start date.
- **15.3** The most we will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $300 per incident.
- **15.4** We will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before you bought the policy.
- **15.5** We will not pay for cancellation because you no longer wish to travel.

## 16. Premium payment
- **16.1** You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
- **16.2** If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

## 17. Market conditions
- **17.1** If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

## 18. Currency
- **18.1** All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
- **18.2** Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

## 19. Electronic documents
- **19.1** We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
- **19.2** You must tell us if your email address changes.
- **19.3** Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

## 20. Other insurance
- **20.1** If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
- **20.2** You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

## 21. Personal liability
- **21.1** We will pay damages you become legally liable to pay for accidental injury to another person or accidental damage to their property during the trip.
- **21.2** This section does not cover liability arising from the use of motor vehicles, boats or aircraft.
- **21.3** The most we will pay under this section is $5,000,000 for all claims arising from one event.

## 22. Third-party administrators
- **22.1** We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
- **22.2** Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

## 23. Cooperation
- **23.1** You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
- **23.2** You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

## 24. Customer support
- **24.1** Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
- **24.2** Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

## 25. Accessibility
- **25.1** This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

## 26. Optional cover: Travel Delay
- **26.1** We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
- **26.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **26.3** We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

## 27. General exclusions
- **27.1** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
- **27.2** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **27.3** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.

## 28. Instalment agreements
- **28.1** If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
- **28.2** Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

## 29. Missed departure
- **29.1** We will pay reasonable additional travel and accommodation costs to reach your destination if you arrive too late to board your booked transport because public transport fails.
- **29.2** You must allow enough time to reach the departure point, and must obtain written confirmation of the delay from the transport operator.

## 30. Subrogation
- **30.1** We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
- **30.2** We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

## 31. Notices
- **31.1** Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
- **31.2** Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

## 32. Geographical limits
- **32.1** Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
- **32.2** Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

## 33. How to read this document
- **33.1** This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
- **33.2** Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
- **33.3** Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

## 34. Waiver
- **34.1** If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

## 35. Governing law
- **35.1** This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
- **35.2** Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

## 36. Making a claim
- **36.1** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
- **36.2** You must notify us of a claim within 30 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **36.3** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

Issued by Wellspring Benefits Administration
In this policy, "the Plan" means Wellspring Benefits Administration and "the Member" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Limit means the most the Plan will pay for all claims under a section arising from one treatment.
(b) Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
(c) Registered practitioner means a practitioner registered with the professional body for their discipline.

Article 2. Limits and deductible
(a) Dental Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
(b) Vision Care: limit $500 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
(c) Therapy Services: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
(d) Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
(e) The deductible is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

Article 3. Inflation
(a) The Plan may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
(b) Any adjustment will be shown in the Member's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

Article 4. Premium payment
(a) The Member must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
(b) If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, the Plan may cancel the policy after giving notice.

Article 5. Market conditions
(a) If the replacement item is no longer available, the Plan will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

Article 6. Therapy Services
(a) The Plan will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
(b) The most the Plan will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $300 per treatment.
(c) The Plan will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
(d) The Plan will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

Article 7. Instalment agreements
(a) If the Member pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
(b) Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

Article 8. Waiver
(a) If the Plan does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Plan has given up the right to enforce it later.

Article 9. Records and evidence
(a) The Member should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
(b) Where proof of value is missing, the Plan may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
(c) The Plan may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

Article 10. Compensation scheme
(a) The Plan is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
(b) If the Plan cannot meet the Plan's obligations, the Member may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

Article 11. Change of address
(a) The Member must tell the Plan within 30 days if the Member changes the Member's address.
(b) The Plan may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

(a) The Plan will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Member.
(b) The Plan will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

Article 13. Salvage
(a) When the Plan replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Plan's property.
(b) If stolen property is recovered after the Plan has paid a claim, the Member must tell the Plan and either return the payment or give the Plan the property.

Article 14. Making a claim
(a) The Member must notify the Plan of a claim within 90 days of the treatment. The Plan will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(b) The Plan may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(c) The Member must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

HOUSEHOLD CONTENTS COVER: POLICY BOOKLET
Issued by Lantern General Insurance
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Lantern General Insurance and "the Policyholder" means the person named in the schedule.

Article 1. Definitions
(a) Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
(b) Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Insurer, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
(c) Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
(d) Family means the Policyholder's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Policyholder.
(e) Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
(f) High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
(g) Home means the private residence at the address shown in the schedule.
(h) Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
(i) Limit means the most the Insurer will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
(j) Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
(k) Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
(l) Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
(m) Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
(n) Unoccupied means not lived in by the Policyholder or a member of the Policyholder's family for more than 60 consecutive days.

Article 2. Limits and excess
(a) Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(b) Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
(c) Accidental Damage: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(d) Flood: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(e) The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

Article 3. Escape of Water
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

Article 4. Theft
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
(b) The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,500 per incident.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $800 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
(f) The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

Article 5. Optional cover: Accidental Damage
(a) The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
(b) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $750 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
(e) The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

Article 6. Flood
(a) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
(b) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
(c) The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

Article 7. General exclusions
(a) The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.
(c) The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
(d) The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

Article 8. Making a claim
(a) The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(b) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(c) The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 60 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.

Article 9. Subrogation
(a) The Insurer will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Policyholder's name the defence or settlement of any claim.
(b) The Insurer can take action in the Policyholder's name to recover any payment the Insurer makes from anyone responsible for the loss.

Article 10. Records and evidence
(a) The Policyholder should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
(b) Where proof of value is missing, the Insurer may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
(c) The Insurer may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

Article 11. Geographical limits
(a) Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
(b) Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

Article 12. Claims documents
(a) The Policyholder must provide, at the Policyholder's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Insurer reasonably ask for.
(b) The Insurer may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

Article 13. Inflation
(a) The Insurer may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
(b) Any adjustment will be shown in the Policyholder's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

Article 14. Alternative accommodation
(a) If the Policyholder's home cannot be lived in after damage covered by this policy, the Insurer will pay the reasonable cost of comparable temporary accommodation.
(b) The Insurer will also pay for the temporary housing of pets that live with the Policyholder.
(c) Cover ends when the home is fit to live in again or after twelve months, whichever is sooner.

Article 15. Discounts
(a) Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
(b) If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Insurer may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

Article 16. Duty of fair presentation
(a) The Policyholder must answer all questions the Insurer asks honestly and to the best of the Policyholder's knowledge.
(b) If the Policyholder gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Insurer may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
(c) If the Policyholder gives incorrect information carelessly, the Insurer may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

Article 17. Payment of claims
(a) The Insurer will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Policyholder's name.
(b) The Insurer aims to pay accepted claims within 10 working days of receiving all the documents the Insurer needs.

Article 18. Joint policyholders
(a) Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
(b) A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

Article 19. Taxes
(a) The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
(b) If the tax rate changes, the Insurer may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

Article 20. Compensation scheme
(a) The Insurer is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
(b) If the Insurer cannot meet the Insurer's obligations, the Policyholder may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

Article 21. Notices
(a) Any notice the Insurer gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Insurer holds.
(b) Notices from the Policyholder should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

Article 22. Customer support
(a) The Insurer's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
(b) Outside these hours the Policyholder can leave a message and the Insurer will call back on the next working day.

Article 23. Assignment
(a) The Policyholder cannot transfer the Policyholder's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Insurer's written consent.

Article 24. Change of address
(a) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer within 30 days if the Policyholder changes the Policyholder's address.
(b) The Insurer may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

Article 25. Garden and outdoor cover
(a) The Insurer will pay for plants, trees and shrubs in the garden of the home that are damaged by fire, lightning or theft.
(b) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by frost, storms, drought or animals.

Article 26. Interest
(a) The Insurer will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

Article 27. Currency
(a) All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
(b) Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

Article 28. Data protection
(a) The Insurer will use the personal information the Policyholder provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
(b) The Insurer will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
(c) The Policyholder can ask for a copy of the personal information the Insurer holds by writing to the Insurer's data protection officer.

ELECTRONICS CARE PLAN
Issued by Brightline Device Cover

PART I: Definitions
I.1  Accessories means cases, chargers and earbuds.
I.2  Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
I.3  Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
I.4  Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 12 months after the device was bought.

PART II: Limits and service fee
II.1  Accidental Damage: limit $800 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
II.2  Breakdown: limit $600 per incident; service fee $25 per claim.
II.3  Theft and Loss: limit $800 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
II.4  Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the service fee is then deducted from the result.

PART III: Instalment agreements
III.1  If the Customer pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
III.2  Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

PART IV: Optional cover: Theft and Loss
IV.1  The Provider will replace the Customer's device if it is stolen or lost.
IV.2  This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Customer's schedule.
IV.3  The most the Provider will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.
IV.4  The Provider will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
IV.5  The Provider will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

PART V: Discounts
V.1  Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
V.2  If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Provider may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

PART VI: Transferring the plan
VI.1  The Customer may transfer the plan to a new owner of the device by telling the Provider in writing.
VI.2  The remaining term of the plan transfers with the device; the term does not restart.

PART VII: Repair process
VII.1  After a claim is accepted, the Provider will send a prepaid mailer or book a courier collection.
VII.2  The Provider aims to return repaired devices within 15 business days of receiving them.

PART VIII: Records and evidence
VIII.1  The Customer should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
VIII.2  Where proof of value is missing, the Provider may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
VIII.3  The Provider may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

PART IX: Breakdown
IX.1  The Provider will repair or replace the Customer's device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
IX.2  No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 45 days after the policy start date.
IX.3  The most the Provider will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $80 per incident.
IX.4  The Provider will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
IX.5  The Provider will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

PART X: General exclusions
X.1  The Provider will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
X.2  The Provider will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Customer.

PART XI: Complaints
XI.1  If the Customer has a complaint, the Customer should first contact the Provider's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
XI.2  The Provider will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
XI.3  If the Customer remains dissatisfied, the Customer may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

PART XII: Making a claim
XII.1  The Customer must notify the Provider of a claim within 21 days of the incident. The Provider will not pay any claim notified after that time.
XII.2  The Customer must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
XII.3  The Provider may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

PART XIII: How to read this document
XIII.1  This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
XIII.2  Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
XIII.3  Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

PART XIV: Renewal
XIV.1  The Provider will write to the Customer at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
XIV.2  The Provider is not obliged to offer renewal.

PART XV: Severability
XV.1  If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

CASE PRESENTATION B
# Single-Trip Travel Protection Plan
Issued by Compass Mutual

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
- **1.2** Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
- **1.3** Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
- **1.4** Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
- **1.5** Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
- **1.6** Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,500 metres.
- **1.7** Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
- **1.8** Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
- **1.9** Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which you received treatment or advice in the 12 months before the policy start date.
- **1.10** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.11** Public transport means any scheduled train, bus, coach, ferry or aircraft.
- **1.12** Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 12 hours.
- **1.13** Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
- **1.14** Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
- **1.15** Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
- **1.16** Travelling companion means a person who has booked to travel with you on the same trip.
- **1.17** Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

## 2. Limits and excess
- **2.1** Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $75 per claim.
- **2.2** Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $150 per claim.
- **2.3** Trip Cancellation: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
- **2.4** Travel Delay: limit $750 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
- **2.5** The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Optional cover: Travel Delay
- **3.1** We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
- **3.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **3.3** We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

## 4. Taxes
- **4.1** The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
- **4.2** If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

## 5. Repatriation
- **5.1** If our medical adviser agrees it is necessary, we will arrange and pay for you to be brought home.
- **5.2** We will decide the method of transport and the time of repatriation after speaking to the treating doctor.

## 6. How to read this document
- **6.1** This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
- **6.2** Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
- **6.3** Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

## 7. Joint policyholders
- **7.1** Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
- **7.2** A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

## 8. Emergency Medical Expenses
- **8.1** We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
- **8.2** The most we will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $400 per incident.
- **8.3** The most we will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $300 per incident.
- **8.4** We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
- **8.5** We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
- **8.6** We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

## 9. Emergency assistance
- **9.1** Our emergency assistance service is available 24 hours a day on the number shown in the schedule.
- **9.2** You must contact the assistance service before being admitted to hospital as an in-patient, unless it is an emergency.
- **9.3** The assistance service can arrange payment guarantees, interpreters and transport home.

## 10. Trip Cancellation
- **10.1** We will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if you must cancel the trip for a reason beyond your control.
- **10.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 10 days after the policy start date.
- **10.3** The most we will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $200 per incident.
- **10.4** We will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before you bought the policy.
- **10.5** We will not pay for cancellation because you no longer wish to travel.

## 11. Rental car excess
- **11.1** If you hire a car during the trip, we will reimburse any excess you must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.
- **11.2** This section applies only to cars hired from a licensed rental company under a written agreement.

## 12. Compensation scheme
- **12.1** We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
- **12.2** If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

## 13. Subrogation
- **13.1** We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
- **13.2** We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

## 14. Geographical limits
- **14.1** Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
- **14.2** Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

## 15. Sanctions
- **15.1** We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

## 16. Fraud
- **16.1** If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
- **16.2** We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

## 17. Governing law
- **17.1** This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
- **17.2** Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

## 18. Instalment agreements
- **18.1** If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
- **18.2** Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

## 19. Assignment
- **19.1** You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

## 20. Customer support
- **20.1** Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
- **20.2** Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

## 21. Notices
- **21.1** Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
- **21.2** Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

## 22. Arbitration
- **22.1** If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
- **22.2** Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

## 23. Baggage and Personal Belongings
- **23.1** We will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to your baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
- **23.2** The most we will pay for Valuables under this section is $250 per incident.
- **23.3** The most we will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $450 per incident.
- **23.4** We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
- **23.5** We will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
- **23.6** We will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

## 24. Recovery of costs
- **24.1** If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

## 25. Complaints
- **25.1** If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
- **25.2** We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
- **25.3** If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

## 26. Severability
- **26.1** If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

## 27. Inflation
- **27.1** We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
- **27.2** Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

## 28. Other insurance
- **28.1** If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
- **28.2** You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

## 29. Market conditions
- **29.1** If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

## 30. Third-party administrators
- **30.1** We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
- **30.2** Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

## 31. Cancellation
- **31.1** You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
- **31.2** After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
- **31.3** We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

## 32. Communication
- **32.1** We will communicate with you in English.
- **32.2** We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

## 33. Personal liability
- **33.1** We will pay damages you become legally liable to pay for accidental injury to another person or accidental damage to their property during the trip.
- **33.2** This section does not cover liability arising from the use of motor vehicles, boats or aircraft.
- **33.3** The most we will pay under this section is $1,000,000 for all claims arising from one event.

## 34. Exchange of information
- **34.1** To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
- **34.2** We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

## 35. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
- **35.1** A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

## 36. Discounts
- **36.1** Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
- **36.2** If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

## 37. Records and evidence
- **37.1** You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
- **37.2** Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
- **37.3** We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

## 38. Accessibility
- **38.1** This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

## 39. Reasonable precautions
- **39.1** You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
- **39.2** You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

## 40. Payment of claims
- **40.1** We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
- **40.2** We aim to pay accepted claims within 10 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

## 41. Interpretation
- **41.1** Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
- **41.2** Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
- **41.3** Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

## 42. Premium payment
- **42.1** You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
- **42.2** If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

## 43. Renewal
- **43.1** We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
- **43.2** We are not obliged to offer renewal.

## 44. Automatic renewal
- **44.1** Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
- **44.2** You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

## 45. Claims documents
- **45.1** You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
- **45.2** We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

## 46. Duty of fair presentation
- **46.1** You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
- **46.2** If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
- **46.3** If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

## 47. Changes in circumstances
- **47.1** You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
- **47.2** We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

## 48. General exclusions
- **48.1** We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
- **48.2** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
- **48.3** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **48.4** We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
- **48.5** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
- **48.6** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.

## 49. Cooperation
- **49.1** You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
- **49.2** You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

## 50. Legal expenses abroad
- **50.1** We will pay legal costs to pursue compensation for your injury or death caused by a third party during the trip.
- **50.2** We will not pay legal costs unless our legal adviser agrees that the claim has a reasonable prospect of success.

## 51. Data protection
- **51.1** We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
- **51.2** We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
- **51.3** You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

## 52. Electronic documents
- **52.1** We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
- **52.2** You must tell us if your email address changes.
- **52.3** Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

## 53. Change of address
- **53.1** You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
- **53.2** We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

## 54. Currency
- **54.1** All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
- **54.2** Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

## 55. Interest
- **55.1** We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

## 56. Waiver
- **56.1** If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

## 57. Environmental commitment
- **57.1** Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
- **57.2** You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

## 58. Salvage
- **58.1** When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
- **58.2** If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

CASE PRESENTATION B
# Gadget Cover: Terms and Conditions
Issued by Brightline Device Cover

## 1. Definitions
- **1.1** Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.
- **1.2** Accessories means cases, chargers and earbuds.
- **1.3** Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any service fee, limit or sublimit is applied.
- **1.4** Authorised repairer means a repairer approved in writing by us.
- **1.5** Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
- **1.6** Breakdown means the failure of a part to work as the manufacturer intended, from an internal electrical or mechanical fault.
- **1.7** Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
- **1.8** Device means the item shown in the schedule, bought new from an authorised retailer.
- **1.9** Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
- **1.10** Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
- **1.11** Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 24 months after the device was bought.
- **1.12** Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
- **1.13** Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
- **1.14** Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
- **1.15** Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
- **1.16** Replacement device means a device of the same or similar specification, which may be refurbished.
- **1.17** Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
- **1.18** Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
- **1.19** Wearables means smartwatches and fitness trackers.

## 2. Limits and service fee
- **2.1** Accidental Damage: limit $800 per incident; service fee $79 per claim.
- **2.2** Breakdown: limit $600 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
- **2.3** Theft and Loss: limit $800 per incident; service fee $149 per claim.
- **2.4** The service fee is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

## 3. Optional cover: Theft and Loss
- **3.1** We will replace your device if it is stolen or lost.
- **3.2** This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
- **3.3** The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.
- **3.4** We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
- **3.5** We will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

## 4. Accidental Damage
- **4.1** We will repair or replace your device if it is accidentally damaged.
- **4.2** The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
- **4.3** The most we will pay for Wearables under this section is $300 per incident.
- **4.4** We will not pay for cosmetic damage, such as scratches or dents, that does not affect how the device works.
- **4.5** We will not pay for damage following a repair by anyone other than us or an authorised repairer. This exclusion does not apply if we approved the repair in writing beforehand.

## 5. Breakdown
- **5.1** We will repair or replace your device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
- **5.2** No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 45 days after the policy start date.
- **5.3** The most we will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $80 per incident.
- **5.4** We will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
- **5.5** We will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

## 6. General exclusions
- **6.1** We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
- **6.2** We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
- **6.3** We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
- **6.4** We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.

## 7. Making a claim
- **7.1** You must notify us of a claim within 30 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
- **7.2** We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
- **7.3** You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

## 8. Cooperation
- **8.1** You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
- **8.2** You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

## 9. Exchange of information
- **9.1** To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
- **9.2** We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

## 10. Accessibility
- **10.1** This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

## 11. Market conditions
- **11.1** If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

## 12. Fraud
- **12.1** If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
- **12.2** We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

## 13. Data protection
- **13.1** We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
- **13.2** We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
- **13.3** You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

## 14. Unrecoverable devices
- **14.1** If a device is found after we have replaced it, the found device becomes our property and must be sent to us.
- **14.2** We may block devices reported as lost or stolen so that they cannot be used on mobile networks.

## 15. Currency
- **15.1** All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
- **15.2** Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

## 16. Renewal
- **16.1** We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
- **16.2** We are not obliged to offer renewal.

## 17. Payment of claims
- **17.1** We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
- **17.2** We aim to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

## 18. Claims documents
- **18.1** You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
- **18.2** We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

## 19. Instalment agreements
- **19.1** If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
- **19.2** Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

## 20. Recovery of costs
- **20.1** If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

## 21. Reasonable precautions
- **21.1** You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
- **21.2** You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

## 22. Other insurance
- **22.1** If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
- **22.2** You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

## 23. Duty of fair presentation
- **23.1** You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
- **23.2** If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
- **23.3** If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

## 24. Taxes
- **24.1** The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
- **24.2** If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

## 25. Communication
- **25.1** We will communicate with you in English.
- **25.2** We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

## 26. Geographical limits
- **26.1** Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
- **26.2** Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

## 27. Replacement devices
- **27.1** If we cannot repair your device economically, we will replace it with a replacement device.
- **27.2** Replacement devices may be a different colour and may be refurbished to an as-new standard.
- **27.3** Accessories are replaced only if they were lost or damaged in the same incident as the device.

## 28. Assignment
- **28.1** You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

## 29. Customer support
- **29.1** Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
- **29.2** Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

## 30. Records and evidence
- **30.1** You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
- **30.2** Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
- **30.3** We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

## 31. Interest
- **31.1** We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

## 32. Software support
- **32.1** Our helpline can give advice on setting up and using your device.
- **32.2** Software support does not include fixing problems caused by third-party apps or unofficial operating systems.

## 33. How to read this document
- **33.1** This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
- **33.2** Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
- **33.3** Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

## 34. Cancellation
- **34.1** You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
- **34.2** After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
- **34.3** We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

## 35. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
- **35.1** A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

## 36. Waiver
- **36.1** If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

## 37. Subrogation
- **37.1** We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
- **37.2** We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

## 38. Joint policyholders
- **38.1** Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
- **38.2** A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

## 39. Transferring the plan
- **39.1** You may transfer the plan to a new owner of the device by telling us in writing.
- **39.2** The remaining term of the plan transfers with the device; the term does not restart.

## 40. Arbitration
- **40.1** If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
- **40.2** Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

## 41. Environmental commitment
- **41.1** Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
- **41.2** You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

## 42. Electronic documents
- **42.1** We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
- **42.2** You must tell us if your email address changes.
- **42.3** Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

## 43. Sanctions
- **43.1** We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

## 44. Compensation scheme
- **44.1** We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
- **44.2** If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

## 45. Automatic renewal
- **45.1** Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
- **45.2** You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

## 46. Discounts
- **46.1** Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
- **46.2** If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

## 47. Premium payment
- **47.1** You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
- **47.2** If an instalment is not paid within 21 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

## 48. Interpretation
- **48.1** Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
- **48.2** Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
- **48.3** Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

## 49. Severability
- **49.1** If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

## 50. Notices
- **50.1** Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
- **50.2** Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.
